The natural colors are prominent: creamy-white chicken, pale yellow potatoes, and off-white cauliflower against the dark, fragrant sauce. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green, chopped fresh coriander leaves garnishes the top, adding fresh contrast. The dish is arranged naturally, components slightly overlapping, for a hearty, home-cooked feel. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple metal spoon and a small portion of fluffy white basmati rice in a separate, small bowl. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with basmati rice or naan bread.
Offer a side of cooling raita (yogurt dip) or pickled vegetables (achar).

ingredients.name: Chicken thigh
ingredients.quantity: 1 boneless, skinless (approx. 150-200g), cut into 3-4 large chunks

ingredients.name: Potato
ingredients.quantity: 1 medium (approx. 150g), peeled and cut into 2cm cubes

instructions: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste. Cook 1 minute.
Add pureed tomato. Cook 2-3 minutes, until oil separates from the mixture.
Add turmeric, cumin, coriander, and chili powders. Cook 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add chicken chunks. Sear all sides until lightly browned.
Add potato cubes and 150 ml water or chicken stock. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add cauliflower florets. Continue simmering 10-15 minutes, until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender.
Stir in garam masala.
Season with salt to taste. Add more water if a thinner gravy is desired.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander.
notes: Adjust red chili powder to your preferred spice level.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Cerdo
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a vibrant, orange-hued rice known as Arroz con Cerdo, served on a clean white porcelain plate. Large, golden-brown seared pork chunks are distributed throughout the fluffy medium-grain rice. Visible pieces of translucent diced onions, minced garlic, green olives, and small capers add textural variety. The rice is garnished with fresh, bright green chopped cilantro. A side of thick-cut fried sweet plantains rests beside the rice. The setting is a modern bistro with a light wood table and a neutral cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the moist texture of the meat and individual grains. The entire plate is visible, showing a balanced restaurant portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fried sweet plantains (amarillos)
Accompany with thick slices of fresh avocado
Serve with a side of crispy tostones
instructions: Season pork chunks with salt, pepper, and oregano.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Brown pork chunks on all sides until golden. Remove pork from pot.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in the same pot until translucent.
Stir in tomato sauce, sazón, green olives, and capers.
Return pork to the pot. Add rice and stir to coat grains.
Pour in water. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid.
Simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use a caldero for the most authentic rice texture.
Do not stir the rice while simmering to allow a crust (pegao) to form at the bottom.
Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pot Spanish Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of One-Pot Spanish Chicken and Rice is presented on a simple, rustic ceramic plate. Golden-brown seared chicken thighs, cooked whole, rest atop a bed of vibrant yellow-orange rice. The rice is studded with diced red bell pepper, softened diced tomatoes, and finely minced garlic, showing varying textures. The dish has a moist, cohesive appearance, characteristic of a well-cooked one-pot meal, not dry. A scattering of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley adds a touch of green. A lemon wedge is placed beside the chicken. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, natural light. A plain linen napkin is casually folded next to the plate. The overall impression is one of comforting, expertly prepared home cooking.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful juices.
Offer lemon wedges for a fresh squeeze over the dish.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and diced bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and their juices. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, to reduce slightly.
Add rice to the pot. Stir well to coat rice with vegetables and spices. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in hot chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the rice. Ensure chicken is partially submerged. Cover the pot tightly.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Internal temperature of chicken should reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove pot from heat. Let rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
While resting, toast crusty bread. Rub with a cut garlic clove if desired.
Garnish One-Pot Spanish Chicken and Rice with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Using a good quality short-grain rice like Bomba or Arborio will yield the best texture for this dish, absorbing liquid well without becoming mushy.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The resting period is crucial for the rice to finish absorbing liquid and for flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mustard Pork Loin with Tomato Bell Pepper Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate, on a well-used wooden dining table. A generous, mounded portion of vibrant Tomato Bell Pepper Rice, with clearly visible diced red and yellow bell peppers and diced tomatoes, sits on one side. The rice grains are separate and fluffy. Next to it, a thick, pan-seared pork loin medallion, about 2cm thick, displays a golden-brown crust. A rich, creamy, light yellow mustard-mayonnaise sauce is generously spooned over the pork, pooling around its base. The sauce is smooth and glossy. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is casually scattered over the pork and sauce. The scene features warm, cozy lighting, evoking a family kitchen. A simple cloth napkin and everyday flatware are casually placed. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad on the side.
Offer warm crusty bread for soaking up the sauce.
instructions: Pat pork loin dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Cut into 4 thick medallions.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced red and yellow bell peppers and diced tomatoes. Cook for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened.
Stir in rice. Pour in chicken or vegetable broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not lift lid.
While rice cooks, heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add pork loin medallions.
Sear pork for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 63°C (145°F).
Transfer seared pork to a plate. Tent with foil. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium-low in the same skillet. Add Dijon mustard, mayonnaise, and heavy cream. Whisk until smooth.
Bring sauce to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until sauce slightly thickens. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Fluff rice with a fork. Plate a portion of rice. Place a pork loin medallion next to the rice. Spoon generous sauce over the pork.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
notes: Adjust mustard and mayonnaise ratios in the sauce to personal preference.
For juicier pork, ensure not to overcook. Resting is crucial.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thigh with Potatoes and Cauliflower
recipes.visual_description: A roasted bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh rests centrally on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. The chicken skin is deeply golden and crisp, with visible seasoning. Surrounding the chicken are generously portioned, roasted potato wedges, their skins golden-brown and slightly crinkled. Interspersed among the potatoes are tender cauliflower florets, some edges lightly caramelized to a deep golden hue, others retaining their creamy white color. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is scattered over the dish. The plate sits on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, silver fork and knife are placed to the side, resting on a casually folded linen napkin. The scene is lit with soft, warm light, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The background is minimal, hinting at a comfortable home setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and pat dry chicken thigh.
Season chicken with half of salt, pepper, and paprika.
Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges. Cut cauliflower into florets.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges and cauliflower florets.
Drizzle vegetables with olive oil. Add remaining salt, pepper, paprika, garlic powder, and dried rosemary. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange seasoned vegetables in a single layer on a baking tray. Place chicken thigh on the tray among the vegetables.
Roast for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender and golden brown. Flip vegetables halfway through cooking.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Baked Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of Mediterranean Baked Chicken and Rice is presented on a simple, slightly rustic ceramic plate, reflecting everyday home cooking. A golden-brown seared chicken thigh, cooked whole, sits prominently atop a bed of tender, slightly moist long-grain rice. The rice is infused with the rich, reddish hue of tomatoes and speckled with vibrant orange chunks of roasted carrots and soft, white potato wedges. Dark, glossy black olive halves are scattered throughout, adding a visual pop. The dish exhibits natural textures: crispy chicken skin, fluffy rice, and tender vegetables. The plating is casual, with ingredients naturally piled. The scene is set on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, inviting natural light, suggesting a cozy family meal. A simple, everyday fork rests beside the plate, and a casually folded cloth napkin adds to the unpretentious, lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the baking dish for a family-style meal.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the flavorful juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown, about 5 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion, chopped carrots, and chopped potatoes. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until vegetables soften slightly.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, oregano, and thyme. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in the rice. Season with salt and pepper.
Nestle the seared chicken thighs into the rice mixture. Scatter halved black olives around the chicken.
Cover the pot with a lid and bake for 30 minutes.
Remove lid and bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender, liquid is absorbed, and chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Consommé with Potato Pearls and Fermented Herb Oil
recipes.visual_description: A clear, amber beef consommé fills a handcrafted, shallow ceramic bowl in an earthy cream tone. At the bottom, small, perfectly spherical potato pearls, about 5mm in diameter, rest like delicate jewels. A few drops of vibrant green fermented herb oil dot the consommé's surface, creating subtle, organic patterns. The presentation is minimalistic, emphasizing the natural beauty and clean lines of each element. The bowl sits on a light bamboo table surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin and a simple, natural wooden spoon. The background is clean and uncluttered, with soft, natural light illuminating the dish, highlighting its pure, sustainable essence.
instructions: Roast beef bones until deeply browned.
Combine roasted bones, diced onion, carrots, celery, and peppercorns in a large pot. Add cold water. Bring to a simmer. Skim foam. Simmer for 6-8 hours.
Strain broth through a fine sieve. Discard solids. Chill broth completely. Skim solidified fat.
For consommé: In a large pot, combine chilled broth, lean beef mince, finely chopped onion, and egg whites. Whisk gently to combine.
Heat slowly over medium-low heat. Stir occasionally until a 'raft' of solids forms on the surface. Stop stirring once raft forms.
Create a small opening in the raft. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes. Do not boil.
Carefully ladle clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Discard raft.
For potato pearls: Peel potatoes. Cut into chunks. Reserve potato peels and any starchy liquid for other uses. Boil potato chunks in lightly salted water until tender. Drain well.
Pass cooked potatoes through a fine sieve or ricer. Mix with a small amount of reserved potato cooking water until a smooth, pliable dough forms. Season with salt.
Roll small portions of potato dough into tiny pearls, approximately 5mm in diameter.
Gently poach potato pearls in simmering water for 2-3 minutes until they float. Remove with a slotted spoon.

For fermented herb oil: Wash herb stems. Roughly chop. Blend with a pinch of salt and 50ml water until smooth. Transfer to a clean jar. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until slightly sour and bubbly.
Blend fermented herb mixture with vegetable oil. Strain through a fine sieve or coffee filter to yield clear green oil.
To serve: Gently warm consommé. Place potato pearls in individual bowls. Ladle hot consommé over pearls. Drizzle with fermented herb oil.
notes: Utilize beef bones and scraps for the broth, embracing a zero-waste approach.
Potato peels and starchy cooking water can be repurposed for other dishes or composted.
Herb stems, often discarded, are transformed into a flavorful fermented oil, promoting sustainability.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Rôti with Pommes Lyonnaise
recipes.special_requests: Potato with chicken and vegetables cuisine
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, its skin a rich, crispy golden-brown, is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it rests a neat, slightly rustic mound of Pommes Lyonnaise. These potato rounds, cut into 5mm thick slices, are golden-edged and gently interspersed with soft, translucent, lightly caramelized onion slices. A glossy, deep amber pan jus is artfully spooned over the chicken and around the base of the potatoes, creating a subtle sheen. The dish is finished with a generous sprinkle of vibrant, finely chopped fresh parsley, adding a pop of green. The overall plating is balanced and professional, with ample negative space. The dish is set on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by traditional flatware and a neatly folded cotton napkin, conveying a modern bistro atmosphere under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a classic main course.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden and crisp. Flip.
Add thyme sprigs and crushed garlic cloves to the skillet.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast chicken for 25-30 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Place on a cutting board to rest for 5 minutes. Tent loosely with foil.
For the jus: Drain excess fat from the skillet, leaving about 1-2 tablespoons.
Place skillet over medium heat. Deglaze with white wine, scraping up all browned bits from the bottom.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half until slightly thickened. Strain if desired. Keep warm.
For Pommes Lyonnaise: Peel potatoes. Cut into 5mm thick rounds.
Boil potato rounds in a pot of salted water for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain very well.
Thinly slice the onions.
Heat butter in a large separate skillet over medium heat.
Add sliced onions. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly caramelized.
Add the drained potato rounds to the skillet with the onions. Toss gently to combine.
Cook potatoes and onions for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until potatoes are golden and slightly crispy. Season with salt and pepper.
Chop fresh parsley.
To serve: Place a portion of Pommes Lyonnaise on each plate.
Arrange one roasted chicken thigh next to the potatoes.
Spoon the warm pan jus over the chicken and potatoes.
Garnish generously with chopped fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Resting the chicken after roasting helps retain its juiciness.

recipes.recipe_name: Chai-Spiced Oat & Root Vegetable Bowl
recipes.special_requests: минимализм углеводние вафли без творога яиц пшеничной муки яиц банана
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of a vibrant, plant-forward bowl. The base is creamy, light beige savory oats, filling the bottom third of a handcrafted, rustic ceramic bowl in an earthy cream tone. On top, 2 cm rustic chunks of roasted root vegetables—bright orange carrots, pale parsnips, and deep red sweet potato—are artfully arranged in a natural, unforced pile, showcasing their caramelized edges and varied textures. A generous scattering of translucent, deep red chai-pickled red onion slices adds a sharp color contrast and visual pop. The dish is finished with a sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green dill fronds. The bowl sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is subtly placed to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the organic textures and colors of the ingredients. The background is clean and minimalist, allowing the food to be the sole focus.

ingredients.name: Seasonal root vegetables (carrots, parsnips, sweet potato)

instructions: Prepare Pickled Onions: In a small pot, combine 100 ml water, apple cider vinegar, 5 ml honey, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Remove from heat. Add chai tea bag. Steep 5 minutes. Remove tea bag. Add thinly sliced red onion. Let cool. Refrigerate at least 30 minutes.

Roast Root Vegetables: Preheat oven to 200°C (392°F). Cut root vegetables into 2 cm rustic chunks. Toss with 10 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized. In the last 5 minutes, drizzle with remaining 10 ml honey.

Cook Savory Oats: In a medium saucepan, heat remaining 5 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Add rolled oats. Stir 1 minute. Pour in 300 ml water and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until oats are tender and liquid is absorbed. Add salt and pepper to taste.

Assemble Bowl: Spoon savory oats into a deep ceramic bowl. Arrange roasted root vegetable chunks artfully on top. Drain pickled red onions and scatter over the vegetables. Garnish with chopped fresh dill or parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing seasonal, local root vegetables. Consider using root vegetable tops (if edible) for other preparations like pesto or broth to further minimize waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Tuna Confit Pasta with Pickled Red Onion
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of sustainable tuna confit pasta is artfully presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate, resting on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The spaghetti is loosely coiled, forming a natural mound at the center. Interspersed within the pasta are generous, naturally flaked chunks of pale pink tuna confit, showcasing its tender texture. Bright, thinly sliced, translucent pink pickled red onions are scattered across the top, providing a vibrant contrast and crisp visual texture. Fresh, roughly chopped green herbs, like parsley or dill, are sparsely sprinkled, adding a touch of natural color and freshness. The overall composition is clean and unforced, emphasizing natural ingredient beauty and ample white space around the dish. Soft, diffused natural light highlights the subtle variations in color and texture. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is folded neatly beside the plate, completing the eco-conscious, minimalist setting.

ingredients.name: Other vegetable scraps (e.g., carrot peels, celery ends)

instructions: Prepare Tuna Confit: Place tuna chunks, smashed garlic, bay leaf, peppercorns, and salt in a small, oven-safe pot. Pour olive oil over to fully submerge the tuna. Cook in an oven preheated to 120°C for 25-35 minutes, or until tuna is cooked through and flakes easily. Do not boil. Let cool in oil. Once cool, gently remove tuna, flake into large chunks, and set aside. Reserve confit oil.

Prepare Pickled Red Onions: In a small saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, and salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Place thinly sliced red onions in a heat-proof jar or bowl. Pour hot pickling liquid over onions. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Make Zero-Waste Broth (Optional): While tuna cooks, combine onion trimmings and other vegetable scraps with 500ml water in a small saucepan. Simmer gently for 20 minutes. Strain and reserve broth. Discard solids.
Cook Pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta cooking water before draining.

Assemble Dish: In a large pan, add 30ml of the reserved tuna confit oil (or fresh olive oil). Add seasonal greens and cherry tomatoes (if using). Sauté briefly until greens wilt. Add cooked pasta, flaked tuna, and 60ml of the zero-waste broth (or reserved pasta water). Toss gently to combine, adding more broth/pasta water if needed to create a light sauce.
Serve: Divide pasta among four plates. Top each portion generously with drained pickled red onions. Garnish with fresh parsley or dill. Season with flaked sea salt and black pepper to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken & Bell Pepper Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Chicken & Bell Pepper Rigatoni is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The rigatoni noodles are coated in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce. Irregularly cut, golden-brown chicken chunks are interspersed throughout the pasta. Bright red and yellow bell pepper strips add contrasting color and texture. The dish is topped with a scattering of fresh, torn green basil leaves and a light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese. The presentation is organized yet naturally flowing, with moderate negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, with traditional Italian flatware and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Enjoy with a glass of a medium-bodied red wine, such as Chianti or Montepulciano d'Abruzzo.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Remove seeds from chili, finely chop. Cut bell peppers into 2 cm strips.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add onion to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add bell peppers, garlic, and chopped chili. Cook for 5-7 minutes until bell peppers begin to soften.

Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Return seared chicken to the skillet. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml of pasta water. Drain pasta.
Add cooked rigatoni to the sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water.
Tear fresh basil leaves. Stir most of the basil into the pasta. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Chickpea Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Fermented Tomato & Chickpea Stew is presented in a wide, shallow, handcrafted ceramic bowl with a natural, unglazed rim. The stew, a rich, deep red, fills the center of the bowl, allowing for generous negative space around the edges. It features tender, whole chickpeas and distinct, roughly chopped tomato pieces, some softened, some holding their shape, alongside finely diced aromatics. A vibrant green basil oil is drizzled in an organic swirl across the top, adding a fresh contrast. A few small, whole fresh basil leaves are artfully placed as a natural garnish. The bowl rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a folded undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the rustic textures and natural colors of the ingredients in a clean, minimalist composition.
instructions: Prepare fermented tomatoes: Roughly chop 300g overripe tomatoes. Combine 300ml water and 6g non-iodized salt to make a brine. Place tomatoes in a clean jar. Pour brine over tomatoes, ensuring they are submerged. Seal the jar. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily. Refrigerate when done.
Soak dried chickpeas overnight in cold water. Drain and rinse. Cook chickpeas in fresh water until tender, about 1-1.5 hours. Drain, reserving cooking liquid if desired for other uses.
Chop 700g ripe tomatoes into 2 cm chunks. Dice the onion finely. Mince garlic.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chopped fresh tomatoes, cooked chickpeas, and fermented tomatoes (including their liquid). Add vegetable stock and nutritional yeast. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Stir occasionally.
While stew simmers, prepare basil oil: Blend 50g fresh basil leaves with 30 ml olive oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve if a very clear oil is desired.
Season stew with sea salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust consistency with more stock or water if needed.
Ladle the stew into individual serving bowls. Drizzle generously with basil oil. Serve immediately.
notes: To maximize zero-waste, use tomato cores and skins from the ripe tomatoes to create a quick stock. Simmer them in water for 15-20 minutes, then strain and use as part of the vegetable stock.
The aquafaba (chickpea cooking liquid) can be used as an egg white substitute in other recipes, such as meringues or mousses.
Adjust fermentation time for tomatoes based on ambient temperature and desired tartness. A longer fermentation yields a stronger flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Home-Style Doner Spiced Sausage Flatbreads
recipes.visual_description: A single warm, slightly charred flatbread is generously filled, folded, and presented on a simple, rustic ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The interior reveals a hearty portion of richly spiced, crumbled sausage, interspersed with tender, small cubes of red bell pepper and softened onion. Layered on top are fresh, crisp shredded iceberg lettuce, vibrant thin slices of ripe red tomato, and delicate, translucent rings of red onion. A creamy white yogurt-cucumber sauce, flecked with fresh green dill, is generously drizzled over the filling, with some pooling subtly. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, evoking a relaxed family meal. A metal fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. A small, dark ceramic bowl containing a few glistening pickled red peppers or olives sits nearby, enhancing the homely, culturally authentic scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with cacik (yogurt sauce)
Serve with fresh salad (shredded lettuce, sliced tomatoes, red onion)
Serve with warm flatbreads or pita
Optionally serve with pickled vegetables or spicy sauce on the side
instructions: Prepare yogurt sauce: In a bowl, combine yogurt, grated cucumber (squeezed dry), minced garlic, chopped dill or mint, lemon juice, and salt. Mix well. Refrigerate.
Prepare sausage: Remove sausage casings. Crumble sausage meat into a large skillet.
Cook sausage: Heat skillet over medium-high heat. Add crumbled sausage. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Set sausage aside.

Sauté aromatics: Add olive oil to the same skillet. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and diced red bell pepper. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until bell pepper is slightly tender.
Add spices: Stir in tomato paste, cumin, smoked paprika, oregano, salt, black pepper, and chili flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Combine: Return cooked sausage to the skillet. Stir well to combine with the spiced vegetable mixture. Cook for 2-3 minutes to allow flavors to meld. Keep warm.
Warm flatbreads: Warm flatbreads in a dry skillet, oven, or microwave until soft and pliable.

Assemble: Lay out warm flatbreads. Fill each with a generous portion of the spiced sausage mixture. Top with shredded lettuce, sliced tomatoes, and red onion rings. Drizzle generously with the prepared yogurt sauce. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe offers a home-cooked adaptation of classic Doner Kebab flavors, using readily available sausage for a comforting, hearty meal.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Russian Beef Stroganoff with Egg Noodles
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Classic Russian Beef Stroganoff is presented in a white, shallow porcelain bowl. A base of golden-yellow wide egg noodles is topped with a rich, creamy, light brown sauce. Tender, dark brown seared beef chunks are prominent, interspersed with diced, slightly browned smoked sausage pieces. The entire dish is generously sprinkled with vibrant green, freshly chopped dill and golden-brown crispy bacon bits, providing textural contrast. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. A slice of dark, dense Borodinsky bread with visible caraway seeds is positioned on a small side plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and texture. The background is a softly blurred, inviting modern bistro setting, emphasizing the dish as the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of fresh smetana (sour cream) on the side for extra richness.
Accompany with slices of dark rye bread, such as Borodinsky bread, to sop up the sauce.
Garnish generously with fresh dill, a staple herb in Russian cuisine.
instructions: Cut beef into 3cm chunks. Dice smoked sausage and bacon. Slice mushrooms. Finely dice onion. Mince garlic.
Heat a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add diced bacon. Cook until crisp. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon; set aside. Reserve bacon fat in the pan.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add vegetable oil to the pan with bacon fat. Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove seared beef; set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms and diced sausage to the pan. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and sausage is lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and sausage. Stir for 1 minute to cook the flour. Gradually whisk in beef broth, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef chunks to the pan. Season with salt and black pepper. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until beef is tender and sauce has thickened.
While the sauce simmers, cook wide egg noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Remove the stroganoff sauce from heat. Stir in sour cream and most of the chopped fresh dill. Do not boil after adding sour cream.
Serve hot beef stroganoff generously spooned over the cooked egg noodles. Garnish with reserved crispy bacon and remaining fresh dill. Serve immediately with slices of Borodinsky bread.
notes: Ensure beef chunks are well seared for maximum flavor before simmering.
Do not boil the sauce after adding sour cream, as it can curdle; remove from heat before stirring in.
traditional_techniques: Using smetana (sour cream) as a finishing agent for richness and tang

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Bacon Broth with Spelt Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Fermented Tomato & Bacon Broth with Spelt Pasta is elegantly presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl in a soft cream color. The bowl sits on a light, natural bamboo table surface, showcasing its organic texture. The soup features a rich, earthy orange-red broth, slightly cloudy from the blended fermented tomatoes, with visible small, diced chunks of carrot and celery, and the occasional piece of spelt pasta. The pasta, small shells or ditalini, is perfectly al dente and distributed throughout the broth. Scattered across the surface are small, crispy bacon bits, providing textural contrast and a deeper color note. Fresh basil leaves, torn into irregular shapes, are gently placed on top, adding vibrant green. A few delicate, bright orange calendula petals are subtly arranged to add a touch of natural color. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space around the bowl. A natural, undyed linen napkin in beige is folded simply beside the bowl. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and natural colors of the ingredients. The background is clean and slightly blurred, with hints of green foliage from a nearby plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Wash and roughly chop tomatoes. Place in a clean 2-liter jar.
Dissolve 20g sea salt in 1 liter filtered water to make a 2% brine.
Pour brine over tomatoes in the jar. Ensure tomatoes are fully submerged using a fermentation weight.
Cover jar loosely. Place at room temperature (18-22°C) for 5-7 days. Check daily for bubbles. Skim any mold.
Once fermented, store tomatoes in the refrigerator.
Drain fermented tomatoes. Reserve liquid. Roughly chop fermented tomatoes.
In a large pot, render diced bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove crispy bacon bits; set aside for garnish.
Leave 2 tablespoons of rendered fat in the pot. Add diced onion, celery, and carrot. Sauté until softened, 8-10 minutes.
Add chopped fermented tomatoes to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring.
Pour in vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15 minutes.
Use an immersion blender to partially blend the soup. Leave some texture.
Add spelt pasta to the simmering soup. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Add reserved fermented tomato liquid gradually, if a tangier flavor is desired.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with crispy bacon bits, torn basil leaves, and thinly sliced spring onion greens. Add edible flower petals if desired.
notes: Fermentation time for tomatoes may vary based on temperature and desired tanginess.

recipes.recipe_name: Shawarma-Spiced Sausage Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Shawarma-Spiced Sausage Skillet is presented on a rustic ceramic plate. Thick, browned sausage chunks are mixed with tender-crisp, vibrantly colored bell pepper strips and translucent onion wedges, arranged casually for a homely feel. The sausage boasts a deep brown sear, complementing the softened, slightly charred vegetables. A small pile of fresh, finely diced red tomato and green cucumber cubes sits alongside. A dollop of creamy tahini sauce is placed nearby. A warm, folded pita bread rests beside the main dish. The scene is on a well-used wooden dining table, evoking a family kitchen. A simple metal fork is present. Soft, warm kitchen lighting creates a cozy atmosphere. The minimal background highlights the comforting meal. Portions are modest and inviting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread for scooping.
Offer creamy tahini sauce as a condiment.
Include fresh diced tomatoes and cucumbers on the side.
Optionally, serve with pickled turnips or cucumbers.
instructions: Slice sausages into thick 3 cm chunks. Cut red and green bell peppers into thick strips. Slice onion into thick wedges. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Add sausage chunks to the skillet. Brown on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove sausages and set aside.
Add bell pepper strips and onion wedges to the same skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic, ground cumin, ground coriander, smoked paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, and black pepper to the vegetables. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Return sausage chunks to the skillet with the vegetables. Stir to coat sausages and vegetables evenly with spices. Season with salt.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover skillet. Cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sausages are cooked through and vegetables are tender-crisp.
While skillet cooks, prepare tahini sauce: In a small bowl, whisk tahini, lemon juice, and cold water until smooth and creamy. Add more water if needed for desired consistency.
Dice tomato and cucumber into small cubes.
Serve Shawarma-spiced sausage and vegetables hot. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve with warm pita breads, tahini sauce, and diced tomato and cucumber on the side.
notes: For an extra layer of flavor, you can marinate the sausage chunks in the spices and a splash of olive oil for at least 30 minutes before cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Vin Blanc
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with crisp, golden-brown skin. They sit in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl filled with a glossy, ivory-colored cream sauce. Thick-cut bacon lardons and browned, halved button mushrooms are distributed naturally around the chicken. Whole, softened shallots are visible in the sauce. Finely chopped flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled over the top for color. The plating is clean with moderate negative space. The setting includes a rustic wooden table, a linen napkin, and a side of crusty baguette slices. Lighting is natural and bright, emphasizing the textures of the seared skin and the velvety sauce consistency. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh, crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with buttery mashed potatoes or buttered egg noodles
Pair with a chilled glass of the same dry white wine used in cooking
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add bacon lardons to the same pan. Fry until crisp.
Add halved mushrooms. Sauté until browned.
Stir in shallots and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the pan bottom to release browned bits.
Add chicken stock and thyme sprigs.
Place chicken back into the pan.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Transfer chicken to a warm plate.
Whisk heavy cream and butter into the pan juices.
Simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to the sauce. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Use a high-quality dry white wine for the best sauce flavor
Do not boil the sauce vigorously after adding cream to avoid curdling
Keep the skin above the liquid level during braising to maintain crispness

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Pork and Paprika Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty Spanish Pork and Paprika Stew is presented in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl. Tender, slow-cooked pork chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, are nestled within a rich, deep red paprika-infused tomato sauce. Vibrant green broccoli florets and crisp-tender green beans, both cut to 4-5 cm lengths, are scattered throughout, adding color and fresh texture. The sauce has a glossy, thick consistency. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley garnishes the top. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a clean white porcelain side plate holding thick slices of crusty, artisanal bread. A cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the stew's comforting warmth and robust colors. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a well-proportioned single serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread (pan rústico) for dipping into the rich sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Pair with a glass of Spanish red wine, such as Tempranillo.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 3-4 cm chunks. Season pork generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove pork from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and sweet paprika to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, stirring constantly.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return seared pork to the pot. Ensure pork is mostly submerged. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until pork is very tender.
While stew simmers, trim green beans. Cut into 4-5 cm lengths. Cut broccoli into small florets.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch green beans for 2 minutes. Remove and shock in ice water. Blanch broccoli florets for 3 minutes. Remove and shock in ice water. Drain well.
Stir blanched green beans and broccoli into the stew during the last 10 minutes of cooking. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Fermented Potato & Root Vegetables
recipes.special_requests: Main dish potato with chicken and vegetables cuisine
recipes.visual_description: A single braised chicken thigh, skin golden-brown and rendered, rests off-center on a smooth, cream-colored handcrafted ceramic plate. The chicken is presented whole. A small cluster of rustic, braised root vegetable chunks (orange carrots, pale parsnips) are arranged beside it. A few firm, pale yellow fermented potato cubes are scattered nearby. A modest pool of rich, dark brown beer reduction sauce gathers beneath. The plating emphasizes clean lines and ample white space, highlighting natural ingredient beauty. A single fresh thyme sprig garnishes. The setup features a light, textured wooden surface, an undyed beige linen napkin, and soft, natural lighting. The background is minimalist, with a hint of greenery. The overall impression is sustainable elegance and ingredient purity.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (waxy, e.g., Yukon Gold), peeled, cut into 3cm chunks
Small potatoes, unpeeled, cut into 1.5cm cubes for fermentation

instructions: Prepare fermented potatoes: Dissolve 5g salt in 200ml water. Place 150g 1.5cm potato cubes in a clean jar. Pour brine over potatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until slightly tangy. Store in refrigerator.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add potato chunks, carrot chunks, parsnip chunks, and smashed garlic to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until lightly browned. Season with salt and pepper.
Deglaze pot with dark beer, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Add chicken stock, thyme sprigs, and rosemary sprigs to the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged. Cover pot with lid.
Braise in the preheated oven for 45-50 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender.
Remove pot from oven. Take out chicken thighs. Keep warm. Remove thyme and rosemary sprigs.
Reduce liquid on stovetop over medium-high heat for 5-7 minutes until slightly thickened. Skim any excess fat.
To serve, place a chicken thigh on each plate. Arrange braised vegetables and a few fermented potato cubes alongside. Spoon a small amount of the reduced sauce over the chicken and vegetables.
notes: The fermented potatoes add a subtle tang and probiotic benefit. Adjust fermentation time to your preferred sourness.
Use seasonal root vegetables available in your region to enhance sustainability.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Chili Braised Chicken with Crispy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Smoky Chili Braised Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A plump, golden-brown braised chicken thigh, with its skin rendered crispy and meat tender, sits centrally. It is generously coated in a rich, glossy, deep reddish-brown braising sauce. The sauce is thick enough to cling to the chicken and pools slightly at the base of the plate, revealing subtle flecks of diced red chili and onion. Arranged artfully alongside the chicken are several thick, golden-brown crispy potato wedges, their irregular shapes adding an organic feel. The potatoes exhibit a textural contrast with their crisp exteriors and soft interiors. A sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley is scattered over the chicken and sauce, providing a pop of color and freshness. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat 30ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot; set aside.

Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and finely diced fresh red chili (remove seeds for less heat), cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in smoked paprika, cumin, and oregano. Cook 1 minute.
Deglaze pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Stir in diced tomatoes and beef stock. Add bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.

Return seared chicken to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Cover and transfer to preheated oven at 170°C (340°F). Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken braises, prepare potatoes. Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Cut potatoes into thick wedges. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 30-40 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and crispy.
Remove braised chicken from oven. Carefully remove chicken to a plate. Discard bay leaf.
If sauce is too thin, simmer sauce on stovetop over medium-high heat until slightly reduced and thickened to desired consistency. Adjust seasoning.
To serve, place a chicken thigh on each plate. Spoon generous amount of braising sauce over chicken. Arrange crispy potato wedges alongside. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Uzbek Beef Plov
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow ceramic platter holds a mountain of glistening, golden-hued long-grain rice. Large, tender 3cm chunks of seared beef are nestled on top and throughout the rice, never sliced. Vibrant orange julienned carrots and translucent caramelized onions are evenly distributed among the grains. A whole head of roasted garlic with charred skin sits prominently in the center. The rice appears fluffy and separate, lightly coated in aromatic oil. The platter rests on a traditional Ikat-patterned textile over a rustic wooden table. A small side dish of thinly sliced tomatoes and onions sits nearby. Soft, natural side-lighting highlights the succulent texture of the beef and the distinct individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Achichuk (tomato and onion salad)
Accompany with hot green tea
Serve with fresh Uzbek non bread
Present on a communal 'Lagan' ceramic platter
instructions: Rinse rice in cold water until the water runs clear.
Soak rice in warm salted water for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed cast iron pot over high heat.
Brown beef chunks in batches until a dark crust forms.
Add onions to the pot. Fry until dark golden brown.
Stir in carrots. Cook 10 minutes until softened.
Pour in 500ml boiling water. Add cumin and salt.
Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes to create the zirvak base.
Drain rice. Spread rice in an even layer over the meat and vegetables.
Pour boiling water over a slotted spoon to cover rice by 1.5cm.
Boil on high heat until water disappears from the surface.
Push the whole garlic head into the center of the rice.
Poke five holes through the rice to the bottom using a spoon handle.
Cover pot with a tight lid. Reduce heat to the lowest setting.
Steam for 20 minutes.
Remove garlic. Mix rice and meat gently. Serve immediately.
notes: Do not stir the rice into the meat until the final steaming is complete.
The color of the plov depends on how dark you fry the onions.
Ensure the beef chunks are at least 3cm to maintain juiciness during the long cook.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Broccoli Rabe, Smoked Provolone, and Artichoke
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Orecchiette with Broccoli Rabe and Smoked Provolone is presented centrally on a round, matte white porcelain dinner plate. The al dente orecchiette is tossed with vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli rabe cut into 2-3 cm pieces, wilted spinach, and quartered artichoke hearts. Small, irregular cubes of creamy, melted smoked provolone cheese are integrated throughout, creating a subtle, cohesive sauce. The dish showcases a natural, organic arrangement. A light sheen of olive oil enhances the fresh appearance. Colors are primarily deep greens and creamy whites, with pale yellow artichoke. Moderate negative space highlights texture and freshness. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table, with a folded white cotton napkin and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its rustic yet refined appeal. No sliced or fanned meat is present. The focus is on the integrated pasta and vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot, optionally with a drizzle of fresh extra virgin olive oil and freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese.

ingredients.name: Freshly grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese (for serving)

instructions: Prepare broccoli rabe: Trim tough ends. Blanch in salted boiling water for 2-3 minutes. Drain well and immediately plunge into ice bath. Squeeze out excess water. Roughly chop into 2-3 cm pieces.
Cook pasta: Cook orecchiette in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta water before draining.

Sauté aromatics: While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add thinly sliced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute. Do not brown garlic.
Add vegetables: Add chopped broccoli rabe to the skillet. Sauté for 3-4 minutes. Add quartered artichoke hearts and fresh spinach. Sauté until spinach wilts, about 2 minutes.

Combine and finish: Add cooked, drained orecchiette to the skillet. Pour in vegetable broth (or reserved pasta water). Add diced or shredded smoked provolone. Toss well to combine. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until cheese melts and forms a light sauce. Add more pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Season: Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve: Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure broccoli rabe is thoroughly drained after blanching to prevent a watery sauce. Adjust pasta water addition for desired sauce consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Tomato Pasta is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm cream tone, centered on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The pasta, a generous nest of al dente rigatoni, is coated in a vibrant, rustic red fermented tomato sauce. Nestled alongside the pasta are two substantial, golden-brown pan-seared chicken chunks, showing a crisp exterior. Scattered around are bright green, roughly chopped wilted seasonal greens and a few glistening, thinly sliced pickled carrot batons, adding a contrasting texture and color. A scattering of fresh, torn basil leaves provides a final aromatic garnish. The composition is clean and natural, with ample negative space. The setting is minimalist with an undyed linen napkin, illuminated by soft, natural overhead light, enhancing the dish's organic beauty.

ingredients.name: Vegetable scraps (e.g., carrot ends, zucchini trimmings) for pickling

instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomatoes: Roughly chop 500g ripe tomatoes. Place in a clean glass jar. Add 20g non-iodized salt. Cover with 500ml filtered water. Seal jar loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily. Refrigerate once fermented.

Prepare Pickled Vegetable Scraps: Thinly slice 100g vegetable scraps (e.g., carrot ends into batons, zucchini trimmings into rounds). In a small saucepan, combine 100ml red wine vinegar, 5g sugar, and 100ml water. Bring to a simmer until sugar dissolves. Pour hot brine over vegetable scraps in a heatproof jar. Cool completely. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and black pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 6-8 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from pan, rest for 5 minutes. Cut each breast into 2-3 substantial chunks.

Prepare Sauce: While chicken rests, finely dice the onion. Mince garlic cloves. In the same pan with residual chicken drippings, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Sauté onion until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the fermented tomatoes and their liquid. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes, crushing tomatoes with a spoon, until sauce thickens slightly.
Cook Pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta and cook according to package instructions until al dente.

Combine: Roughly chop seasonal greens. Add greens to the tomato sauce; cook until just wilted, about 2-3 minutes. Drain pasta, reserving 60ml pasta water. Add drained pasta to the sauce. Add reserved pasta water if needed to achieve a desired consistency. Toss well to coat.
Serve: Divide pasta among 4 plates. Arrange chicken chunks alongside the pasta. Scatter pickled vegetable scraps and fresh torn basil over the dish. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust fermentation time for tomatoes based on desired level of tanginess and ambient temperature. Longer fermentation yields more sourness.
Any sturdy vegetable scraps can be used for pickling, such as broccoli stems, radish tops, or bell pepper cores.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Mushroom and Arugula Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of vibrant green arugula forms the base on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. Dark, earthy roasted mushrooms, sliced 1 cm thick, are scattered generously over the greens, showing their caramelized edges. Bright red cherry tomato halves and thinly sliced red onion rings are interspersed. Shaved Parmesan curls are lightly scattered on top, catching the light. The dressing lightly coats the leaves. The arrangement is natural and casual, as if served at a family meal. The plate rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple, folded linen napkin is casually placed beside. Lighting is soft and warm, typical of a cozy kitchen. A small, rustic ceramic bowl with extra dressing or Parmesan shavings might be subtly in the background, enhancing the homely feel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the dressing.
A simple glass of water or a light Italian red wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss sliced mushrooms with 2 tablespoons olive oil, minced garlic, thyme, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.
Spread mushrooms in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and browned. Stir halfway through. Let cool slightly.
While mushrooms roast, prepare vinaigrette. Whisk 60 ml olive oil, balsamic vinegar, beer, Dijon mustard, maple syrup (if using), 1/4 teaspoon salt, and a pinch of pepper in a small bowl.
In a large salad bowl, combine arugula, sliced red onion, and halved cherry tomatoes.
Add slightly cooled roasted mushrooms to the salad bowl.
Pour vinaigrette over salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat.
Top with shaved Parmesan cheese just before serving.
notes: This salad is hearty enough to be a light meal.
Adjust dressing to your taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Seasonal Zero-Waste Pasta Broth
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of clear, golden broth soup is presented in a smooth, handcrafted ceramic bowl in a soft cream tone. Small pasta shapes and finely diced vegetables like vibrant orange carrot, pale green celery, and translucent leek slices are suspended in the broth. Thin, earthy mushroom slices add depth. The surface is adorned with naturally scattered vibrant green chopped fresh herbs and thin slivers of spring onion greens. The composition is clean and minimalistic, allowing ample negative space around the bowl. The setting is a light, natural wood table surface, with a simple, undyed linen napkin folded beside the bowl. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the natural colors and textures of the ingredients. The background is clean and slightly blurred, with a hint of natural greenery.

ingredients.name: Vegetable scraps (carrot peels, onion skins, celery ends, mushroom stems, herb stems, leek greens)
Leek, white and light green parts, thinly sliced
Fresh herb leaves (e.g., parsley, chives), chopped

instructions: Combine vegetable scraps, water, salt, and peppercorns in a large pot.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer for 45 minutes.
Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.
Return strained broth to the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Add diced carrot, celery, leek, and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in lacto-fermented vegetable brine and finely diced fermented vegetables. Heat through gently for 1 minute. Do not boil.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with chopped fresh herb leaves and thinly sliced spring onion greens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Ragu with Orange and Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Braised Beef Ragu with Pappardelle is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The pappardelle, thick and flat, is coated richly in the deep reddish-brown ragu. Tender, irregular chunks of braised beef, ranging from small shredded pieces to larger, rustic 2-3 cm chunks, are visibly integrated throughout the pasta, showcasing their fork-tender texture. The ragu itself has a slightly glossy sheen, indicative of a well-reduced sauce, with flecks of finely diced carrots and celery visible. A scattering of bright orange zest provides a subtle pop of color and freshness. The dish is topped with a generous sprinkle of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese, adding a contrasting texture and color. The composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space around the pasta. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware (fork and spoon). Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the rich colors and inviting textures of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the ragu.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a robust red wine, such as a Chianti or Barolo.

ingredients.name: Boneless beef chuck or short ribs

instructions: Pat beef dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer. Cover and transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F).
Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef from pot. Shred or break into large chunks using two forks. Discard herbs and bay leaf.
Return shredded beef to the ragu. Simmer on stovetop for 15-20 minutes to thicken.
Grate zest of one orange into the ragu. Squeeze 15ml orange juice into the ragu. Stir well.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions in salted water until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly.
Serve immediately. Garnish with grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: For richer flavor, brown the beef well before adding vegetables.
Adjust consistency of ragu by simmering longer if too thin, or adding a splash of pasta water if too thick.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Calabrian Chicken Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Spicy Calabrian Chicken Rigatoni is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centered with a slight mound. Al dente rigatoni pasta, coated in a vibrant, rustic red tomato sauce, is loosely arranged. Scattered throughout are golden-brown, seared chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm. The sauce has a rich, slightly textured consistency, with visible flecks of minced garlic and diced onion. Fresh, roughly torn basil leaves provide bright green accents against the deep red and golden hues. A generous dusting of grated Parmigiano Reggiano tops the dish, adding a light, creamy texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown and cooked through, approximately 6-8 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pan. Add finely diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened, creating a soffritto base.
Stir in Calabrian chili paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan. Add crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer sauce for 15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water before draining.
Add cooked chicken chunks to the sauce. Simmer for 2 minutes to heat through.
Add drained rigatoni to the sauce. Add grated Parmigiano Reggiano and roughly torn basil. Toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water until desired consistency is reached.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust the amount of Calabrian chili paste to suit your preferred spice level.
Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C internal temperature for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Braisé aux Légumes Racines
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of braised chicken is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, a golden-brown, tender piece, rests beside a mix of earthy-toned root vegetables. Thick chunks of vibrant orange carrots are arranged naturally alongside substantial potato wedges, their skins slightly browned and interiors soft. A rich, glossy, dark amber braising sauce pools around the chicken and vegetables, reflecting the light. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green parsley is scattered over the dish, providing a bright color contrast. The plate is set on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. Beside the plate, a neatly folded crisp white cotton napkin is placed. Standard polished silver flatware (fork and knife) are arranged beside the plate. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual, inviting bistro atmosphere with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette for dipping in the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad with vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add carrot chunks and potato wedges. Sauté for 3-5 minutes.
Deglaze the pot with white wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Return chicken to the pot. Pour in chicken stock. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove chicken and vegetables from pot. Keep warm.

If desired, reduce the sauce over medium-high heat until slightly thickened. For a thicker sauce, whisk 1 tablespoon of flour with a little cold water to form a slurry, then whisk into the simmering sauce and cook for 2 minutes. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve chicken and vegetables on individual plates, spooning generous amount of sauce over. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The sauce can be strained for a smoother consistency if desired, but leaving it rustic is also authentic.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Macaroni with Roasted Tomato Garlic Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Chicken and Macaroni with Roasted Tomato Garlic Sauce is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Tender, seared golden-brown chicken chunks are interspersed among al dente macaroni pasta, all coated in a rich, rustic red sauce. The sauce features softened, slightly mashed roasted cherry tomatoes and hints of caramelized garlic. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered over the top, adding a vibrant color contrast. The dish has a natural, flowing arrangement, avoiding rigid symmetry. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere. The background is subtly blurred, maintaining focus on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty artisan bread for dipping the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad with a vinaigrette dressing.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss halved cherry tomatoes and 6 peeled garlic cloves with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.

Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the same pan. Add diced onion and remaining 2 peeled garlic cloves, minced. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add roasted tomatoes and garlic to the pan. Mash slightly with a spoon. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Meanwhile, cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Return seared chicken to the sauce. Add cooked macaroni. Toss gently to coat all ingredients in the sauce.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil.
notes: Using good quality, ripe tomatoes will significantly enhance the flavor of the sauce.
Do not overcook the macaroni; it should retain a slight bite.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Paprika and Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of rich, deep amber braised beef with paprika, presented in a clean white porcelain bowl. Tender, dark brown 3 cm beef cubes are nestled among vibrant red bell pepper 2 cm dice, quartered cremini mushrooms, and soft 2 cm potato cubes, all coated in a glossy, thick reddish-brown sauce. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast. The dish is centered on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a clean white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the stew's hearty texture and comforting warmth. The composition is professional yet inviting, with moderate negative space. A small side bowl of white sour cream is placed beside the main bowl for traditional accompaniment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of sour cream (tejföl)
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping

ingredients.name: Beef Chuck
ingredients.quantity: 800 g, trimmed, cut into 3 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 400 g, peeled, cut into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Heat olive oil in large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef cubes in batches until well browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onions to pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in sweet paprika, smoked paprika, and crushed caraway seeds. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Return beef to pot. Add crushed tomatoes, red bell pepper dice, quartered mushrooms, bay leaf, and beef stock.
Bring mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add potato cubes to the pot. Continue simmering, covered, for another 30-45 minutes, or until beef and potatoes are very tender.
Remove bay leaf. Season generously with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot braised beef into individual serving bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Tabaka with Garlic Butter
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of crispy, golden-brown Chicken Tabaka rests on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The chicken, comprising a succulent leg-thigh quarter and a breast piece, is seared to perfection with visible charring and a glossy, taut skin. A small pool of shimmering garlic-herb butter sauce gathers around the chicken. Fresh, vibrant green dill sprigs are casually scattered over the dish, with a bright lemon wedge placed beside the chicken, ready to be squeezed. The plate, intentionally leaving moderate negative space, sits on a rustic wooden table. A traditional Russian-style fork and knife are placed beside the plate. A small ceramic bowl of creamy smetana and a few bright green pickled cucumbers accompany the dish, enhancing the authentic casual dining atmosphere under soft, natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with smetana (sour cream) on the side.
Accompany with pickled cucumbers or tomatoes.
Traditionally served with a simple potato side dish or fresh bread.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Spatchcock the chicken by removing the backbone. Flatten it. Pat chicken thoroughly dry with paper towels.
Combine salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika. Rub mixture generously all over the chicken, front and back.
Melt butter in a small saucepan. Mince garlic. Finely chop dill and parsley. Add minced garlic, chopped dill, and parsley to melted butter. Stir well.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet (cast iron preferred) over medium-high heat.
Place chicken, skin-side down, in the hot skillet. Place a heavy weight (like another pan or foil-wrapped brick) on top of the chicken to press it flat.
Sear for 15-20 minutes until the skin is golden brown and crispy.
Flip chicken. Continue cooking with the weight for another 10-15 minutes.
Generously baste the chicken with the garlic-herb butter mixture.
Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the thickest part of the thigh reaches 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest on a cutting board for 10 minutes.
Cut chicken into 4 serving pieces (e.g., breast halves, leg-thigh quarters). Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Using a cast iron skillet provides the best crispy skin and even cooking.
The heavy weight is crucial for achieving the signature flattened, crispy chicken.
traditional_techniques: Pan-pressing (using a heavy weight to flatten and crisp chicken)

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Sausage and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted Italian sausage and potatoes is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The scene is a homely family kitchen, with warm light from above. Two plump, browned sausages rest amidst a generous pile of golden-brown roasted potato cubes, tender caramelized red onion wedges, and vibrant roasted bell pepper squares (red and green). The potatoes have slightly crispy edges, and the vegetables show tender, cooked textures. A few fresh, chopped parsley leaves are scattered over the dish for a pop of green. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually placed cloth napkin and a standard fork and knife beside it, creating a relaxed, inviting atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the pan juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut potatoes into 2.5 cm cubes. Slice onions into thick wedges. Cut bell peppers into 2.5 cm squares. Mince garlic.
Place potatoes, onions, and bell peppers on a large baking sheet. Add olive oil, salt, pepper, minced garlic, and rosemary sprigs. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange sausages among the vegetables on the baking sheet.
Roast for 30 minutes. Flip sausages and stir vegetables.
Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes. Cook until sausages are browned and cooked through. Potatoes should be tender and golden. Internal temperature of pork sausage must reach 71°C.
Remove rosemary sprigs. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve hot directly from the baking sheet or transfer to a large serving platter.
notes: Adjust spice level by choosing mild or spicy Italian sausages.
For easier cleanup, line the baking sheet with parchment paper.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, roasted chicken thigh, skin-on and bone-in, rests centrally on a modest, round ceramic plate. The chicken skin is deeply golden and visibly crisp, showing slight char marks. Surrounding the chicken is an abundant, casual arrangement of roasted root vegetables: chunky, tender potatoes with slightly browned edges, vibrant orange carrot chunks, and soft, caramelized onion wedges. The vegetables are rustic-cut and naturally piled, displaying their varied textures and earthy tones. A scattering of fresh, chopped green parsley provides a functional, bright garnish over the dish. The plate is positioned on a warm, well-worn wooden dining table, with a simple, folded cloth napkin and standard flatware nearby. The scene is bathed in soft, inviting kitchen light, evoking a comforting, lived-in family atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 300g, peeled and cut into 2-3 cm chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with half of the salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine potato chunks, carrot chunks, and onion wedges.
