Drizzle vegetables with olive oil. Add remaining salt, pepper, rosemary, thyme, and garlic powder. Toss to coat evenly.
Spread seasoned vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Place chicken thighs skin-side up on top of the vegetables on the same tray.
Roast for 35-45 minutes. Chicken skin should be crispy and golden. Vegetables should be tender and lightly caramelized.
Check internal temperature of chicken. It must reach 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, matte-finished ceramic bowl on a dark wood table. The base is a vibrant, reddish-orange long-grain rice, cooked to a moist, free-flowing consistency. Two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs with crispy skin rest atop the rice. The chicken is not sliced. Accompanying the chicken are charred tomato wedges and small cubes of sautéed onion mixed within the grains. Garnishes include fresh, bright green cilantro leaves and thin wedges of lime placed on the side. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textural contrast between the crispy chicken skin and the soft rice. A linen napkin and a heavy silver fork sit beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Provide extra lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with pickled red onions
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from guajillo and arbol chilies.
Toast chilies in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Soak toasted chilies in 200ml hot water for 10 minutes.
Blend soaked chilies, tomatoes, half the onion, and garlic until smooth.
Pat chicken dry and season with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes then remove from pot.
Add rice and remaining onion to the pot.
Toast rice for 3 minutes until opaque and slightly golden.
Pour blended chili-tomato mixture into the rice.
Cook for 5 minutes while stirring until sauce thickens.
Add chicken stock and return chicken to the pot.
Reduce heat to low and cover with a tight lid.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat and let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs to ensure the meat remains juicy during simmering
Do not over-toast the dried chilies as they can turn bitter
The rice should be moist and flavorful, absorbing all the chili-tomato broth

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Fermented Rice and Pickled Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted chicken and brown rice is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone, centered with ample white space. A fluffy mound of perfectly cooked brown rice forms the base. Two thick, rustic pieces of pan-seared chicken thigh, boasting crispy, golden-brown skin, are placed artfully beside the rice. Vibrant green seasonal vegetables, such as blanched broccoli florets or sautéed kale, are arranged naturally alongside the chicken. Bright, translucent slivers of pickled red onion are scattered over the chicken and rice, adding a contrasting pop of color and a tangy, fermented element. The dish is garnished simply with a few fresh parsley leaves or finely chopped chives. The setting features a light reclaimed wood table, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, natural lighting with a clean, minimalist background.

ingredients.name: Chicken or vegetable stock (made from scraps)
Seasonal green vegetables (e.g., kale, broccoli florets)

instructions: Prepare pickled red onions: Thinly slice the red onion. In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat. Place sliced onions in a heatproof jar or bowl. Pour the hot pickling liquid over the onions. Let cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or until ready to serve.

Cook the brown rice: Rinse the brown rice thoroughly under cold water. In a medium pot with a tight-fitting lid, combine the rinsed rice and chicken or vegetable stock. Bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Cook the chicken: Pat chicken thighs very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides. Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes, pressing gently, until the skin is deeply golden brown and crispy. Flip the chicken. If the skillet is oven-safe, transfer to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F) and cook for 10-15 minutes, or until an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) is reached. Alternatively, continue cooking on the stovetop over medium heat for another 10-15 minutes, ensuring it reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Prepare seasonal greens: While chicken rests, quickly blanch or sauté the seasonal green vegetables until tender-crisp. Season with a pinch of salt.

Plate the dish: Place a generous mound of fluffy brown rice slightly off-center on each plate. Slice each rested chicken thigh into 2-3 thick, rustic pieces. Arrange the chicken pieces next to the rice. Place the cooked green vegetables alongside. Drain the pickled red onions and scatter a spoonful over the chicken and rice. Garnish with fresh parsley leaves or finely chopped chives. Serve immediately.
notes: This dish prioritizes seasonal ingredients and zero-waste cooking. Chicken bones and vegetable scraps can be used for future stocks.
The pickled onions offer a fermented element and can be prepared in advance, improving flavor over time.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Potato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rustic beef and potato stew is presented in a deep, earthenware bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The stew features generous chunks of tender, dark brown beef, nestled among soft, golden-yellow potato cubes, vibrant orange carrot rounds, and earthy brown quartered mushrooms. A rich, thick reddish-brown gravy coats all ingredients, with visible flecks of dried herbs. A light scattering of fresh green chopped parsley brightens the top. The stew has a comforting, slightly irregular texture, reflecting home cooking. The bowl sits on a simple ceramic plate. A linen napkin and a sturdy spoon are casually placed beside it. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread.
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add chopped onion and carrots to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and flour. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually stir in beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Add diced tomatoes and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add potato cubes and quartered mushrooms. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 30-40 minutes, or until beef and potatoes are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Potato & Fromage Blanc Mousse with Berry Preserve
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the Sustainable Potato & Fromage Blanc Mousse is elegantly presented in a clear, footed glass tumbler, showcasing its layered textures and colors. The base is a creamy, pale ivory potato and fromage blanc mousse, appearing light and airy with a smooth texture. Spooned generously over the mousse is a vibrant, deep purple-red fermented berry preserve, glistening slightly and showing hints of mashed fruit. A few delicate, golden-brown candied potato peels are artfully placed on top, providing a subtle contrast and a hint of crispness. The glass tumbler sits on a natural, light-colored reclaimed wood table surface. The background is clean and minimalist, allowing the dish to be the focal point, with soft, natural lighting illuminating the scene. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed nearby, enhancing the eco-conscious aesthetic. The entire composition emphasizes purity, natural beauty, and a minimalistic, sustainable approach to dessert presentation.
instructions: Prepare candied potato peel: Thoroughly wash potatoes. Peel thinly. In a small saucepan, combine 100ml water, 50ml maple syrup, and 5ml lemon juice. Bring to a simmer. Add potato peels. Simmer gently for 10-15 minutes until peels are translucent. Remove peels with tongs. Arrange on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake at 120°C (250°F) for 30-45 minutes until crisp. Alternatively, use a dehydrator. Let cool completely.

Prepare fermented berry preserve: In a clean jar, combine mixed berries, 20ml maple syrup, and 20ml water. Stir gently. Cover jar loosely with a lid or cloth. Let stand at room temperature (20-24°C / 68-75°F) for 2-3 days. Check daily for small bubbles and a slightly tangy aroma. Mash berries lightly with a fork. Store in the refrigerator.

Prepare potato & fromage blanc mousse: Peel and cut potatoes into small, even chunks. Steam or boil potatoes until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Pass the hot potatoes through a ricer or mash very thoroughly until completely smooth. Ensure no lumps remain. In a large bowl, combine riced potato, fromage blanc, remaining 50ml maple syrup, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt. Mix until well combined. In a separate chilled bowl, whip the heavy cream until soft peaks form. Gently fold the whipped cream into the potato mixture until just combined and airy. Do not overmix.

Assemble and chill: Spoon the potato & fromage blanc mousse into four individual clear glass tumblers or small ceramic bowls. Top each serving with a generous spoonful of the fermented berry preserve. Garnish with a few pieces of candied potato peel. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour before serving to allow flavors to meld and the mousse to set.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, charred chunks of succulent chicken submerged in a glossy, vibrant orange-red tomato gravy. The sauce has a thick, velvety texture with visible flecks of ground spices. The chicken chunks show dark, caramelized edges from the high-heat roasting. Plating is in a clean, white porcelain bowl set on a dark wooden table. A single portion is shown with a light swirl of heavy cream on top and a scattering of bright green chopped cilantro. To the side sits a stack of warm, charred garlic naan bread and a small bowl of steamed long-grain basmati rice. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the rich colors and creamy consistency of the sauce while maintaining professional negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or buttered roti
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Side of mint-yogurt raita and kachumber salad
Serve in a traditional hammered copper karahi
instructions: Combine yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp chili powder.
Toss chicken chunks in marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 220°C. Place chicken on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Roast chicken 15 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté onions until golden brown.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in remaining garam masala, turmeric, and chili powder. Toast for 30 seconds.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens and oil separates.
Stir in butter and heavy cream. Season with salt.
Add roasted chicken chunks to the sauce. Simmer 2 minutes to combine flavors.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Kashmiri chili powder provides color without excessive heat.
Ensure the chicken is well-charred for authentic smoky flavor.
Let the sauce simmer until the oil separates to ensure spices are fully cooked.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mushroom and Herb Oatotto
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, inviting portion of creamy mushroom and herb oatotto is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The oatotto is a warm, earthy beige, generously studded with tender, sautéed cremini mushroom slices and vibrant green flecks of finely chopped fresh parsley and thyme. Its texture is rich and velvety, with the softened rolled oats visible, hinting at its comforting creaminess. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese tops the dish, and a small sprig of fresh parsley is placed casually on the side. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple, sturdy metal spoon. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, homely atmosphere. The background is minimally cluttered, showing hints of a lived-in kitchen.
instructions: Slice mushrooms. Dice onion. Mince garlic. Chop herbs.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large pot or deep skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until browned and tender, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and fresh thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rolled oats to the pot. Stir to coat oats with oil and aromatics. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in 250 ml of warm vegetable broth. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding remaining broth, 250 ml at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed. This takes about 20-25 minutes.
The oatotto should be creamy but still have a slight bite.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and chopped fresh parsley.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Feta and Shrimp Orzo
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Baked Feta and Shrimp Orzo rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed with ample negative space. The orzo pasta is visibly coated in a creamy, rustic sauce formed by roasted, partially burst cherry tomatoes, softened feta cheese, and plain Greek yogurt. Tender, plump pink shrimp, some whole, are interspersed throughout, along with vibrant julienned red bell pepper and thinly sliced red onion. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish exhibits a warm palette of reds, creams, and greens, with a slightly textured, inviting appearance. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and comforting appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread or pita bread for dipping.
Accompany with a simple green salad.
Pair with a crisp white Greek wine.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: 1/2 cup packed, plus extra for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place feta block in center of a large oven-safe baking dish.
Arrange cherry tomatoes, julienned red bell pepper, thinly sliced red onion, minced garlic, and sliced red chili around the feta.
Drizzle generously with olive oil. Sprinkle with dried oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Bake for 25-30 minutes. Tomatoes should burst, vegetables should be tender. Feta should be softened and slightly golden.
While baking, cook orzo according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving about 120ml pasta water.
Remove baking dish from oven. Add shrimp to the hot baking dish, tossing gently with the roasted vegetables and feta.
Return to oven for 5-7 minutes. Shrimp should be pink and cooked through. Do not overcook.

Remove from oven. Add Greek yogurt and fresh basil to the baking dish. Mash the feta and tomatoes with a fork. Stir well to create a creamy sauce, incorporating some reserved pasta water for desired consistency.
Add drained orzo to the baking dish. Toss everything together until well combined and coated.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust chili to your preferred spice level.
Ensure shrimp are not overcooked; they cook quickly in the hot dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A wide white porcelain pasta bowl sits on a light oak bistro table. A mound of broad pappardelle ribbons is thoroughly coated in a deep red, thick tomato sauce. Large, intact chunks of slow-braised beef are distributed throughout the pasta, showing a moist, tender texture. The sauce is glossy and emulsified, featuring visible flecks of minced garlic and finely diced vegetables. A light dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese is concentrated in the center. Three vibrant green whole basil leaves provide a fresh garnish. A heavy stainless steel fork and a white cotton napkin rest to the right. Natural side-lighting creates soft shadows, emphasizing the rich texture of the braised meat and the silky pasta surface.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread to mop up remaining sauce.
Pair with a glass of Chianti or Sangiovese wine.
Present in a shallow bowl to maintain sauce temperature.
instructions: Pat beef dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown beef chunks in batches. Remove and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape bottom of pot to release brown bits.
Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, and browned beef.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 2.5 hours until beef is tender.
Boil salted water. Cook pappardelle until al dente.
Drain pasta. Reserve 60ml of pasta water.
Toss pasta with ragu and reserved water until glossy.
Plate immediately. Top with cheese and basil.
notes: Do not shred the beef; maintain distinct chunks for texture.
Use high-quality canned tomatoes for authentic sweetness.
Ensure the pasta water is added to achieve a restaurant-quality silkiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Brined Chicken, Crispy Potato Cubes, Cultured Cheese Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Brined Chicken is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. The pan-seared chicken thigh, with its deeply golden, crispy skin, rests as a whole piece, unsliced. Alongside are irregular, golden-brown crispy potato cubes, showcasing their unpeeled texture. Scattered over and around the chicken and potatoes are pale, irregular pieces of cultured cheese crumble and rustic, toasted sourdough crumbs, adding textural contrast. Bright, thinly sliced quick-pickled radishes provide vibrant pops of red and a touch of freshness. A few fresh parsley leaves are scattered as a simple, natural garnish. The composition is minimalistic, with ample white space on the plate, highlighting the natural beauty of each ingredient. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, with soft, natural light illuminating the dish from above, creating subtle shadows. The background is clean and unfussy, with a hint of natural elements, maintaining a focus on the sustainable and ingredient-centric presentation.
instructions: Prepare chicken brine: Combine 1 liter water, 60g salt, 30g sugar, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a large bowl. Stir until salt and sugar dissolve. Add chicken thighs to the brine. Ensure chicken is fully submerged. Cover and refrigerate for 4-6 hours.
Remove chicken from brine. Pat chicken very dry with paper towels. Reserve chicken bones for stock if desired (zero-waste).
Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).

Prepare crispy potato cubes: Wash potatoes thoroughly. Do not peel. Cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway, until golden brown and crispy.

Prepare cultured cheese crumble: Grate Parmesan cheese. Spread grated cheese thinly on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 8-10 minutes until golden and crispy. Let cool completely. Break into small, irregular crumbles.
Prepare sourdough crumbs: Tear sourdough bread into small, rustic pieces. Toss with 5 ml olive oil. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake for 8-10 minutes until golden and crunchy. Set aside.
Prepare quick-pickled radishes: Wash and thinly slice radishes into rounds. Place in a small bowl. Add a pinch of salt. Let sit for 10 minutes. Drain any liquid. This is a quick lacto-fermentation.

Cook chicken: Heat remaining 10 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Add thyme sprigs to the skillet. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Rest chicken: Remove chicken from oven. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes before serving.

Assemble plates: Place a portion of crispy potato cubes on each plate. Arrange a chicken thigh alongside. Scatter cultured cheese crumble and sourdough crumbs over the chicken and potatoes. Garnish with quick-pickled radishes and fresh parsley leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chili Pineapple Ragù Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of rigatoni pasta tossed with a hearty ragù, mounded centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rich, deep red tomato-based sauce generously coats the ridged pasta. Browned beef and chicken mince are visible as small, irregular chunks throughout the sauce. Bright yellow, small diced pineapple cubes are interspersed, adding vibrant color and a hint of sweetness. Thinly sliced red chili pieces provide subtle pops of vivid red. The dish is garnished with fresh green, roughly torn basil leaves scattered over the top, enhancing the color contrast. Textures include tender pasta, hearty meat, juicy pineapple, and soft vegetables. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin positioned beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating soft shadows. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a modern bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
Offer grated Parmesan cheese as an optional topping.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add beef mince and chicken mince. Break apart with a spoon. Brown thoroughly. Drain any excess fat.
Add diced onion and finely sliced red chilies. Cook, stirring occasionally, until onion softens, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Add small diced pineapple. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While the ragù simmers, cook rigatoni pasta according to package directions. Cook until al dente. Drain well.
Season the ragù with salt and black pepper to taste.
Combine the cooked pasta with the ragù in the pot. Toss gently to coat all pasta.
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with fresh basil leaves. Offer grated Parmesan cheese on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Tomato Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, its skin a deep golden-brown, sits as the centerpiece on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The chicken is glazed with a vibrant, rustic red fermented tomato paste, showcasing its natural texture. Beside it, a small, artfully arranged cluster of bright green seasonal vegetables, such as blanched asparagus spears or crisp green beans, provides a fresh contrast. Scattered around the chicken are irregular shards of golden, crispy chicken skin, adding a textural element and demonstrating zero-waste practice. A clear, amber tomato consommé subtly pools around the chicken, reflecting the soft, natural light. The overall presentation is minimalist, with ample negative space. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a natural beige linen napkin.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato Glaze: Dice 400g tomatoes finely. Place in a clean jar with 10g sea salt, 5g thyme leaves, and 3g rosemary leaves. Stir well. Cover loosely. Let ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, stirring daily. Store refrigerated.
Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season all sides with remaining 5g sea salt and black pepper. Separate skin from meat carefully without detaching.

Sear Chicken Thighs: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crisp. Remove skin carefully and set aside.
Finish Chicken: Flip chicken thighs meat-side down. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.

Make Tomato Consommé: While chicken cooks, collect all remaining tomato trimmings (cores, seeds, skins from the 100g fresh tomatoes). Combine with chicken bones (if any) and 500ml water/vegetable stock in a saucepan. Simmer gently for 20 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Discard solids. Keep consommé warm.

Render Crispy Chicken Skin: While chicken rests, place reserved chicken skin in a separate dry skillet over medium-low heat. Cook slowly, pressing occasionally, until completely crisp and all fat is rendered. Drain on paper towel. Break into shards.
Cook Vegetables: Blanch or steam green vegetables until tender-crisp. Toss with remaining 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.

Glaze and Plate: Brush cooked chicken thighs generously with the fermented tomato glaze. Arrange one chicken thigh on each plate. Place a portion of green vegetables next to it. Garnish with crispy chicken skin shards and a few fresh thyme sprigs. Serve with a small pour of warm tomato consommé around the chicken or in a separate small jug.
notes: The fermented tomato glaze can be prepared up to 2 weeks in advance and stored refrigerated. Its flavor will deepen over time.
Adjust fermentation time based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.
This recipe prioritizes utilizing all parts of the ingredients, minimizing food waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Shiitake Mushroom Udon Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Shiitake Mushroom Udon Soup is presented in a clean, white ceramic bowl, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The clear, golden amber broth fills the bowl, showcasing the neatly arranged ingredients. Tender chicken breast medallions, 1 cm thick, are gracefully placed alongside dark brown, thinly sliced shiitake mushrooms. Bright green, thinly diagonally sliced spring onions are scattered over the top, providing a fresh contrast. A subtle sheen of sesame oil glistens on the broth's surface. The presentation is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space around the bowl. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the bowl on a light cotton napkin, completing the modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's vibrant colors and textures.
instructions: Rehydrate dried shiitake mushrooms in hot water for 20 minutes. Reserve the mushroom liquid. Slice the rehydrated mushrooms.
In a large pot, combine chicken stock, reserved shiitake liquid, sliced ginger, smashed garlic, and the white parts of spring onions. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add chicken breast to the simmering broth. Poach chicken gently for 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from broth.
Let chicken rest briefly. Slice chicken into 1 cm thick medallions. Set aside.
Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Return strained broth to the pot.
Stir soy sauce and mirin into the broth. Season with salt and white pepper to taste. Keep broth warm.
Cook udon noodles according to package instructions. Drain well.
Divide cooked udon noodles among four individual serving bowls. Arrange sliced chicken medallions and sliced shiitake mushrooms over the noodles.
Ladle hot broth over the ingredients in each bowl. Drizzle with sesame oil. Garnish generously with thinly sliced green parts of spring onions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora con Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora con Pappardelle is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The al dente pappardelle pasta forms a base, thoroughly coated in a rich, rustic reddish-brown tomato sauce. A tender, braised bone-in chicken thigh, with its skin a deep golden-brown, rests prominently on top of the pasta. The sauce is visibly chunky with softened, roughly chopped red bell pepper and green bell pepper, sliced cremini mushrooms, and diced soffritto vegetables (onion, carrot, celery). A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped flat-leaf parsley adds a pop of green, contrasting with the deep red sauce. Delicate, thin shavings of Parmigiano Reggiano are scattered over the dish, adding a light, creamy texture. The plating is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by traditional Italian flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. A small side dish holds a slice of crusty artisan bread, ready for dipping. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and colors in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the rich sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot (this is the soffritto). Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic, sliced mushrooms, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper. Cook for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften slightly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken braises, cook pappardelle according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente.
Remove bay leaf, rosemary, and thyme sprigs from the sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the pot with the chicken and sauce. Toss gently to coat.
Serve immediately in deep bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and shavings of Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Sausage, Rice, and Potato Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of One-Pan Sausage, Rice, and Potato Skillet is presented on an everyday ceramic plate. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Golden-brown seared sausage rounds are nestled among fluffy white rice and tender, soft yellow potato cubes. Diced, translucent sautéed onion and flecks of green dried oregano are visible throughout the dish. The components are naturally arranged, touching and slightly overlapping, creating a comforting, informal mound. The dish appears hearty and inviting. A casually placed cloth napkin and simple flatware accompany the plate. Warm, cozy natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the homely, lived-in atmosphere of a family kitchen.

ingredients.name: Pork sausage
ingredients.quantity: 150 g (1 large link), sliced into 2 cm thick rounds

ingredients.name: Potato
ingredients.quantity: 150 g (1 medium), peeled and diced into 1.5 cm cubes

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add sliced sausage rounds. Sear until browned on both sides. Remove sausage from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced potato and rice to the skillet. Stir to combine with onion and garlic.
Pour in chicken broth. Stir in dried oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Bring liquid to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet.
Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Return seared sausage to the skillet. Gently stir to combine.
Serve hot directly from the skillet or on a plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Apple Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A modest, single serving of Creamy Chicken and Apple Pasta is presented on a simple, rustic off-white ceramic plate. The penne pasta is generously coated in a creamy, light beige sauce, mixed with irregular 2 cm cubes of pan-seared golden-brown chicken and tender, small 1 cm cubes of sautéed apple. The components are naturally intertwined, showcasing the comforting textures. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a vibrant contrast and fresh aroma. The plate is casually centered on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. A casually folded, muted plaid cloth napkin rests beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the homely, satisfying nature of the dish. The background suggests a lived-in family kitchen, slightly out of focus, maintaining focus on the hearty meal.
instructions: Cook penne pasta according to package directions. Drain. Reserve 60 ml pasta water.
Cut chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add cubed chicken. Cook for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Dice onion into small pieces. Dice apple into 1 cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Add onion to the same skillet. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced apple. Cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly tender.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Simmer for 3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Add cooked pasta and cooked chicken back to the skillet. Toss to coat evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Fermented Broccoli Puree and Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Roasted Chicken with Fermented Broccoli Puree and Tomato Confit is presented on a large, round, handcrafted ceramic plate with a matte cream finish, resting on a light bamboo table surface. The central element is a whole, golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, skin-side up, positioned slightly off-center. Beside it, a generous, organic smear of vibrant green fermented broccoli puree provides a striking color contrast and fluid texture. Scattered around the plate are roasted broccoli florets, some exhibiting slight charring, showcasing their tender-crisp texture. A small cluster of glistening, ruby-red cherry tomato halves and a soft confit garlic clove are nestled near the chicken, adding pops of concentrated color. The plating is minimalistic and unforced, highlighting each ingredient's natural beauty. A few small, fresh parsley leaves are lightly scattered over the dish as a natural garnish. The setting includes an undyed linen napkin in natural beige and simple, rustic cutlery. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the dish from the side, casting gentle shadows. The background is clean and uncluttered, with subtle hints of natural elements, maintaining focus on the food while embodying an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Tomato Confit: Halve cherry tomatoes. Place in a small oven-safe dish. Add 4 crushed garlic cloves and 4 thyme sprigs. Cover tomatoes with 70 ml olive oil. Bake at 150°C for 45-60 minutes until tomatoes are very soft and slightly shriveled. Set aside.

Prepare Broccoli Florets: Cut broccoli florets into bite-sized pieces. Mince 2 garlic cloves. In a bowl, toss florets with minced garlic, 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast at 200°C for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.

Prepare Fermented Broccoli Puree: Ensure you have pre-fermented broccoli stems (see notes). Blend 150g of fermented broccoli stems until smooth. Add a splash of water or vegetable stock if needed to reach a fluid puree consistency. Season lightly with salt and pepper.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towel. Season generously on both sides with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deep golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken.

Finish Chicken: Transfer the skillet to the preheated 200°C oven. Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven and rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

Plate the Dish: On each plate, spread a generous smear or dollop of the vibrant green fermented broccoli puree. Place one whole roasted chicken thigh on top or slightly beside the puree. Arrange roasted broccoli florets around the chicken. Add a small cluster of the glistening tomato confit and a confit garlic clove to the plate. Garnish lightly with fresh parsley leaves or snipped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Mustard-Crusted Beef Medallions with Onion-Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single mustard-crusted beef medallion, seared to a deep golden-brown, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The beef, cut into a thick, round medallion, showcases a tender, medium-rare interior. Adjacent to the beef is a generous mound of slow-cooked onion-tomato confit, a rich medley of thinly sliced caramelized red and yellow onions intertwined with vibrant halved cherry tomatoes. The confit offers deep reddish-brown and bright red hues. A sprinkle of pale blue and white crumbled blue cheese adorns the top of the beef, adding textural contrast. The plate is arranged with moderate negative space, allowing each component to stand out. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate, and standard polished flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the food's textures. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Thinly slice red and yellow onions. Thinly slice garlic. Halve cherry tomatoes.

Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions, garlic, and thyme sprigs. Cook slowly for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until onions are very soft and caramelized.

Add halved cherry tomatoes, beef broth, and red wine vinegar to the pan. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until liquid reduces and tomatoes are tender. Season the onion-tomato confit with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Spread Dijon mustard evenly over all sides of each beef medallion.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil and butter in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until butter melts and foams.
Carefully place beef medallions in the hot skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until deeply browned and a crust forms.
Transfer the skillet with the beef to the preheated oven. Cook for 5-8 minutes for medium-rare (internal temperature 55-60°C). Adjust cooking time for desired doneness.
Remove skillet from oven. Transfer beef medallions to a cutting board. Let them rest for 5 minutes.
Crumble blue cheese into small pieces.
Place a generous portion of onion-tomato confit on each of four dinner plates.
Position one rested beef medallion next to the confit on each plate.
Sprinkle crumbled blue cheese evenly over each beef medallion.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni con Pancetta, Tonno e Pomodorini
recipes.visual_description: A generous single portion of Rigatoni con Pancetta, Tonno e Pomodorini is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain pasta bowl. The al dente rigatoni noodles are lightly coated in a glistening, emulsified sauce from olive oil and pasta water. Interspersed among the pasta are golden, crispy diced pancetta pieces and tender, flaky chunks of oil-packed tuna. Bright red halved cherry tomatoes, slightly softened and bursting, provide vibrant color and a touch of acidity. Thinly sliced garlic and a scattering of red pepper flakes are visible throughout the dish, adding subtle texture and visual interest. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green, freshly chopped Italian parsley is draped over the top, offering a fresh contrast. The composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish is centered in the bowl, showcasing the rich textures and colors. A silver fork rests elegantly beside the bowl on a light wooden table surface, with a simple white cotton napkin folded neatly. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the ingredients' freshness and the dish's warmth, set against a subtle, blurred restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a main course.
Offer additional grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table for individual preference.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.

ingredients.name: Canned tuna in olive oil, drained

instructions: Cook rigatoni in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced pancetta. Cook until crispy and golden. Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon; set aside. Leave rendered fat in the skillet.
Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes to the skillet. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Add halved cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes until slightly softened and beginning to burst.
If using, pour in white wine. Bring to a simmer and cook for 1 minute, scraping up any browned bits.
Add drained tuna to the skillet. Break up tuna gently with a spoon. Stir to combine with tomatoes and garlic.
Add the cooked rigatoni and reserved crispy pancetta to the skillet. Toss to combine.
Add 120-180 ml of reserved pasta water, a little at a time, tossing vigorously to create a light, emulsified sauce that coats the pasta.
Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Stir in most of the chopped fresh parsley. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining fresh parsley and optional grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
notes: Use high-quality canned tuna in olive oil for the best flavor and texture.
Adjust the amount of red pepper flakes to control the spice level.
The amount of pasta water needed may vary; add just enough to create a light sauce that coats the pasta without being soupy.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Baked Macaroni with Sausage and Crab
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy baked macaroni and cheese is presented in a clean white porcelain oval gratin dish, centrally placed on a simple, light-colored wooden table. The dish features a golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted cheese and crispy panko breadcrumbs. Beneath the crust, the rich, creamy pasta is visible, generously mixed with tender elbow macaroni, crumbled, browned sausage, vibrant yellow corn kernels, and substantial flakes of white lump crab meat. The sauce is thick and luscious, coating all ingredients evenly. A light sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley adds a touch of fresh color. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish's comforting textures and inviting colors. A folded white cotton napkin and a simple silver fork are neatly placed beside the dish. The background is softly blurred, maintaining focus on the food while suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Frozen corn kernels, thawed and drained
Lump crab meat, picked over for shells

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a 2.5-liter baking dish.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Set aside.
In a large skillet, cook sausage over medium heat. Break up with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Remove sausage from skillet. Set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Melt over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Whisk in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in warm milk until smooth. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens, about 5-7 minutes.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in grated cheddar cheese, cream cheese, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Stir until cheeses are melted and sauce is smooth.
Add cooked macaroni, cooked sausage, corn kernels, and crab meat to the cheese sauce. Stir gently to combine all ingredients.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish. Sprinkle panko breadcrumbs evenly over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and the topping is golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken and Tomato Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Chicken and Tomato Pappardelle is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple light wooden table. Tender, golden-brown braised chicken chunks are nestled among wide, al dente pappardelle ribbons, all generously coated in a rich, vibrant red San Marzano tomato sauce. The sauce has a rustic texture, flecked with small, soft diced bell peppers and onion. Fresh green basil leaves, some whole, some torn, are scattered over the top, providing a bright color contrast. Delicate, thin shavings of Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese are gracefully draped over the chicken and pasta. The overall composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. A silver fork rests beside the plate on a folded white cotton napkin. The scene is bathed in natural, even light, creating a professional yet approachable restaurant-style ambiance with a minimal, out-of-focus background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Canned whole peeled San Marzano tomatoes

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced yellow onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced red and green bell peppers. Cook for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits.
Crush canned San Marzano tomatoes by hand or with a spoon. Add them to the pan with chicken broth.
Bring sauce to a simmer. Return seared chicken thighs to the pan. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
While chicken simmers, cook pappardelle according to package directions until al dente.
Remove chicken from sauce. Shred or cut into large chunks. Return chicken to sauce.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pappardelle directly to the sauce. Toss to coat.
Stir in fresh basil leaves, torn. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, topped with freshly shaved Parmigiano-Reggiano.
notes: Using high-quality San Marzano tomatoes is crucial for the depth of flavor in the sauce.
The chicken can be braised ahead of time, then reheated gently and combined with freshly cooked pasta.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy chicken and mushroom pasta rests in a round, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown, 2 cm seared chicken cubes are nestled amongst the al dente pasta strands, which are thoroughly coated in a rich, pale cream sauce. Sliced, earthy brown mushrooms are interspersed throughout, adding depth. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley provides a pop of color on top. The dish is presented casually, as if just served from the stove, with the pasta naturally piled. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a plain cloth napkin, emphasizing the homely, unpretentious comfort of the meal.
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Pat chicken breast cut into 2 cm cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Add cooked chicken back to the pan with the sauce. Add drained pasta. Toss to coat everything evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo e Peperoni Arrostiti con Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo e Peperoni Arrostiti con Pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Al dente penne pasta is coated in a rich, creamy roasted red pepper and tomato sauce, displaying vibrant orange-red hues. Tender, golden-brown chicken breast chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, are interspersed and visible atop the pasta. The chicken pieces are whole, not sliced. Sliced roasted red pepper strips are mixed within. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the dish. Fresh green basil leaves are thoughtfully placed on top, providing a vibrant contrast. The dish has a natural, flowing arrangement with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light wooden table, standard silver flatware, and a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting creates a warm atmosphere with a blurred casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Halve and deseed red peppers. Place skin-side up on a baking sheet. Roast at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until skin blackens. Transfer to a bowl. Cover tightly. Let steam 10 minutes. Peel skins. Slice peppers into strips.
Bring a large pot of salted water to boil. Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Cut chicken breasts into 3-4 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (75°C internal temperature). Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to simmer. Cook 5 minutes, scraping up browned bits. Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 3 minutes.
Add roasted pepper strips to sauce. Return chicken chunks to skillet. Stir to coat.
Add drained pasta to skillet with sauce. Add reserved pasta water as needed for desired consistency. Toss to combine. Stir in grated Parmesan.
Garnish with fresh basil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of Hearty Beef and Vegetable Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The stew features tender, irregular chunks of browned beef, approximately 3-4 cm, nestled amongst soft, diced carrots (1.5 cm cubes) and creamy, diced potatoes (2 cm cubes). The rich, dark brown gravy, thickened slightly, coats all ingredients, with a gentle sheen from slow cooking. A few vibrant green, roughly chopped fresh parsley leaves are sprinkled over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The bowl sits on a well-worn, light wooden dining table. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a home kitchen. A simple, off-white linen napkin is casually folded beside the bowl. The overall presentation is homely, comforting, and unpretentious, reflecting a satisfying family meal.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 300g, peeled and diced into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 150g, peeled and diced into 1.5 cm cubes

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in beef broth, stirring to scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Return beef to the pot. Add bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5 hours, or until beef is tender.
Add diced potatoes and carrots to the pot. Stir well.
Cover and continue to cook for 30-40 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. The stew should be thick.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Chicken and Roasted Bell Pepper Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Lemon Herb Chicken and Roasted Bell Pepper Pasta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple light wooden table surface. Golden-brown chicken breast chunks, approximately 3cm, are interspersed with vibrant red and yellow bell pepper strips and halved bright red cherry tomatoes. The al dente penne pasta forms a cohesive base, lightly coated in a shimmering, savory sauce. Freshly chopped green parsley and dill are generously sprinkled over the entire dish, providing a verdant contrast. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits at the plate's edge. The composition is natural and flowing, avoiding rigid geometry, with ample negative space. A folded white cotton napkin and a silver fork are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh colors and varied textures, creating an inviting casual dining scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Serve with a light green salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut bell peppers into 2cm strips. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Place bell pepper strips and unpeeled garlic cloves on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender. Remove from oven.
Peel roasted garlic cloves. Mash into a paste.
While vegetables roast, cook pasta according to package directions. Drain pasta. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Cut chicken breasts into 3cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the pan. Cook for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Add roasted bell peppers, mashed garlic, cherry tomatoes, and chicken broth to the same pan. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Return cooked pasta and chicken chunks to the pan. Toss to combine all ingredients.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley, chopped fresh dill, and lemon juice. Add reserved pasta water if needed to achieve desired consistency.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Garlic Chicken with Jasmine Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Spicy Garlic Chicken with Jasmine Rice is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wood table surface. The dish features golden-brown, irregularly diced chicken pieces, coated in a glossy, savory sauce. Visible flecks of finely minced red chilies and garlic are interspersed among the chicken. Diagonally sliced, vibrant green beans add color and texture to the chicken mixture. The chicken is not fanned, appearing as substantial, seared chunks. Beside the main plate, a small, separate white porcelain rice bowl holds a mound of fluffy jasmine rice. Garnishes include a few fresh cilantro leaves scattered over the chicken and a lime wedge placed on the side of the plate. A small ceramic chopstick rest holds a pair of dark wooden chopsticks. A folded natural cotton napkin is placed to the side. A tiny ceramic dish containing 'Prik Nam Pla' (fish sauce with sliced chilies) sits near the rice bowl. The scene is illuminated by soft, even natural lighting, creating a casual bistro atmosphere with a minimalist background that highlights the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional fresh lime wedges.
Offer 'Prik Nam Pla' (fish sauce with sliced chilies) on the side for added spice and savory depth.
Accompany with fresh cucumber slices to balance the heat.
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Dice chicken thighs into 2 cm cubes. Pat dry.
Finely mince garlic cloves. Thinly slice red bird's eye chilies.
Trim green beans. Slice diagonally into 2 cm pieces.
In a small bowl, whisk together fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and water/stock. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or high-sided skillet over medium-high heat.
Add minced garlic and sliced chilies. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced chicken to the wok. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Add sliced green beans to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until crisp-tender.
Pour the prepared sauce mixture over the chicken and vegetables. Stir well to coat everything. Cook for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Remove from heat. Serve immediately with jasmine rice.
traditional_techniques: Balancing sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Fermented Tomato & Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Chicken with Fermented Tomato & Root Vegetables. A plump, golden-brown braised chicken thigh rests centrally in a handcrafted, earth-toned ceramic bowl. Surrounding the chicken are substantial, irregular chunks of tender, orange-hued carrots and pale yellow potatoes, softened but holding their shape. Dark green, wilted kale leaves are interspersed throughout the rich, reddish-brown sauce. The sauce is thick and rustic, with visible pieces of softened tomato and onion from the fermented base. A few fresh thyme leaves are scattered over the top as a simple garnish. The bowl sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded neatly beside the bowl. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from above, highlighting the textures and natural colors. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of green from a nearby plant, suggesting a connection to nature and sustainability.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown, about 5 minutes. Flip. Sear other side 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add fresh chopped onion to pot. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in pre-fermented chopped onion, fresh chopped tomatoes, pre-fermented chopped tomatoes, and cayenne pepper. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add carrots and potatoes. Stir to coat.
Pour in vegetable broth. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to pot. Nest them into the vegetables and liquid.
Cover. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 45-50 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and vegetables are tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Stir in chopped kale. Cook 5 minutes until wilted.
Taste. Adjust salt and pepper. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Salmon and Dill Frittata
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, puffed frittata wedge is centrally placed on a clean, white round porcelain dinner plate. The frittata has visible pockets of pale pink torn smoked salmon and creamy white crumbled cheese, contrasting with the dark green of roughly chopped spinach. The surface is lightly browned and slightly irregular, indicating a soft, custardy interior. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh dill covers the top, providing a fresh aromatic highlight. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene from the side, highlighting the frittata's texture. The background is softly blurred, showing hints of a casual restaurant atmosphere. No distracting elements.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Whisk eggs, cream, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Stir in half the chopped dill.
Melt butter in an oven-safe, non-stick 24 cm skillet over medium heat.
Add diced red onion. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add chopped spinach. Cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Pour egg mixture into the skillet.
Gently distribute torn smoked salmon pieces, crumbled cheese, and capers evenly over the egg mixture.
Cook on stovetop for 2-3 minutes until edges begin to set.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until frittata is set and golden brown. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with remaining fresh dill.
Slice into wedges. Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Shrimp and Roasted Pineapple Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white round porcelain plate, centrally placed. A generous portion of golden-hued spaghetti forms the base, loosely coiled. Plump, pink seared shrimp, cooked whole, are arranged naturally atop the pasta. Interspersed throughout are vibrant red halved cherry tomatoes and caramelized golden-brown roasted pineapple chunks, adding pops of color and texture. Thinly sliced, translucent red onion pieces are visible, adding depth. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a final fresh garnish. The dish is naturally illuminated, casting soft shadows, with a simple wooden table surface and a white cotton napkin beside the plate. A single fork rests to the right. The plate is not overcrowded, allowing for negative space.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss pineapple chunks with 15ml olive oil. Roast on a baking sheet for 15-20 minutes until caramelized.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, heat 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add sliced red onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and red chili flakes. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add shrimp to skillet. Cook 2-3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary.
Add halved cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Cook 3-4 minutes until slightly softened.
Add cooked pasta to the skillet. Add roasted pineapple.
Pour in 120ml vegetable broth or reserved pasta water. Toss well.
Add lemon juice, chopped fresh parsley, salt, and black pepper. Toss to combine.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Red Pepper Sauce and Vegetable Orzo
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and whole, rests slightly offset on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beneath it, a vibrant, smooth pool of roasted red pepper sauce provides a rich crimson base. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of al dente orzo pasta is presented, studded with small diced zucchini, yellow squash, and vibrant red cherry tomato halves. The dish showcases a balance of colors: the golden chicken, deep red sauce, light yellow orzo, and fresh greens and yellows from the vegetables. Fresh basil leaves are scattered over the orzo and chicken for a final aromatic touch. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin beside it, under natural, even lighting, creating a professional yet approachable bistro aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve red bell peppers. Remove seeds. Place cut-side down on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes until skin is blistered and charred.
Transfer roasted peppers to a bowl. Cover tightly with plastic wrap for 10 minutes. Peel off skins. Discard skins. Roughly chop peppers.
In a blender, combine roasted bell peppers, 1 crushed garlic clove, and 120ml vegetable broth. Blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Set sauce aside.
Finely dice half of the yellow onion. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Small dice the zucchini or yellow squash. Halve cherry tomatoes.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add orzo to the saucepan. Stir for 1 minute. Pour in remaining vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until orzo is al dente and most liquid is absorbed, about 10-12 minutes.
Stir in diced squash and halved cherry tomatoes during the last 3-4 minutes of orzo cooking. Remove from heat. Season orzo with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 45ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest for 5 minutes.

To plate, spoon a pool of roasted red pepper sauce onto the center of each plate. Place one whole pan-seared chicken breast on top or slightly beside the sauce. Neatly mound a portion of the vegetable orzo next to the chicken.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Lemon Herb Chicken and Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty One-Pan Lemon Herb Chicken and Roasted Vegetables is presented on an everyday round ceramic plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh rests prominently on a bed of tender, caramelized roasted vegetables. The vegetables include rustic chunks of potato, bright orange carrot pieces, and softened red onion wedges, all showing slight charring. Smashed garlic cloves and wilted fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs are interspersed. A few vibrant yellow lemon slices are tucked alongside the chicken, hinting at the dish's bright flavor. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen. Soft, warm lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and natural colors. A simple cloth napkin is casually placed nearby.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
In a large roasting pan, combine potato chunks, carrot chunks, red onion wedges, and smashed garlic cloves.
Drizzle vegetables with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Place seasoned chicken thighs skin-side up among the vegetables in the roasting pan.
Arrange lemon slices, rosemary, and thyme sprigs around chicken and vegetables.
Drizzle remaining 30ml olive oil over chicken and vegetables.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and skin is golden and crispy. Vegetables should be tender and caramelized.
Remove from oven. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the entire dish before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of homestyle roasted chicken and potatoes rests on a simple, round ceramic plate. Two golden-brown roasted chicken drumsticks, their skin crisped and glistening, are placed naturally on the plate. Alongside, a heap of rustic, thick-cut potato wedges, their exteriors a mix of golden and deeper brown with some crispy edges, spill casually. Interspersed are soft, caramelized onion wedges and flecks of green from fresh rosemary. The arrangement is organic and unpretentious, reflecting a true home-cooked meal. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen. Simple, everyday flatware is present, suggesting a family meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Season generously with half the salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes thoroughly. Cut potatoes into thick 2-3 cm wedges or large chunks. Leave skin on.
In a large roasting pan, combine potato wedges and onion wedges. Add olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, paprika, remaining salt, and pepper. Toss until vegetables are evenly coated.
Add seasoned chicken pieces to the roasting pan with the potatoes and onions. Arrange in a single layer, ensuring chicken skin is facing up.
Roast for 45-55 minutes. Flip potatoes halfway through cooking for even browning.
Chicken is cooked when internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and juices run clear. Potatoes should be tender inside and golden brown and crispy outside.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Saffron Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Saffron Rice is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-yellow bomba rice, infused with saffron, is mounded slightly in the center, appearing moist and flavorful, not dry. Scattered throughout the rice are vibrant orange diced carrots and bright green peas. Nestled naturally within and on top of the rice are golden-brown, tender chunks of boneless chicken thigh, showcasing their seared exterior. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of green and freshness. A lemon wedge rests on the side of the plate, ready for squeezing. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a soft, casual restaurant-style background that remains unobtrusive.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide pan or shallow pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan and set aside. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Add diced onion and carrots to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced.
Add bomba rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the rice.
Pour in hot chicken broth. Add saffron threads. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan, nestling it into the rice. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan tightly. Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice has absorbed most of the liquid and is tender. Do not stir frequently.
Stir in frozen peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Remove pan from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Vegetable Frittata
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown Hearty Vegetable Frittata sits as the centerpiece on a well-used wooden dining table. The frittata, baked in an everyday ceramic baking dish or a cast-iron skillet, is sliced into generous, rustic wedges. Its surface is lightly browned with visible pockets of melted, bubbly cheddar cheese and vibrant specks of green spinach and red cherry tomatoes. Diced onion and bell pepper are embedded within the fluffy, set egg matrix. The frittata has a natural, slightly uneven top, reflecting its homemade preparation. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley provides a contrasting color garnish. The setting features an everyday ceramic plate with natural imperfections, a simple fork and knife, and a casually placed cloth napkin. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a relaxed family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (pane casereccio).
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Whisk eggs, milk, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a 24 cm oven-safe non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion and bell pepper. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add spinach. Cook 2-3 minutes until wilted.
Stir in halved cherry tomatoes. Cook 1 minute.
Pour egg mixture evenly over vegetables in the pan.
Sprinkle shredded cheese over the top.
Cook on stovetop 3-4 minutes until edges set.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Bake 15-20 minutes until frittata is set and golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slice into wedges. Garnish with fresh parsley. Serve warm.
notes: This frittata is excellent served warm or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Roasted Chicken and Potatoes is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two golden-brown, skin-on chicken thighs, roasted to a crisp exterior, are positioned alongside several thick-cut, roasted potato wedges. The potatoes display a tender interior with slightly browned, crisp edges. Scattered amongst the chicken and potatoes are caramelized wedges of red onion and whole roasted garlic cloves. The dish is vibrant with warm tones of golden chicken and potatoes, deep red from smoked paprika, and fresh green from scattered rosemary leaves. A fresh rosemary sprig and a bright yellow lemon wedge garnish the plate, ready for squeezing. The texture is a delightful contrast of crispy skin, tender chicken, and soft, earthy potatoes. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware, under even, natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Offer a simple green salad on the side.

ingredients.name: lemon, cut into wedges, for serving

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken generously with salt, pepper, and half the smoked paprika.
In a large roasting pan, combine potato wedges, onion wedges, whole garlic cloves, remaining smoked paprika, chopped rosemary, and olive oil. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange potatoes, onion, and garlic in a single layer. Place seasoned chicken thighs skin-side up on top of vegetables.
Roast for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden-brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken & Shrimp with Fermented Tomato Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. Three to four golden-brown pan-seared chicken chunks are arranged organically on one side, alongside three to four perfectly seared, pink shrimp. A vibrant, red-hued fermented tomato and finely diced red onion salsa is spooned artfully beside the proteins, showcasing its juicy texture and bright color.
