A small cluster of vibrant green blanched green beans provides a crisp counterpoint. A clear, light golden reclaimed vegetable broth forms a shallow pool beneath the ingredients, reflecting the natural light. The overall presentation is clean, minimalist, and celebrates the natural beauty of each ingredient. The setting features a light, textured reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige, and soft, natural light illuminating the dish. No fanned meat slices; chicken and shrimp are presented as whole pieces or chunks.

ingredients.name: Fermented cherry tomatoes, halved or quartered
Mixed vegetable scraps (e.g., onion ends, carrot peels, celery leaves, mushroom stems)

instructions: Prepare Reclaimed Vegetable Broth: Combine vegetable scraps and water in a pot. Simmer for 30 minutes. Strain broth. Discard solids. Season broth with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Prepare Fermented Tomato-Onion Salsa: In a bowl, gently combine fermented cherry tomatoes, fermented red onion, chopped parsley, 1 tbsp olive oil, and apple cider vinegar. Set aside.
Cook Green Beans: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add green beans. Blanch for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately.

Cook Chicken: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm thick chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C (approximately 6-8 minutes), turning occasionally. Remove chicken from pan. Keep warm.
Cook Shrimp: Add remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the same pan. Season shrimp with salt and pepper. Add shrimp to the hot pan. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Remove from pan.

Plate Dish: Ladle a small amount of warm reclaimed vegetable broth into each of four shallow bowls. Arrange chicken chunks, shrimp, and blanched green beans artistically in each bowl. Top each serving with a generous spoonful of the Fermented Tomato-Onion Salsa. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto with Peas and Swiss Chard
recipes.visual_description: A generous, fluid portion of creamy, pale golden Chicken and Mushroom Risotto is served in a clean, shallow white porcelain bowl. The risotto maintains a loose, flowing consistency. Tender, bite-sized pan-seared chicken chunks, golden-brown, are arranged naturally atop the risotto. Vibrant green peas are speckled throughout the creamy rice, alongside earthy, thinly sliced sautéed mushrooms. Deep green, tender wilted Swiss chard ribbons are gently folded in. A light sprinkle of finely grated Parmesan and fresh parsley leaves garnish the dish. Presented on a simple wooden table with standard silver flatware and a cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting, suggesting a modern bistro. The background is minimal, keeping focus on the inviting, well-balanced dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately. Risotto loses its creamy texture if left to sit.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
instructions: Heat chicken stock in a saucepan. Keep it at a gentle simmer.
Dice chicken breast into 2 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, deep pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same pan. Reduce heat to medium. Add finely diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced cremini mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes until grains are coated and slightly translucent at the edges.
Pour in dry white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Begin adding hot chicken stock, one ladleful (about 120 ml) at a time. Stir continuously until each addition is almost completely absorbed before adding the next.
After about 15 minutes, when rice is halfway cooked, stir in frozen green peas and chopped Swiss chard. Continue adding stock and stirring.
Cook for another 5-7 minutes. Risotto should be creamy and al dente, not mushy. It should be fluid, not stiff.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in cooked chicken chunks, unsalted butter, and 80 g grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cover the pan. Let risotto rest for 2 minutes.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and remaining grated Parmesan.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Risotto should be creamy and flowable, not stiff or dry. Adjust stock as needed.
traditional_techniques: Risotto method (gradual stock addition, constant stirring)
Soffritto (aromatic base of onion and garlic)

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of beer-braised chicken is presented on a simple, cream-colored ceramic plate. Two tender, bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, deeply caramelized golden-brown from searing and then braising, rest atop a mound of fluffy, pearly white rice. The chicken skin retains some crispness, contrasting with the succulent meat beneath. A rich, glossy, amber-brown braising sauce, thick with reduced beer and chicken juices, pools around the chicken and lightly coats the rice. Finely chopped fresh green basil is sprinkled generously over the entire dish, adding a pop of vibrant color and freshness. The scene is set on a warm, well-worn wooden kitchen table, with a casually folded off-white cloth napkin and a standard fork and knife beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from an overhead fixture illuminates the comforting meal, emphasizing its homely appeal.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until deeply golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour beer into the pot. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes to reduce slightly.
Add chicken broth to the pot. Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in liquid. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot and transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) is reached.

While chicken braises, cook rice according to package instructions. Typically, combine 300 grams rice with 600 milliliters water or broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is fluffy.
Remove pot from oven. Carefully remove chicken to a plate. If sauce is too thin, simmer uncovered on stovetop for a few minutes until desired consistency.
Serve braised chicken over a bed of fluffy rice. Spoon generous amounts of the rich braising sauce over the chicken and rice. Garnish with fresh chopped basil.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Use a beer you enjoy drinking, as its flavor will concentrate in the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Baked Rigatoni with Savory Tomato-Chocolate Sauce and Cheddar
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty baked rigatoni is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The rigatoni is coated in a rich, deep reddish-brown savory tomato-chocolate sauce, intertwined with small grains of brown rice, and topped with a bubbly, golden-brown crust of melted sharp cheddar cheese. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are scattered artfully over the cheese crust, providing a contrasting color. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed beside. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting textures. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual bistro. The dish appears as a comforting, substantial main course.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the savory sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Grease a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced yellow onion. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, unsweetened cocoa powder, dried oregano, and bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer sauce for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Remove bay leaf.
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Stir cooked brown rice into the tomato sauce.
Combine cooked rigatoni with the sauce in the large pot. Mix thoroughly to coat all pasta.
Pour pasta mixture into the prepared baking dish. Spread evenly.
Sprinkle grated sharp cheddar cheese generously over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden brown.
Let stand for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.
notes: The unsweetened cocoa powder adds depth and richness to the sauce, not sweetness. It enhances the savory tomato flavor.
Cook the pasta al dente as it will continue to cook in the oven.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mushroom Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of pan-seared chicken breast rests on a simple, slightly imperfect off-white ceramic dinner plate. The golden-brown chicken, presented as a whole piece, is generously covered with a rich, creamy, off-white mushroom sauce. Sliced, earthy-brown cremini mushrooms and diced onions are visible within the velvety sauce, which pools naturally around the chicken. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of color. The plate is positioned on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy kitchen lighting, evoking a comfortable family meal setting.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil and 15g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside. Keep warm.
Add remaining 15g butter to the skillet. Add sliced cremini mushrooms and diced yellow onion. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender and onion is softened.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over the mushroom mixture. Stir for 1 minute to cook the flour.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Return cooked chicken breasts to the skillet. Spoon sauce over the chicken. Simmer for 2-3 minutes to heat through.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. It is generously coated with a rich, creamy mushroom sauce. The sauce features irregularly sliced, deeply browned cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots, creating a rustic yet refined texture. Bright green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the chicken and sauce, adding a fresh color contrast. The chicken breast shows a crisp exterior and a tender interior. A small pool of sauce surrounds the base of the chicken. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and texture. A single portion, balanced and appealing.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan.
Add sliced shallot. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add irregularly sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Sprinkle flour over mushrooms. Stir for 1 minute to coat.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken breasts to the pan. Turn to coat with sauce.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Chicken with Orzo and Cucumber Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared chicken breast, golden-brown and cut into thick, rustic chunks, rests centrally on a bed of fluffy, herb-tossed orzo pasta on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The orzo, light ivory, is cooked al dente, mixed with fresh parsley and lemon zest. Alongside, a vibrant cucumber salad features small diced, bright green cucumber pieces, tossed with fresh dill and a light vinaigrette. Thin lemon slices and a sprig of fresh thyme garnish the dish, adding color and freshness. Moderate negative space ensures a balanced composition. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, white cotton napkin, and standard silver cutlery. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh textures and inviting colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, and a pinch of chopped thyme.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Rest 5 minutes. Cut into thick chunks.

While chicken cooks, prepare cucumber salad. Dice cucumber into small cubes. In a medium bowl, combine diced cucumber, chopped dill, red wine vinegar, 1 tablespoon olive oil, juice of 1/2 lemon, salt, and pepper. Toss well. Set aside.
In the same skillet, add minced garlic. Cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add orzo to the skillet. Stir 1 minute. Pour in chicken broth and juice of 1/2 lemon. Bring to a simmer.
Cook orzo according to package directions, stirring occasionally, until liquid is absorbed and orzo is al dente (about 10-12 minutes).
Stir in chopped parsley and remaining chopped thyme into the cooked orzo. Adjust seasoning.
Serve orzo as a base. Arrange chicken chunks on top. Spoon cucumber salad alongside. Garnish with fresh lemon slices.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Tomato Chicken Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant single portion of Spicy Tomato Chicken Pappardelle is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Long, wide pappardelle ribbons are loosely twirled in the center, generously coated in a rich, rustic red-orange tomato sauce. Distributed throughout the pasta are golden-brown, seared 2 cm chicken cubes, exhibiting a tender texture. Creamy, melted chunks of fresh mozzarella are visible, adding contrasting white accents. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh, vibrant green basil leaves and a dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese, enhancing both color and aroma. The plate is set on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a neatly folded light grey linen napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and inviting textures, creating a professional yet approachable restaurant style.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Pair with a simple green salad.
Enjoy with a glass of red wine.
instructions: Dice chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and black pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes in batches until golden brown and cooked through, reaching 75°C internal temperature. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pan. Add finely diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and Calabrian chili paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
While sauce simmers, cook pappardelle pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 120ml pasta water.
Add cooked chicken and drained pasta to the tomato sauce. Toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency is reached.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in torn fresh mozzarella until it begins to melt and become creamy.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh basil leaves and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Adjust chili paste for desired spice level.
Freshly grated Parmesan cheese enhances flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Spanish Tortilla
recipes.visual_description: A thick, golden-brown Classic Spanish Tortilla sits centrally on a simple, round ceramic plate. The tortilla is round, with rustic, slightly uneven edges, showcasing its home-cooked nature. Its surface is a rich golden brown, indicating a perfectly cooked crust. A cross-section reveals a moist, tender interior, pale yellow in color, with visible, soft slices of potato and translucent, caramelized onion pieces embedded throughout. The texture is invitingly soft inside with a firm exterior. A few flecks of chopped fresh parsley are sprinkled over the top. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table. Adjacent to the plate, a simple, rustic fork and a casually folded cloth napkin complete the homely setting. The lighting is warm and cozy, suggestive of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve at room temperature or slightly warm.
Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Cut into wedges for individual portions.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Slice into thin medallions, about 2-3mm thick. Peel onion. Slice thinly.
Heat olive oil in a 20cm non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced potatoes and onion. Ensure they are submerged in oil.
Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes. Potatoes and onions should be very tender, almost confit, but not browned. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Carefully drain almost all olive oil from the pan, reserving about 2 tablespoons in the pan. Transfer cooked potatoes and onions to a large bowl.
Crack eggs into the bowl with potatoes and onions. Season generously with salt and pepper. Gently mix to combine, mashing some potato slices slightly.
Return the pan with reserved oil to medium heat. Pour the egg and potato mixture into the hot pan. Spread evenly.
Cook for 5-7 minutes. Edges should set and turn golden. Center should still be slightly soft.
Place a large plate over the pan. Invert the pan to flip the tortilla onto the plate. Slide the tortilla back into the pan, uncooked side down.
Cook for another 3-5 minutes until golden brown and set through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F).
Slide the tortilla onto a serving plate. Let it rest for a few minutes before slicing.
traditional_techniques: Confit-style frying of potatoes and onions in olive oil
Flipping the tortilla using a plate

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Chicken Orzo with Fresh Cucumber
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lemon Herb Chicken Orzo is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The dish features golden-brown seared chicken cubes, creamy al dente orzo pasta, and vibrant diced cucumber. Bright red cherry tomato halves and flecks of fresh green dill and parsley are interspersed throughout. Crumbled white feta cheese is scattered generously over the top. The textures are varied: tender chicken, soft orzo, crisp cucumber, and crumbly feta. The overall color palette is fresh and inviting, with warm browns, bright reds, and various greens against the creamy white pasta. The dish is arranged naturally, allowing ingredients to mix, showcasing the freshness. It is placed on a simple, light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and basic silver flatware are beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a minimal, soft-focus background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty bread to sop up any remaining sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken cubes dry. Cut chicken breast into 2.5 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken until golden-brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the same pan. Add finely diced red onion. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add orzo to the pan. Stir 1 minute to toast lightly.
Pour in 250ml warm chicken broth. Stir constantly until absorbed by the orzo.
Continue adding broth, 125ml at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed before adding more. This takes about 15-20 minutes, until orzo is al dente.
Return cooked chicken to the pan with orzo. Stir to combine.
Dice cucumber into 1 cm cubes. Halve cherry tomatoes. Chop dill and parsley.
Add diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, chopped dill, chopped parsley, and lemon zest to the pan. Stir gently to combine.
Squeeze in lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with crumbled feta cheese.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C internal temperature for safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy chicken and mushroom pasta rests in a round, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown, 2 cm seared chicken cubes are nestled amongst the al dente pasta strands, which are thoroughly coated in a rich, pale cream sauce. Sliced, earthy brown mushrooms are interspersed throughout, adding depth. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley provides a pop of color on top. The dish is presented casually, as if just served from the stove, with the pasta naturally piled. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a plain cloth napkin, emphasizing the homely, unpretentious comfort of the meal.
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Pat chicken breast cut into 2 cm cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Add cooked chicken back to the pan with the sauce. Add drained pasta. Toss to coat everything evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef Ragu with Dark Chocolate, Pappardelle, and Saffron Arancini
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, classic white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table surface. A generous portion of broad, flat pappardelle pasta forms a nest, glistening with a rich, deep reddish-brown slow-cooked beef ragu. The ragu features tender, dark brown beef chunks, approximately 4 cm cubes, enveloped in a thick, glossy tomato-based sauce, subtly enhanced by dark chocolate. Flecks of finely diced carrot, celery, and onion are visible within the sauce, adding texture and color. Resting beside the pasta are two or three perfectly golden-brown saffron arancini, about 5 cm in diameter. Their crispy, textured breadcrumb coating contrasts with the smooth pasta and ragu. A small, vibrant green sprig of fresh basil or parsley is placed atop the ragu for a pop of color. The setting includes a simple linen napkin and traditional silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and rich colors. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, showcasing a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the ragu.
Pair with a robust red wine, such as a Chianti or Barolo.

ingredients.name: Saffron threads
ingredients.quantity: 0.5 g, steeped in 30 ml hot water

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown beef cubes in batches on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced pancetta to the pot. Cook until crispy. Remove pancetta and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook over medium heat until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze pot with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce wine by half.
Return beef and pancetta to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, bay leaves, rosemary, and thyme.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove bay leaves and herb sprigs. Stir in chopped dark chocolate until melted and incorporated.
Season ragu with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add Arborio rice. Cook for 1 minute, stirring.
Add saffron-infused water and a ladle of hot vegetable broth to the rice. Stir constantly.
Continue adding broth ladle by ladle, stirring until absorbed. Cook until rice is al dente, about 18-20 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese. Spread rice on a baking sheet. Let cool completely.
Once cool, take small portions of rice (about 30g). Flatten in your palm.
Place a small cube of mozzarella in the center. Form rice into a ball, sealing the mozzarella inside.
Prepare three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten egg, one with breadcrumbs.
Roll each rice ball in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, ensuring full coating.
Heat frying oil in a deep pot to 175°C (350°F).
Fry arancini in batches until golden brown and crispy, 3-4 minutes.
Remove arancini with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Add pappardelle pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta.
Portion cooked pappardelle onto plates.
Spoon generous amount of beef ragu over the pasta.
Place 2-3 saffron arancini beside the pasta.
Garnish with fresh parsley or basil, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Herb Chicken and Potato Traybake
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown baked chicken thigh, skin crispy and glistening, rests on a rustic, round ceramic plate. Surrounding the chicken is a generous, natural pile of roasted potato wedges, their skins slightly charred and interiors fluffy. Interspersed among the potatoes are soft, caramelized chunks of roasted onion and whole, tender garlic cloves. Fresh green rosemary and thyme leaves are scattered over the dish, adding small pops of color. The arrangement is casual and homey, with ingredients touching and slightly overlapping, suggesting a comforting family meal. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light. A simple, casually folded linen napkin and a plain water glass are visible in the soft-focus background, completing the lived-in, authentic home kitchen scene.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and scrub potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges.
Peel onion. Cut onion into thick 2 cm chunks.
Peel garlic cloves. Leave whole.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, onion chunks, and whole garlic cloves.
Strip leaves from rosemary and thyme sprigs. Add to vegetables.
Drizzle vegetables with 30ml olive oil. Season with half the salt and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken thighs all over with remaining salt and pepper.
Drizzle chicken thighs with remaining 30ml olive oil.
Place chicken thighs skin-side up on top of the vegetables on the baking tray.
Pour chicken broth into the bottom of the baking tray.
Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and skin is golden and crispy. Potatoes should be tender and lightly browned.
Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Dark Beer Stew with Rice and Peas
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of dark beer beef stew is served generously over a bed of fluffy white rice in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The stew features large, seared beef chunks, slow-braised until fork-tender, interspersed with rustic-cut, softened carrots, celery, and onions, all coated in a rich, glossy, deep reddish-brown gravy. Vibrant green peas are stirred into the stew, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish is casually plated, allowing components to touch and overlap naturally. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley garnishes the top. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table in a homely kitchen, illuminated by warm, inviting light. A simple metal fork rests beside the bowl on a casually placed, folded linen napkin. The overall presentation is comforting and unpretentious.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty bread for dipping into the gravy
A pint of dark beer, similar to that used in the stew
instructions: Pat beef dry. Cut into 4-5 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper. Dredge beef in flour.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add chopped onion, rustic-cut carrots, and roughly chopped celery to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Deglaze the pot with a splash of dark beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return seared beef to the pot. Pour in remaining dark beer and beef broth. Add bay leaf and fresh thyme sprigs.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly.
Simmer for 2-3 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
While the stew simmers, cook rice according to package directions.
Five minutes before serving, stir frozen green peas into the stew. Cook until heated through.
Taste the stew and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve hearty portions of stew over cooked rice. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This stew tastes even better the next day. It can be made ahead of time and reheated.
For best flavor, use a good quality dark beer like a stout or porter.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Potato Stew
recipes.visual_description: The dish features golden-browned chicken thigh chunks and irregular potato wedges in a rich, reddish-orange sauce. The potatoes are cracked with rough edges to thicken the stew naturally. Serve in a shallow terracotta cazuela on a rustic wooden table. The chicken is presented as whole bone-in pieces, never sliced. Sautéed onion and garlic bits are visible in the glossy sauce. A light sprinkle of chopped fresh parsley adds green contrast. The lighting is warm and domestic, suggesting a family kitchen. A crusty loaf of bread sits nearby on a linen cloth. The arrangement is casual and hearty, filling the bowl with a single, generous portion. Everything is captured in a clean, realistic photo.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty white bread for dipping.
Pair with a simple green salad.
Enjoy with a glass of light red wine.
instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a deep pan over medium heat.
Brown chicken on all sides for 8 minutes.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pan.
Cook until translucent.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika.
Stir for 1 minute.
Add potatoes cut into irregular chunks.
Return chicken to the pan.
Pour in chicken stock and add bay leaf.
Simmer for 25 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Check chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove bay leaf before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Cracking the potatoes by snapping them off the knife releases starch to thicken the sauce naturally.
Use high-quality smoked pimentón for the most authentic flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Onion Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and whole, rests slightly off-center on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. Beneath and beside the chicken, a natural mound of vibrant green, wilted seasonal greens provides a soft contrast. Alongside, a rustic spoonful of the fermented tomato and onion mixture showcases the varied reds of the tomatoes and purples of the onions. A single shard of crispy, golden chicken skin is placed delicately on the chicken. The composition is minimalistic, clean, and unforced, with ample negative space. The plate sits on a light reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed to the side. Simple, unadorned fork and knife rest beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene from the side, with a clean, minimalist background featuring a hint of blurred green plant foliage.
instructions: Prepare fermented tomato and onion. Combine roughly chopped tomatoes, thinly sliced red onions, and 10g sea salt in a clean glass jar. Press down firmly to submerge vegetables in their own liquid. Seal the jar loosely to allow gas release.
Ferment at room temperature (18-22°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Check daily for small bubbles. Refrigerate to slow fermentation once ready.

Separate chicken skin from thighs, leaving a small attachment point. Place skin in a cold, dry pan. Cook over medium-low heat until crispy and golden. Remove skin. Season with a pinch of salt. Reserve crispy skin shards for garnish.

Season chicken thighs with salt and black pepper. Increase pan heat to medium-high. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down in the rendered chicken fat (or a splash of olive oil) until deeply golden and crispy.
Flip chicken thighs. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While chicken roasts, add thinly sliced garlic to the same pan with a splash of olive oil. Sauté briefly. Add seasonal greens. Cook until just wilted. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.

Plate each portion: arrange a bed of wilted greens. Place one roasted chicken thigh on top. Spoon a generous amount of the fermented tomato and onion mixture alongside. Garnish with a shard of crispy chicken skin.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Rustico al Forno con Erbe
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo Rustico al Forno con Erbe is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table surface. The golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh, a whole piece, is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Around the chicken are tender, rustic chunks of roasted potato with lightly crisped edges, and soft, caramelized red onion wedges. Several whole, roasted garlic cloves are nestled among the vegetables. The dish is naturally glistening with the pan juices, which form a light, savory sauce at the bottom of the plate. Fresh green oregano sprigs are artfully placed over the chicken and vegetables, adding a vibrant color contrast. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware are placed beside the plate, hinting at a casual bistro setting. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich, savory colors.

ingredients.name: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Cut potatoes into 2 cm chunks. Cut red onions into 2 cm wedges. Peel garlic cloves, leave whole.
Roughly chop half of the fresh oregano.
In a large roasting pan, combine potatoes, onion wedges, whole garlic cloves, chopped oregano, and 30 ml olive oil. Toss to coat.
Nestle chicken pieces among the vegetables in the pan, skin-side up.
Drizzle remaining 30 ml olive oil over chicken skin.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Remove pan from oven. Pour white wine and chicken broth into the pan, around the chicken and vegetables. Return to oven.
Continue roasting for another 25-35 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and skin is golden and crispy. Vegetables should be tender and slightly caramelized.
Remove pan from oven. Let chicken rest in the pan for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with remaining fresh oregano sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Tomato Risotto with Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, creamy Chicken and Tomato Risotto is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The risotto, a rich orange-red hue from the tomatoes, flows naturally, maintaining its characteristic fluid consistency. Tender, golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled atop the risotto. Alongside, bright green roasted broccoli florets and vibrant orange carrot batons are artfully arranged, providing a textural contrast. Fresh basil leaves, a vibrant green, are scattered over the dish, adding a fragrant pop of color. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh ingredients and appealing textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with extra freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
Offer a side of crusty Italian bread for soaking up the creamy sauce.

ingredients.name: Carrots peeled cut into 5 cm batons

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Toss broccoli florets and carrot batons with 10 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Cut chicken into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat 10 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) later.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat remaining 10 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the rice kernels.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add crushed tomatoes. Stir well to combine.

Add hot chicken broth, one ladleful (about 120 ml) at a time. Stir constantly. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue this process for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is creamy and al dente.
Return seared chicken chunks to the risotto. Stir to combine and allow chicken to finish cooking through in the risotto.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in cold butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously until the risotto is creamy and emulsified (mantecatura).
Season risotto with additional salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in most of the fresh basil leaves. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve risotto immediately in wide, shallow bowls. Top with roasted broccoli and carrots. Garnish with reserved fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Risotto should be creamy and flowable, not stiff. Add a splash more broth if needed to achieve this consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Herb Frittata
recipes.visual_description: A modest, individual portion of golden-brown Potato and Herb Frittata is presented on a round, rustic ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The frittata, baked in a cast iron pan, shows a slightly puffed, golden-brown top with visible specks of green herbs and melted, lightly browned cheese. It is cut into a generous wedge, revealing layers of soft, diced potatoes and finely chopped sautéed onions embedded within the fluffy, set egg. A scattering of fresh, roughly chopped parsley garnishes the top. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table, alongside a simple fork and a folded, off-white linen napkin. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. A small, crusty bread roll is casually placed beside the plate, hinting at a comforting family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Peel and dice potatoes into 1 cm cubes. Finely dice onion.
Heat olive oil in a 24 cm oven-safe non-stick or cast iron pan over medium heat.
Add diced potatoes to the pan. Cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender-crisp.
Add diced onion to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
While potatoes and onion cook, whisk eggs in a large bowl. Stir in grated cheese, chopped parsley, salt, and pepper.
Pour egg mixture evenly over the cooked potatoes and onions in the pan. Distribute ingredients evenly.
Cook on stovetop for 2-3 minutes until edges begin to set.
Transfer the pan to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until frittata is set and golden brown on top.
Remove from oven. Let cool slightly before serving.
notes: The frittata is cooked through when a knife inserted into the center comes out clean.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes rests on an everyday cream-colored ceramic plate. Two golden-brown roasted chicken drumsticks, with crispy, crackled skin, are positioned naturally beside a generous pile of thick-cut, golden-brown roasted potato wedges. The potatoes show a slightly crispy exterior and tender interior, some edges lightly charred. Scattered among the potatoes and chicken are a few wilted rosemary and thyme sprigs and roasted garlic cloves. The arrangement is casual and unpretentious, reflecting home cooking. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple cloth napkin and standard flatware nearby. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a comfortable family kitchen setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and pat dry chicken pieces. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut into thick wedges, about 2-3 cm thick.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, olive oil, smashed garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange chicken pieces and potato wedges in a single layer on a large baking tray. Ensure chicken skin faces up.
Roast for 30 minutes. Flip potatoes once during cooking.
Continue roasting for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden-brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Green Tortelloni with Fermented Broccoli Rabe
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of handmade green tortelloni is artfully arranged on a round, matte cream ceramic plate. Six to eight plump, vibrant green tortelloni, their spinach-ricotta filling peeking subtly, rest within a smooth, verdant pool of broccoli rabe cream. The pasta exhibits a delicate, tender texture. A scattering of finely diced, lacto-fermented broccoli rabe stems provides a contrasting textural pop and bright, acidic notes. A whisper of toasted, golden breadcrumbs adds a subtle crunch and earthy hue. The dish is framed by ample negative space, highlighting its organic form. It is presented on a reclaimed wood surface with an undyed linen napkin and a simple, elegant fork, bathed in soft, natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of freshly grated Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano-Reggiano on the side for individual preference.
Offer a cruet of high-quality extra virgin olive oil for a final drizzle.
instructions: Prepare pasta dough: Combine '00' flour and semolina on a clean surface. Form a well. Crack eggs into the well. Slowly incorporate flour into eggs with a fork. Knead dough for 10-12 minutes until smooth and elastic. Wrap in cling film. Rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.

Prepare spinach filling: Blanch spinach in salted boiling water for 1 minute. Drain well. Squeeze out all excess water. Finely chop spinach. In a bowl, combine chopped spinach, ricotta, cottage cheese, grated Parmesan, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix well. Set aside.

Prepare fermented broccoli rabe stems: Separate broccoli rabe florets and leaves from the tougher stems. Wash stems thoroughly. Finely dice the stems (approx. 150g). Place diced stems in a clean jar. Add 1 teaspoon sea salt. Cover with filtered water, ensuring stems are fully submerged. Seal loosely. Allow to ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate after fermentation. (This can be prepared in advance).

Prepare broccoli rabe cream: Blanch broccoli rabe florets and tender leaves in salted boiling water for 2-3 minutes until tender. Drain and refresh in ice water to preserve color. Heat 20 ml olive oil in a pan. Add sliced garlic and chili flakes. Sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add blanched broccoli rabe. Sauté briefly. Transfer to a blender. Add vegetable broth and remaining 40 ml olive oil. Blend until very smooth and creamy. Season with salt, pepper, and lemon zest. Keep warm.

Assemble tortelloni: Roll pasta dough very thinly using a pasta machine or rolling pin. Cut into 7 cm circles. Place a teaspoon of spinach filling in the center of each circle. Fold each circle in half to form a semi-circle. Press edges to seal. Bring the two points of the semi-circle together and pinch to form a tortelloni shape. Repeat for all dough and filling.
Cook tortelloni: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Gently drop tortelloni into boiling water. Cook for 3-4 minutes, or until al dente and floating. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Prepare toasted breadcrumbs: While pasta cooks, toast stale bread in a dry pan until golden and crisp. Crush into coarse crumbs.

Plate the dish: Ladle a generous swirl of warm broccoli rabe cream onto the center of each serving plate. Arrange 6-8 cooked tortelloni artfully on top of the cream. Sprinkle finely diced fermented broccoli rabe stems over the tortelloni for texture and tang. Finish with a light dusting of toasted breadcrumbs. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing the tougher stems of the broccoli rabe for fermentation, adding a unique flavor and texture.
The combination of ricotta and cottage cheese provides a lighter, yet creamy, filling for the pasta.
For best results, prepare fermented stems a few days in advance. If time is short, a quick pickle with vinegar can be used as a substitute.
traditional_techniques: Use of cime di rapa (broccoli rabe) in traditional Southern Italian cuisine

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef Ragu with Potato Gnocchi and Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-cooked beef ragu with potato gnocchi is centrally mounded on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The rich, dark red ragu features tender, shredded beef chunks visibly coating the golden-brown potato gnocchi. A generous snowfall of freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese blankets the top. Around the base of the gnocchi, a few vibrant green, slightly charred roasted broccoli florets are artfully placed, adding a pop of color and texture. A small sprig of fresh flat-leaf parsley rests atop the cheese. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A fork and spoon are neatly arranged beside the plate. A folded white cotton napkin completes the casual yet refined presentation. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish as the primary subject without distraction.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping into the rich ragu.
Pair with a robust red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into large 5 cm chunks. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot and set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery (soffritto) to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until softened and translucent. Add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed San Marzano tomatoes and beef stock. Stir to combine. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and simmer for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally. Remove beef from pot and shred with two forks. Return shredded beef to the sauce. Stir well.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Toss broccoli florets with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add potato gnocchi. Cook according to package directions, usually 2-3 minutes, until gnocchi float to the surface.
Drain gnocchi. Add cooked gnocchi directly to the beef ragu. Toss gently to coat.
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano and roasted broccoli florets. Sprinkle with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Greek Chicken Giouvetsi with Orzo and Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Greek Chicken Giouvetsi is presented in a shallow, matte white ceramic bowl. A tender, whole braised chicken thigh, its skin golden-brown from searing, rests partially submerged in the rich, reddish-orange orzo and rice mixture. The pasta and rice are cooked to a creamy al dente texture, interspersed with soft diced carrots and flecks of vibrant green thyme. A scattering of fresh chopped parsley and crumbled white feta cheese garnishes the dish, adding contrasting color and freshness. The setting is a clean, light wooden table, with a simple white cotton napkin beside the bowl. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting warmth and inviting textures. A small side dish of Kalamata olives and a slice of rustic bread complete the authentic Mediterranean casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce
Accompany with a simple Greek salad
Offer a small bowl of Kalamata olives on the side
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion and diced carrot to the pot. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Add chopped fresh thyme. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Cover. Simmer on stovetop for 20 minutes.
Stir in orzo pasta and long grain rice. Ensure pasta and rice are fully submerged in the liquid.
Cover the pot. Transfer to the preheated oven. Bake 25-30 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and pasta and rice are tender.
Remove from oven. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and crumbled feta cheese, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Bacon Potato Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Hearty Bacon Potato Pasta Bake is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The dish features a golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted cheddar cheese and toasted breadcrumbs, covering a creamy, hearty mixture beneath. Crispy, diced bacon pieces are scattered throughout and visible on the surface. Tender, par-boiled potato cubes and vibrant diced tomatoes are interspersed with short pasta, all coated in a rich, comforting cheese sauce. The pasta is cooked al dente, holding its shape. The dish appears warm and inviting, with steam gently rising. A few fresh, chopped parsley leaves are sprinkled on top as a functional garnish, adding a touch of green. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. Simple, everyday silver flatware is placed casually beside the plate. A soft, warm light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The background is minimally cluttered, focusing entirely on the comforting meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Peel potatoes. Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Boil potatoes in salted water for 5-7 minutes until slightly tender. Drain.
Dice bacon into 1 cm pieces. Cook bacon in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve 15 ml bacon fat.
Dice onion. Add onion to the skillet with reserved bacon fat. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Mince garlic. Add garlic to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes. Simmer for 5 minutes.
In a separate saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Stir in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in milk. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Add 150 g grated cheddar cheese to the sauce. Stir until melted and smooth.
Combine cooked pasta, par-boiled potatoes, cooked bacon, and tomato mixture in the skillet. Pour cheese sauce over the mixture. Stir to combine.
Sprinkle remaining 50 g grated cheddar cheese and breadcrumbs evenly over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and bubbly.
Let stand for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Salad is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, suitable for a homely family meal. Diced sweet potatoes, roasted until caramelized and golden-brown, are scattered throughout, offering warm orange hues. Dark green, massaged kale forms the base, softened but retaining texture. Thinly sliced red onion adds pops of purple. Chopped pecans and dried cranberries are sprinkled generously, providing contrasting textures and colors—earthy browns and vibrant reds. The maple-Dijon dressing lightly coats all ingredients, creating a subtle sheen without pooling. The arrangement is natural and unpretentious, with components casually mixed. It sits on a well-used wooden dining table with a simple linen napkin, under warm, inviting kitchen light, emphasizing comfort and approachability.

ingredients.name: Sweet potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium (about 600g), peeled, diced into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss diced sweet potatoes with 30 ml olive oil, 2 ml salt, and 1 ml black pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned. Turn once.
While sweet potatoes roast, prepare the dressing. Whisk remaining 30 ml olive oil, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, apple cider vinegar, remaining 3 ml salt, and 1 ml black pepper in a small bowl.
Place chopped kale in a large bowl. Pour half of the dressing over kale. Massage kale with hands for 1-2 minutes until slightly softened.
Add roasted sweet potatoes, thinly sliced red onion, chopped pecans, and dried cranberries to the bowl with kale.
Pour remaining dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Serve immediately or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Herb Chicken and Mushroom Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Creamy Herb Chicken and Mushroom Skillet rests on an everyday off-white ceramic plate. A golden-brown seared chicken thigh, whole and un-sliced, is nestled amongst tender, sliced cremini mushrooms coated in a rich, creamy, herb-flecked sauce. The sauce shows natural variations in texture and color, pooling slightly around the chicken. Roasted potato wedges, with crispy edges and soft interiors, are casually arranged around the chicken, some slightly overlapping. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and knife lie to the side. A casually folded linen napkin completes the homely setting, bathed in warm, inviting kitchen light.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2 cm wedges. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, until golden and tender. Flip halfway through.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Stir often.
Add diced onion to skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes until translucent. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, reducing slightly.
Stir in heavy cream and fresh thyme leaves. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Simmer for 2-3 minutes to heat chicken through. Remove thyme sprigs.
Chop fresh parsley. Serve chicken and sauce with roasted potato wedges. Garnish with chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Baked Chicken Thighs with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lemon Herb Baked Chicken Thighs and Roasted Potatoes sits on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. The chicken thigh, with its crispy, golden-brown skin, is positioned naturally alongside several irregular, golden-edged roasted potato wedges. Scattered amongst the potatoes are browned lemon slices and tender, roasted garlic cloves. Fresh sprigs of rosemary and thyme are casually tucked in, adding a pop of green. The overall arrangement is unpretentious and hearty, reflecting a home-cooked meal. The dish is presented on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, with warm, inviting light casting soft shadows. A simple cloth napkin is casually draped nearby. The scene evokes a comforting, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad
Serve with crusty bread for soaking up juices
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into rustic 2-3 cm wedges or chunks. No need to peel.
Peel garlic cloves. Leave them whole.
In a large bowl, toss potato wedges and whole garlic cloves with 30ml olive oil, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper.
On a large baking tray, arrange seasoned potatoes and garlic in a single layer.
Place seasoned chicken thighs among the potatoes on the baking tray.
Slice the lemon into thin rounds. Distribute lemon slices over and around the chicken and potatoes.
Tuck rosemary and thyme sprigs among the ingredients.
Drizzle remaining 30ml olive oil over everything.
Bake for 35-45 minutes. Chicken skin should be golden and crispy. Potatoes should be tender.
Check chicken internal temperature with a meat thermometer. It must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Let rest on the tray for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: For crispier chicken skin, ensure chicken is very dry before seasoning.
Do not overcrowd the baking sheet; use two if necessary for even roasting.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet aux Pommes de Terre
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic French chicken and potatoes served on a cream-colored ceramic plate with slight imperfections. The focal point is a whole, golden-brown seared chicken thigh with crispy skin, nestled against large, irregular chunks of tender, braised potatoes. The potatoes are glossy with a light herb-flecked sauce. Small bits of softened shallot and whole cloves of roasted garlic are scattered throughout. The dish is garnished with a single fresh sprig of thyme. The plate sits on a weathered oak dining table. Beside it lies a simple stainless steel fork and knife on a folded white linen napkin. Soft, warm kitchen light creates a cozy, lived-in atmosphere, highlighting the natural textures of the poultry and root vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed in vinaigrette
Pair with a dry white wine like Chardonnay or a light red like Pinot Noir

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil and butter in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down. Sear until skin is golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Sear for 2 minutes. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add shallots and garlic to the remaining fat. Sauté for 2 minutes until translucent.
Add potato chunks to the pan. Cook for 5 minutes until edges are lightly browned.
Return chicken to the pan, nestling it among the potatoes.
Pour in chicken stock. Add thyme and rosemary sprigs.
Reduce heat to low. Cover with a lid.
Simmer for 20 minutes. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove lid. Simmer for 5 minutes to reduce and thicken the sauce.
Discard herb sprigs before serving.
notes: Use waxy potatoes to ensure they hold their shape during braising
Always use a meat thermometer to confirm the chicken reaches 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Creamy Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Tuscan Creamy Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A generous portion of golden pappardelle pasta, gently tossed in a creamy, blush-toned sauce, forms the base. Thick medallions of seared chicken thigh are arranged naturally atop the pasta, showcasing their golden-brown crust. Bright red halved cherry tomatoes and vibrant green wilted spinach leaves are interspersed throughout the pasta, adding color and freshness. Julienne strips of rich red sun-dried tomatoes provide visual depth. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley leaves and a light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A crisp, folded linen napkin and traditional silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a subtly blurred background hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere. The composition is clean, professional, and inviting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes, packed in oil, julienned
Dry white wine or chicken broth

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a cutting board to rest. Do not clean the skillet.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and julienned sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add halved cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Cook for 3-5 minutes until they begin to soften and burst.
Pour in white wine or chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Return to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Meanwhile, cook pappardelle pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.
Slice rested chicken thighs into thick medallions.
Add fresh spinach to the sauce in the skillet. Cook until just wilted.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and lemon juice. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add drained pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Gently fold in sliced chicken medallions.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Skillet Chicken with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single, boneless, skinless chicken thigh is positioned on an everyday ceramic plate. The chicken, seared to a golden-brown, is generously coated with a creamy, light-brown sauce. Abundant thin slices of deeply caramelized yellow onions are draped over and around the chicken, some peeking out from beneath the sauce. Scattered fresh thyme leaves add subtle green flecks. The dish fills the center of the plate, with components naturally overlapping. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and knife are casually placed beside it. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, homely atmosphere. Portions are hearty and approachable.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add thinly sliced onions to the skillet. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until onions are soft and deeply caramelized.
Add minced garlic to the skillet with onions. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over the onions and garlic. Stir well. Cook 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in heavy cream and fresh thyme leaves.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nesting them into the sauce.
Cover skillet. Simmer on low heat 5-7 minutes, or until chicken is heated through and sauce is thickened. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Paccheri with Slow-Roasted Cherry Tomatoes and Burrata
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Paccheri with Slow-Roasted Cherry Tomatoes and Burrata is presented in a clean, white porcelain deep plate, set on a simple wooden table. The large, tubular paccheri pasta is coated in a vibrant, glossy sauce of deep red, slow-roasted cherry tomatoes. The tomatoes are plump, some gently burst, revealing their tender interiors, and are interspersed with thin slices of golden-brown roasted garlic. Irregular, creamy white chunks of torn burrata cheese are nestled among the pasta, contrasting beautifully with the rich red. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered generously over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. A light drizzle of golden extra virgin olive oil glistens over the top. The dish is centrally composed with moderate negative space, showcasing the textures and colors. A folded white cotton napkin and classic Italian flatware are placed beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a light, dry white wine like Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Wash cherry tomatoes. Place whole tomatoes in a large baking dish.
Add sliced garlic, 80 ml olive oil, sea salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes (if using). Toss to coat.
Roast tomatoes for 30-40 minutes. Tomatoes should be soft and slightly burst.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Add paccheri pasta to boiling water. Cook according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving 120 ml of pasta cooking water.
Add drained pasta directly to the baking dish with roasted tomatoes. Toss to combine.
Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to create a light sauce. Toss again.
Tear burrata cheese into irregular chunks. Gently mix half of the burrata into the pasta.
Serve pasta immediately in individual deep plates.
Top each serving with remaining torn burrata pieces and fresh basil leaves. Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil.
notes: For extra depth of flavor, use a mix of heirloom cherry tomatoes.
Ensure burrata is at room temperature before serving for optimal creaminess.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, skin lightly crisp, rests on a rustic white ceramic plate. Alongside, a generous serving of tender, golden-brown potato wedges, their exteriors slightly caramelized. Fresh sprigs of rosemary and thyme are naturally scattered over the chicken and potatoes, adding vibrant green accents. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits nearby. The chicken is presented whole, not sliced. The plate is positioned on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. A casually folded blue and white checkered cloth napkin and simple silver cutlery are placed beside it. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, homely family meal. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the baking sheet for family-style meals.
Pair with a simple green salad or steamed seasonal vegetables.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2cm thick wedges. Place in a large bowl.
Mince garlic cloves. Finely chop rosemary and thyme leaves.
Add olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, salt, and pepper to the bowl with potatoes. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange potato wedges in a single layer on one half of the prepared baking sheet.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Place chicken thighs, skin-side up, on the other half of the baking sheet alongside the potatoes.
Slice the lemon into thin rounds. Place a few lemon rounds on top of and around the chicken and potatoes.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, and potatoes are tender and browned. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: For extra crispiness, broil chicken for the last 2-3 minutes, watching carefully to prevent burning.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Tomato Penne
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Chicken and Tomato Penne is presented in a clean, white, shallow porcelain bowl. The penne pasta is generously coated in a rich, creamy, orange-red tomato sauce. Interspersed are golden-brown, seared chicken cubes, visible and plump. A scattering of bright green, freshly chopped basil leaves adds a vibrant contrast on top. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the dish. The overall composition is inviting and rustic, yet refined. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed neatly beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and warm colors. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty ciabatta bread for dipping in the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2.5 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same pan. Add diced onion. Cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While sauce simmers, cook penne pasta according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 120ml pasta water.
Stir heavy cream into the tomato sauce. Return cooked chicken to the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Add drained penne to the sauce. Add half of the grated Parmesan cheese. Toss to coat pasta evenly. Add reserved pasta water as needed to reach desired consistency.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining grated Parmesan and fresh chopped basil.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Al dente pasta ensures best texture.
Adjust red pepper flakes for desired spiciness.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Cheddar and Roasted Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of rigatoni pasta rests in a clean white porcelain pasta bowl, centrally placed on a simple light wooden table. The pasta is coated in a creamy, savory sauce, tinted orange-red from roasted tomatoes and melted smoked cheddar. Scattered throughout are vibrant, burst roasted cherry tomatoes, some still whole, others gently collapsed. Crispy, small diced pancetta pieces are visibly interspersed, adding textural contrast and golden-brown highlights. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are artfully torn and sprinkled over the dish, providing a fragrant and colorful garnish. The composition is natural and flowing, with moderate negative space. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and inviting textures. A simple silver fork rests beside the bowl on a folded cotton napkin.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Place cherry tomatoes on a baking tray. Drizzle with 30 ml olive oil. Season with salt and black pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tomatoes are burst and slightly caramelized.
While tomatoes roast, dice pancetta into small cubes.

Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced pancetta. Cook until crispy and golden brown. Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon. Set aside on paper towels to drain. Pour off all but 15 ml of rendered fat from the skillet.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add rigatoni. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.
While pasta cooks, mince garlic.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the skillet with pancetta fat. Add minced garlic and optional red pepper flakes. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add roasted cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Gently mash some tomatoes with a spoon to release juices.
Add cooked and drained rigatoni to the skillet with tomatoes. Add 125 ml of reserved pasta water. Stir to combine.

Grate smoked cheddar cheese. Gradually add grated cheddar to the pasta, stirring constantly until cheese is melted and forms a creamy sauce. Add more pasta water, 30 ml at a time, if needed to reach desired consistency.
Tear fresh basil leaves. Add crispy pancetta and torn basil to the pasta. Toss gently.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper as needed. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure pasta is cooked al dente for best texture.
