Strain the chicken stock through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot. Discard solids. Keep stock warm.

While chicken cools, prepare vegetables. Peel carrots. Wash celery and leek thoroughly. Finely dice carrots, celery, and the white and light green parts of the leek into small, uniform 5 mm cubes (brunoise). Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a separate saucepan over medium heat. Add diced carrots, celery, and leek. Sauté gently for 5-7 minutes until softened but not browned. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Shred or cut the cooled chicken into small, neat chunks or cubes. Avoid fanning.
Add sautéed vegetables and chicken pieces to the warm strained stock. Simmer gently for 5 minutes to combine flavors and heat through.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper as needed.
Finely chop fresh parsley for garnish.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Saffron Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-hued chicken and saffron rice fills a clean white porcelain dinner plate, leaving moderate negative space. The rice is moist and free-flowing, infused with vibrant yellow from saffron and speckled with small, soft pieces of diced red tomato and caramelized onion. A single, perfectly seared chicken thigh, with a crispy, golden-brown skin, rests atop the rice. The chicken is presented whole, not sliced. Alongside, two roasted tomato halves, slightly softened and showing caramelized edges, add a touch of deep red. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley and a vibrant yellow lemon wedge placed beside the chicken. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, with a cotton napkin neatly folded beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere typical of a modern bistro.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful juices
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 30ml olive oil in a large, shallow pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the pan. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced large tomatoes. Cook for 3 minutes until tomatoes soften slightly.
Stir in Arborio rice, smoked paprika, and saffron threads. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to toast the rice.
Pour in warm chicken stock. Add bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the rice. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Chicken internal temperature should reach 75°C.
Cover pan. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed.
While rice cooks, preheat oven to 200°C. Halve the 2 small tomatoes. Drizzle with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 10-12 minutes until slightly softened and caramelized.
Remove pan from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Discard bay leaf. Fluff rice gently.
Serve individual portions of chicken and saffron rice. Garnish with roasted tomato halves, fresh chopped parsley, and a lemon wedge.
notes: For extra depth of flavor, toast a pinch of saffron threads in a dry pan before adding them to the rice.
Use Bomba rice for a more authentic Spanish texture, if available.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Tortilla de Patatas
recipes.visual_description: A thick, golden-brown Spanish Tortilla sits centered on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. The tortilla is a circular, dense cake, approximately 4 centimeters thick. Visible through the lightly seared surface are tender, translucent 3mm potato rounds and soft, caramelized onion strips. The exterior has a matte, slightly toasted finish without being greasy. Beside the plate lies a piece of crusty baguette and a small bowl of green olives. The setting is a weathered wooden table with a linen napkin. Natural light from a side window highlights the soft textures of the egg and the starchy edges of the potatoes. The portion is a single, substantial wedge cut from the whole tortilla.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve at room temperature or warm
Accompany with crusty bread
Serve with a side of alioli
instructions: Peel and slice potatoes into 3mm rounds.
Thinly slice the onion.
Heat olive oil in a 24cm non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Add potatoes and onions to the oil.
Fry gently for 15 minutes until potatoes are tender but not browned.
Drain potatoes and onions through a sieve over a bowl.
Reserve 30ml of the frying oil.
Beat eggs and salt in a large mixing bowl.
Fold the warm potato mixture into the eggs.
Let the mixture sit for 10 minutes to absorb flavor.
Heat the reserved oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat.
Pour the egg and potato mixture into the pan.
Cook for 2 minutes until the edges are set.
Invert a large flat plate over the pan and flip the tortilla onto it.
Slide the tortilla back into the pan with the uncooked side down.
Cook for 2 minutes until the center is just set.
notes: Do not overcook the eggs to maintain a moist center
Use Yukon Gold potatoes for the best texture
The slow frying in oil creates a confit texture in the potatoes

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto with Poached Egg
recipes.visual_description: A creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The Arborio rice is cooked to a tender, al dente consistency, coated in a rich, pale yellow sauce from butter and Parmesan. Scattered throughout are golden-brown, pan-seared chicken chunks (approximately 2-3 cm) and earthy, thinly sliced cremini mushrooms. A perfectly poached egg rests gently atop the risotto, its vibrant yellow yolk peeking through. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. It sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a fork and spoon, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's comforting textures and warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a 'primo piatto' (first course) or a main course.
Often accompanied by a glass of dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks (2-3 cm). Sear until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Season with salt and pepper. Remove chicken from pan; set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil and 20 g butter to the same pan. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until tender and browned. Remove mushrooms; set aside.
Add remaining 40 g butter to the pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Heat chicken broth in a separate saucepan until simmering. Do not boil.

Add one ladle of hot broth to the rice. Stir continuously until broth is absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed before adding more. This takes about 20-25 minutes.
After 15 minutes of broth additions, add cooked chicken chunks and sautéed mushrooms back into the risotto. Continue adding broth and stirring.

When risotto is creamy and rice is al dente (tender with a slight bite), remove from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper to taste. The risotto should be fluid, not stiff.

While risotto cooks, poach 4 eggs. Bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add a splash of vinegar. Carefully crack each egg into the water. Cook for 3-4 minutes until whites are set and yolks are runny.
Ladle risotto into individual serving bowls. Top each portion with a poached egg. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Use high-quality chicken broth for the best flavor.
Do not overcook the risotto; it should be creamy and slightly flowing, not stiff or dry.
Stirring continuously is key for a creamy risotto texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Potato Tomato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Chicken and Potato Tomato Bake is presented in a deep, everyday ceramic bowl with a slightly chipped rim, showcasing its homely comfort. Golden-brown melted cheddar cheese forms a bubbly, slightly crisp crust over tender, roasted potato rounds. Beneath the potatoes, chunks of seared chicken are nestled in a rich, rustic tomato sauce with visible pieces of softened onion and garlic. The chicken pieces are irregularly shaped, maintaining a hearty appearance. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the top. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. A simple white cloth napkin and a metal fork are casually placed beside it. Warm, soft light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family dining area with a hint of natural clutter in the blurred background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Dice chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt, pepper, and half the oregano.
Peel potatoes. Slice thinly into 3 mm rounds.
Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and remaining oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pan. Arrange potato slices over the chicken and sauce. Overlap slightly.
Cover the pan. Bake for 30 minutes.
Uncover the pan. Sprinkle shredded cheese evenly over the potatoes.
Bake uncovered for another 20-25 minutes. Potatoes should be tender. Cheese should be melted and golden brown. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Let the bake rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve with crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Vin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Coq au Vin is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are positioned centrally, coated in a glossy, deep-burgundy wine sauce. Surrounding the chicken are whole, golden-brown button mushrooms, translucent pearl onions, and crispy bacon lardons. The sauce is rich and thick, clinging to the meat. A pinch of fresh green parsley is scattered over the top. The background features a dark wood bistro table with a clean white cotton napkin and a small side plate of crusty baguette. Natural, even lighting highlights the velvety texture of the sauce and the rustic, braised appearance of the vegetables. The entire plate is visible with elegant negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty French baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of the same red wine used in the braise
Serve in wide, shallow bowls

ingredients.name: dry red wine (Pinot Noir or Burgundy)

instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken in a heavy pot over medium-high heat until skin is golden. Remove from pot.
Fry bacon lardons in the same pot until crisp.
Add whole pearl onions and whole mushrooms to the bacon fat. Brown for 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Return chicken to the pot. Pour in red wine and chicken stock.
Add thyme and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise over low heat for 30 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Mix butter and flour into a smooth paste.
Whisk the paste into the simmering liquid to thicken the sauce.
Simmer for 5 minutes until glossy. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Use a high-quality dry red wine for the best flavor profile
Ensure the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tomato Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. The penne pasta is coated in a luscious, creamy reddish-orange tomato sauce, forming a gently mounded pile. Nestled within and atop the pasta are several golden-brown, seared chicken medallions, cut into thick, substantial chunks, showcasing their tender interior. The dish is garnished with vibrant green chopped fresh parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space around the food. A standard silver fork and knife rest beside the plate on a white cotton napkin. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a casual yet refined bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with standard flatware.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside. Let rest 5 minutes.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100 ml pasta water.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Sauté diced onion 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream and American cheese slices until cheese is fully melted and sauce is smooth.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency is reached.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions or substantial chunks.
Serve pasta onto plates. Arrange chicken medallions on top of the pasta. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Turkey Thigh and Fermented Root Vegetable Hash
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty, rustic hash presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. Braised turkey thigh chunks, roughly 4-5 cm, are nestled among diced, earthy-toned root vegetables – roasted potatoes, carrots, and parsnips, each retaining distinct shapes and soft textures. Interspersed are vibrant, tangier pieces of lacto-fermented carrots, adding pops of brighter orange. The hash has a natural, slightly moist sheen from the rich turkey stock reduction. A few shards of golden-brown, shatteringly crisp turkey skin are strategically placed atop the hash, providing textural contrast. Fresh rosemary sprigs and thyme leaves are scattered sparingly for aromatic garnish. The plate is largely negative space, emphasizing the natural beauty and warmth of the ingredients. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, diffused natural light from the side, creating a clean, inviting, and sustainable aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Carefully remove skin from turkey thighs. Reserve skin. Debone thighs. Cut turkey meat into 4-5 cm chunks.
Place turkey skin on a baking tray. Season with salt and pepper. Bake for 15-20 minutes until golden and crispy. Remove, drain on paper towel, break into shards. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add turkey meat chunks. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove turkey, set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine, if using. Deglaze the pot, scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Return turkey meat to the pot. Add diced potatoes, carrots, and parsnips.
Pour in turkey stock and apple cider vinegar. Add rosemary and thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until turkey is tender and vegetables are soft.
Remove rosemary and thyme sprigs. Stir in lacto-fermented carrots.
Continue to simmer uncovered for 5-10 minutes to allow liquid to reduce slightly, creating a thicker hash consistency.
Season hash with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, topped with crispy turkey skin shards.
notes: Turkey bones can be used to make fresh turkey stock, aligning with zero-waste principles.
Lacto-fermented carrots can be prepared at home in advance or purchased.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Mayo Baked Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown baked chicken thigh, generously topped with a bubbly, melted mixture of grated cheese, diced red tomatoes, and translucent white onions. The cheese topping is slightly caramelized at the edges, revealing the vibrant red of the tomatoes and the soft texture of the onions. The chicken is presented whole, moist and tender, on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A casually folded plain cloth napkin is positioned to the side. Natural, soft kitchen light illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and inviting warmth. The overall scene is homely and unpretentious.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet or baking dish over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 2-3 minutes per side until lightly browned.
Remove skillet from heat.
In a medium bowl, combine mayonnaise, grated cheese, diced onion, and diced tomato. Mix thoroughly.
Spoon the cheese-mayonnaise mixture evenly over the top of each seared chicken thigh.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C and topping is golden and bubbly.
Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A 'Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Rice Bowl' is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an off-white tone, resting on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. At the center, a soft mound of earthy brown rice forms the base. Arranged naturally around the rice are golden-brown, seared chicken chunks (3-4cm), exhibiting a crisp exterior and tender interior. Vibrantly colored quick-pickled julienned carrots and thinly sliced red onions are artfully placed, offering bright orange and deep purple accents and a crisp texture. Small, diced pieces of sautéed yellow onion and carrot add subtle cooked elements. A light drizzle of natural pan juices adds moisture. The dish is garnished sparingly with a few fresh, roughly chopped green parsley leaves, providing a touch of natural freshness. The composition is clean, with ample negative space. A simple, undyed linen napkin and a small, green potted plant are visible in the soft, natural light, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm as a complete main course.
instructions: Prepare quick-pickled vegetables: Thinly slice red onion. Julienne one carrot. In a small saucepan, combine 250ml water, 125ml white vinegar, 15g salt, and 10g sugar. Bring to a boil, stirring until salt and sugar dissolve. Pour hot brine over red onion and julienned carrot in a heatproof jar. Let cool, then refrigerate.

Cook brown rice: Rinse 250g brown rice. Combine with 500ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Prepare chicken: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4cm chunks. Season with salt and black pepper.

Sear chicken: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks in a single layer. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Reduce heat to medium. Cook chicken until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Sauté vegetables: Dice yellow onion and remaining carrot. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same pan. Add diced yellow onion and carrot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Combine: Pour vegetable broth into the pan with sautéed vegetables. Bring to a simmer. Return chicken to the pan. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Assemble bowls: Divide cooked brown rice among four bowls. Arrange chicken chunks and sautéed vegetables around the rice. Drain quick-pickled red onion and carrot. Place a generous portion of pickled vegetables alongside the chicken and rice. Garnish with fresh, roughly chopped parsley or cilantro.
notes: For zero-waste cooking, use vegetable scraps (onion peels, carrot tops, etc.) to make homemade vegetable broth for this recipe.
The quick-pickled vegetables can be prepared up to a week in advance and stored in the refrigerator.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Apples and Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single bone-in pork chop, golden-brown and pan-seared, rests on an everyday off-white ceramic plate. Adjacent to the chop are tender, lightly caramelized apple wedges and soft, translucent onion slices, some slightly overlapping the pork. A modest drizzle of the rich pan sauce lightly coats the pork and surrounding ingredients. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley. The plate is placed on a well-used, rustic wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. A plain, folded linen napkin sits nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a relaxed, lived-in family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with mashed potatoes or creamy polenta.
Accompany with steamed green beans or roasted root vegetables.

ingredients.name: Large firm apple (e.g., Honeycrisp, Fuji), cored and cut into 8 wedges

instructions: Pat pork chops dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear pork chops for 4-5 minutes per side until deeply golden brown. Reduce heat if browning too quickly.
Transfer chops to a plate. Set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Reduce heat to medium.
Add onion slices and apple wedges to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Stir in fresh thyme sprigs. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Return pork chops to the skillet with the apple and onion mixture. Ensure chops are nestled in the sauce.
Cover skillet and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until pork reaches an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F).
Remove from heat. Let chops rest in the skillet for 5 minutes.
Remove thyme sprigs. Taste pan sauce and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve pork chops with apples and onions, drizzled with pan sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best results, use thick-cut pork chops to prevent drying out.
Adjust cooking time based on the thickness of your pork chops and desired doneness.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Rigatoni with Sausage and Three Cheeses
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Baked Rigatoni with Sausage and Three Cheeses rests in a pristine white porcelain deep bowl, centered on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface. The dish presents a rich, golden-brown crust of melted, bubbly mozzarella cheese on top, with inviting peeks of tender, ridged rigatoni pasta, deep red tomato sauce, and creamy white cheese mixture beneath. The sausage is crumbled throughout the sauce, providing textural contrast. A scattering of vibrant green fresh basil leaves, some whole and some in small pieces, garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The composition is clean and balanced, professional yet approachable. Beside the bowl, a classic silver fork and knife are neatly placed. A folded, light grey cotton napkin sits elegantly to the left. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro atmosphere with natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's warmth and inviting textures. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.

ingredients.name: Italian Sausage (mild or hot, casings removed)

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook rigatoni in salted water until al dente, about 8 minutes. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add sausage, break into crumbles. Cook until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes (if using). Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 15 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine ricotta cheese, cottage cheese, 50 g grated Parmesan, egg, and 30 g chopped fresh basil. Mix well.
Add cooked rigatoni to the tomato sauce. Stir to coat pasta evenly.
Spread half of the sauced rigatoni mixture into a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Spoon dollops of the cheese mixture over the pasta layer.
Top with half of the shredded mozzarella.
Repeat layers: remaining rigatoni, remaining cheese mixture, remaining mozzarella.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, until bubbly and mozzarella is melted and golden brown.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is a warm, pale yellow hue, studded with tender, golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2cm) and sautéed earthy brown mushroom slices. Finely diced onion pieces are visible throughout the creamy rice. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the top, alongside delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese. The dish has a natural, organic arrangement, showcasing its rich texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with classic silver Italian flatware (fork and spoon) placed beside it, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same pot.
Sauté finely diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, ensuring all grains are coated.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add one ladleful (about 250ml) of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly and wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is creamy and al dente, stir in cooked chicken.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra shaved Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken Alfredo Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous, inviting portion of creamy fettuccine Alfredo is piled naturally on a round, rustic ceramic plate. The pasta is coated in a rich, velvety white sauce. Irregularly shaped, golden-brown seared chicken chunks (approximately 2-3 cm) are nestled amongst and on top of the pasta. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley adds a touch of color. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple fork and knife beside the plate. A casually placed cloth napkin and warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures complete the homely family kitchen setting. The plate is adequately filled, showcasing the natural textures and inviting warmth of the comfort food.
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Cook fettuccine according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120 ml pasta water.
Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden-brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. If sauce is too thick, add a splash of reserved pasta water.
Add cooked fettuccine and seared chicken chunks to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Adjust sauce consistency with reserved pasta water as needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato & Zucchini Panzanella Salad with Crispy Beef Crumbles
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, placed on a light reclaimed wood table. The composition is minimalistic, highlighting the natural beauty of each ingredient. Quartered heirloom tomatoes in shades of red and yellow are nestled among vibrant green zucchini slices and thin purple red onion slivers. Cooked ditalini pasta adds a creamy texture, interspersed with golden, crispy sourdough croutons. A scattering of finely diced, crispy beef crumbles provides a savory accent without dominating the plate. Fresh basil and parsley leaves are gently integrated, adding bursts of green. The dressing lightly coats the ingredients, enhancing their natural colors. The plate features ample negative space, creating an uncrowded, clean aesthetic. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige and a subtle plant in the background complete the eco-conscious setup under soft natural lighting.

ingredients.name: Grass-fed beef (e.g., flank steak or sirloin)

instructions: Slice zucchini and red onion very thinly. Prepare a quick pickling brine: combine 120 ml water, 60 ml apple cider vinegar, 5 ml salt, and a pinch of sugar. Pour over sliced zucchini and half of the red onion. Let sit for at least 30 minutes.
Cut stale sourdough bread into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toast in a pan over medium heat until golden and crispy. Set aside.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to cool. Drizzle with a little olive oil to prevent sticking.
Cut beef into very small, 0.5 cm dice. Heat a pan over medium-high heat. Add beef and cook until crispy and browned. Season with salt and pepper. Drain excess fat. Set aside.
Chop fresh basil and parsley. Quarter or halve the mixed heirloom tomatoes.
Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 30 ml olive oil, fermented vegetable brine, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine cooled pasta, pickled zucchini, pickled red onion, remaining fresh red onion, and mixed tomatoes. Add toasted sourdough cubes and chopped herbs.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Divide salad among four plates. Garnish each serving with a small portion of crispy beef crumbles. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Umami Mushroom Risotto and Quick-Pickled Red Onion
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, matte white ceramic plate, embodying a minimalistic and eco-conscious aesthetic. A generous, fluid pool of creamy, light brown Umami Mushroom Risotto forms the base, its natural texture visible. Nestled organically atop the risotto, a golden-brown, pan-seared chicken thigh, unsliced, showcases its tender, cooked surface. The chicken's natural shape is preserved, avoiding any fanned arrangements. Thinly sliced, vibrant purple Quick-Pickled Red Onion pieces are scattered sparingly over the risotto, providing a contrasting pop of color and delicate texture. A light sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green chives adds a final touch of natural freshness. The entire composition is clean and uncluttered, with ample white space on the plate. The scene is set on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, with an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone, under soft, diffused natural lighting. A single, refined restaurant portion is depicted.
instructions: Prepare Quick-Pickled Red Onion: Combine vinegar, water, sugar, and 5g salt in a small saucepan. Heat until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Place thinly sliced red onion in a heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over onions. Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.

Sear Chicken: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs flat. Sear for 6-8 minutes until deep golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Flip and cook for another 5-7 minutes, or until cooked through. Remove chicken from skillet, set aside, and rest.

Start Risotto: In the same skillet (add more olive oil if needed), melt 30 g butter with 30 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced yellow onion. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and finely chopped mushroom stems (if using) or a small portion of the sliced mushrooms. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add Rice and Wine: Add Arborio rice to the skillet. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges. Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed.

Cook Risotto: Add hot vegetable broth, one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly. Wait until each ladleful is almost completely absorbed before adding the next. Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is creamy and al dente.
Add Mushrooms: With the last two ladles of broth, add the remaining thinly sliced mushrooms to the risotto. Cook until tender.
Finish Risotto: Remove from heat. Stir in 60 g Parmesan cheese (if using) and 30 g cold butter. Season with salt and pepper to taste. The risotto should be fluid and creamy.

Plate: Spoon a generous portion of warm risotto onto each plate. Place a seared chicken thigh naturally on top or alongside the risotto. Garnish with a few spoonfuls of quick-pickled red onion and a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley or chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Pork Loin with Crispy Patatas Bravas
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared pork loin medallions and crispy patatas bravas is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pork, cut into thick, irregular medallions, exhibits a deep golden-brown crust from searing, revealing a tender, pale interior. Adjacent, 2-3 cm potato cubes are golden and visibly crisp. A vibrant, rich red bravas sauce is artfully drizzled over the potatoes and pooled slightly beside the pork. Fresh, coarsely chopped flat-leaf parsley is scattered sparingly for a pop of green. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and a small, rustic ceramic ramekin filled with additional bravas sauce. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Accompany with a glass of robust Spanish red wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place potato cubes in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Simmer 5 minutes until slightly tender. Drain well.
Toss drained potatoes with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast 25-30 minutes until golden and crispy.
While potatoes roast, prepare bravas sauce. Heat 15ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock and red wine vinegar. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Transfer sauce to a blender. Blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Pat pork loin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork loin 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast pork 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F).
Remove pork from oven. Rest 5 minutes on a cutting board.
Slice pork into 2 cm thick medallions.
To serve, arrange crispy potatoes on plates. Place pork medallions beside potatoes. Drizzle generously with bravas sauce. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti con Calamari e Pomodorini
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A neat mound of golden spaghetti forms the base. Tender, translucent white squid rings and whole tentacles are interspersed within and artfully placed on top of the pasta. Vibrant red cherry tomato halves are scattered generously, adding pops of color and juicy texture. A delicate sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley garnishes the entire dish, enhancing its freshness. A final drizzle of golden extra virgin olive oil adds a subtle sheen. The composition is balanced, allowing for moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard Italian flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's natural colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a light-bodied white wine, such as Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.

ingredients.name: Squid
ingredients.quantity: 300 g, cleaned, body cut into 1 cm rings, tentacles left whole

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta cooking water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sliced garlic and chili flakes. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Add squid to the skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring frequently, until opaque and tender. Do not overcook.
Pour in white wine. Cook for 1 minute, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Add halved cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes until they begin to soften and release their juices.
Add drained spaghetti to the skillet with the squid and tomatoes. Add half of the reserved pasta water and half of the chopped parsley.
Toss everything together vigorously for 1-2 minutes, allowing pasta to absorb sauce. Add more pasta water if needed to create a light sauce.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Divide spaghetti into two portions. Garnish each with remaining fresh parsley and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure squid is cooked quickly to remain tender; overcooking makes it rubbery.
The reserved pasta water is crucial for creating a silky sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Chicken Roulade with Creamy Potato-Cheddar Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, classic white porcelain dinner plate. The main focus is the Stuffed Chicken Roulade, sliced into thick, substantial medallions, revealing the vibrant cross-section of pork, sausage, rice, apple, and onion stuffing. The chicken skin is a rich golden-brown from searing, contrasting with the lighter, moist interior. Beside the roulade sits a generous, neatly mounded portion of creamy potato-cheddar pasta, its pale yellow hue indicating richness, with visible short pasta shapes coated in a smooth, thick sauce. A light scattering of fresh chopped parsley or chives adds a pop of green over both the roulade and pasta, enhancing visual freshness. A small, vibrant pile of mixed salad greens, lightly dressed, sits elegantly on the side of the plate, providing a fresh counterpoint. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple, natural wooden table surface, a folded white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating soft shadows and highlighting textures without harshness.

ingredients.name: cooked sausage, crumbled or finely diced

instructions: Prepare Chicken Roulade Stuffing: Heat 5ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add pork mince and crumbled sausage. Cook, breaking up meat, until browned. Drain excess fat. Stir in diced apple and cooked rice. Cook for another 3-5 minutes until apple softens slightly. Remove from heat. Stir in chopped parsley, salt, and pepper. Let cool.

Assemble Roulades: Pound each chicken thigh flat to an even thickness, about 1 cm. Spread a quarter of the stuffing mixture over each thigh, leaving a small border. Roll up tightly. Secure with kitchen twine or toothpicks.

Cook Roulades: Heat remaining 10ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear roulades on all sides until golden brown. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven, cover loosely with foil, and rest for 5 minutes.

Cook Pasta and Potatoes: While roulades bake, cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain. In a separate pot, boil diced potato until very tender, about 10-12 minutes. Drain well. Mash or purée the cooked potato.

Make Potato-Cheddar Sauce: In a saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook for 1 minute to form a roux. Gradually whisk in milk until smooth and thickened. Stir in mashed potato and grated cheddar cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine Pasta: Add drained pasta to the potato-cheddar sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Prepare Salad: In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper for vinaigrette. Toss with mixed salad greens just before serving.

Serve: Remove twine/toothpicks from roulades. Slice each roulade into thick medallions (2-3 per person). Plate a portion of creamy potato-cheddar pasta. Arrange roulade medallions beside the pasta. Serve with a side of mixed greens.

recipes.recipe_name: Cabbage & Lentil Salad with Poached Chicken and Parmesan Crisps
recipes.visual_description: The Cabbage & Lentil Salad is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. At the center, a mound of finely shredded, vibrant green and purple fermented cabbage forms the base, its natural tanginess evident in its slightly softened texture. Interspersed within the cabbage are perfectly cooked, tender green lentils, adding a subtle earthy brown hue and soft texture. Around the base, small, irregularly shaped chunks of poached chicken, glistening white, are thoughtfully placed, providing a lean protein accent without dominating the plate. Thinly sliced, crisp orange carrots and delicate pink radish rounds are artfully scattered, contributing pops of color and fresh crunch. A light vinaigrette glistens on the ingredients, binding them together. Two to three golden-brown, irregular parmesan crisps stand upright or lean against the salad, offering a savory, brittle contrast. Fresh dill and parsley sprigs are sparingly placed for a touch of vibrant green. The overall plating is clean and minimalist, allowing natural textures and colors to shine, with ample white space on the plate. The setting features a light, textured bamboo table surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, diffused natural light from the side, with a hint of green foliage in the clean background.
instructions: Prepare fermented cabbage: Finely shred the white cabbage. Place in a large bowl. Add 10 g salt. Massage cabbage vigorously for 5-10 minutes until water releases. Pack tightly into a clean jar, pressing down to submerge cabbage in its brine. Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature for 3-7 days, burping daily, until desired tanginess achieved. Refrigerate.
Cook lentils: Rinse green lentils. Place in a saucepan with 600 ml cold water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender. Drain well. Set aside to cool.

Poach chicken: Place chicken breast in a small saucepan. Cover with cold water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Cool completely. Cut chicken into small, irregular chunks.

Make parmesan crisps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Grate parmesan cheese. Form small mounds of cheese on the parchment paper. Bake for 5-7 minutes, until golden and crispy. Cool completely on the sheet. Break into irregular pieces.
Prepare vegetables: Peel carrots. Thinly slice carrots into rounds or julienne. Thinly slice radishes into rounds.
Make dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, 5 g salt, and 2 g black pepper. Adjust seasoning to taste.

Assemble salad: In a large bowl, combine cooled fermented cabbage, cooked lentils, carrot slices, and radish slices. Pour dressing over. Toss gently to combine. Finely chop fresh dill and parsley. Add to the salad. Toss again.
Plate and serve: Divide salad among four plates. Arrange small chicken chunks among the salad. Garnish each plate with 2-3 parmesan crisp pieces.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Roasted Chicken and Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of One-Pan Roasted Chicken and Vegetables is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. Two golden-brown, roasted chicken drumsticks, with crispy skin, are placed centrally. Around the chicken, a colorful medley of roasted vegetables is scattered naturally. Bright green broccoli florets, some with slightly charred tips, are interspersed with earthy brown mushroom slices. Deep red cherry tomatoes, some burst open, add pops of color and juicy texture. Caramelized red onion wedges and minced garlic cloves are visible amongst the vegetables. A light dusting of melted, golden-brown cheddar cheese covers parts of the chicken and vegetables. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A casually placed, folded beige linen napkin and a simple fork and knife are beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and colors of the home-cooked meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Trim broccoli into small florets. Slice mushrooms. Cut red onion into 2cm wedges. Mince garlic.
Place chicken drumsticks, broccoli florets, mushroom slices, red onion wedges, and minced garlic on a large baking sheet.
Drizzle ingredients evenly with olive oil. Season generously with dried oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Toss all ingredients on the baking sheet to ensure even coating.
Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender.
Remove baking sheet from oven. Sprinkle grated cheddar cheese evenly over the chicken and vegetables.
Return to oven for 5 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Serve immediately.
notes: For extra flavor, squeeze fresh lemon juice over the dish before serving.
This dish pairs well with a side of simple rice or crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Peruvian Chicken and Potato Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Peruvian Chicken and Potato Soup is presented in a deep, clean white ceramic bowl, resting on a simple light wooden table. The soup displays a rich, creamy yellow hue from the aji amarillo, with visible chunks of soft, white potato and tender shredded chicken pieces. The surface is gently garnished with two half-moon slices of hard-boiled egg, neatly placed on one side, and a light sprinkle of vibrant green chopped cilantro on the other. The soup's texture appears smooth and inviting. The bowl is positioned slightly off-center, allowing for moderate negative space. Beside the bowl, traditional flatware is arranged. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and creamy texture. The background hints at a modern bistro, clean and uncluttered.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally served with a side of steamed white rice
Garnish with black olives or additional lime wedges

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped, for garnish

instructions: Place chicken breasts in a pot. Cover with chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature, about 15-20 minutes. Remove chicken. Shred finely. Reserve broth.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Boil in lightly salted water until tender, about 10-12 minutes. Drain.
Soak bread slices in a small amount of evaporated milk until soft. Mash into a paste.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced red onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in aji amarillo paste. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly. This is the sofrito base.
Gradually add 500 millilitres of reserved chicken broth to the sofrito, stirring to combine. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the mashed bread paste to the soup. Whisk well until smooth. Add remaining evaporated milk. Stir.

Add shredded chicken and cooked potato cubes to the soup. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and chopped walnuts. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish each serving with hard-boiled egg slices and fresh chopped parsley or cilantro.
notes: Adjust aji amarillo paste quantity for desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Ragu with Truffle Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a generous swirl of golden tagliatelle, richly coated in a deep red Braised Beef Ragu. Prominent, tender chunks of slow-cooked beef, fork-shredded within the sauce, showcase their caramelized edges and succulent texture. The rustic sauce, flecked with finely diced vegetables, gleams. A generous snowfall of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese crowns the pasta, offering a pale contrast. Delicate, thin shavings of fresh black truffle are scattered over the top, their dark patterns providing a luxurious accent. A vibrant green parsley sprig offers a final color pop. The dish is served on a clean, classic white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed with moderate negative space. The entire plate is visible, presented on a simple wooden table, with a crisp white cotton napkin and standard flatware beside it, under soft, natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty ciabatta bread for dipping in the ragu.
A simple mixed green salad with a light vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Black truffle
ingredients.quantity: 15 g fresh, or 15 ml black truffle oil/paste

instructions: Season beef chunks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook until reduced by half.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, Dijon mustard, beef broth, bay leaf, and thyme. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot and transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove bay leaf and thyme stems. Shred beef chunks directly in the pot using two forks, or leave in large chunks. Stir to combine beef with the rich sauce. Keep warm.
Cook tagliatelle according to package instructions in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving 120 ml of pasta water. Add drained pasta to the ragu, tossing to coat. If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water.
Divide pasta and ragu among four plates.
Grate fresh Pecorino Romano cheese over each serving.
Shave fresh black truffle over each plate, or drizzle with truffle oil/paste.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Spicy Chicken Noodles
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Korean Spicy Chicken Noodles is presented in a modern, deep white ceramic bowl, showcasing a vibrant composition. Thick udon noodles are generously coated in a glossy, rich red-orange gochujang sauce. Tender, browned chicken chunks are interspersed throughout. Bright green broccoli florets and earthy sliced cremini mushrooms and translucent yellow onion slices provide contrasting colors and textures. A delicate layer of melted, slightly bubbly mozzarella cheese lightly blankets a portion of the noodles and chicken. The dish is topped with thinly sliced bright green spring onions and a sprinkle of white toasted sesame seeds. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a pair of dark wooden chopsticks placed neatly beside it and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and inviting appeal. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere, allowing the food to be the focal point without distraction. The entire bowl is visible, with appropriate negative space around it.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of kimchi.
Offer a small bowl of pickled radish (danmuji).
Accompany with a traditional Korean beverage like soju or makgeolli.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Whisk together gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, brown sugar, and chicken broth in a small bowl. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cook udon noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or deep skillet over medium-high heat.

Add chicken chunks to the hot wok. Cook, stirring occasionally, until chicken is browned and cooked through, approximately 6-8 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from wok and set aside.
Add sliced onion to the same wok. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add broccoli florets and sliced mushrooms to the wok. Stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Add cooked udon noodles.
Pour the prepared gochujang sauce over the chicken, vegetables, and noodles. Toss well to coat all ingredients evenly.
Continue to cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly and flavors to meld.
Remove from heat. Sprinkle shredded mozzarella cheese over the top. Cover for 1 minute to allow cheese to melt.
Serve immediately in individual bowls. Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust gochujang quantity to control spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Tomato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single baked chicken breast sits on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate. The chicken is topped with a golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted cheddar cheese, beneath which a creamy, baked mayonnaise layer is visible. Tender, softened rounds of red tomato are nestled into the cheese and mayonnaise. The chicken itself is presented as a whole piece, or in 2-3 thick, natural chunks. Thinly sliced, translucent onion half-moons form a soft bed underneath the chicken, their edges slightly caramelized. A light sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley adds a touch of color. The plate is adequately filled, showcasing a modest, homely portion. The ceramic plate, with its subtle imperfections, rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A folded, plain linen napkin in a neutral tone is casually placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting light, characteristic of a cozy kitchen or dining area. The background is soft and unobtrusive, hinting at a lived-in, family kitchen atmosphere with everyday flatware visible.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Lightly grease a large baking dish with olive oil.
Spread the thinly sliced onion evenly across the bottom of the baking dish.
Season chicken breasts with salt, black pepper, and garlic powder on both sides.
Place the seasoned chicken breasts over the onion slices in the baking dish.
Evenly spread mayonnaise over the top of each chicken breast.
Arrange the sliced tomato rounds over the mayonnaise layer on each chicken breast.
Sprinkle the shredded cheddar cheese generously over the tomatoes and chicken.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and the cheese is golden brown and bubbling.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

The chicken is topped with a golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted cheddar cheese, beneath which a creamy, baked mayonnaise layer is visible. recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon-Garlic White Wine Sauce and Cucumber-Dill Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown with a slightly crisp exterior, rests on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. It is presented as a whole piece, glistening with a vibrant lemon-garlic white wine pan sauce drizzled generously over it. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of fresh cucumber-dill salad adds a burst of green and white. The cucumber is cut into 1 cm half-moon slices, mixed with thinly sliced red onion and abundant chopped fresh dill, showing a fresh, crisp texture. A sprinkle of crumbled white feta cheese is visible within the salad. The dish is garnished with bright green chopped fresh parsley and finely grated yellow lemon zest. The overall color palette is inviting, with golden chicken, clear light sauce, and verdant salad. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a refined individual portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
Pair with a light-bodied white wine, such as a Sauvignon Blanc or Pinot Grigio.
Offer a side of simple rice pilaf or roasted potatoes.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to skillet. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze skillet, scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half, about 2 minutes.
Add chicken stock and lemon juice. Bring to a simmer. Cook until sauce slightly thickens, about 3 minutes.
Return chicken to skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Keep warm.
Prepare cucumber-dill salad: Halve cucumber lengthwise. Scoop out seeds. Cut cucumber into 1 cm thick half-moon slices.
Combine cucumber slices, thinly sliced red onion, and chopped fresh dill in a bowl.
Drizzle with a small amount of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss gently. Add crumbled feta if desired.
Plate chicken breast. Spoon white wine sauce over chicken. Place a generous portion of cucumber-dill salad beside the chicken.
Garnish with fresh parsley and lemon zest.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
Adjust lemon and dill quantities in the salad to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Braised Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The Tuscan Braised Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A single, golden-brown braised chicken thigh, skin-side up, rests prominently. The chicken is cooked whole, not sliced. It is surrounded by a rich, rustic sauce composed of tender, diced red bell peppers and onions, and crushed tomatoes. The sauce boasts deep red and orange hues, with visible pieces of cooked vegetables. A sprig of fresh rosemary or a sprinkle of bright green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, providing a fresh contrast. The plate is placed on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin and classic European flatware are positioned beside the plate, completing a casual yet refined restaurant-style setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and vibrant colors of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with creamy polenta or pasta
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large braising pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden-brown and crisp, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pan.
Add diced onion and diced red bell pepper to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine (if using). Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce by half, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, rosemary sprig, and thyme sprig. Bring the sauce to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Carefully remove chicken from the pan. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Adjust seasoning of the sauce if needed. Remove herb sprigs.
Serve chicken with generous portions of the braised sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Lemon Herb Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of One-Pan Lemon Herb Chicken and Rice is presented on a rustic, round, cream-colored ceramic plate. A whole, roasted chicken thigh, with crispy, golden-brown skin, rests atop a generous bed of fluffy, pale-yellow long-grain rice. The rice is tender, with individual grains visible, and subtly mixed with finely diced white onion and small specks of minced garlic and dried oregano. Two thin, bright yellow lemon slices are casually placed on the rice, next to the chicken. A scattering of vibrant green, chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley garnishes the dish, adding a fresh contrast. The plate fills approximately two-thirds of the frame, leaving comfortable negative space. The setting is a well-worn, light brown wooden kitchen table. A simple, folded linen napkin in a muted blue hue is casually placed to the left of the plate. Standard, polished metal flatware (a fork and a knife) lie to the right. A clear glass tumbler with water is positioned in the background. Lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread to soak up the flavorful pan juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Season chicken generously with salt, pepper, and 5 ml of dried oregano.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 5-7 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy.
Flip chicken. Sear for 2 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook for 3-5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and remaining 5 ml of dried oregano to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly to lightly toast the grains.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Nestle the seared chicken thighs into the rice mixture, skin-side up.
Arrange lemon slices around the chicken and rice.
Cover the skillet tightly with a lid or foil.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until rice is tender and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove skillet from oven. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The resting period allows the rice to fully absorb moisture and the chicken juices to redistribute, ensuring a tender and flavorful result.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sirloin with Grains of Paradise Reduction and Creamy Taleggio Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of pan-seared sirloin steak, presented in thick, rustic chunks, rests beside a generous, free-flowing mound of creamy, golden Taleggio polenta. The beef, seared to a deep mahogany crust, reveals a juicy, rosy interior. A rich, dark brown reduction sauce, infused with grains of paradise, is elegantly spooned over the beef, catching the light. The vibrant green of finely chopped chives sprinkles over the dish, adding a fresh contrast. The plate is clean white porcelain, set on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and standard silver cutlery complete the modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting illuminates the textures and colors, creating an inviting, professional presentation with ample negative space.
instructions: Pat sirloin steaks dry. Season generously with ground grains of paradise, sea salt, and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear steaks for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Use tongs to sear edges briefly.
Transfer steaks to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium. Add 15g butter to the pan. Add diced shallots and sauté until softened, about 2-3 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with Worcestershire sauce, scraping up any browned bits. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half, about 5-7 minutes, until slightly thickened. Stir in remaining 15g butter. Keep warm.
For polenta, bring 1 litre water or vegetable broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Slowly whisk in quick-cooking polenta, ensuring no lumps.
Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 5-7 minutes until polenta is creamy and thickened.
Remove from heat. Stir in diced Taleggio cheese and grated Parmesan until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice rested sirloin steaks into thick chunks or medallions.
Ladle creamy polenta onto plates. Arrange sliced sirloin alongside or on top of the polenta.
Spoon grains of paradise reduction over the beef. Garnish with fresh chopped chives. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure beef reaches desired doneness; internal temperature for medium-rare is 57-60°C (135-140°F).
Resting the beef is crucial for juiciness and even distribution of internal temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Pan-Seared Chicken with White Wine Garlic Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Pan-Seared Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed. A glossy, pale golden-brown white wine garlic sauce generously coats the chicken and pools around its base. Alongside the chicken, a vibrant mound of fresh cucumber herb salsa is neatly arranged. The salsa features small, crisp cubes of bright green cucumber, intermingled with finely chopped verdant parsley and dill. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits beside the chicken. The textures are varied: tender chicken, smooth sauce, and crisp, fresh salsa. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and a water glass are subtly placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a clean, inviting scene.

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.quantity: 1, half for juice, half for wedges

instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season chicken generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken to skillet. Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a plate. Cover loosely.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to skillet. Add sliced garlic. Sauté garlic for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Pour white wine into skillet. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Add chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook until sauce slightly thickens, about 5-7 minutes.
While sauce simmers, prepare cucumber salsa. In a medium bowl, combine diced cucumber, chopped parsley, and chopped dill.
Squeeze half a lemon over cucumber mixture. Drizzle with a small amount of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss gently.
Return cooked chicken to skillet with sauce. Turn chicken to coat. Simmer for 1 minute to reheat.
Serve chicken immediately. Spoon white wine garlic sauce over chicken. Top with a generous portion of cucumber herb salsa. Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Pork Loin with Crispy Potatoes and Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted pork loin is artfully arranged on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pork, cut into thick, succulent chunks, displays a beautiful golden-brown sear on its exterior and a tender, slightly pink interior. Accompanying the pork are golden-crisp 2 cm potato cubes, perfectly roasted and scattered around the main protein. Deep amber, glistening caramelized onions are nestled beside the pork, adding a touch of sweetness and rich color. A glossy, reduced pan sauce is lightly spooned over the pork, enhancing its savory appeal. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, all under natural, even lighting, creating a modern bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the delicious pan sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat pork loin dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Wash and cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes. In a large bowl, toss potatoes with 30 ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and finely chopped leaves from one rosemary sprig and two thyme sprigs. Spread in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 25 minutes.
While potatoes roast, heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork loin on all sides until deeply golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Transfer the pan with the seared pork to the oven with the potatoes. Roast pork for 15-20 minutes, or until an internal temperature of 68°C is reached. (Temperature will rise to 75°C while resting).
Remove pork from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil and let rest for at least 10 minutes.
While pork rests, thinly slice the onions. Mince garlic cloves.

In a separate medium pan, melt butter over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender. Add minced garlic during the last 5 minutes of cooking.

For the pan sauce: Place the pork searing pan (from the oven) over medium heat on the stovetop. If using, add red wine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce by half. Add chicken or beef broth. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half again, until slightly thickened. Whisk in any accumulated juices from the resting pork. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice the rested pork loin into thick 2-3 cm chunks or medallions.

To plate: Arrange a portion of pork chunks, crispy potato cubes, and caramelized onions on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Spoon the warm pan sauce over the pork. Garnish with freshly chopped parsley or chives.
notes: Ensure pork rests properly after cooking to retain juiciness.
Adjust seasoning of all components to personal taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chili Chicken & Noodle Bowl
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a soft cream hue, set against a light, reclaimed wood table. A single portion of al dente egg noodles forms a natural, slightly mounded base, tossed lightly with a subtle, savory sauce. Above the noodles, three to four substantial, rustic chunks of seared chicken, each glazed with a deep red-orange fermented chili sauce, are artfully placed, showcasing their golden-brown crust and moist interior. Alongside the chicken, vibrant green broccoli florets, blanched to retain their crispness, are arranged organically, interspersed with earthy, pan-seared mushroom slices, their edges slightly caramelized. Finely grated pale yellow hard cheese lightly dusts a small section of the noodles and chicken, adding a textural contrast without overwhelming the natural palette. A small sprig of fresh herb is placed deliberately to one side as a singular, natural garnish. The composition is clean, with ample negative space around the elements, emphasizing each ingredient's natural beauty and texture. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, casting gentle shadows and highlighting the organic forms. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually draped beside the plate. The background is minimalist, featuring a hint of blurred green foliage from a houseplant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.

ingredients.name: Aged hard cheese (e.g., cheddar or Parmesan)

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut chicken into 3-4cm rustic chunks. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15ml neutral oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.

Reduce heat to medium. Add fermented hot sauce to the pan. Toss chicken to coat evenly. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and the glaze thickens. Remove chicken from pan.
Separate broccoli florets from stems. Finely chop the broccoli stems. Slice mushrooms.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli florets. Blanch for 2 minutes. Drain. Plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain again thoroughly.
In the same pan used for chicken, or a clean one, heat the remaining 15ml neutral oil. Add sliced mushrooms. Sear for 4-5 minutes until golden and tender. Season with salt.
Mince garlic cloves. Grate fresh ginger. In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame oil. Stir in minced garlic and grated ginger.
Cook egg noodles according to package instructions until al dente. Drain well.
Return drained noodles to the pot. Add the finely chopped broccoli stems and the prepared noodle sauce. Toss to combine thoroughly.
Divide the savory noodles among four individual serving bowls. Arrange the glazed chicken chunks, blanched broccoli florets, and seared mushroom slices artfully on top of the noodles.
Finely grate the aged hard cheese over the assembled dish. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is a warm, pale yellow hue, studded with tender, golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2cm) and sautéed earthy brown mushroom slices. Finely diced onion pieces are visible throughout the creamy rice. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the top, alongside delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese. The dish has a natural, organic arrangement, showcasing its rich texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with classic silver Italian flatware (fork and spoon) placed beside it, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same pot.
Sauté finely diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
