instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Reserve excess chicken skin for crispy salt if desired.
Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Wash and scrub carrots, parsnips, and potatoes. Cut carrots into thick batons. Cut parsnips into large wedges. Cut potatoes into rustic chunks.
In a large roasting pan, toss root vegetables with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add rosemary sprigs.
Place chicken thighs, skin-side up, on top of the vegetables in the roasting pan. Ensure chicken skin is not touching.
Roast for 30 minutes. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F) when done.

While chicken roasts, if making crispy chicken skin salt: Render reserved chicken skin in a dry pan over medium-low heat until very crispy and golden. Remove from pan, drain excess fat. Cool completely. Crumble or finely chop into a coarse salt-like texture. Mix with a pinch of salt.
After 30 minutes, remove pan from oven. Drizzle fermented garlic honey over the chicken thighs. Toss vegetables gently.
Return to oven and roast for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken skin is deeply golden and crispy, and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Vegetables should be tender and caramelized.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
Plate one chicken thigh per person with a portion of roasted root vegetables. Garnish lightly with crispy chicken skin salt.

recipes.recipe_name: Zero-Waste Fermented Chicken & Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: Individual shallow, wide ceramic bowls in earth tones hold the dish. A single, golden-brown seared chicken thigh, skin crispy and glistening, rests prominently on a fluffy mound of long-grain brown rice. Around the chicken, vibrant seasonal vegetables like bright green broccoli florets and orange carrot batons are artfully arranged in distinct, natural groupings, cooked to retain their tender-crisp texture. Small, contrasting pops of color and texture come from thinly sliced quick-pickled vegetable trimmings, scattered organically. A light drizzle of pan juices from the chicken adds a subtle sheen. The plate is clean, with ample negative space. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin, and a simple, handcrafted ceramic spoon. Soft, natural lighting highlights the ingredients' inherent beauty against a clean, minimalist background with subtle plant elements, creating an inviting, eco-conscious presentation.

ingredients.name: Mixed seasonal vegetables (e.g., broccoli florets, carrot batons, red bell pepper strips)
Vegetable trimmings for quick pickle (e.g., radish tops, cucumber ends, carrot peels), thinly sliced or julienned
Chicken bones/scraps (from thighs or other cuts) and additional vegetable scraps (onion ends, celery trimmings) for stock

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
For chicken stock: Place chicken bones/scraps and additional vegetable scraps in a pot. Cover with 1 litre water. Simmer 30 minutes. Strain stock. Discard solids.

For quick pickled vegetables: Combine 250ml water, 250ml white vinegar, 20g sugar, and 10g salt in a small pot. Bring to boil. Stir to dissolve. Let cool slightly. Place thinly sliced vegetable trimmings in a jar. Pour warm brine over. Seal. Refrigerate at least 30 minutes.

Rinse brown rice. In a medium pot, combine rice, 600ml chicken stock, 2 minced garlic cloves, and a pinch of salt. Bring to boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 35-40 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with fork.

Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down 8-10 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip. Add 2 smashed garlic cloves to skillet. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast 15-20 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken 5 minutes.
While chicken roasts, toss seasonal vegetables with remaining 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast in oven for 10-15 minutes until tender-crisp.

Spoon rice into individual shallow bowls. Place one chicken thigh on each rice portion. Arrange cooked seasonal vegetables and quick-pickled vegetables around chicken and rice. Drizzle with pan juices from chicken. Garnish with fresh herbs.

recipes.recipe_name: Keto Beef & Cabbage Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Keto Beef & Cabbage Skillet is centrally arranged on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. The dish features browned, crumbly ground beef mixed with tender, slightly wilted shredded green cabbage and soft diced onions. Components are naturally intermingled, forming a hearty mound. A light sprinkle of fresh, roughly chopped green parsley provides a vibrant contrast on top. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table. A simple metal fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, casting soft shadows. The background is a subtly blurred, homely kitchen setting, suggesting a relaxed family meal.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add diced yellow onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground beef to the skillet. Brown the beef, breaking it apart with a spoon. Cook until no pink remains, about 8-10 minutes.
Drain any excess fat from the skillet.
Stir in tomato paste, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add shredded green cabbage and beef broth to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Cover the skillet. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until cabbage is tender.
Remove lid. Increase heat slightly if needed to reduce liquid.
Taste and adjust seasoning as desired.
Serve hot. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Mustard Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Spicy Mustard Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The al dente penne pasta is neatly mounded, coated in a creamy, pale golden sauce. Interspersed within the pasta are prominent, irregularly cut, thick chunks of seared chicken, displaying a rich golden-brown exterior. Flecks of vibrant red chili and finely chopped fresh green parsley are scattered throughout, adding color contrast. A light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese crowns the dish. The overall composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. A silver fork and knife are placed to the right of the plate, resting on a folded white cotton napkin. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm thick chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Cook penne pasta in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 125 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and finely chopped red chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Dijon mustard and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Pour in heavy cream. Simmer for 2-3 minutes, allowing sauce to slightly thicken.
Return cooked chicken chunks to the skillet with the sauce. Add drained pasta.
Toss to coat pasta and chicken in the sauce. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water until desired consistency.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir half of the parsley into the pasta. Season with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining fresh parsley and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, fluid risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto forms an organic, slightly mounded pool in the center, exhibiting a rich, off-white color with flecks of golden-brown seared chicken chunks, earthy sliced mushrooms, and vibrant red chili pieces. The surface glistens, indicating its creamy texture, and is topped with a generous sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and bright green chopped parsley. The chicken chunks are irregularly shaped, showcasing the rustic searing. There is moderate negative space around the risotto on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's textures and colors against a soft, slightly blurred restaurant background. Traditional flatware (fork and spoon) are neatly arranged.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately after preparation. Risotto is traditionally enjoyed hot and fresh.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a crisp dry white wine.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breast or thigh

instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Season with salt and pepper. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the same pan. Add chopped onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chopped red chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until mushrooms release their liquid and start to brown, about 5-7 minutes.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is completely absorbed.
Add hot chicken stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait until each ladleful is almost completely absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
Continue adding stock and stirring until rice is creamy and al dente. It should be firm to the bite but not hard.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in cold butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously (mantecatura) to create a creamy, fluid consistency.
Gently fold in the seared chicken chunks.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.
notes: Constant stirring is crucial for releasing starch from the rice and achieving a creamy risotto.
Ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
The risotto should be loose and flowing, not stiff or dry.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom Risotto and Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom Risotto and Roasted Vegetables is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous, free-flowing mound of creamy, light beige mushroom risotto occupies the center, its texture smooth and inviting. Resting beside the risotto is a golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast, showcasing a tender, juicy interior. Around the chicken and risotto, a vibrant medley of roasted vegetables is artfully scattered: rustic chunks of golden-brown potatoes, bright yellow corn kernels, and vivid red halved cherry tomatoes, each with slightly caramelized edges. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley adds a final touch of color and freshness. The plate is well-proportioned with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware placed beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's fresh ingredients and appealing textures. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and approachable, embodying a casual dining aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp green salad dressed simply with olive oil and lemon.
Offer crusty bread for soaking up any remaining risotto.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (small, like new potatoes or fingerlings)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato chunks, corn kernels, and halved cherry tomatoes with 15ml olive oil, 2 minced garlic cloves, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast 20-25 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized.

Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest 5 minutes.

In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 30g butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook 5 minutes, until softened. Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves and sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes, until mushrooms release their liquid and brown.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir 1 minute, coating rice in butter. Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is absorbed.

Add warm chicken broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for liquid to be almost absorbed before adding next ladle. Continue for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is creamy and al dente. Risotto should be fluid.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Ladle creamy risotto onto plates. Place a pan-seared chicken breast or thick chicken chunks next to or on top of risotto. Arrange roasted potatoes, corn, and cherry tomatoes around the chicken and risotto. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
Stir risotto constantly for best creamy texture.
Use good quality chicken broth for maximum flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken and Beef Ragu with Pappardelle and Orange Gremolata
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Braised Chicken and Beef Ragu with Pappardelle is presented on a clean, wide-rimmed white porcelain pasta bowl. The golden pappardelle noodles are generously coated and tossed with the rich, deep red ragu. Visible chunks of tender, braised beef and chicken are nestled within the sauce, not fanned or shredded. A vibrant sprinkle of bright green gremolata, made from finely chopped fresh parsley and grated orange zest, adorns the top, alongside a delicate dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese. The dish displays varying textures: the al dente pasta, the succulent meat, and the fresh, aromatic gremolata. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware beside the bowl, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the sauce
Pair with a glass of dry red wine
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4-5 cm chunks. Cut beef chuck roast into 4-5 cm chunks.
Season chicken and beef chunks generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.

Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove and set aside. Sear chicken chunks until browned. Remove and set aside. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) during braising.
Add diced pancetta to the pot. Cook until crispy. Remove pancetta and set aside, leaving rendered fat in the pot.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook over medium heat for 8-10 minutes, until softened (soffritto).
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2-3 minutes until wine reduces slightly.
Return seared beef and chicken to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, bay leaves, and rosemary sprig.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 2-3 hours, or until meat is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaves and rosemary sprig. Gently shred or break apart larger pieces of meat with a fork. Stir in cooked pancetta.
While ragu simmers, prepare gremolata: finely chop parsley. Grate zest from the orange. Combine parsley and orange zest.
Cook pappardelle pasta according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with a sprinkle of orange gremolata and freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Slow cooking allows the flavors to meld and the meats to become exceptionally tender.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Chicken with White Beans and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, tender, golden-brown braised chicken thigh is centrally placed on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is nestled amongst a rustic, vibrant medley of creamy white cannellini beans, bright red diced tomatoes, and dark Kalamata olive halves. A few fresh green parsley leaves are scattered over the dish for a pop of color. The chicken retains its whole, natural shape. The background features a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, and a subtle, blurred modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s textures and rich colors. A lemon wedge is placed to the side, ready for squeezing. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the flavorful sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced red onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine, if using, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Reduce by half.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, chopped fresh oregano, and chopped fresh thyme. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in the liquid. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in drained cannellini beans and halved Kalamata olives. Cook for another 5 minutes to heat through.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with lemon wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Penne all'Arrabbiata
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Penne all'Arrabbiata is presented centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The penne pasta is uniformly coated in a vibrant, rustic red tomato sauce, flecked with small, dark red chili flakes. A generous sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green parsley adorns the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. A light drizzle of golden olive oil glistens on the sauce. The plating is organized yet natural, with moderate negative space around the pasta. The dish sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a silver fork and spoon placed to the right, and a folded white cotton napkin to the left. The scene is illuminated with natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere reminiscent of a modern Italian bistro.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Salt the water generously.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or wide pan over medium heat.
Add thinly sliced garlic and red chili flakes to the pan. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Do not brown the garlic.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes. Season with salt and black pepper.
Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly.
While the sauce simmers, add the penne pasta to the boiling water. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Drain the pasta, reserving 120ml of the pasta cooking water.
Add the cooked pasta directly to the tomato sauce in the skillet. Toss thoroughly to coat the pasta evenly.
Add reserved pasta water gradually, if needed, to achieve a desired sauce consistency. The sauce should cling to the pasta.
Stir in finely chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Corn Salsa and Herbed Macaroni
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving of pan-seared chicken on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The seared chicken thigh, skin golden and crisp, is presented whole and unsliced, positioned beside a compact mound of al dente macaroni, flecked with bright green chopped parsley and chives. A generous spoonful of vibrant yellow fermented corn salsa, featuring glossy kernels and finely minced garlic, provides a pop of color adjacent to the chicken. Thinly sliced quick-pickled cucumber, pale green, is scattered sparingly around the main elements. Crushed toasted peanuts provide a rustic textural element. The plate rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface with an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, enhancing natural colors and textures. The background is clean and minimalist, emphasizing a sustainable, ingredient-focused presentation.

ingredients.name: Cucumber, thinly sliced or small diced
White wine vinegar or apple cider vinegar

instructions: Prepare quick-pickled cucumber: Combine sliced cucumber, vinegar, sugar, a pinch of salt. Let stand 15 minutes.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.

Place chicken skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear 8-10 minutes until skin is crispy and golden. Flip chicken. Cook another 8-10 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Rest 5 minutes.
While chicken cooks, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add macaroni. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain macaroni, reserving 100ml pasta water.

In a bowl, combine cooked macaroni, cottage cheese, grated hard cheese, chopped parsley, and chopped chives. Add a splash of reserved pasta water to create a creamy consistency. Season with salt and pepper.
Assemble plates: Place a portion of herbed macaroni on each plate. Arrange one seared chicken thigh next to the macaroni.
Spoon a generous amount of fermented corn salsa beside the chicken. Drain quick-pickled cucumber. Arrange cucumber slices around the dish.
Garnish with crushed toasted peanuts. Serve immediately.
notes: To make lacto-fermented corn: Combine fresh corn kernels with 2% brine (20g salt per 1 liter water) and 1-2 minced garlic cloves. Ferment in a clean jar with an airlock or burp daily for 3-5 days at room temperature until desired tanginess is achieved. Store in the refrigerator.
Use chicken bones and corn cobs to make a simple stock for other dishes, reducing food waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Filipino Pork Adobo with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a single, generous portion of Filipino Pork Adobo with Potatoes on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Tender, braised pork belly chunks, approximately 3-4 cm cubes, are nestled among 2 cm potato cubes and softened tomato quarters. A rich, glossy, dark brown sauce, infused with soy and vinegar, coats all ingredients. The pork pieces exhibit a slightly caramelized exterior from initial browning, contrasting with the soft, yielding interior. The potatoes are fork-tender, absorbing the savory sauce. Garnished simply with a sprinkle of fresh chopped green onions for a pop of color. The presentation is natural and abundant, reflecting a hearty, home-cooked meal. Served on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a small bowl of steamed white rice and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks, with a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting warmth and texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed white rice.
Offer a side of fresh tomato and onion salad (Filipino ensalada) for contrast.
A small dish of patis (fish sauce) and calamansi lime for optional dipping or seasoning.
Serve on a communal table, allowing diners to share from the main pot or serve individual portions with rice as desired.
Traditionally eaten with a spoon and fork, or by hand (kamayan style) when served informally.
A small glass of cold water or a refreshing fruit juice is a common accompaniment to balance the rich flavors.
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown pork cubes on all sides. Remove pork.
Add onions and smashed garlic to the pot. Sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Return pork to the pot. Add soy sauce, vinegar, water, black peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer for 45 minutes, or until pork is tender.
Add potato cubes and quartered tomatoes to the pot.
Continue to simmer, uncovered, for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and sauce has thickened slightly. Stir occasionally.
Adjust seasoning if needed. Remove bay leaves before serving.
Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 70°C (160°F) for safe consumption.
notes: The vinegar flavor mellows significantly during cooking. Do not stir immediately after adding vinegar to prevent a raw vinegar taste.
Pork adobo tastes even better the next day as flavors meld.
Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 70°C (160°F) for safe consumption.
The amount of soy sauce and vinegar can be adjusted to personal preference, aiming for a balance of savory and tangy notes.
Some variations include adding hard-boiled eggs or green chilies for extra flavor and spice.
traditional_techniques: Adobo method (cooking meat in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, and peppercorns)

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are stacked slightly in the center, featuring deeply browned, caramelized skin. A thick, rustic sauce covers the base of the plate, filled with visible small cubes of orange carrots, green celery, and translucent onions. Whole, dark purple kalamata olives are nestled within the vibrant red tomato sauce. A light dusting of bright green chopped parsley and a single fresh rosemary sprig garnish the top. Two thick batons of grilled sourdough bread lean against the side of the chicken. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the glossy texture of the braised sauce and the crispness of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine
Place on a bed of soft, buttery polenta
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide braising pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the remaining fat.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and sage. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer wine for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Always use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C
Browning the skin thoroughly at the start is essential for the final texture
The sauce should be thick and chunky, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Creamy Herb Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, with its crispy, savory exterior and tender interior, is generously coated with a rich, creamy, light-beige herb sauce. Vibrant green flecks of finely chopped parsley and chives are visible throughout the sauce and as a delicate, fresh garnish over the chicken. The chicken is presented as a whole piece. Moderate negative space surrounds the dish, ensuring a balanced composition. The plate is positioned on a simple, light wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate, with standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting textures and warm colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet.
Add diced shallot and minced garlic. Sauté 2-3 minutes until fragrant and softened.
Pour in chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in chopped parsley and chives. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Return chicken to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken to coat. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Basil-Crusted Stuffed Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Onions
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, whole seared and roasted chicken breast is placed centrally on a round white porcelain plate. Its exterior is crisp, hinting at the tender, flavorful interior. Alongside it, a cluster of rustic potato wedges, roasted to a golden crisp exterior and fluffy interior, are arranged. Thick, caramelized onion segments are artfully scattered among the potatoes, adding depth of color and sweetness. A small, vibrant green sprig of fresh basil rests atop the chicken, providing a pop of color and freshness. The plate maintains moderate negative space, ensuring a clean, professional, yet approachable presentation. The chicken breast is presented as a whole piece. Potatoes are cut into rustic 2 cm wedges. Onions are cut into thick 2 cm segments. The plate is centered on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded light grey cotton napkin is placed to the left. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro environment. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting textures and colors. This is a single, refined restaurant portion.

ingredients.name: Small potatoes (e.g., new potatoes, Yukon Gold)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Finely chop basil leaves. Mince garlic cloves.
In a small bowl, combine chopped basil, half of the minced garlic, breadcrumbs, Parmesan cheese, 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Butterfly each chicken breast by slicing horizontally almost all the way through, opening it like a book. Season inside and out with salt and pepper.
Spoon the basil-breadcrumb mixture into the center of each butterflied chicken breast. Fold the chicken over to enclose the filling. Secure with toothpicks if needed.
Cut potatoes into 2 cm rustic wedges. Cut onions into thick 2 cm segments. In a large bowl, toss potatoes and onions with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a large baking tray.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil and butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear stuffed chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer seared chicken to the baking tray with the potatoes and onions. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender and caramelized. Remove toothpicks from chicken.

If desired, return skillet to medium heat. Add remaining minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half to create a light pan sauce.
Serve chicken with roasted potatoes and onions. Drizzle with pan sauce, if using. Garnish with a fresh basil sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy chicken and mushroom pasta rests in a round, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown, 2 cm seared chicken cubes are nestled amongst the al dente pasta strands, which are thoroughly coated in a rich, pale cream sauce. Sliced, earthy brown mushrooms are interspersed throughout, adding depth. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley provides a pop of color on top. The dish is presented casually, as if just served from the stove, with the pasta naturally piled. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a plain cloth napkin, emphasizing the homely, unpretentious comfort of the meal.
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Pat chicken breast cut into 2 cm cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Add cooked chicken back to the pan with the sauce. Add drained pasta. Toss to coat everything evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Chicken and Caramelized Onion Brown Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Spiced Chicken and Caramelized Onion Brown Rice Pilaf is presented centrally on a round, clean white porcelain plate. The brown rice is fluffy and distinct, its grains visible, flecked with deep golden-brown strands of thinly sliced, slow-cooked caramelized onions. Scattered generously atop and around the rice are substantial, golden-brown seared chicken chunks, each piece retaining its natural shape and showing a rich, caramelized crust from cooking. The overall color palette is warm and earthy, dominated by the rich browns of the rice and chicken, accented by the deep amber of the onions. A vibrant sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley provides a fresh contrast and pop of color. The dish is arranged organically, allowing the textures of the rice, tender chicken, and soft onions to be evident. A small, elegant white bowl containing a dollop of creamy plain yogurt and a lemon wedge sits beside the main plate. The setting is a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin and standard silverware, under soft, natural lighting, creating a warm, inviting bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain yogurt or a simple yogurt sauce.
Accompany with a small plate of pickled vegetables or a fresh cucumber and tomato salad.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut chicken into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove chicken and set aside. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

Slice onions thinly. Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the pot. Add sliced onions. Cook over medium-low heat for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and caramelized. Do not rush this step.
Mince garlic. Add minced garlic, cumin, coriander, paprika, and turmeric to the caramelized onions. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Rinse brown rice thoroughly under cold water. Add rinsed brown rice to the pot. Stir to coat the rice with the spices and onions. Toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
Gently stir in the seared chicken chunks and half of the chopped fresh parsley. Cover and let rest off the heat for 10 minutes.
Fluff the pilaf with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Serve hot, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Meat Ragu with Crispy Potatoes and Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Slow-Cooked Meat Ragu with Crispy Potatoes and Rigatoni is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The rigatoni pasta, cooked al dente, forms a base, generously topped with the rich, deep red ragu. The ragu features tender, slow-cooked chunks of beef, pork, and chicken (diced to 2-3 cm), nestled in a thick, savory tomato sauce. A scattering of golden-brown, crispy potato cubes (1.5 cm diced) adds texture and contrast on top. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a fresh accent. The dish is centered on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork and spoon. Natural, even lighting highlights the vibrant colors and varied textures of the dish, creating an inviting, professional bistro ambiance.
instructions: Dice beef, pork, and chicken into 2-3 cm chunks. Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Dice onion, carrots, and celery. Mince garlic.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef and pork in batches until browned on all sides. Remove meat. Set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to pot. Add diced potatoes. Fry until golden brown and crispy. Remove. Season with salt. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onion, carrots, and celery to pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Return seared beef and pork to pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Cover pot. Transfer to preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Cook 2 hours.

Remove pot from oven. Add diced chicken to ragu. Stir. Return to oven. Cook another 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and meats are tender. Internal temperature for chicken should reach 75°C (167°F).
While ragu finishes, cook rigatoni according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain.
Remove bay leaves, rosemary, and thyme stems from ragu. Season ragu with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve ragu over rigatoni. Top with crispy potatoes. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: For richer flavor, ensure beef and pork are well-browned before stewing.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika Chicken and Chili Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Smoked Paprika Chicken and Chili Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous mound of golden-orange rice, cooked to a fluid consistency with distinct grains, forms the base, flecked with diced red bell pepper, onion, and green thyme leaves. A perfectly seared bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, with crispy, golden-brown skin and visible tender meat, is placed whole atop the rice. The dish is garnished with a vibrant sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, showcasing rich warm tones of orange, red, and brown, contrasted with fresh green. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, with a soft, out-of-focus restaurant background.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt, black pepper, and 1 teaspoon of smoked paprika.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken, skin-side down, for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, remaining smoked paprika, dried chili flakes, and fresh thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add rice to the skillet. Stir well to coat all grains. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Nestle the seared chicken thighs back into the rice mixture, ensuring they are partially submerged. Cover the skillet tightly.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Shakshuka
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Shakshuka is presented in a rustic, well-used ceramic bowl. The vibrant red, chunky tomato sauce forms the base, with two perfectly poached eggs nestled within. The egg whites are opaque and set, while the yolks appear soft and slightly runny, adding a contrasting yellow hue. Finely chopped fresh green parsley is generously sprinkled over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The diced onions and red bell pepper are visible within the rich sauce, showcasing their tender texture. The bowl sits on a warm, natural wooden dining table. A simple, everyday fork rests casually beside the bowl. The lighting is soft and warm, characteristic of a cozy family kitchen, emphasizing the comforting nature of the dish. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in home environment without distracting from the food.
instructions: Dice onions and red bell pepper. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large, deep skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onions and bell pepper. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, paprika, and cumin. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Season with salt and black pepper. Stir well.
Bring sauce to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Create 8 small wells in the tomato sauce. Carefully crack one egg into each well.
Cover the skillet. Cook for 8-10 minutes, or until egg whites are set and yolks are to your desired firmness.
Remove from heat. Garnish generously with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro.
Serve immediately, directly from the skillet or in individual bowls.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Beef Ragu with Cheesy Polenta and Basil-Strawberry Gremolata
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of rustic Tuscan Beef Ragu with Cheesy Polenta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The golden, creamy polenta, cooked to a fluid consistency, forms a base, with a generous well in its center. Rich, dark brown beef ragu, featuring fork-tender beef chunks (approx. 3 cm cubes), finely diced onions, carrots, and bright green peas, fills the well, glistening with its savory sauce. A subtle sheen from the melted dark chocolate is visible. The dish is garnished with vibrant green fresh basil leaves, artfully placed, and a spoonful of red, small-diced strawberries, offering a fresh, contrasting pop of color and texture against the deep ragu. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. A cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and texture, with a blurred, casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread for dipping in the ragu.
Pair with a robust red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
Enjoy as a hearty family meal, a staple in Italian home cooking.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, diced into 3 cm cubes

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Dust lightly with flour.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.

Add diced onions, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until wine reduces slightly.
Return seared beef to the pot. Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, bay leaves, and rosemary. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaves and rosemary sprig. Stir in grated dark chocolate until melted and combined.
While ragu simmers, prepare polenta. Bring 800 ml water (or milk for creamier polenta) to a boil in a separate saucepan. Gradually whisk in cornmeal, ensuring no lumps.
Reduce heat to low. Cook polenta, stirring frequently, for 20-25 minutes, or until creamy and thickened. Stir in 70 g grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt. Polenta should be fluid, not dry.
For the gremolata, combine small diced strawberries and half of the chopped fresh basil in a small bowl.
Stir frozen green peas into the ragu during the last 5 minutes of cooking to warm through. Adjust seasoning of ragu with salt and pepper.
To serve, spoon a generous portion of cheesy polenta onto each plate. Create a well in the center. Ladle hot beef ragu into the well.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves and a spoonful of the basil-strawberry gremolata. Sprinkle with remaining grated Parmesan.
notes: For best flavor, prepare the ragu a day in advance and reheat slowly. Flavors deepen overnight.
Adjust the amount of dark chocolate to your preference; it should add depth, not overt sweetness.
traditional_techniques: Soffritto: A foundational aromatic base of finely diced onion, carrot, and celery, slowly cooked in olive oil.
Braising: Slow cooking meat in liquid over low heat until very tender.
Mantecaura: The final vigorous stirring of polenta with butter/cheese to achieve creaminess.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Rice Enchiladas
recipes.visual_description: A rectangular ceramic baking dish holds several generously sized chicken and rice enchiladas. They are tightly rolled, their corn tortillas softened and slightly browned, peeking from under a rich, reddish-brown chili sauce. The sauce is thick, clinging to the enchiladas, and is topped with a generous layer of melted, golden-brown Monterey Jack and cheddar cheese, bubbly and slightly browned at the edges. A few fresh cilantro sprigs are casually scattered over the top, adding a vibrant green contrast. The dish is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, perhaps a simple checkered cloth placemat underneath. A casual white cloth napkin and a rustic ceramic bowl for crema are nearby. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, homely atmosphere. The focus is on the hearty, comforting food, presented as if for a family meal, with natural portions and a lived-in feel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of refried beans or Mexican rice (if not already in filling).
Offer lime wedges and a mild salsa.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with a lime vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Shredded Monterey Jack or cheddar cheese

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a large baking dish (approx. 23x33 cm).
Cook rice: Combine rice and 400 ml chicken broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes. Remove from heat, let stand 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

Cook chicken: Heat 15 ml oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Cook 6-8 minutes per side, until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Let cool slightly, then shred using two forks.

Make sauce: Add remaining 15 ml oil to the same skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, and oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in tomato paste and remaining 100 ml chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare filling: In a large bowl, combine shredded chicken, cooked rice, 150 g shredded cheese, and 125 ml of the prepared sauce. Mix well.

Assemble enchiladas: Briefly warm tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave to make them pliable. Dip each tortilla quickly into the remaining sauce. Place a portion of filling (approx. 60g) down the center of each tortilla. Roll tightly and place seam-side down in the prepared baking dish.
Bake enchiladas: Pour remaining sauce over the rolled enchiladas. Sprinkle remaining 150 g shredded cheese evenly over the top. Bake 20-25 minutes, until cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Serve: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Offer crema or sour cream on the side.
traditional_techniques: Sautéing aromatics for a flavor base

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Sausage Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide white porcelain pasta bowl. Rigatoni pasta is generously coated in a rich, deep red tomato sauce. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks (2-3 cm) and browned crumbles of Italian sausage are scattered throughout, maintaining natural forms. Vibrant green fresh basil and parsley speckle the dish, adding color. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese tops the pasta, melting slightly. A thin drizzle of olive oil adds a subtle sheen. The composition is natural and inviting. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and silver flatware beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors. A slice of crusty artisanal bread rests on a small side plate nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese.
Accompany with crusty bread for soaking up the sauce.
A simple green salad with vinaigrette often precedes or accompanies pasta dishes.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 2-3 cm chunks

instructions: Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add crumbled sausage to the same pot. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Remove sausage from pot. Drain excess fat if needed, leaving about 15 ml.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil and diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken and cooked sausage to the pot. Stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer, uncovered, for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly and chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Stir cooked rigatoni, fresh basil, and fresh parsley into the sauce. Add lemon juice. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately in bowls. Garnish with grated Parmesan cheese. Serve with crusty bread on the side.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
Adjust sugar based on tomato acidity and personal preference.
traditional_techniques: Simmering sauce slowly to meld flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Buffalo Blue Cheese Stuffed Chicken Breast
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast is centrally plated on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is plump, cooked whole, and sliced diagonally in half to reveal a creamy, blue-cheese-flecked filling within. Its exterior has a subtle crispness. Scattered around the chicken are vibrant red, roasted cherry tomatoes, some slightly burst, releasing their juices. A light drizzle of bright orange Buffalo hot sauce adorns the chicken and plate. Freshly chopped green chives are sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple wooden table. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with celery sticks and carrot sticks.
Offer a side of ranch or blue cheese dressing for dipping.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Butterfly each chicken breast. Pound gently to even thickness.
In a small bowl, combine blue cheese, cream cheese, and 30ml hot sauce. Mix well.
Spoon cheese mixture into each chicken breast. Fold chicken over to enclose filling. Secure with toothpicks if needed.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Add cherry tomatoes and minced garlic to the skillet with the remaining 15ml olive oil. Toss lightly.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Drizzle remaining 30ml hot sauce over chicken and tomatoes.
Garnish with fresh chives or parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Use good quality blue cheese for best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. It is generously coated with a rich, creamy mushroom sauce. The sauce features irregularly sliced, deeply browned cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots, creating a rustic yet refined texture. Bright green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the chicken and sauce, adding a fresh color contrast. The chicken breast shows a crisp exterior and a tender interior. A small pool of sauce surrounds the base of the chicken. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and texture. A single portion, balanced and appealing.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan.
Add sliced shallot. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add irregularly sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Sprinkle flour over mushrooms. Stir for 1 minute to coat.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken breasts to the pan. Turn to coat with sauce.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, succulent chunks of bone-in poached chicken with glossy, pale skin. The chicken rests on a bed of fragrant, light-yellow Jasmine rice infused with ginger and pandan. Slices of fresh, cool cucumber are arranged neatly to the side. The chicken is lightly drizzled with a mixture of soy sauce and sesame oil. Three small ceramic dipping bowls contain bright red chili sauce, dark soy sauce, and a vibrant green ginger-scallion oil. The meal is served on a clean white porcelain plate on a light wood table. A pair of dark wood chopsticks and a traditional ceramic soup spoon sit to the right. Natural light highlights the moist texture of the meat and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side bowl of hot chicken broth
Include chili sauce, ginger-garlic sauce, and dark soy sauce
Serve at room temperature as per tradition
instructions: Rub chicken with salt to remove impurities.
Rinse chicken under cold water.
Boil 3 liters of water with 30g crushed ginger and scallions.
Submerge chicken in boiling water.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Turn off heat and cover pot.
Steep chicken for 30 minutes.
Confirm internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Submerge chicken in ice water for 5 minutes.
Drain chicken and rub skin with sesame oil.
Sauté 20g minced ginger and minced garlic in chicken fat.
Add rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Add 600ml poaching liquid and pandan leaves.
Cook rice until liquid is absorbed.
Cut chicken into large chunks.
notes: Save the remaining poaching liquid for a light soup
Rubbing the chicken with salt ensures a smooth skin texture
Using rendered chicken fat for the rice is essential for authenticity

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Tenderloin with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A thick-cut, pan-seared beef tenderloin medallion forms the centerpiece, displaying a deep, caramelized crust and a visibly pink, juicy interior. It rests on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A rich, creamy mushroom sauce, studded with sliced cremini mushrooms, pools elegantly beside the beef, its earthy brown color contrasting with the vibrant green of blanched asparagus spears. The asparagus, tender-crisp, is arranged neatly alongside the beef. A light sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley garnishes the beef and sauce, adding a pop of fresh green. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors.
instructions: Pat beef tenderloin medallions dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add beef medallions and thyme sprig. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Transfer beef to a plate. Tent with foil. Let rest.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add sliced cremini mushrooms. Sauté until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced shallots and minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 5 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Meanwhile, bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add asparagus spears. Cook for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately.
Stir chopped fresh parsley into the mushroom cream sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Place one beef tenderloin medallion on each plate. Spoon creamy mushroom sauce generously over and around the beef. Arrange asparagus spears neatly beside the beef.

recipes.recipe_name: Bacon and Cheddar Stuffed Chicken with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, pan-seared and oven-finished chicken breast, golden-brown and plump, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is cut in half diagonally to reveal a rich, creamy stuffing of melted cheddar, crisp bacon, and seasoned breadcrumbs. Alongside, a generous portion of roasted potato chunks are piled artfully, their skins lightly crisped and interiors tender, generously topped with melted golden cheddar and scattered with crispy bacon bits. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is sprinkled over both the chicken and potatoes, adding a pop of color. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with a balanced composition and moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting. Standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin are placed beside the plate. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 800g, medium, peeled and cut into 2.5 cm chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cook diced bacon in a skillet until crispy. Drain excess fat. Crumble bacon and set aside.
Melt butter in the same skillet. Sauté finely diced onion and minced garlic until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
In a bowl, combine cooked onion and garlic, 100g shredded cheddar cheese, breadcrumbs, and half of the crumbled bacon. Mix well.
Carefully butterfly each chicken breast, cutting almost all the way through horizontally to create a pocket. Season the inside with salt and pepper.
Spoon the stuffing mixture evenly into each chicken breast pocket. Fold the chicken over and secure the opening with one or two toothpicks.
Season the exterior of the stuffed chicken breasts generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the stuffed chicken breasts for 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer the skillet with the chicken to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
While chicken bakes, place potato chunks on a separate baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Roast potatoes in the oven for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway through, until tender and golden brown.
Remove roasted potatoes from the oven. Sprinkle with the remaining 50g shredded cheddar cheese and the remaining crumbled bacon.
Return potatoes to the oven for an additional 5 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove chicken from oven and let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Remove toothpicks.
Serve each stuffed chicken breast with a portion of the cheesy bacon roasted potatoes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Sirloin with Potato Gratin and Red Wine Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared beef sirloin steak, exhibiting a deep, rich brown crust with a hint of char, rests as the focal point on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The steak is presented whole, showcasing its robust form. Beside it, a neatly cut, golden-brown square of potato gratin rises with distinct layers, its top subtly crisp and glistening. A vibrant cluster of blanched and sautéed green beans provides a fresh, verdant contrast, adding a natural, organic flow. A generous pool of glossy, dark red wine jus is spooned elegantly beside the beef, partially flowing underneath. A small, fresh sprig of thyme adorns the steak. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by classic European flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating a professional yet approachable bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a vinaigrette.
Offer crusty baguette slices for dipping in the jus.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20x20 cm baking dish.
Slice potatoes thinly, about 2mm thick. A mandoline is recommended.
Layer half the sliced potatoes in the prepared dish. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine cream, milk, minced garlic, and nutmeg in a bowl. Season well.
Pour half the cream mixture over the first potato layer. Repeat with remaining potatoes and cream mixture.
Bake gratin for 50-60 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown. Let rest 10 minutes.
For the red wine jus, melt 10g butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add diced shallots. Cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Increase heat to high. Reduce by half, scraping up any browned bits.
Add beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer until sauce thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon, about 10-15 minutes.
Strain jus through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Keep warm. Season to taste.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add green beans. Blanch for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately.
Heat a large, heavy-bottomed pan over high heat. Add olive oil until shimmering.
Pat beef sirloin steaks very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Carefully place steaks in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
During the last 2 minutes of cooking, add remaining butter and fresh thyme sprigs to the pan. Baste the steaks continuously with the melted butter and herbs.
Remove steaks from pan. Place on a cutting board. Rest for 5-7 minutes before serving.

To plate, place a portion of potato gratin on each plate. Position a seared sirloin steak beside it. Arrange blanched green beans next to the gratin. Spoon a generous amount of red wine jus over and around the beef.
notes: Always rest the beef after cooking; this allows juices to redistribute, ensuring a tender and flavorful steak.
For the potato gratin, thin, uniform slices are key for even cooking and a beautiful presentation.

recipes.recipe_name: Sheet Pan Soy-Ginger Chicken and Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of sheet pan roasted chicken and vegetables is arranged naturally on a simple, everyday ceramic plate. The whole chicken breast or large chunks are prominently placed. Around it, a colorful mix of roasted baby potato halves, 2 cm thick carrot rounds, 2-3 cm bell pepper pieces, quartered mushrooms, large onion wedges, and 2 cm celery pieces are casually scattered. Vegetables show slight caramelization and a glossy sheen. Colors are natural: golden chicken, rustic browns, vibrant reds and yellows, earthy mushrooms. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, plain white ceramic plate with minor imperfections. A casually folded cloth napkin is nearby. The background suggests a relaxed family dining area with warm, natural kitchen lighting and minimal clutter. A single, hearty individual portion.

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley or cilantro (for garnish, optional)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash baby potatoes. Halve or quarter larger ones.
Peel carrots. Cut into 2 cm thick rounds or large chunks.
Cut bell pepper into 2-3 cm pieces.
Quarter mushrooms.
Peel and chop onion into large wedges.
Slice celery into 2 cm pieces.
Mince garlic and ginger.
In a large bowl, combine potatoes, carrots, bell pepper, mushrooms, onion, and celery.
Add 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Roast for 20 minutes.
While vegetables roast, pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, minced garlic, minced ginger, 15ml olive oil, and honey (if using).
After 20 minutes, remove baking sheet. Push vegetables to one side.
Place chicken breasts on the empty side of the baking sheet.
Pour half of the soy-ginger glaze over the chicken.
Toss remaining glaze with the roasted vegetables.
Return baking sheet to oven. Roast for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature and vegetables are tender.
Let chicken rest 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh parsley or cilantro if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of roasted chicken thigh rests on a well-used wooden dining table. The chicken, with its crispy, golden-brown skin, is placed alongside a generous portion of roasted potato chunks. The potatoes are fork-tender with slightly browned, crisp edges. Fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs, along with roasted lemon slices, are scattered naturally around the chicken and potatoes. The dish is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate with a rustic rim, showing natural imperfections. Warm, soft light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene. A simple cloth napkin and a standard fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. The overall scene is homely and inviting, focusing on comforting textures and natural colors.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
In a large roasting pan, toss potato chunks with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer.
Place chicken thighs skin-side up over and among the potatoes.
Tuck lemon slices, smashed garlic cloves, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs around chicken and potatoes.
Drizzle remaining 30ml olive oil over chicken and potatoes.
Roast for 35-45 minutes. Chicken skin should be golden and crispy.
Check chicken internal temperature. It must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the dish before serving.
notes: This dish is a complete meal. Adjust roasting time for larger chicken pieces.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, charred chunks of succulent chicken submerged in a glossy, vibrant orange-red tomato gravy. The sauce has a thick, velvety texture with visible flecks of ground spices. The chicken chunks show dark, caramelized edges from the high-heat roasting. Plating is in a clean, white porcelain bowl set on a dark wooden table. A single portion is shown with a light swirl of heavy cream on top and a scattering of bright green chopped cilantro. To the side sits a stack of warm, charred garlic naan bread and a small bowl of steamed long-grain basmati rice. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the rich colors and creamy consistency of the sauce while maintaining professional negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or buttered roti
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Side of mint-yogurt raita and kachumber salad
Serve in a traditional hammered copper karahi
instructions: Combine yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp chili powder.
Toss chicken chunks in marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 220°C. Place chicken on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Roast chicken 15 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté onions until golden brown.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in remaining garam masala, turmeric, and chili powder. Toast for 30 seconds.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens and oil separates.
Stir in butter and heavy cream. Season with salt.
Add roasted chicken chunks to the sauce. Simmer 2 minutes to combine flavors.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Kashmiri chili powder provides color without excessive heat.
Ensure the chicken is well-charred for authentic smoky flavor.
Let the sauce simmer until the oil separates to ensure spices are fully cooked.

recipes.recipe_name: Pineapple Ferment Braised Chicken with Root-to-Stem Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown, bone-in chicken thigh is the centerpiece, its skin crisp and taut from braising. It rests on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy, matte off-white tone, offering ample negative space. Beside the chicken, a vibrant medley of roasted root-to-stem vegetables is artfully arranged. Thick carrot batons show slight caramelization, alongside tender broccoli florets and neatly sliced, peeled broccoli stems. Red bell pepper wedges and zucchini rounds add contrasting colors and textures. A small, glistening pool of the rich, reduced pineapple braising liquid acts as a natural sauce. A few fresh coriander leaves and small, bright pineapple chunks are scattered thoughtfully for garnish, adding a touch of freshness without clutter. The presentation is clean and unforced, highlighting the natural beauty and textures of each ingredient. The setting is minimalist, featuring a light wood or stone surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, natural lighting from the side, creating a serene and inviting atmosphere. The background is simple and unobtrusive, allowing the dish to be the sole focus.

ingredients.name: Large ripe pineapple
ingredients.quantity: 1 (fruit for serving, core and skin for ferment)

instructions: Prepare pineapple ferment: Peel pineapple, reserving skin and core. Cut skin and core into small pieces. Combine with 1 litre filtered water, 50 g brown sugar, and a pinch of salt in a large glass jar. Cover loosely with cloth or lid. Let ferment at room temperature for 1-2 days until slightly bubbly and tangy. Strain liquid, discard solids.
Preheat oven to 190°C.
Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 10 ml olive oil to the pot. Sauté smashed garlic, sliced ginger, and chopped red onion until fragrant, about 3-4 minutes.
Pour in the strained pineapple ferment liquid. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up.
Cover the pot and transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 30 minutes. Internal temperature of chicken must reach 75°C.

While chicken braises, prepare root-to-stem vegetables: Cut carrots into thick batons. Separate broccoli into florets; peel and slice the stem into rounds. Cut bell pepper into wedges. Slice zucchini into thick rounds or half-moons. Toss vegetables with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables on a baking tray. Roast in the oven alongside the chicken for the last 20-25 minutes of braising, or until tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.

Once chicken is cooked, remove pot from oven. Carefully remove chicken thighs and set aside to rest. Return pot with braising liquid to stovetop over high heat. Reduce liquid by half until it forms a light glaze, about 5-7 minutes.

Plate individual chicken thighs. Arrange a generous portion of roasted root-to-stem vegetables beside the chicken. Spoon reduced pineapple glaze over the chicken and vegetables. Garnish with fresh coriander or parsley leaves and a few fresh pineapple chunks (from the fruit of the fermented pineapple). Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing pineapple core and skin for the braising liquid, and preparing vegetables 'root-to-stem'.
Adjust braising time based on chicken thigh size to ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The pineapple ferment adds a unique tangy depth to the braising liquid; adjust fermentation time based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Spanish chicken and rice served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice is moist and fluid, colored a vibrant golden-orange from the smoked paprika and broth. Thick 4cm chunks of seared chicken thighs are nestled into the rice, showing a crisp, dark golden-brown exterior. Small dices of softened red bell pepper and translucent onions are evenly distributed throughout the grains. The dish is finished with a scatter of bright green chopped parsley. A single yellow lemon wedge sits on the side of the plate. The background features a rustic wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and natural side-lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional terracotta cazuela
Accompany with crusty bread and aioli
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine like Albariño

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, and half the paprika.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 5 minutes until golden. Remove from pan.
Add onion and red pepper to the same pan. Sauté until softened.
Stir in garlic and remaining paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 18 minutes. Do not stir.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Use short-grain rice to ensure the correct starchy consistency.
Avoid stirring the rice once the broth is added to allow a slight crust to form.
Ensure the broth is hot before adding it to the pan to maintain cooking temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A deep, white porcelain bowl holds a generous individual portion of Pork Ragu with Pappardelle. The wide, flat pappardelle noodles are thoroughly coated in a rich, dark reddish-brown ragu. Tender, shredded pork chunks are visible throughout the sauce, integrated seamlessly. Finely diced vegetables like onion, carrot, and celery have cooked down into the thick, flavorful sauce. A few small, vibrant red chili slices peek through, hinting at a gentle warmth. The dish is garnished with a scattering of freshly chopped bright green flat-leaf parsley and a generous dusting of finely grated white Pecorino Romano cheese. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl, along with standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating soft shadows and highlighting its inviting textures and colors. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a clean, casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the rich sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Accompany with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 3-4 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chunks in batches until well-browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove pork and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery (soffritto) to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and thinly sliced deseeded red chilies. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Return seared pork to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, bay leaves, and rosemary sprig. Stir to combine.
