Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not stir during cooking.
Remove from heat. Stir in frozen peas. Cover and let rest for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Check seasoning and adjust.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best results, use good quality smoked paprika and authentic saffron threads.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Beef & Potato Stew with Macaroni
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The centerpiece is a hearty beef and potato stew, featuring tender, dark brown beef chunks (approximately 4-5 cm) and roughly diced potatoes (2 cm cubes) in a rich, thick, savory gravy. Bright orange carrot pieces (2 cm cubes) and softened onion add color. A generous portion of cooked macaroni pasta is nestled beside the stew, partially submerged in the luscious sauce. Fresh, roughly chopped parsley is sprinkled over, adding vibrant green. A thick slice of crusty, artisanal bread, with a golden-brown crust, rests casually against the bowl. The setting is a cozy, natural-lit family kitchen, with simple flatware nearby. The focus is on comfort and warmth, with modest, natural portions.
instructions: Trim beef stewing steak. Cut into 4-5 cm chunks. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef chunks in batches until deep golden on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in plain flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Stir in tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, dried thyme, and bay leaves.
Return browned beef to the pot. Bring mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5 hours, or until beef is tender.
While stew simmers, peel potatoes and carrots. Cut both into 2 cm cubes.
After 1.5 hours, add potatoes and carrots to the stew. Stir well. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 30-40 minutes, or until vegetables are tender and beef is very tender.
About 15 minutes before serving, cook macaroni pasta according to package directions in a separate pot of salted boiling water until al dente. Drain well.
Remove bay leaves from the stew. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. The gravy should be thick and rich.
Roughly chop fresh parsley for garnish.
Serve hot. Ladle stew into bowls. Add a portion of macaroni pasta beside the stew. Garnish with fresh parsley. Serve with slices of crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Sudado Colombiano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo Sudado is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two pieces of bone-in, skin-on chicken (a thigh and a drumstick) are centrally placed, glistening with the rich, deep orange-red stewing sauce. Large, rustic chunks of tender yellow potato, yuca, and thick rounds of green plantain are nestled around the chicken, partially submerged in the vibrant, thick sauce. A generous sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped cilantro garnishes the dish, along with a bright green lime wedge positioned beside the chicken. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with a cotton napkin placed neatly beside the plate. A small white bowl of fluffy white rice and a side of fanned sliced avocado are presented as traditional accompaniments. A small ramekin of ají (Colombian hot sauce) is also visible. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warm tones and inviting textures, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of steamed white rice.
Offer sliced avocado as a fresh accompaniment.
Provide ají (Colombian hot sauce) on the side for those who prefer more spice.
instructions: Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat achiote oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until golden brown on all sides. Do not crowd the pot. Work in batches if necessary. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced white onion, red bell pepper, and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add diced red tomatoes and ground cumin. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes until tomatoes break down and form a thick sauce (hogao).
Return seared chicken to the pot. Add peeled and roughly chunked yellow potatoes, yuca, and thick rounds of green plantain around the chicken.
Pour in chicken broth. Ensure liquid mostly covers ingredients. Add more broth if needed.
Bring to a simmer. Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are fork-tender.
Stir in half of the chopped fresh cilantro during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. The sauce should be rich and slightly thickened.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked through to 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The hogao is the flavorful base; allow it to cook down properly for best results.
Yuca can be substituted with more potatoes if unavailable.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika Chicken with Crispy Potatoes, Roasted Corn, and Tomato-Bell Pepper Medley
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, rustic-elegant plate featuring a golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast as the focal point. The chicken, left whole, exhibits a rich, smoky paprika crust. Beside it, a generous portion of crispy roasted potato cubes, their edges slightly browned, provides textural contrast. Scattered around the plate are bright, roasted bell pepper chunks (red and yellow), plump, slightly blistered cherry tomatoes, and sweet corn kernels, all retaining their vibrant colors and soft-crisp textures. A light drizzle of pan sauce subtly pools beneath the chicken. The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain plate, set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver cutlery and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting colors and varied textures. A single individual portion is displayed, showcasing professional yet approachable plating with ample negative space.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).

Cut potatoes into 2cm cubes. Toss with 30ml olive oil, 5g smoked paprika, 2g garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-35 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crispy.

Cut bell peppers into 2cm chunks. Carefully slice kernels off corn cobs. Place bell pepper chunks, corn kernels, and cherry tomatoes on a separate baking sheet. Toss with remaining 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes in the same oven as potatoes, until tender-crisp.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with remaining 10g smoked paprika, 3g garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add a splash of olive oil. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
While chicken rests, place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add chicken broth to deglaze, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced (optional pan sauce).

Arrange a portion of crispy potatoes, roasted bell pepper, corn, and cherry tomatoes on each plate. Place one whole chicken breast beside the vegetables. Spoon pan sauce over chicken, if using. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef & Mushroom Cottage Pie
recipes.visual_description: The Beef & Mushroom Cottage Pie is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic baking dish, showcasing a generous, single individual portion. The top layer of golden-brown mashed potatoes is visibly fluffy with fork-tine ridges, slightly browned and crisp on the peaks from baking, and dotted with melted, bubbly cheddar cheese. Peeking from beneath the potato crust, the rich, savory beef and mushroom filling is a deep reddish-brown, hinting at the tomato and beef broth base. The diced mushrooms and chunks of beef are discernible within the robust sauce. The dish sits on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple white ceramic plate. A casually folded linen napkin and a fork rest beside it. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen window illuminates the scene, emphasizing the comforting, hearty nature of the home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed green peas or buttered carrots.
Offer crusty bread for soaking up any extra sauce.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into large chunks. Place in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Cook until tender, about 15-20 minutes.
While potatoes cook, heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add ground beef to the skillet. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat if needed.
Add sliced mushrooms and minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms soften and release their liquid.

Stir in diced tomatoes, beef broth, dried thyme, and Worcestershire sauce (if using). Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 15-20 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Drain cooked potatoes well. Return to the pot. Add milk, butter, and half of the grated cheese. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the beef mixture evenly into the bottom of the oven-safe skillet (if using a skillet, otherwise transfer to a baking dish).
Carefully spread the cheesy mashed potato topping over the beef mixture. Use a fork to create ridges on top. Sprinkle remaining grated cheese over the mashed potatoes.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.
Let stand for 5-10 minutes before serving.
notes: For extra flavor, add a bay leaf to the beef mixture while simmering, then remove before topping with potatoes.
The pie can be assembled ahead of time and refrigerated. Add an extra 10-15 minutes to baking time if baking from cold.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, skin lightly crisp, rests on a rustic white ceramic plate. Alongside, a generous serving of tender, golden-brown potato wedges, their exteriors slightly caramelized. Fresh sprigs of rosemary and thyme are naturally scattered over the chicken and potatoes, adding vibrant green accents. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits nearby. The chicken is presented whole, not sliced. The plate is positioned on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. A casually folded blue and white checkered cloth napkin and simple silver cutlery are placed beside it. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, homely family meal. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the baking sheet for family-style meals.
Pair with a simple green salad or steamed seasonal vegetables.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2cm thick wedges. Place in a large bowl.
Mince garlic cloves. Finely chop rosemary and thyme leaves.
Add olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, salt, and pepper to the bowl with potatoes. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange potato wedges in a single layer on one half of the prepared baking sheet.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Place chicken thighs, skin-side up, on the other half of the baking sheet alongside the potatoes.
Slice the lemon into thin rounds. Place a few lemon rounds on top of and around the chicken and potatoes.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, and potatoes are tender and browned. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: For extra crispiness, broil chicken for the last 2-3 minutes, watching carefully to prevent burning.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Onion Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of clear, golden chicken broth is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with a natural, unglazed finish, resting on a light reclaimed wood table. The broth is infused with subtle notes from vegetables. Poached chicken meat, cut into irregular, tender chunks, is gently arranged within the broth. Distinct thin slices of translucent fermented onion add a delicate pink hue and textural contrast. A few vibrant green fresh parsley leaves, naturally placed, provide a pop of color. A light drizzle of chive oil, made from discarded chive stems, creates subtle green streaks on the broth's surface. The setting features a simple undyed linen napkin and a minimalist background with soft, natural lighting, emphasizing the dish's purity and sustainable essence.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Onions: Thinly slice 1 large onion. Place in a clean jar. Dissolve 10g salt in 250ml water. Pour brine over onions. Ensure onions are submerged. Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Burp daily. Refrigerate when desired tang is reached.

Make Chicken Broth: Pat dry chicken thighs. Season lightly with 5g salt. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown. Flip. Sear other side. Remove chicken from pot.
Add roughly chopped 1 onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 carrot, and 1 celery stalk (or equivalent vegetable scraps) to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Add 1.5 litres water and 5g black peppercorns. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes. Skim foam as needed.
Remove chicken thighs from broth. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Debone chicken thighs. Shred or dice chicken meat into small chunks. Set aside.
Prepare Chive Oil: Blend chive stems/scraps with 30ml neutral oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth to create a clear green oil.

Assemble Soup: Return strained broth to pot. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add shredded chicken and 60g of fermented onions. Taste broth. Adjust salt if needed. Simmer for 5 minutes to heat through. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Ladle soup into bowls. Drizzle lightly with chive oil. Garnish with fresh parsley leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Garlic Mushroom Chicken Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Garlic Mushroom Chicken Tagliatelle is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The pasta is loosely coiled, forming a natural mound at the center, allowing for ample negative space on the plate. Shredded, golden-brown chicken pieces are nestled amongst the strands of pasta, along with rustic slices of browned mushrooms. The sauce is light and clings to the pasta, showcasing a subtle creamy-beige hue from the nutritional yeast and mushroom broth, with dark flecks of fermented garlic. A scattering of roughly chopped fresh green parsley adds a touch of vibrant color and freshness without being overly manicured. The textures are varied: tender pasta, succulent chicken, and earthy mushrooms. The dish is placed on a light-colored, subtly textured reclaimed wood surface. A natural beige, undyed linen napkin is folded simply beside the plate. The background is clean and minimalist, with soft, natural lighting highlighting the dish's organic forms.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a main course.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette as an accompaniment.
instructions: Cook pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add tagliatelle. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 150ml pasta cooking water before draining.

Prepare chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Let rest, then shred into bite-sized pieces.
Sauté aromatics: In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Add diced shallots and sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and softened.
Add fermented garlic: Stir in fermented garlic cloves for 1 minute.
Deglaze: Pour in white wine (if using) and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Cook until liquid reduces slightly.
Build sauce: Add chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in shredded chicken.
Combine: Add cooked tagliatelle and nutritional yeast to the pan with the sauce and chicken. Toss to combine. If needed, add reserved pasta cooking water gradually to achieve desired consistency.
Finish: Stir in fresh parsley. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
notes: To make fermented garlic: Peel garlic cloves and place them in a clean jar. Cover with a 2% brine (20g salt per 1 liter of non-chlorinated water). Seal loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature for 1-2 weeks, or until bubbling subsides and garlic is tangy. Store in the refrigerator.
For zero-waste broth: Simmer mushroom stems, chicken trimmings (if any), and parsley stems in water for 30 minutes to an hour. Strain before use.
Seasonal vegetables like asparagus or spinach can be added to the sauce during the last few minutes of cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Herb Roasted Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tuscan Herb Roasted Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A thick, golden-brown seared chicken breast, cooked to perfection, is placed slightly off-center. Alongside, a vibrant medley of roasted vegetables – halved cherry tomatoes, 2cm thick zucchini half-moons, and 2cm wide strips of red and yellow bell peppers – are arranged naturally, showcasing their slightly charred edges and bright colors. A light, glossy pan sauce, made from deglazed chicken drippings, is spooned over the chicken, adding a subtle sheen. The dish is garnished with a few fresh sprigs of rosemary and thyme, enhancing the aromatic appeal. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware positioned neatly beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a minimal, casual restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread to sop up the pan sauce.
A simple side salad with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve 500g cherry tomatoes. Cut 2 medium zucchini into 2cm thick half-moons. Cut 2 bell peppers (mixed colors) into 2cm strips.
Toss vegetables with 30ml olive oil, 4 minced garlic cloves, 5g chopped fresh rosemary, 5g chopped fresh thyme, 5g chopped fresh oregano, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
Pat dry 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts. Season with 5g salt and 2g black pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Cook chicken for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.
Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add 120ml chicken broth to deglaze. Scrape up browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Whisk in 30g cold butter until sauce slightly thickens. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice chicken breasts into thick medallions or serve whole. Plate chicken with roasted vegetables. Spoon pan sauce over chicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Red Wine and Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised beef, consisting of two substantial, dark brown, fork-tender chunks, is centered on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The beef is richly coated in a glossy, deep reddish-brown red wine sauce, which pools elegantly around the base of the meat. Small, vibrant green flecks of freshly chopped parsley are sprinkled sparingly over the beef and sauce, providing a fresh, aromatic contrast. The beef chunks are presented as whole pieces. The plating is clean and professional, focusing on the rich color and tender texture of the beef and its luscious sauce. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro setting. A crisp, white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a softly blurred background hinting at a casual restaurant ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy polenta or mashed potatoes to absorb the rich sauce.
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes to reduce slightly.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaves.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Remove beef from the pot. Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing on solids to extract liquid. Discard solids.
Return strained sauce to the pot. Simmer over medium heat until slightly thickened to desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Return beef to the sauce. Gently warm through.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Tuna with Roasted Broccoli, Mushrooms, and Herb Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A thick, seared tuna chunk (not sliced) is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Its crust is golden-brown with a rosy-pink interior visible from a clean cut edge. Around the tuna, neatly arranged roasted broccoli florets (deep green with some charred tips) and thickly sliced cremini mushrooms (earthy brown, tender) create a rustic yet organized ring. A vibrant mound of mixed salad greens, lightly dressed, sits beside the main elements. Crispy golden pita wedges are strategically placed to add height and texture. A drizzle of bright green herb vinaigrette glazes the tuna and vegetables. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food. The background is a subtly blurred, warm-toned bistro setting, hinting at a casual, inviting atmosphere without distraction. A single, generous individual portion is shown.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately. Offer additional lemon wedges on the side.
instructions: Prepare vegetables. Cut broccoli into small florets. Slice mushrooms thickly.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss broccoli and mushrooms with 30ml olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables on a baking tray. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized.
Prepare pita. Cut pita rounds into wedges. Brush lightly with 15ml olive oil.
Bake pita wedges alongside vegetables for 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp.
Prepare herb vinaigrette. Finely chop fresh dill and basil. In a small bowl, whisk remaining 35ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, juice of half a lemon, salt, and pepper. Stir in chopped dill and basil.
Season tuna fillets generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a large skillet over high heat until very hot. Sear tuna fillets for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare, or longer to desired doneness.
Toss salad greens with half of the herb vinaigrette.
Plate the dish. Arrange roasted vegetables on plates. Place seared tuna chunks beside vegetables. Add a mound of dressed salad greens.
Drizzle remaining vinaigrette over tuna and vegetables. Garnish with crispy pita wedges and fresh lemon wedges.
notes: For best results, use fresh, high-quality tuna. Adjust searing time to your preferred doneness.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Chicken with Rice and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A rustic Spanish braised chicken dish, centrally plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A single bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, golden-brown from searing, sits atop a bed of tender brown rice, diced potatoes, and rich red tomato sauce. The rice and potatoes are infused with the vibrant reddish-brown hue of smoked paprika and tomato. Diced red bell pepper and onion pieces are visible throughout the saucy rice mixture. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a contrasting garnish. The dish exhibits a moderately saucy, comforting texture. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface. Beside it, a cotton napkin and traditional flatware are neatly arranged. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warm colors and inviting textures. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, maintaining focus on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar
instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and diced red bell pepper to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in canned diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan. Add diced potatoes. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover pan. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 minutes.

Stir in brown rice. Ensure rice is submerged in liquid. Cover and continue to simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Garnish with freshly chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust liquid amount if rice is too dry or too soupy during cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Carrot & Tomato Salad with Chickpeas and Seared Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant mix of colors and textures. Thin, bright orange carrot ribbons form the base, interspersed with halved crimson cherry tomatoes and crisp green cucumber cubes. Scattered among these are creamy beige chickpeas and delicate slivers of purple-red onion, all lightly coated in a glistening, golden lemon-herb vinaigrette. A small portion of golden-brown, seared chicken chunks is artfully arranged on top of the salad, providing a savory counterpoint. Fresh green parsley leaves are sprinkled over the dish as a garnish. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate, all bathed in soft, natural, even lighting to highlight the freshness of the ingredients.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes per side until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest, then cut into 2 cm chunks.
Peel carrots. Use a vegetable peeler to create long, thin ribbons.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Dice cucumber into 1 cm cubes. Thinly slice red onion.
Roughly chop fresh parsley.
Mince garlic cloves.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 45 ml olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, honey, minced garlic, salt, and pepper to create the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine carrot ribbons, halved cherry tomatoes, diced cucumber, sliced red onion, drained chickpeas, and chopped parsley.
Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat.
Divide salad among four plates. Arrange chicken chunks over the salad. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sizzling Beef with Broccoli and Chili-Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sizzling Beef with Broccoli and Chili-Garlic is presented on a round, clean white porcelain plate. A neat mound of fluffy white steamed rice occupies one side of the plate. Adjacent to the rice, the stir-fried beef and broccoli mixture is artfully arranged, forming a vibrant and appealing composition. The beef is cut into tender, thin strips, showcasing its rich, deep brown color from searing and sauce coating. Broccoli florets, crisp-tender, retain their bright green hue. Thinly sliced red onion pieces are interspersed throughout the dish, offering a contrasting purple-red tone. Halved cherry tomatoes add pops of bright red, while minced garlic and sliced chili provide subtle texture and color. The dish is generously garnished with fresh green basil leaves and a few thin slices of red chili, enhancing its visual appeal. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space, avoiding any overcrowding. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by chopsticks and a white cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's textures and colors. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Slice beef against the grain into 0.5 cm thin strips. Toss beef with 15 ml soy sauce and 5 g cornstarch. Set aside.
Cut broccoli into small florets. Thinly slice red onion. Mince garlic. Grate ginger. Thinly slice red chili.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Pick basil leaves.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 45 ml soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, 10 g cornstarch, brown sugar, and 60 ml water. Set aside.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until shimmering. Add beef in a single layer. Sear for 1-2 minutes per side until browned. Remove beef from wok. Set aside.

Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the wok. Add broccoli florets. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender. Add sliced red onion, minced garlic, grated ginger, and sliced red chili. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Return beef to the wok. Pour in the prepared sauce. Stir constantly for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens and coats ingredients.
Remove from heat. Gently fold in halved cherry tomatoes and most of the fresh basil leaves.
Serve immediately with steamed rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Ricotta and Sausage Stuffed Pasta Shells
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white porcelain dinner plate cradles three generously stuffed jumbo pasta shells, partially submerged in a vibrant, rich red tomato sauce. Each shell, perfectly al dente, is brimming with a creamy, pale ricotta and crumbled Italian sausage filling, subtly flecked with green spinach and herbs. A crisp, golden-brown topping of toasted Panko breadcrumbs and savory, rendered pancetta crumbles covers the shells, providing a textural contrast. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered artfully over the dish, with a light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese. The presentation is organized yet inviting, showcasing the dish's comforting warmth and refined execution. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a polished fork and knife, and a folded cream-colored cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's appealing colors and textures against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook pasta shells according to package directions until al dente. Drain. Rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.
In a large skillet, heat 15 mL olive oil over medium heat. Add diced pancetta. Cook until crispy. Remove pancetta with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
In the same skillet with rendered fat, add crumbled Italian sausage. Cook, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Transfer sausage to a large bowl.
In the same bowl, combine cooked sausage, ricotta cheese, 100 g grated Parmesan, egg, chopped spinach, chopped parsley, 5 g red pepper flakes (if using), 5 mL salt, and 2.5 mL black pepper. Mix well.
For the sauce, add remaining 15 mL olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Stir in 15 g chopped basil, 2.5 mL salt, and 2.5 mL black pepper. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce in the bottom of a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Carefully stuff each cooked pasta shell with the ricotta-sausage mixture. Arrange stuffed shells in the baking dish.
Pour remaining tomato sauce over the shells.
In a small bowl, combine crispy pancetta and Panko breadcrumbs. Sprinkle evenly over the stuffed shells.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until bubbling and the topping is golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves and extra grated Parmesan before serving.
notes: Ensure shells are not overcooked to maintain shape during stuffing and baking.
Adjust seasoning of filling and sauce to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Oat Risotto with Roasted Autumn Fruits
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Savory Oat Risotto is elegantly mounded in a free-flowing, organic shape on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy, off-white oats are studded with tender, caramelized roasted fruit wedges, showcasing rich golden-brown hues from the apple, pear, and peach. The fruits are cut into rustic 2 cm thick chunks, naturally arranged atop and around the risotto. A delicate dollop of airy, white savory egg white foam rests gracefully on one side of the risotto, adding a contrasting texture and height. Fresh green thyme sprigs are scattered thoughtfully for vibrant color and aroma. The plate sits on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, all bathed in soft, natural, even lighting within a modern bistro setting. The background remains minimal and uncluttered, focusing solely on the inviting presentation of the dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cut apple, pear, and peach into rustic 2 cm wedges. Discard cores and pits.
Toss fruit wedges with 15 ml olive oil, 2 thyme sprigs, salt, and pepper on the baking sheet.
Roast fruit for 20-25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized. Remove thyme sprigs. Set aside.
Heat vegetable broth in a saucepan. Keep it simmering over low heat.
Finely dice onion and mince garlic.
In a large saucepan or Dutch oven, melt 30 g butter and 15 ml olive oil over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rolled oats to the pan. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add one ladle of hot vegetable broth to the oats. Stir continuously until absorbed.
Continue adding broth one ladle at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed before adding more. This process takes about 20-25 minutes, until oats are creamy and al dente.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in remaining 30 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese until melted and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
For the savory egg white foam: Whisk egg white vigorously until soft peaks form. Gently fold in a tablespoon of warm vegetable broth and a pinch of salt.
Serve risotto immediately. Spoon a generous portion onto each plate. Arrange roasted fruit wedges artfully over the risotto.
Garnish with a dollop of savory egg white foam and fresh thyme sprigs.
notes: Ensure vegetable broth is hot when adding to oats for best risotto consistency.
Adjust seasoning to taste throughout the cooking process.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Baked Rice with Mushrooms and Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A generous, comforting portion of golden-brown Cheesy Baked Rice is served on a simple ceramic plate. The rice is moist and creamy, showcasing melted cheddar and mozzarella, with tender brown mushroom slices and bright green broccoli florets interspersed. The baked surface is slightly crusted, topped with roughly broken, golden-crisp tortilla pieces for crunch. Freshly diced cucumber cubes offer a cool, textural contrast alongside. A vibrant red hot sauce is drizzled atop. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casual cloth napkin. Soft, warm natural light evokes a relaxed family kitchen.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Grease a large baking dish (approx. 30x40 cm) or two smaller dishes.
Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear.

In a large pot, combine rinsed rice and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Remove from heat. Keep covered.
While rice cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms soften and release their liquid.
Add broccoli florets to the skillet. Cook for another 5 minutes until broccoli is tender-crisp. Remove from heat.

In a very large bowl, combine the cooked rice, sautéed mushrooms and broccoli, grated cheddar cheese, shredded mozzarella cheese, softened cream cheese, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly until all ingredients are well combined and cheeses are somewhat melted into the warm rice.
Transfer the rice mixture evenly into the prepared baking dish(es).
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and bubbling.
While the rice bakes, roughly break or cut tortillas into small pieces. Toast them lightly in a dry pan or bake them for a few minutes until crispy.
Dice the cucumber into small cubes.
Remove baked rice from oven. Let stand for 5 minutes.
Serve hot, topped with crispy tortilla pieces, diced cucumber, and a drizzle of hot sauce to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Pepper & Tomato Chicken with Roasted Roots
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and glistening, rests centrally on a clean, undyed linen napkin atop a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table. The chicken is a whole, bone-in piece, its skin crisped from roasting. Around it, a rustic arrangement of roasted vegetables: halved or quartered small potatoes, their skins slightly blistered, and thick wedges of red and yellow bell peppers, softly caramelized at the edges. Bright orange corn kernels are scattered artfully among the vegetables. A vibrant spoonful of tangy, fermented red tomato and green bell pepper relish, diced into small cubes, sits beside the chicken, adding a pop of fresh color. The plate is a handcrafted ceramic in an earthy cream or beige tone, providing ample negative space. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth. A sprig of fresh rosemary and a couple of thyme sprigs, from the roasting, are placed naturally on the plate, adding an organic garnish. A simple, clean, minimalist background ensures focus on the sustainable dish.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Relish (start 3-5 days in advance for full fermentation): Dice 200g tomatoes and 1 bell pepper into small cubes. Combine diced vegetables in a clean glass jar. Dissolve 10g sea salt in 500ml filtered water to make brine. Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermenting weight if available. Cover jar loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until desired tang is reached. Refrigerate when ready.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Halve or quarter potatoes depending on size. Cut remaining 200g tomatoes into wedges. Cut remaining 1 bell pepper into thick wedges. Leave garlic cloves unpeeled.
Toss potatoes, tomato wedges, bell pepper wedges, and unpeeled garlic cloves with 45ml olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Add rosemary and thyme sprigs.
Place seasoned chicken thighs skin-side up on a large baking tray. Arrange seasoned vegetables around chicken on the tray.
Roast for 30 minutes. Flip vegetables. Continue roasting for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized.
While chicken roasts, bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add corn cobs. Cook for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp. Remove corn from cobs; reserve kernels.

Plate one roasted chicken thigh per person. Arrange roasted potatoes, tomato wedges, and bell pepper wedges around chicken. Scatter corn kernels. Spoon a generous amount of fermented bell pepper and tomato relish beside the chicken. Serve immediately.
notes: To minimize waste, chicken bones and vegetable trimmings (bell pepper cores, tomato ends, corn cobs) can be simmered with water for a flavorful stock. This stock can be used for future recipes or as a cooking liquid.
If peeling potatoes, their skins can be roasted separately until crisp for a zero-waste garnish or snack.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Coffee Friands with Coffee Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white porcelain dessert plate holds a single, perfectly golden-brown Lemon Coffee Friand. The friand, oval-shaped with gently rounded edges, has a delicate, slightly crisp crust and a moist, light interior. Its surface is generously coated with a glossy, dark coffee glaze that drips subtly down the sides, creating elegant lines. A vibrant yellow curl of candied lemon peel is artfully placed on top, providing a striking color contrast and textural counterpoint. The friand sits slightly off-center, allowing for balanced negative space on the plate. The background features a simple, clean wooden table surface and a subtle, blurred bistro-style setting, illuminated by soft, natural light, emphasizing the dessert's refined simplicity.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 6-cavity friand or muffin tin.
Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook until butter turns golden brown and smells nutty (beurre noisette). Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Let cool slightly.
In a large bowl, whisk egg whites until foamy.
Add caster sugar, rice flour, and instant coffee powder to the egg whites. Mix gently until just combined.
Stir in the cooled brown butter and lemon zest until batter is smooth. Do not overmix.
Pour batter evenly into prepared friand cavities, filling about two-thirds full.
Bake for 18-22 minutes, or until golden brown and a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove from oven. Let cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
For the glaze: Sift icing sugar into a bowl. Gradually whisk in strong brewed coffee/espresso until a smooth, pourable glaze forms. Adjust consistency as needed.
Once friands are completely cool, dip the tops into the coffee glaze, or drizzle generously over them.
Garnish each friand with a piece of candied lemon peel.

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo de Cerdo con Patatas Asadas y Sofrito de Tomate
recipes.visual_description: A professional, clean presentation of Spanish pork loin. Two thick, seared pork loin medallions, golden-brown with a slight crust, are placed prominently on one side of a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside the pork, a generous portion of rustic, golden-brown roasted potato chunks, about 3cm in size, are piled. A rich, deep red tomato sofrito, thick and glossy from slow simmering, is spooned beside the potatoes, showcasing the cooked-down diced tomatoes and soft onions. Hints of vibrant green fresh chopped parsley are sprinkled over the pork and sofrito, providing a fresh contrast. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a subtle, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sofrito.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel potatoes, cut into 3cm chunks. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, pepper. Spread on baking sheet. Roast 30-35 minutes until golden, tender.
Heat 20ml olive oil in saucepan over medium-low heat. Finely dice onion. Add to saucepan. Cook 10-12 minutes until very soft, translucent. Mince garlic. Add to saucepan. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, smoked paprika, pinch of sugar. Simmer gently 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Season with salt, pepper.

Pat pork loin dry. Cut into 8 medallions. Season generously with salt, pepper. Heat remaining 10ml olive oil in large pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork medallions 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 63°C). Remove pork from pan, rest loosely tented with foil.
Deglaze pork pan with white wine, scraping up browned bits. Add pan liquid to sofrito. Stir in chicken broth. Simmer 5 minutes.
Spoon sofrito onto each plate. Arrange roasted potato chunks beside sofrito. Place two pork medallions on each plate. Chop fresh parsley. Garnish dish with chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Italian Sausage and Roasted Red Pepper Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Italian Sausage and Roasted Red Pepper Rigatoni is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The al dente rigatoni pasta is generously coated in a vibrant, rustic red tomato sauce. Irregularly crumbled, golden-brown sausage chunks are interspersed throughout the pasta. Strips of roasted red pepper, about 2cm wide, add bursts of rich red and soft texture. Freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese is lightly sprinkled over the top, along with several bright green, torn basil leaves, providing a fresh aromatic contrast. The dish has a balanced composition with moderate negative space, highlighting the robust textures and colors. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a silver fork. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and enhancing the food's natural appeal. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add rigatoni. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add Italian sausage. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Add diced yellow onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Add roasted red peppers, cut into 2cm wide strips. Simmer for 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld.

Add cooked rigatoni to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat. Add half of the reserved pasta water, if needed, to achieve desired consistency. Stir in grated Pecorino Romano and chopped fresh basil.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Masala
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a vibrant, deep amber-colored masala sauce with a thick, glossy consistency. Large 4cm chunks of tender, browned chicken thighs and meaty, golden-seared halved button mushrooms are the focal point. The ingredients are nestled together in a shallow white porcelain bowl, showing a rich texture from the reduced onion and tomato base. Fresh, bright green chopped cilantro is scattered over the top. The plate is positioned on a rustic dark wood table. Beside the bowl sits a small stack of warm, charred garlic naan and a side of fluffy, long-grain white basmati rice. Lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the steam rising from the savory sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Side of cucumber raita
Fresh lime wedges
instructions: Cut chicken into 4cm chunks.
Halve the mushrooms.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sauté onions until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides.
Add mushrooms. Cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in curry powder and salt. Toast for 30 seconds.
Pour in tomato puree and water.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in garam masala.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.
notes: Do not overcook mushrooms to maintain texture
Ensure sauce is thick and coats the chicken
Use high-quality fresh ginger-garlic paste for best aroma

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Medallions with Cranberry-Orange Reduction
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate set on a simple wooden table surface. A single portion of two to three pan-seared pork medallions, each a golden-brown, plump chunk, is arranged centrally. The pork has a slight sheen from the sauce. A vibrant, deep red cranberry-orange reduction is generously spooned over and around the pork, pooling attractively on the plate. Scattered around the pork are small, glistening cubes of fresh pineapple, providing a bright yellow contrast and textural interest. A few fresh thyme leaves are artfully placed as a garnish. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, showcasing the rich colors of the sauce and the perfectly cooked pork. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish. A cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. The background suggests a modern bistro with subtle, out-of-focus elements.
instructions: Pat pork tenderloin dry. Season with salt and pepper. Slice into 2.5 cm thick medallions.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear pork medallions 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove pork from pan. Set aside.
Add diced shallots to pan. Sauté 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute more.
Deglaze pan with chicken stock and juice from the orange. Scrape up browned bits.
Add cranberries, orange zest, and thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Cook 8-10 minutes until cranberries burst and sauce thickens slightly.
Remove thyme sprigs. Stir in lemon juice and butter. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Return pork medallions to pan. Spoon sauce over pork.
Serve immediately with a side of small diced fresh pineapple.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef Ragu with Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of Italian beef ragu with tagliatelle pasta is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. The rich, deep reddish-brown ragu, featuring tender, thick chunks of slow-cooked beef, generously coats the golden tagliatelle strands. The pasta and sauce are naturally intertwined, forming a comforting mound at the center of the plate. A scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley adds a touch of color and freshness. Grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the top, hinting at the savory flavor. The dish is set on a well-worn wooden dining table, with visible grain and natural imperfections. Simple, everyday flatware rests beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, inviting kitchen light, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere, reflecting a comfortable family meal. The overall presentation is casual and unpretentious, focusing purely on the appetizing quality of the home-cooked food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmesan cheese on the side.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the ragu.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 3-4 cm chunks

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine (if using). Scrape up browned bits from the bottom. Simmer 2 minutes.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Uncover during the last 30 minutes if sauce is too thin.
Cook tagliatelle according to package instructions in salted water until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Lemon Herb Chicken with Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents as a wholesome, comforting meal on a simple ceramic plate. A single, golden-brown baked chicken breast, cooked whole, sits prominently, showing a light crust and hint of lemon. Around the chicken, generous portions of casually arranged roasted root vegetables. Thick chunks of roasted potatoes display a soft, browned exterior. Bright orange carrot chunks and large, softened red onion wedges are interspersed. Vibrant green broccoli florets are tender-crisp. The palette is warm and inviting, with natural textures. Fresh green parsley adds freshness. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, with soft, natural kitchen lighting. A simple cloth napkin and standard flatware complete the homely setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel carrots and cut into thick chunks. Scrub potatoes and cut into thick wedges. Peel red onion and cut into large wedges.

In a large bowl, toss chopped carrots, potatoes, and red onion with 1 tablespoon olive oil, oregano, thyme, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Spread vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Bake vegetables for 20 minutes.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Rub with remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, pepper, and juice from half a lemon. Slice the remaining half lemon.
Remove baking tray from oven. Push vegetables to one side. Place chicken breasts on the other side of the tray. Add broccoli florets to the tray. Place lemon slices on top of chicken.
Return tray to oven. Bake for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Vegetables should be tender.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish dish with chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Red Onion Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a single, refined portion of pasta and chicken on a smooth, handcrafted ceramic plate in a muted cream tone. The plate rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface. Thick, golden-brown seared chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, are nestled amongst the al dente fusilli pasta, which is lightly coated in a translucent, savory sauce. Vibrant green wilted baby spinach leaves are interspersed throughout the pasta, providing a fresh contrast. Thin, translucent slices of quick-pickled red onion, with their delicate pink hue, are carefully placed on top and around the chicken and pasta, adding pops of color and visual interest. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley provides a final touch of natural green. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space on the plate, emphasizing the natural textures and colors of the ingredients. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded neatly beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, casting gentle shadows and highlighting the organic forms of the food. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural greenery, creating an eco-conscious, serene dining atmosphere.
instructions: Thinly slice red onions. In a small saucepan, combine red wine vinegar, 120ml water, 15g sugar, and 5g salt. Bring to a simmer until dissolved. Pour hot liquid over sliced onions in a heatproof jar. Let cool. Marinate for at least 30 minutes. Drain, reserving some slices for garnish.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 120ml pasta water.

Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Let rest for 5 minutes. Cut into thick chunks.
In the same skillet, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Mince garlic. Add minced garlic to skillet. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Add drained quick-pickled red onions. Sauté 2 minutes.
Pour in vegetable stock and reserved pasta water. Bring to a simmer.
Add cooked pasta and baby spinach to the skillet. Toss until spinach wilts and pasta is coated. Add chicken chunks. Gently toss to combine.
Divide pasta and chicken among four plates. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and reserved quick-pickled red onion slices.
notes: For a truly fermented element, prepare red onions submerged in a 2% brine solution (20g salt per 1 liter water) and ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days before use. This recipe uses a quick-pickling method for immediate use.
Use chicken bones or vegetable scraps to make homemade stock for a zero-waste approach.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto al Pomodoro e Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy, free-flowing Risotto al Pomodoro e Pollo is artfully presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The risotto, a rich orange-red hue from the tomatoes, spreads naturally across the plate, showcasing its fluid, un-molded consistency. Golden-brown, seared chicken chunks, approximately 3 cm in size, are nestled atop the risotto, their irregular shapes adding rustic appeal. Scattered among the risotto are small, tender diced carrots, providing pops of bright orange. A few vibrant green fresh basil leaves are strategically placed on the risotto as a garnish, along with a light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano. The scene is set on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware (fork and spoon) rest beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Pair with a dry white wine.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled, diced into 1 cm pieces

instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.

Add remaining 15 ml olive oil and butter to the pot. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrots. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring often. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. This is the soffritto.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the rice grains until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add crushed tomatoes. Stir well.
Begin adding hot chicken broth, one ladleful (about 120 ml) at a time. Stir frequently. Wait for each ladleful to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next.
After about 10 minutes of adding broth, return the cooked chicken to the pot. Continue adding broth and stirring.
Cook for 18-20 minutes total, or until rice is al dente (tender but with a slight bite in the center). The risotto should be creamy and fluid.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Let rest for 2 minutes. This is the mantecatura.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Risotto should be creamy and fluid, not dry.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Chicken and Olive Penne
recipes.visual_description: The Tuscan Chicken and Olive Penne is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous individual portion. Tender penne pasta forms the base, lightly coated in a rich, rustic sauce. Placed artfully on top are golden-brown, seared chicken chunks, interspersed with vibrant red halved cherry tomatoes and deep purple-black Kalamata olive halves. Wilted green spinach leaves are subtly integrated throughout, adding a pop of fresh color. The dish has a natural, slightly free-form arrangement, avoiding any rigid or overly structured shapes. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the top, with fresh, roughly chopped basil leaves scattered over for a fragrant, verdant garnish. The colors are balanced and natural: the golden chicken, red tomatoes, dark olives, and green spinach against the pale pasta. The texture of the chicken is visibly seared and moist. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. Beside the plate, a white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are neatly placed. Natural, even lighting highlights the ingredients without harsh shadows, creating an inviting and authentic presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette dressing complements the meal.
instructions: Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides and cooked through to 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of skillet. Reduce liquid by half.
Stir in chicken broth, halved cherry tomatoes, and halved Kalamata olives. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes until tomatoes soften slightly.
Return cooked chicken to skillet. Stir in fresh spinach until wilted.
Add cooked penne pasta and reserved pasta water to skillet. Toss to combine.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
notes: For a spicier kick, add a pinch of red pepper flakes with the garlic.
Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Chipotle Chicken and Corn Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous individual portion. A mound of fluffy, golden-hued rice, infused with smoked paprika and flecked with bright yellow corn kernels, forms the base. Resting atop the rice are thick, seared chicken chunks, exhibiting a deep golden-brown crust and juicy interior. The chicken is presented as whole pieces, not sliced or fanned. A vibrant sprinkle of freshly chopped green cilantro garnishes the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. A bright green lime wedge is placed neatly beside the chicken. The overall presentation is clean and organized, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a cotton napkin, and natural, even lighting, creating a casual yet refined bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional hot sauce on the side for those who prefer more heat.
Offer warm tortillas or tortilla chips as an accompaniment for scooping.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with 5g smoked paprika, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to skillet. Add diced small onion. Sauté 3 minutes until soft.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice, remaining 5g smoked paprika, 3g salt, and 1g black pepper. Toast rice 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet tightly. Simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in corn kernels. Place cooked chicken on top of the rice mixture. Cover. Cook 5-7 minutes more, until liquid is absorbed and chicken is heated through.
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest 5 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork. Stir in chipotle hot sauce and juice from half a lime.
Slice chicken into thick chunks.
Serve rice on individual plates. Top with chicken chunks. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and a lime wedge.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature for food safety.
Adjust chipotle hot sauce quantity to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken with Mediterranean Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of baked chicken and roasted Mediterranean vegetables is presented on an everyday, round ceramic plate with a subtle off-white glaze. A golden-brown, whole baked chicken breast sits prominently, its surface showing light charring. Around the chicken, a vibrant medley of roasted vegetables is arranged naturally, with components touching. Thick strips of red, yellow, and green bell peppers display tender, slightly wrinkled skins. Robust half-moon slices of zucchini and tender red onion wedges are interspersed with whole, burst cherry tomatoes, all showcasing caramelized edges. The dish is lightly garnished with chopped fresh green parsley. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen light. A simple, folded cloth napkin and basic metal fork and knife rest beside the plate, creating a relaxed, homely atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Can be served with a side of whole grain bread or a light couscous.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut bell peppers into thick strips. Cut zucchini into thick half-moons. Cut red onion into wedges.
In a large bowl, combine bell peppers, zucchini, red onion, and cherry tomatoes. Add minced garlic, 1 tablespoon olive oil, oregano, thyme, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat.
Place chicken breasts on a baking sheet. Drizzle with remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Arrange seasoned vegetables around the chicken on the baking sheet. Ensure chicken is not overcrowded by vegetables.
Bake for 25-30 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C. Vegetables should be tender and lightly browned.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: This dish is naturally low in calories and can be adapted with other seasonal vegetables like asparagus or broccoli.
Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Chorizo, Roasted Potatoes & Mushrooms, and Apple-Almond Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Chicken with Chorizo, Roasted Potatoes & Mushrooms, and Apple-Almond Salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The plate features three distinct, yet harmonious, components. In the center, golden-brown pan-seared chicken chunks are generously spooned with a rustic, vibrant red tomato-chili sauce, flecked with bright red chili pieces and softened tomato. Alongside, roasted potato wedges, with their browned, slightly crisp edges, and earthy roasted cremini mushroom slices are artfully arranged. Crispy, reddish-orange chorizo rounds are nestled among the chicken and vegetables. A fresh side salad, composed of mixed green leaves, thin apple slices, and toasted slivered almonds, occupies a separate, distinct section of the plate. The dish is garnished with fresh green parsley sprigs. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by classic silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, soft lighting highlights the varied textures and colors, creating an inviting and balanced presentation suitable for a modern bistro.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut potatoes into 2 cm wedges. Slice cremini mushrooms. Mince garlic. Finely dice red chili. Dice chicken breasts into 3-4 cm chunks. Slice chorizo into 0.5 cm rounds. Core and thinly slice apple.
Toss potato wedges with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to the baking sheet with potatoes. Toss. Roast for another 15-20 minutes, until potatoes are tender and browned.

Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes. Ensure internal temperature is 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add chorizo slices to the same skillet. Cook until slightly crispy and fat is rendered, about 3-4 minutes. Remove chorizo.
Reduce heat to medium. Add 1 tbsp olive oil to the skillet. Sauté minced garlic and diced red chili for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until they soften and burst, about 5 minutes.
Pour in chicken stock and hot sauce. Stir well. Add cream cheese. Stir until cream cheese melts and the sauce is slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a dry pan, toast slivered almonds over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until golden. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
In a medium bowl, combine mixed salad greens, thin apple slices, and toasted slivered almonds. Dress with 1 tbsp olive oil, the juice of half a lemon, salt, and pepper. Toss gently.

To serve, arrange roasted potato wedges, roasted mushrooms, cooked chicken chunks, and chorizo rounds on individual plates. Spoon the tomato-chili sauce generously over the chicken. Serve with a side of the apple-almond salad. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust hot sauce to your preferred spice level.
The apple-almond salad provides a fresh, bright contrast to the savory main components.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Cheesy Rice Skillet with Crispy Tortillas and Cucumber Relish
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous portion of the creamy cheesy rice. The rice is golden-yellow from the melted cheddar and mozzarella, with visible flecks of green broccoli florets and dark brown sautéed mushroom slices interspersed throughout. The texture is rich and unctuous, flowing naturally on the plate without being overly stiff. A scattering of golden-brown crispy corn tortilla strips adds a contrasting crunch on top. A small side of vibrant green cucumber relish, with its finely diced pieces, sits neatly beside the main mound of rice. A fresh lime wedge and a sprinkle of chopped cilantro provide bright color and freshness. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin, evoking a relaxed yet refined bistro ambiance. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional hot sauce on the side for individual preference.
Offer a side of pickled jalapeños.
Accompany with a light, refreshing beverage like horchata or agua fresca.
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large, deep skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion and bell pepper. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Cook until browned and tender, about 8-10 minutes.
Add broccoli florets. Cook 3-5 minutes until bright green and slightly tender-crisp.
Stir in rinsed rice, dried oregano, and hot sauce. Pour in broth.
Bring to a simmer. Cover and reduce heat to low. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in softened cream cheese until fully melted and combined.
Add shredded cheddar and mozzarella cheeses. Stir until cheese is melted and creamy. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Cut tortillas into thin strips. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden and crispy. Alternatively, fry in shallow oil until crispy. Drain on paper towels.
In a medium bowl, combine diced cucumber, a pinch of salt, and juice from 1 lime. Add a small amount of chopped cilantro.
Spoon creamy cheesy rice onto plates. Top with crispy tortilla strips. Serve with a side of fresh cucumber relish and a lime wedge. Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity based on desired spice level.
For a richer flavor, use chicken broth. For vegetarian, use vegetable broth.
Any remaining crispy tortillas can be served as a snack.
traditional_techniques: Simmering rice to absorb liquid and flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Beef and Chicken Ragu with Macaroni and Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Tuscan Beef and Chicken Ragu with Macaroni and Rosemary Potatoes is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The macaroni forms a base, generously coated in the rich, deep red-brown ragu. Tender, large chunks of braised beef and shredded chicken pieces are nestled within the sauce. Alongside, golden-brown roasted potato wedges, with crisp edges and soft interiors, are arranged organically. A sprinkle of bright green, fresh basil leaves provides vibrant contrast. Grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the ragu. The setting is a simple wooden table in a modern bistro, bathed in natural, even lighting. A soft cotton napkin and rustic flatware complete the casual yet refined dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Grated Parmesan cheese
Crusty bread for dipping
instructions: Prepare vegetables: Dice onion and carrots. Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic. Cut potatoes into 3cm chunks.

Sear meat: Pat beef and chicken dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until well browned. Remove. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown. Flip. Sear briefly. Remove.
Sauté aromatics: Add onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened. Add garlic and mushrooms. Sauté 3-4 minutes until fragrant and mushrooms soften.
Deglaze (optional): Pour in red wine. Scrape up browned bits from pot bottom. Cook until wine reduces by half.
Simmer ragu: Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, dried oregano, dried basil. Bring to simmer. Return seared beef to pot. Cover. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 2 hours.

Add chicken: After 2 hours, add seared chicken thighs to pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Continue simmer, covered, 45-60 minutes, or until beef and chicken are fork-tender and chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Roast potatoes: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato chunks with 15ml olive oil, fresh rosemary, salt, pepper on baking tray. Roast 30-40 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.
Cook macaroni: 15 minutes before serving, cook macaroni according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain.
Finish dish: Remove beef and chicken from ragu. Shred beef with two forks. Debone chicken and shred meat. Return shredded beef and chicken to ragu. Stir. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve: Divide macaroni among 4 bowls. Ladle generous portions of ragu over macaroni. Place roasted potatoes alongside. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Chicken and Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mexican Chicken and Rice Skillet is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features a natural mound of vibrant reddish-orange rice, cooked with diced tomatoes and spices. Visible amongst the fluffy rice are golden-brown, seared chicken chunks (3-4 cm). Bright yellow corn kernels are interspersed throughout, adding pops of color and texture. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped green cilantro garnishes the top. A bright green lime wedge rests beside the main dish. The plating is organized but not overly arranged, with moderate negative space.
