The setting is a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a professional yet approachable restaurant-style atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side for scooping.
Offer a small bowl of salsa verde or pico de gallo as an optional accompaniment.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Cut into 3-4 cm chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the hot skillet. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, ground cumin, smoked paprika, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in undrained diced tomatoes and rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to coat the rice.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Pour in chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.

Reduce heat to low. Cover the skillet tightly. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Check chicken internal temperature with a thermometer; it must reach 75°C (167°F).
Stir in frozen corn kernels. Cook for 3-5 minutes more, uncovered, until corn is heated through and any remaining liquid is absorbed.
Remove skillet from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff rice gently with a fork.
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with fresh chopped cilantro and a lime wedge.
notes: For best results, use a heavy-bottomed skillet to ensure even cooking.
Adjust spice levels to your preference by adding a pinch of cayenne pepper or a chopped jalapeño with the onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Chipotle Chicken with Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, pan-seared boneless chicken thigh, cooked whole, sits prominently as the centerpiece. Around the chicken, vibrant roasted vegetables are artfully arranged: deep orange sweet potato cubes, bright red and yellow bell pepper chunks, and tender red onion wedges, all showing slight charring from roasting. A glossy, reddish-brown chipotle-lime sauce is lightly drizzled over the chicken and vegetables, creating glistening highlights. Fresh green cilantro leaves are scattered across the dish, providing a pop of contrasting color and freshness. The textures are varied: tender chicken, sweet, slightly caramelized vegetables, and a smooth sauce. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate is placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a clean white cotton napkin and standard flatware.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side.
Offer a small bowl of salsa verde or black beans as accompaniments.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt, pepper, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder.
Combine minced chipotle peppers and adobo sauce in a bowl. Rub half onto chicken thighs.
Toss diced sweet potatoes, bell pepper chunks, red onion wedges with olive oil, salt, pepper.
Spread vegetables on a baking sheet. Roast 15 minutes.
Add chicken thighs to baking sheet. Roast 20-25 minutes, until chicken reaches 75°C and vegetables are tender.
Whisk remaining chipotle mixture with lime juice and chicken broth for sauce.
Let chicken rest 5 minutes.
Serve chicken with roasted vegetables. Drizzle chipotle-lime sauce. Garnish with fresh cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala with Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: Golden pan-seared chicken breast, whole or in two thick pieces, positioned on a pristine white round plate. Earthy brown sautéed cremini mushroom slices are artfully scattered around. A rich, glossy Marsala wine sauce, deep amber, pools around the chicken, lightly coating it. Vibrant green fresh chopped Italian parsley garnishes the dish. Presented on a light wooden table with a crisp white linen napkin and silver flatware. A subtle glass of red wine in the background. Natural, even lighting highlights textures: crisp chicken surface, tender mushrooms, smooth shimmering sauce. Balanced composition with negative space, focusing on the refined single serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple buttered pasta or creamy polenta.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a dry red wine, such as a Chianti or Merlot.

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter, cold, cut into cubes

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Pound each breast to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Dredge chicken breasts lightly in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add sliced cremini mushrooms to the same skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with Marsala wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Reduce heat to low. Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Allow chicken to warm through in the sauce.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in cold butter until melted and incorporated (mantecare).
Stir in fresh chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use a good quality dry Marsala wine for best flavor, not cooking Marsala.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Pepper Chicken with Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: The Black Pepper Chicken with Bell Peppers is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Plump, glossy brown chicken chunks are interspersed with vibrant, crisp-tender red and green bell pepper diamonds and translucent yellow onion wedges. All ingredients are coated in a rich, dark, glistening black pepper sauce. The chicken pieces are seared to a golden-brown exterior, showcasing their tender interior. The vegetables retain their distinct shapes and bright colors, adding visual contrast. A sprinkle of diagonally sliced green onions provides a fresh, bright green garnish on top. The dish is arranged naturally in the center of the plate, allowing for moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. Beside the plate, a small, elegant white porcelain rice bowl filled with fluffy steamed jasmine rice and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks are neatly placed. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and sheen of the food. A cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer chopsticks as traditional utensils.
instructions: Cut chicken into 3cm chunks. In a bowl, combine chicken with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and 1 tablespoon cornstarch. Marinate 15 minutes.
Cut bell peppers into 3cm diamond shapes. Cut onion into 2cm wedges. Mince garlic and ginger.
In a separate bowl, whisk together chicken stock, oyster sauce, 1 tablespoon light soy sauce, dark soy sauce (if using), sugar, and 1 tablespoon cornstarch for the sauce. Set aside.

Heat 2 tablespoons vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over high heat until smoking. Add marinated chicken. Stir-fry 4-5 minutes until browned and cooked through (internal temp 75°C). Remove chicken from wok.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon vegetable oil to wok. Add minced garlic, ginger, and 1 tablespoon coarse black pepper. Stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add bell peppers and onion wedges. Stir-fry 3-4 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Return cooked chicken to wok. Whisk sauce mixture again. Pour sauce over chicken and vegetables.
Stir constantly for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens and coats all ingredients.
Stir in sesame oil.
Transfer to serving plates. Garnish with sliced green onions. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure wok or pan is very hot before adding ingredients for proper stir-frying.
Stir-fry in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding the pan and steaming the ingredients.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Beef Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, rustic Chicken and Beef Cacciatore is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing rich Italian-American comfort. Tender, browned chicken thigh chunks and beef cubes are nestled within a robust, simmering tomato sauce. The sauce is studded with vibrant red and yellow bell pepper pieces, diced onion, and dark, briny Kalamata olives. A generous sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly coats the top, complemented by a scattering of fresh basil leaves for a pop of green. The dish offers a harmonious blend of deep reds, greens, and browns, with varied textures from the succulent meats to the soft vegetables and the creamy cheese. The bowl is centered on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and a slice of crusty artisan bread on a small side plate, all under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread for dipping
Serve over creamy polenta or pasta
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Cut beef stewing cubes into 3 cm cubes. Season chicken and beef with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add beef cubes to the pot. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Dice the onion. Roughly chop red and yellow bell peppers into 2-3 cm pieces. Mince garlic cloves.
Add diced onion and chopped bell peppers to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2-3 minutes until wine reduces slightly.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken and beef to the pot. Stir to combine. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until meats are tender.
Halve the pitted Kalamata olives. Stir olives into the cacciatore during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and grated Parmesan cheese before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Veal with Mushrooms and Macaroni
recipes.visual_description: A hearty portion of Braised Veal with Mushrooms and Macaroni rests in a deep, wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl, positioned slightly off-center. The rich, dark brown stew features tender, irregular chunks of braised veal, approximately 3-4 cm, interspersed with whole and halved cremini mushrooms, diced orange carrots (1.5 cm cubes), and softened onion pieces. A glistening, thick gravy coats the ingredients, pooling slightly at the bottom, hinting at its deep, savory flavor. Beneath the stew, a bed of al dente macaroni pasta peeks out, absorbing the sauce. The dish is garnished with a vibrant scattering of freshly chopped bright green parsley and a few delicate sprigs of fresh rosemary. A light dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese adds a final touch. The bowl sits on a simple, matte wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl, along with standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rustic appeal and inviting textures. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the rich gravy.
Pair with a robust red wine or a dark, malty beer.

ingredients.name: Veal stew meat, cut into 3-4 cm chunks
Brown mushrooms (cremini or button), whole or halved if large

instructions: Pat veal chunks dry. Season with salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Toss with breadcrumbs and flour until lightly coated.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear veal in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove veal and set aside.
Add diced onions and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste, oregano, and savory. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Pour in dark beer and beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Return seared veal to the pot. Add rosemary sprigs.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2-2.5 hours, or until veal is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Add mushrooms to the pot during the last 30 minutes of cooking. Continue simmering until mushrooms are tender.
While stew finishes, cook macaroni pasta according to package instructions until al dente. Drain well.
Remove rosemary sprigs from the stew. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
To serve, spoon macaroni into deep bowls. Ladle generous portions of braised veal and vegetables over the macaroni. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Mayonnaise and corn were omitted as they do not align with the authentic flavor profile and ingredients of a traditional Rustic European braised veal dish.
The breadcrumbs are used to aid in browning the veal and creating a slight crust, contributing to flavor and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Clear Chicken and Mushroom Soup
recipes.visual_description: A clear, golden Japanese soup is presented in a deep, clean white ceramic bowl. Thin, tender slices of cooked chicken breast are visible, interspersed with delicate, dark brown shiitake mushroom slices and slender, pale enoki mushroom clusters. The broth is translucent, allowing the ingredients to be clearly seen. A sprinkle of vibrant green, thinly sliced spring onion rests on top, providing a fresh contrast. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface. Beside it are traditional dark wooden chopsticks resting on a ceramic chopstick rest, and a small, shallow, white ceramic bowl, possibly for rice. The setting is clean, minimalist, and well-lit with natural, even light, emphasizing the soup's fresh ingredients and inviting warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of steamed white rice on the side.
Accompanied by chopsticks and a traditional Japanese soup spoon.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into thin, bite-sized slices. Set aside.

Slice shiitake mushrooms thinly. Trim roots from enoki mushrooms; separate into small clusters. Thinly slice spring onions, keeping white and green parts separate. Peel and thinly slice or julienne ginger.
Heat dashi stock in a large pot over medium heat. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Add chicken slices to the simmering dashi. Cook for 3-4 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (75°C internal temperature). Skim any foam from the surface. Add shiitake mushrooms and enoki mushrooms. Simmer for 2-3 minutes, until mushrooms are tender.
Stir in soy sauce, mirin, and sake. Add ginger slices. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt as needed.
Ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish each bowl with sliced green spring onion. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Provençal with Olives and Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly braised bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken boasts a rich golden-brown, slightly crispy skin, contrasting with its tender interior. A generous portion of vibrant, rustic Provençal sauce surrounds the chicken, featuring discernible diced red and yellow bell peppers, softened yellow onion, and dark, plump Kalamata olives. The sauce has a deep red hue from the tomatoes, with hints of green from fresh thyme sprigs. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the dish. The plating is organized yet organic, allowing moderate negative space around the components. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and traditional flatware beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices to soak up the sauce
Pair with a light green salad dressed with vinaigrette
Accompany with simple boiled potatoes or rice
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 8-10 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add diced yellow onion, red bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in dry white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Stir in canned diced tomatoes, chicken broth, Herbes de Provence, and fresh thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in the liquid.
Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F).
Braise for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove pot from oven. Stir in pitted Kalamata olives.
Let chicken rest in the sauce for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken Thighs with Parmesan Rice and Quick-Pickled Radishes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beer-Braised Chicken Thighs with Parmesan Rice and Quick-Pickled Radishes is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate, sitting on a light, reclaimed wood table. The braised chicken thigh, a single whole piece with deep brown, crispy skin, is placed atop a mound of creamy, off-white Parmesan rice. Adjacent, a vibrant cluster of thinly sliced, translucent pink quick-pickled radishes adds a bright pop of color. A few sprigs of fresh green parsley are scattered over the chicken and rice. The composition is clean and uncluttered, with ample negative space. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting textures and colors. The background is simple and out of focus. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed beside the plate. The presentation is organic and unforced, emphasizing the natural beauty and sustainable preparation of ingredients.
instructions: Prepare quick-pickled radishes: Combine sliced radishes, white wine vinegar, 120 ml water, sugar, and 5g salt in a jar. Stir. Let sit at room temperature while preparing the rest of the meal.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until deep golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in dark beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.

Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Add chicken stock and bay leaf. Ensure chicken is partially submerged. Cover and transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 45-50 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.

While chicken braises, prepare Parmesan rice: Rinse rice under cold water until clear. Combine rinsed rice and 600 ml water in a medium saucepan. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Once rice is cooked, remove from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Carefully remove braised chicken from the oven. Let rest briefly.

To serve, spoon a generous portion of cheesy rice onto each plate. Place one braised chicken thigh on top of the rice. Arrange a small portion of quick-pickled radishes beside the chicken. Drizzle with fermented hot sauce to taste. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
notes: To make this dish even more zero-waste, save chicken bones from previous meals to make homemade stock for braising.
Vegetable scraps like onion ends or carrot peels can be added to the braising liquid for extra flavor, then strained out before serving.
The quick-pickled radishes can be prepared several hours or even a day in advance for deeper flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Shrimp Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous, home-style portion of Creamy Chicken and Shrimp Tomato Pasta is casually arranged on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slight lip. The pasta, likely fusilli or penne, is coated in a rich, reddish-orange creamy tomato sauce, showing natural variations in color. Visible among the pasta are irregular, thick chunks of seared chicken breast, cooked to a light golden-brown, and plump, pink shrimp. Some of the shrimp show a slight curl. The dish has a moist, saucy texture, with the sauce clinging well to the pasta. A scattering of coarsely chopped fresh green parsley leaves provides a vibrant contrast on top. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, suggesting a family kitchen setting. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually folded beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating soft shadows. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in, cozy home environment.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2.5 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Sear chicken until golden brown and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the skillet. Add shrimp. Cook for 2-3 minutes until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp from skillet.
Finely chop onion. Mince garlic.
Add onion to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, Dijon mustard, chicken broth, and heavy cream. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer sauce for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
While sauce simmers, cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 60ml pasta water.
Return cooked chicken and shrimp to the sauce. Stir to combine.
Add drained pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat. If needed, add reserved pasta water to reach desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Chop fresh parsley. Serve immediately, garnished with parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Herb-Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown, roasted bone-in chicken thigh is the focal point on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken skin is crisp and rich in color. Beside it, several rustic, golden-brown potato wedges are artfully arranged, some showing their fluffy interior. Scattered around the plate are vibrant halved cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly blistered, and dark, briny Kalamata olives. A light, glossy pan sauce, infused with herbs and lemon, is subtly drizzled over the chicken and potatoes, adding a touch of moisture and sheen. Fresh sprigs of rosemary and thyme are placed for garnish, providing a pop of green. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver cutlery are placed beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors, creating an inviting, casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the pan juices.
A simple green salad with a lemon vinaigrette complements the richness.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Maris Piper or Russet), medium

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Cut potatoes into 2 cm thick wedges.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Roughly chop Kalamata olives.
Thinly slice half the lemon into rounds. Juice the other half.
Finely chop garlic. Roughly chop rosemary and thyme leaves.
In a large roasting pan, combine potato wedges, halved cherry tomatoes, chopped olives, garlic, rosemary, thyme, and lemon slices.
Drizzle with 40 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Arrange chicken thighs skin-side up among the vegetables in the pan.
Drizzle remaining 20 ml olive oil over chicken.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Pour chicken broth and lemon juice into the pan. Stir vegetables around chicken.
Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
For extra crispy potatoes, ensure they are in a single layer and not overcrowded.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Tuscan Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. The rigatoni pasta is generously coated in a rich, rustic red-orange tomato sauce, infused with oregano and garlic. Tender, seared chicken breast, cut into thick chunks, is nestled amidst the pasta and sauce. Diced red bell peppers and onions are visible within the sauce, adding vibrant color and texture. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped oregano leaves garnishes the dish, providing a contrasting green. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the top. The overall presentation is inviting and abundant, with moderate negative space. A folded cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish as the focal point with a soft, blurred background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the delicious sauce.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a light-bodied Italian red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm thick chunks. Season chicken with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken simmers, cook rigatoni pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta.
Add drained pasta to the skillet with the sauce and chicken. Toss to coat all ingredients evenly.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh chopped oregano or basil and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust salt and pepper to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Shkmeruli Chicken
recipes.visual_description: Chicken pieces, including golden-brown seared thighs, drumsticks, and breast chunks, are nestled in a creamy, off-white garlic milk sauce on a rustic, dark ceramic plate. The sauce pools naturally around the chicken, highlighting its rich texture. A generous sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped cilantro garnishes the dish. The plate rests on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden dining table. A torn piece of Georgian Shotis Puri bread and a small bowl of fresh green herbs are casually placed nearby. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a lived-in, comfortable atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with fresh Shotis Puri (Georgian bread) for dipping into the sauce
A side of fresh herbs
Often accompanied by Georgian dry red wine
instructions: Cut chicken into 8 serving pieces. Pat chicken pieces dry thoroughly. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken pieces, skin-side down. Sear until deeply golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes.
Flip chicken pieces. Reduce heat to medium. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F), about 15-20 minutes, turning occasionally. Remove chicken from pan. Keep warm.
Drain excess oil from the pan, leaving about 1 tablespoon of drippings. Add butter to the pan.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown the garlic.
Pour in milk. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring constantly. Cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Return chicken pieces to the pan, nestling them into the sauce. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Stir in chopped cilantro. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot directly from the pan or transfer to a serving dish.
notes: The sauce should be flavorful with garlic but not overpowering.
Ensure chicken is cooked through to 75°C (167°F) for safety.
For a richer sauce, replace half the milk with heavy cream.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Beef, Tomato, and Rice Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of baked beef, tomato, and rice pasta rests in a clean white porcelain oval baking dish, showcasing a rich, golden-brown mozzarella and Parmesan crust. Visible underneath the bubbling cheese are tender penne pasta, hearty ground beef chunks, and a vibrant red tomato sauce. The dish presents a rustic yet refined appearance. Freshly torn green basil leaves are scattered over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The scene is set on a simple, light wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware positioned beside the dish. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and inviting warmth of the baked pasta, with a subtle, blurred background of a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add ground beef to skillet. Cook, breaking it apart, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, dried oregano, dried basil, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in cooked short-grain rice. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
In a large bowl, combine cooked pasta, beef and tomato sauce, ricotta cheese, and 100 grams of mozzarella cheese. Mix thoroughly.
Transfer pasta mixture to a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Sprinkle remaining 100 grams of mozzarella cheese and grated Parmesan cheese evenly over the top.
Bake 25-30 minutes, or until cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh torn basil.
notes: Ensure pasta is al dente before baking, as it will continue to cook in the oven.
The cooked rice adds body and a unique texture to the traditional baked pasta.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Cherry Clafoutis
recipes.visual_description: A warm, golden-brown Cherry Clafoutis is presented in a rustic, round ceramic baking dish, slightly sunken in the center after cooling. The surface shows a beautiful, irregular golden crust with hints of caramelized sugar. Dark red, plump cherries are visible, partially submerged within the creamy, custard-like base. The edges of the clafoutis are slightly puffed and browned. A light, even dusting of white icing sugar covers the entire surface, providing a gentle contrast. The dish sits on a well-used, light wooden kitchen table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. A single portion is scooped onto a simple, off-white ceramic dessert plate with a slightly uneven rim, accompanied by a small, traditional silver spoon. The setting is a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, with warm, natural light illuminating the scene. A casually placed linen napkin in a neutral tone rests beside the plate. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a comfortable, everyday dining environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm, not hot.
Traditionally served plain, but can be accompanied by a dollop of crème fraîche or plain whipped cream.
Dust with icing sugar just before serving.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Grease a 20-22 cm diameter baking dish with butter. Dust lightly with sugar.
Arrange pitted cherries evenly in the prepared dish.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs and granulated sugar until light and frothy.
Sift flour and salt into the egg mixture. Whisk until smooth.
Gradually whisk in the cream and vanilla extract until the batter is smooth.
Pour the batter over the cherries in the baking dish.
Bake for 40-50 minutes. The clafoutis should be puffed, golden brown, and set in the center.
Remove from oven. Let cool slightly on a wire rack.
Dust generously with icing sugar before serving.
notes: If using frozen cherries, thaw them completely and drain any excess liquid before adding to the dish.
The clafoutis will puff up significantly in the oven and then settle as it cools; this is normal.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Beef Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous mound of penne pasta occupies the center of a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Interspersed throughout the pasta are golden-brown roasted chicken chunks and beef chunks, their exteriors showing slight caramelization. Bright red and yellow bell pepper strips, along with tender, caramelized red onion wedges, are scattered amongst the pasta and meats, adding vibrant color and varied textures. Minced roasted garlic is subtly present. A light, savory tomato-herb sauce coats all ingredients, providing a cohesive sheen. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley, adding a pop of green. The composition is organic and inviting, not rigid. A small, separate white bowl holds a simple green salad of mixed leaves, dressed lightly. The setting is a clean, light-colored wooden table, with a simple white cotton napkin folded neatly beside the bowl. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the food's inviting colors and textures.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut chicken and beef into 3cm chunks. Cut bell peppers into 2cm strips. Cut red onion into thick wedges. Smash and roughly chop garlic cloves.

In a large roasting pan, combine chicken chunks, beef chunks, bell pepper strips, onion wedges, and chopped garlic. Drizzle with 45ml olive oil. Season with salt, black pepper, dried oregano, and dried basil. Toss to coat evenly.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken and beef are cooked through and browned. Internal temperature for chicken must reach 75°C. Stir halfway through roasting.
While meat and vegetables roast, cook pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving 125ml pasta water.

Remove roasting pan from oven. Transfer roasted chicken, beef, and vegetables to a separate bowl. Place roasting pan on stovetop over medium heat. Add diced tomatoes and chicken broth to pan. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.

Add cooked pasta to the sauce in the roasting pan. Return roasted chicken, beef, and vegetables to the pan. Toss everything together to coat. Add reserved pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Dress mixed salad greens with remaining 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Serve pasta immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley. Serve with the side salad.

recipes.recipe_name: Homely Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.visual_description: A generous, comforting single portion of Homely Chicken Noodle Soup in a deep, off-white ceramic bowl. The golden-yellow broth is rich and clear, with tender, shredded chicken pieces visible. Alongside are vibrant, small diced carrots and celery, and translucent diced onions. The wide, flat egg noodles are perfectly cooked, slightly submerged in the broth. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a pop of color on top. The ingredients are naturally arranged, allowing components to touch and overlap, creating a rustic, inviting look. The soup fills the bowl adequately, showing its hearty nature. The bowl sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, showing subtle grain. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone is casually placed beside it. The scene is lit by warm, soft kitchen light, evoking a cozy, lived-in atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. The background is minimal, blurred, focusing entirely on the soup.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Add chicken thighs, dried thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken thighs from the pot. Shred chicken using two forks. Set aside.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add egg noodles to the simmering broth. Cook according to package directions, usually 7-10 minutes, until tender.
Return shredded chicken to the pot.
Season the soup with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust seasoning to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Mushroom Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown seared chicken breast, cooked whole, sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken has a rich, caramelized crust. A generous portion of creamy, savory mushroom sauce is spooned artfully over and around the chicken. The sauce is off-white with varying shades of earthy brown from the sliced mushrooms. The mushrooms are tender, with some retaining a slight chew. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its succulent texture. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface beside a folded cotton napkin. Standard European flatware is neatly placed. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, creating a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour if using.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until browned and tender.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the skillet. Cook 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in white wine if using. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Simmer 1 minute until reduced.
Stir in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Do not boil vigorously.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Simmer 2 minutes to heat through.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Tomato-Garlic Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, substantial pan-seared chicken thigh, its skin deeply golden and crispy, rests atop a bed of rustic roasted potatoes. The potatoes, halved and quartered, exhibit tender, floury interiors and golden-brown, slightly blistered skins, scattered loosely on the plate. A vibrant, rich red tomato-garlic sauce, thick and slightly chunky, is spooned generously over the chicken and potatoes, its surface glistening. A few fresh sprigs of rosemary and thyme are artfully placed for a natural, subtle green accent. The overall composition is minimalistic, featuring ample negative space on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm cream or beige tone. The setting is a light-colored, natural wood surface, illuminated by soft, diffused natural light, with an undyed linen napkin subtly folded beside the plate, emphasizing an eco-conscious, clean aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes thoroughly. Halve or quarter small potatoes.
Toss potatoes with 15ml olive oil, rosemary sprigs, thyme sprigs, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, until tender and golden.
Pat chicken thighs completely dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs, skin-side down, in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crispy.
Flip chicken thighs. Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven. Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While chicken cooks, prepare the sauce. Dice the tomatoes. If using fresh garlic, mince it.
In a small saucepan, heat a splash of olive oil over medium heat. Add fermented garlic paste (or minced fresh garlic). Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes to the saucepan. Simmer for 10-12 minutes, breaking down the tomatoes with a spoon. Season with salt and pepper.
For a smoother sauce, lightly mash or partially blend with an immersion blender, leaving some texture.
To plate, arrange roasted potatoes on a serving plate. Place a chicken thigh on top of the potatoes.
Spoon a generous amount of the tomato-garlic sauce over the chicken and potatoes. Garnish with a fresh herb sprig.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing skin-on potatoes and whole tomatoes. The fermented garlic adds a preserved, umami-rich element to the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon-Herb Pan Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken, cut into thick medallions, is centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken boasts a golden-brown sear, revealing a tender, juicy interior. A glossy, light golden lemon-herb pan sauce is generously drizzled over the chicken and pools elegantly around it. Vibrant green asparagus spears, lightly roasted, are neatly arranged alongside the chicken, adding a fresh color contrast. The plate maintains moderate negative space, showcasing a professional yet approachable presentation. The setting features a simple wooden table, standard silver flatware, and a white cotton napkin, illuminated by natural, even light, hinting at a modern bistro ambiance.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 5-6 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C. Bake 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Rest on a cutting board.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced shallot and garlic to the skillet. Sauté 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Deglaze with white wine, scraping up browned bits. Reduce wine by half.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half, about 5-7 minutes.

Remove skillet from heat. Stir in lemon juice, lemon zest, chopped parsley, and thyme. Whisk in cold butter until sauce is emulsified and slightly thickened. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice each chicken breast into 3-4 thick medallions. Arrange chicken on plates. Spoon pan sauce over chicken. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Ajillo (Spanish Garlic Chicken)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo al Ajillo served in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The dish features three large, whole chunks of bone-in chicken with crispy, deep-golden skin. Scattered around the chicken are twenty whole, softened garlic cloves, caramelized to a rich mahogany color. A glossy, amber-colored sherry reduction coats the base of the bowl. Vibrant green, finely chopped parsley is sprinkled over the meat and sauce. The arrangement is natural and rustic. The bowl sits on a dark oak bistro table. Beside the bowl is a small plate with two thick wedges of crusty sourdough bread and a clean white cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and soft from the side.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the garlic oil
Accompany with a glass of chilled Fino sherry
Traditional side of fried potatoes or a simple green salad

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, bone-in, skin-on, cut into large chunks

instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry with paper towels.
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-based skillet over medium heat.
Add garlic cloves to the oil.
Fry garlic until golden brown on all sides.
Remove garlic and set aside.
Increase heat to medium-high.
Brown chicken chunks in batches skin-side down first.
Cook until skin is crisp and golden.
Remove excess oil, leaving 2 tablespoons in the pan.
Return all chicken and fried garlic to the skillet.
Add smoked paprika and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sherry and deglaze the pan.
Reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Use high-quality Spanish olive oil for the best flavor profile
Do not burn the garlic or the sauce will turn bitter
Ensure chicken skin is very dry before browning to achieve maximum crispness

recipes.recipe_name: Sous Vide Beef Cheek, Brown Mustard Jus, Fermented Chili Oil
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly portioned sous vide beef cheek, approximately 200g, presents a deep, burnished mahogany hue, its surface subtly glistening from a final gentle sear. The beef, unsliced, is placed organically off-center on a pristine white bone china plate with a very subtle, elegant pattern. Beside it, a lustrous, dark amber-brown brown mustard seed jus forms an inviting, naturally flowing pool, its surface catching the light. A few precise droplets of vibrant, fiery red fermented chili oil are artfully dotted around the beef and jus, creating a striking color contrast. A single, perfectly placed delicate microgreen, such as a pea shoot or cress, rests atop the beef, providing a fresh, verdant accent. The plate is surrounded by abundant negative space, emphasizing the dish's architectural precision and minimalist elegance. The setting features a cool white Carrara marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a sharp triangle, and traditional European flatware. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing depth and texture, with an ultra-minimalist background to ensure the dish is the sole focus.
instructions: Season beef cheeks generously with sea salt and black pepper. In a hot pan, sear beef cheeks on all sides until deeply caramelized. Cool slightly.

Place seared beef cheeks into vacuum-sealable bags with a small sprig of thyme and a tablespoon of beef stock. Seal completely. Cook in a preheated water bath at 82°C for 12-16 hours, or until fork-tender.

For the Brown Mustard Seed Jus: In a saucepan, sauté diced shallot and smashed garlic in a touch of oil until translucent. Deglaze with red wine, reducing by half. Add brown mustard seeds and beef stock. Bring to a simmer and reduce by two-thirds until a rich, glossy jus forms. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding solids. Return jus to clean saucepan. Keep warm.

For the Fermented Chili Oil: In a small saucepan, combine fermented red chilies and neutral oil. Heat gently over low heat for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to infuse. Do not let oil smoke. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding solids. Cool.
Once beef cheeks are cooked, remove from bags. Pat dry. Reheat gently in a pan with a splash of the cooking liquid, or briefly sear for a fresh crust.
Just before serving, whisk cold butter into the warm mustard jus until emulsified and glossy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

On each plate, place a single beef cheek, or cut into two thick, irregular chunks. Spoon a generous pool of the glossy brown mustard jus beside or beneath the beef. Drizzle a few drops of the vibrant red fermented chili oil artfully around the beef. Garnish with a single delicate microgreen. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Chicken Orzo with Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lemon Herb Chicken Orzo with Roasted Vegetables is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The orzo forms a cohesive base, lightly coated with a delicate sheen from olive oil and infused with herbs. Arranged artfully atop the orzo are substantial chunks of golden-brown seared chicken breast, cooked to tender perfection. Interspersed among the chicken and orzo are vibrant, roasted vegetables: thick strips of red, yellow, and orange bell peppers, thick half-moon slices of green zucchini, bright red whole cherry tomatoes, and tender wedges of red onion. The vegetables exhibit slight charring at their edges, showcasing the roasting technique. Fresh green sprigs of parsley, oregano, and thyme are scattered across the dish, adding a burst of color and aromatic freshness. A light dusting of shaved Parmesan cheese is visible. A lemon wedge is placed alongside the dish. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a professional and appealing restaurant-style image.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut bell peppers into thick strips. Slice zucchini into thick half-moons. Cut red onion into wedges. Halve cherry tomatoes.
Toss bell peppers, zucchini, red onion, and cherry tomatoes with 30ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables for 20-25 minutes, until tender and lightly charred. Set aside.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, and a pinch of dried oregano and thyme.

Heat 20ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-6 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Transfer chicken to a cutting board. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add orzo to the skillet. Stir for 1 minute. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook orzo, stirring occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until liquid is absorbed and orzo is al dente.
Slice rested chicken into substantial chunks or thick medallions.
Stir roasted vegetables, chopped parsley, oregano, and thyme into the cooked orzo. Squeeze in juice from half a lemon.
Divide orzo mixture among four plates. Arrange chicken chunks on top. Garnish with shaved Parmesan and a lemon wedge. Serve immediately.
notes: Resting the chicken after searing ensures it remains juicy.
Adjust herbs to your preference, using fresh for best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, charred chunks of succulent chicken submerged in a vibrant, velvety orange-red tomato gravy. The chicken is presented as whole 4cm cubes, never sliced. A delicate swirl of white heavy cream decorates the surface, contrasting with the rich sauce. Freshly chopped bright green cilantro and a sprinkle of crushed dried fenugreek leaves provide texture. The meal is served in a traditional hammered copper bowl placed on a dark wooden table. Beside the bowl lies a piece of charred garlic naan and a small mound of fluffy basmati rice. A side of thinly sliced red onion rings and a lemon wedge add authentic color. Natural, warm lighting highlights the glossy sheen of the butter-enriched sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Include lachha pyaz (sliced red onion salad with lemon)
Provide fresh lime wedges

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs (boneless, skinless), cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Whisk yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp chili powder, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Add chicken chunks to the marinade. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat. Sear chicken until charred and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken.
Melt butter in the same pan. Add remaining ginger-garlic paste. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add tomato puree and remaining chili powder. Simmer for 15 minutes until sauce thickens.
Stir in garam masala, honey, and salt.
Return chicken chunks to the pan. Mix well.
Pour in heavy cream. Add crushed dried fenugreek leaves. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for safety.
Kashmiri chili powder provides the signature red color without excessive heat.
Crushing fenugreek leaves between palms releases maximum aroma.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Herb-Roasted Chicken Thighs with Crispy Smashed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Herb-Roasted Chicken Thighs with Crispy Smashed Potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface. A golden-brown, crisp-skinned roasted chicken thigh, presented as a whole piece, is the focal point. Adjacent to it are several irregularly shaped, golden-brown crispy smashed potatoes, showing their textured, rustic exteriors and soft interiors. Scattered around the plate are plump, pale golden garlic confit cloves. A rich, glossy pan sauce, amber in color, is artfully drizzled over and around the chicken and potatoes. Fresh green rosemary and thyme leaves are sprinkled for vibrant color and aroma. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits nearby, ready for squeezing. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting includes a folded cotton napkin beside the plate and hints of a casual bistro background with even, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with lemon vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread to sop up the sauce.

ingredients.name: Small potatoes (e.g., new potatoes, Yukon Gold)
Olive oil
ingredients.quantity: 150 ml (for confit and roasting) + extra for potatoes

instructions: Prepare Garlic Confit: Place peeled garlic cloves in a small saucepan. Cover with 100 ml olive oil. Heat gently over low heat. Cook for 25-30 minutes until very soft and golden. Do not brown. Set aside.
Prepare Potatoes: Wash potatoes. Boil in salted water until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Smash Potatoes: Place cooked potatoes on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Use a potato masher or the bottom of a glass to gently smash each potato until flattened to about 1.5-2 cm thick.
Roast Potatoes: Drizzle smashed potatoes with olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Roast in a preheated oven at 200°C for 25-30 minutes, or until deeply golden and crispy.
Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken thighs very dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Sear Chicken: Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deep golden brown and crispy.

Finish Chicken in Oven: Flip chicken thighs. Add remaining rosemary and thyme sprigs to the skillet. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven (200°C). Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.

Make Pan Sauce: Remove chicken from skillet; set aside to rest. Discard herb sprigs. Place skillet over medium heat. Deglaze with white wine (if using) and chicken stock, scraping up browned bits. Reduce liquid by half. Stir in butter and squeeze in juice from half a lemon. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Serve: Plate one chicken thigh per person. Arrange crispy smashed potatoes alongside. Spoon garlic confit cloves around. Drizzle generously with pan sauce. Garnish with fresh rosemary and thyme leaves, and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Pappardelle with Italian Sausage Ragu
recipes.visual_description: The Pappardelle with Italian Sausage Ragu is presented in a deep, classic white porcelain pasta bowl, showcasing a rich, inviting composition. Long, broad pappardelle ribbons are loosely twirled, forming a generous base. The robust ragu, featuring tender, rustic chunks of browned Italian sausage and a deep red, slow-simmered tomato sauce, is spooned generously over the pasta. Finely diced soffritto vegetables are subtly integrated, adding texture and depth. A scattering of vibrant green fresh basil leaves provides a fresh counterpoint, alongside a generous grating of pale yellow Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese. The dish exhibits a warm, comforting palette of deep reds, earthy browns, and fresh greens. The overall plating is clean, professional, and abundant, with appropriate negative space. It sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the remaining ragu.
Pair with a robust Italian red wine, such as a Sangiovese or Chianti.
instructions: Remove sausage meat from casings. Break into rustic chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery (soffritto). Cook 8-10 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sausage meat to the pot. Increase heat to medium-high. Brown well, breaking up meat with a spoon. Cook 8-10 minutes. Drain any excess fat.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer 5 minutes until reduced by half.
Stir in crushed San Marzano tomatoes, beef stock, red pepper flakes (if using), salt, and black pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover partially. Simmer 60-90 minutes, stirring occasionally. The sauce should thicken and flavors meld.
Cook pappardelle in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions. Cook until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add directly to the ragu. Toss to coat the pasta thoroughly with the sauce.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh basil leaves and a generous grating of Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese.
notes: For best flavor, use high-quality Italian sausages with good fat content.
Adjust the simmering time of the ragu to achieve your desired sauce consistency; longer simmering yields a richer, thicker sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz Caldo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz Caldo is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, resting on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. The soup is a creamy, thick rice porridge with a comforting golden-yellow hue, showcasing tender chunks of chicken. The texture is visually rich and comforting. The surface of the soup is garnished with vibrant green thinly sliced spring onions, contrasting with golden-brown crispy fried garlic flakes. Two hard-boiled egg quarters, revealing their white and yellow parts, are carefully placed on top of the porridge. A bright yellow calamansi or lemon wedge is positioned on the rim of the bowl, ready to be squeezed. The overall composition is balanced with appropriate negative space, highlighting the dish's warmth and authentic elements. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene. A cotton napkin and a soup spoon are placed beside the bowl, contributing to a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra calamansi or lemon wedges on the side for added tartness.
Offer small bowls of fish sauce (patis) with chopped chilies (siling labuyo) for additional seasoning.
instructions: Wash rice thoroughly. Drain well. Set aside.
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks.
Dice the onion. Julienne the ginger. Mince the garlic.
Heat cooking oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté diced onion until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add julienned ginger. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until lightly golden.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Cook 5-7 minutes until lightly browned on all sides.
Pour in fish sauce. Stir to coat chicken and aromatics.
Add washed rice to the pot. Stir to combine and coat rice grains.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a boil.

Reduce heat to low. Simmer, uncovered, for 30-40 minutes. Stir occasionally to prevent rice from sticking to the bottom. Continue cooking until rice is very tender and the soup has thickened to a porridge-like consistency.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Slice spring onions thinly. Quarter the hard-boiled eggs.
Ladle hot Arroz Caldo into individual serving bowls.
Garnish each bowl with sliced spring onions, crispy fried garlic, and hard-boiled egg quarters. Place a calamansi or lemon wedge on the side of each bowl.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Wild Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Wild Rice Pilaf is presented on a round white porcelain dinner plate. A neat mound of creamy wild rice pilaf, showcasing deep brown grains, forms the base. Two substantial, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast pieces, cut into thick diagonal chunks, are placed beside the pilaf. The chicken shows a beautiful sear. Small, crispy bits of smoked bacon are scattered over the pilaf and chicken. A light sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley and a few bright red chili flakes provide color contrast. The arrangement is balanced with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded cream-colored cotton napkin and standard silver flatware accompany the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a professional bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Rinse wild rice under cold water. Combine wild rice and chicken broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 45-50 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid absorbed. Set aside.
Cut bacon into 1 cm lardons. Cook bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Drain excess fat, leaving 15ml in the skillet. Set crispy bacon aside.

Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat remaining bacon fat and olive oil in the same skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest 5 minutes. Slice each breast into two thick diagonal pieces.
Finely dice the onion. Mince the garlic. Finely mince the candied ginger.
Melt butter in the same skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and minced candied ginger. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.

Stir in the cooked wild rice, cream cheese, and grated Parmesan cheese. Mix until cream cheese melts and forms a creamy pilaf. Stir in half of the crispy bacon bits and half of the chili flakes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Spoon a generous portion of creamy wild rice pilaf onto the center of each plate. Arrange two thick pieces of pan-seared chicken beside the pilaf. Garnish with remaining crispy bacon bits, a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley, and remaining chili flakes.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Sausage and Potato Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Smoked Sausage and Potato Skillet is presented on a clean, rustic white ceramic dinner plate. Golden-brown potato cubes, roughly 1.5 cm, are mixed with 1 cm thick rounds of pan-seared smoked sausage, tender diced onion, bright green peas, and a scattering of vibrant red diced tomatoes. A light layer of melted, bubbling yellow cheddar cheese gently binds some elements. The textures are varied: crisp-edged potatoes, slightly caramelized sausage, soft vegetables, and gooey cheese. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley, adding a pop of color. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A neat grey cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting appeal. The background is minimal, ensuring the focus remains on the food.
instructions: Slice smoked sausage into 1 cm thick rounds.
Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes.
Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add potato cubes. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until tender and golden-brown.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until onion softens and becomes translucent.
Add sausage rounds to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned.
Stir in diced tomatoes and green peas. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing peas to warm through.
Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese over the skillet mixture. Cover the skillet for 1-2 minutes, allowing cheese to melt.
Remove from heat. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Tenderloin with Cherry-Verjus Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Pork Tenderloin with Cherry-Verjus Sauce, presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. Three to four thick, rustic medallions of golden-brown seared pork tenderloin, each about 2-3 cm thick, are arranged slightly overlapping in the center of the plate. A rich, glossy, reddish-brown sauce, studded with plump, halved pitted cherries and flecks of finely diced shallots, is generously spooned over and around the pork. The sauce has a subtle sheen from the verjus and butter. The pork medallions show a tender, pale pink interior, indicating proper cooking. A few fresh thyme leaves are scattered naturally over the dish as a functional garnish. The plate rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain and subtle imperfections. Beside the plate, a simple set of everyday metal flatware – a fork and knife – are casually placed. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy lighting, typical of a home kitchen, creating a relaxed, inviting atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, focusing entirely on the homely, comforting presentation of the meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Pat pork tenderloin dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear pork tenderloin on all sides until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes total.
Transfer pan to the preheated oven. Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 70°C. It will reach 75°C while resting.
Remove pork from pan. Set aside on a cutting board to rest, loosely tented with foil.
Return pan to medium heat. Add butter. Sauté diced shallots until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and thyme sprigs. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in pitted cherries. Cook for 2 minutes.
Deglaze pan with verjus. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Add chicken stock, vanilla extract, and lemon zest. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, until sauce slightly thickens.
If a thicker sauce is desired, whisk 15g flour with a tablespoon of cold water to make a slurry. Stir into simmering sauce. Cook 1-2 minutes until thickened.
Remove thyme sprigs from the sauce. Stir in lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Slice pork tenderloin into thick medallions, about 2-3 cm thick.
Serve pork medallions immediately with a generous spoon of cherry-verjus sauce over top.
notes: Resting the pork tenderloin after cooking is crucial for juiciness. Do not skip this step.
Adjust the sauce consistency by reducing more for a thicker sauce or adding a touch more stock for a thinner one.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single serving of chicken and rice is casually plated on a round, off-white ceramic dinner plate. Diced, seared chicken chunks are nestled within fluffy, golden-hued long-grain rice, which is interspersed with bright red diced tomatoes and flecks of sautéed onion. The rice has a natural, slightly uneven texture. Alongside, a generous portion of vibrant green broccoli florets, roasted to a tender-crisp texture with subtle char marks, is arranged naturally, slightly overlapping the rice. The dish is presented on a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table, illuminated by warm, natural overhead light. A simple metal fork rests beside the plate. The scene is homely and inviting, focusing on comforting, well-prepared food without any pretense.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread on the side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Dice chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook in batches if needed. Remove chicken from skillet. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C when fully cooked.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to skillet. Add chopped onion. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried herbs. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to skillet. Stir gently.
Cover skillet tightly. Transfer to preheated oven. Bake 20-25 minutes, until rice is tender and liquid absorbed.
While skillet bakes, toss broccoli florets with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast in oven for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Remove skillet from oven. Let rest 5 minutes, covered.
Fluff rice with a fork. Serve chicken and rice mixture alongside roasted broccoli.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken and Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a single, generous portion in a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, are nestled amidst saffron-infused rice. The rice is moist and free-flowing, not compacted, showcasing vibrant red and yellow bell pepper diced into 2 cm pieces, and earthy sliced mushrooms. Small bursts of red from diced tomatoes are visible. A light sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley provides a contrasting color and freshness. The composition is balanced and organic, allowing ingredients to naturally mingle. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A clean white linen napkin is folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive background, creating an approachable yet refined visual.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for soaking up juices.
Offer a simple green salad on the side.
instructions: Dice chicken into 3-4 cm chunks.
Chop onion.
Mince garlic.
Slice mushrooms.
Dice bell peppers into 2 cm pieces.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or braiser over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook to 75°C internal temperature. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add onion, bell peppers, and mushrooms to skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add garlic, smoked paprika, and saffron threads. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to skillet. Stir well to coat rice grains. Cook for 2 minutes, toasting lightly.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken chunks to skillet. Stir gently to combine.
Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet tightly.
Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Do not stir excessively during cooking.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Adjust salt and pepper to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Braised Pork and Potato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A robust individual portion of Spicy Braised Pork and Potato Stew is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features tender, dark brown braised pork chunks, visibly soft and creamy potato cubes, vibrant red and green bell pepper squares, and earthy brown sliced mushrooms, all coated in a rich, reddish-brown, savory sauce. The pork pieces are whole and substantial, not sliced. The stew maintains a slight fluidity, with the sauce clinging to the ingredients without being overly dry or watery. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast on top. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded plain white cotton napkin is placed to the left, and standard silver flatware (fork and spoon) are arranged to the right. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction. The composition is balanced and professional, with appropriate negative space around the food, showcasing the entire plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the rich sauce
Pair with a simple side salad of mixed greens
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 3 cm cubes. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Dice onions. Peel and cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Core and cut bell peppers into 2 cm squares. Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add pork cubes. Sear pork on all sides until deeply browned. Work in batches if needed to avoid overcrowding. Remove seared pork from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onions to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Return seared pork to the pot. Add potatoes, bell peppers, and sliced mushrooms.
Pour in chicken or beef broth and hot sauce. Stir well to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and simmer for 60-90 minutes, or until pork is fork-tender and potatoes are cooked through. Stir occasionally.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Chop fresh parsley for garnish.
notes: For a deeper flavor, use bone-in pork shoulder and remove bones after cooking.
Adjust hot sauce quantity to preferred spice level.
Ensure pork is fork-tender for best texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Tomato Ragu with Herb Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Tomato Ragu with Herb Pasta is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate, off-white with a subtle earthy texture. The plate rests on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood table surface. The dish features a generous portion of golden-brown shredded chicken ragu, its rich, deep red-orange hue from the fermented tomatoes contrasting with the earthy beige of the al dente tagliatelle. The pasta is subtly coated, not drowned, in the savory ragu, allowing its natural form to remain visible. The chicken pieces are tender, in irregular, natural chunks, not uniformly cut. Specks of vibrant green from fresh basil and parsley are interspersed throughout, providing a fresh counterpoint. A few whole, small fermented cherry tomatoes, if used, are visible, adding textural interest. The plating is minimalistic, with ample white space around the food. Natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting the varying textures of the pasta, the succulent chicken, and the rustic sauce. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded neatly beside the plate. In the background, out of focus, are subtle hints of green from a potted plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.

ingredients.name: Vegetable Scraps
ingredients.quantity: 200g (e.g., onion skins, carrot peels, celery ends)

instructions: Prepare Zero-Waste Stock: Combine beef bones/scraps, vegetable scraps, 2 litres of water, and a pinch of salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 2-3 hours. Strain stock. Discard solids. Set aside 1 litre of stock. Reserve remaining stock for future use.

Sear Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy (approx. 6-8 minutes). Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.

Sauté Mirepoix: Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same pot. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Sauté over medium heat until softened (approx. 8-10 minutes). Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Build Ragu: Add fermented tomatoes and bay leaf to the pot. Stir well. Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Pour in 500ml of the prepared stock. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Slow Cook Ragu: Reduce heat to low. Cover pot. Simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Shred Chicken: Remove chicken from pot. Shred meat from bones using two forks. Discard bones and skin. Return shredded chicken to the ragu. Stir well. Taste and adjust seasoning.
