recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato-Potato Confit and Quick Pickled Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, golden-brown with crispy skin, anchors the plate. Adjacent, tender pale yellow potato wedges and halved roasted cherry tomatoes, infused with olive oil and thyme, are arranged organically. A vibrant mound of thinly sliced quick pickled red onion and carrot adds a contrasting fresh element. A single, delicate golden-brown cheese crisp provides textural accent. The composition emphasizes negative space, allowing each ingredient to stand out. Served on a handcrafted cream-colored ceramic plate, set on a light natural wood surface. An undyed linen napkin rests subtly. Soft, natural light creates gentle shadows, highlighting the clean textures. A minimalist background with a blurred plant reinforces the sustainable aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare quick pickled vegetables: Thinly slice red onion and carrot into rounds. In a small saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, and 5g salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Pour hot brine over sliced onion and carrot. Let cool to room temperature. Set aside to pickle.

Prepare tomato-potato confit: Halve small waxy potatoes or cut into 2cm wedges. Halve cherry tomatoes. Peel and smash garlic cloves. In a medium oven-safe pot or pan, combine potatoes, tomatoes, smashed garlic, thyme sprigs, and olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Cover tightly. Bake at 160°C for 45-60 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and slightly caramelized. Stir occasionally.

Prepare chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to oven with confit. Cook for another 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.

Make cheese crisps: Grate aged hard cheese. On a parchment-lined baking sheet, place small mounds (approx. 2cm diameter) of grated cheese. Bake at 180°C for 5-7 minutes, or until golden and crispy. Let cool on the sheet.

Assemble dish: On a clean ceramic plate, place one pan-seared chicken thigh. Spoon a portion of the tomato-potato confit next to the chicken. Drain and arrange a small mound of quick pickled vegetables beside the confit. Place one or two cheese crisps on the plate. Serve immediately.
notes: To minimize waste, chicken bones and vegetable trimmings can be used to make a flavorful stock.
The quick pickled vegetables can be prepared a day in advance and stored in the refrigerator.
Adjust baking time for confit based on potato size and desired tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Apple Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of classic apple crumble served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with subtle rim imperfections. The topping is a rugged, golden-brown crust featuring coarse flour crumbs and toasted rolled oats. Soft, 2cm chunks of stewed Granny Smith apples are visible beneath the topping, with thick, caramelized amber juices bubbling slightly at the dish's edges. A single, generous pour of thick, pale yellow vanilla custard pools naturally on one side, partially melting into the warm crumble. The bowl sits on a dark, weathered oak table beside a folded linen napkin and a tarnished silver spoon. Soft, warm kitchen light emphasizes the crunchy textures and steam rising from the fruit.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with hot vanilla custard
Accompany with a dollop of clotted cream
Pair with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel, core, and cut apples into 2cm chunks.
Toss apples with 50g sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Transfer apple mixture to a 20cm baking dish.
Cut cold butter into small cubes.
Rub butter into flour using fingertips until mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Stir in remaining 100g sugar and rolled oats.
Spread crumble topping evenly over the apples.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden brown and fruit is bubbling.
Remove from oven and rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use cold butter to ensure a crisp, crumbly texture.
Do not overwork the dough or it will become tough.
Granny Smith apples provide the best tart balance to the sweet topping.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken and Ricotta Stuffed Shells
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Baked Chicken and Ricotta Stuffed Shells is presented in a clean, white, oval ceramic baking dish. Three plump, al dente conchiglioni shells, generously filled with creamy chicken and ricotta, are nestled in a vibrant red marinara sauce. Each shell is topped with a golden-brown crust of melted mozzarella and Parmesan, interspersed with crisp, toasted panko breadcrumbs, offering delightful textural contrast. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered over the top for color and freshness. The sauce pools invitingly around the shells. The dish rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware lie beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s textures and colors, creating an inviting, casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of warm garlic bread
Pair with a simple green salad with vinaigrette
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add conchiglioni shells. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain shells. Rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.
Heat 10 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground chicken to the pan. Break up chicken with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Drain any excess fat.
In a large bowl, combine cooked chicken mixture, ricotta cheese, 50 g grated Parmesan cheese, chopped fresh basil, and egg. Season with salt and black pepper. Mix well.
Preheat oven to 190°C. Spread half of the marinara sauce evenly over the bottom of a large oven-safe baking dish (approx. 30cm x 20cm).
Carefully fill each cooked pasta shell with the chicken and ricotta mixture. Arrange stuffed shells in a single layer in the baking dish over the marinara sauce.
Pour remaining marinara sauce over the stuffed shells. Sprinkle evenly with shredded mozzarella cheese and remaining 50 g grated Parmesan cheese.
In a small bowl, toss panko breadcrumbs with 5 ml olive oil. Sprinkle breadcrumbs over the cheese layer.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and breadcrumbs are golden brown.
Let rest for a few minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure ground chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For best results, use fresh, good quality ricotta cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken, Tomato, and Mushroom Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of golden Hearty Chicken, Tomato, and Mushroom Rice Soup rests in a clean white porcelain bowl. The broth is a warm golden hue, clear but rich. Large, irregular chunks of seared chicken are visible. Plump, short-grain rice grains are suspended throughout. Vibrant red diced tomatoes and earthy, thinly sliced cremini mushrooms add color and texture. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley garnishes the top, providing a pop of green. The bowl is centered on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and polished silver soup spoon are placed neatly beside it. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the dish, creating a warm and inviting scene.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Finely dice onion. Thinly slice mushrooms. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in thinly sliced mushrooms. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add short-grain rice and diced tomatoes to the pot. Stir well.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to medium-low.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes. Cook until chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature. Rice should be tender.
Season soup with salt and pepper to taste.
Finely chop fresh parsley.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Vin Blanc
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with crisp, golden-brown skin. They sit in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl filled with a glossy, ivory-colored cream sauce. Thick-cut bacon lardons and browned, halved button mushrooms are distributed naturally around the chicken. Whole, softened shallots are visible in the sauce. Finely chopped flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled over the top for color. The plating is clean with moderate negative space. The setting includes a rustic wooden table, a linen napkin, and a side of crusty baguette slices. Lighting is natural and bright, emphasizing the textures of the seared skin and the velvety sauce consistency. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh, crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with buttery mashed potatoes or buttered egg noodles
Pair with a chilled glass of the same dry white wine used in cooking
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add bacon lardons to the same pan. Fry until crisp.
Add halved mushrooms. Sauté until browned.
Stir in shallots and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the pan bottom to release browned bits.
Add chicken stock and thyme sprigs.
Place chicken back into the pan.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Transfer chicken to a warm plate.
Whisk heavy cream and butter into the pan juices.
Simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to the sauce. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Use a high-quality dry white wine for the best sauce flavor
Do not boil the sauce vigorously after adding cream to avoid curdling
Keep the skin above the liquid level during braising to maintain crispness

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Onion and Apple Salad with Grilled Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. A vibrant bed of mixed greens forms the base. Golden-brown caramelized onion strips are scattered across the greens. Thinly sliced apple pieces provide crispness and sweetness. Small, irregular chunks of grilled chicken, seared to a light golden hue, are interspersed among the vegetables. A glossy basil-rosemary vinaigrette lightly coats the ingredients. Fresh basil leaves are scattered as garnish, enhancing the green palette. The presentation is balanced and approachable, with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting highlights the fresh ingredients. A cotton napkin is folded beside the plate, with standard silverware.
instructions: Season chicken breast with salt, pepper, and a pinch of finely chopped rosemary. Grill or pan-sear chicken until cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C. Let rest. Cut into 2 cm chunks.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced red onions. Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes until softened and golden. Add 30 ml balsamic vinegar and 5 ml honey. Cook for another 5-7 minutes until deeply caramelized.
In a small bowl, whisk together 45 ml olive oil, 30 ml balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, chopped basil, and remaining chopped rosemary. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine mixed greens, thinly sliced apples, and caramelized onions.
Drizzle salad with dressing. Toss gently to combine. Divide salad among four plates. Arrange grilled chicken chunks on top of each salad. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Vin Blanc

They sit in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl filled with a glossy, ivory-colored cream sauce. Thick-cut bacon lardons and browned, halved button mushrooms are distributed naturally around the chicken. Whole, softened shallots are visible in the sauce. Finely chopped flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled over the top for color. The plating is clean with moderate negative space. The setting includes a rustic wooden table, a linen napkin, and a side of crusty baguette slices. Lighting is natural and bright, emphasizing the textures of the seared skin and the velvety sauce consistency. The entire plate is visible.

Accompany with buttery mashed potatoes or buttered egg noodles
Pair with a chilled glass of the same dry white wine used in cooking

Add bacon lardons to the same pan. Fry until crisp.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Spanish chicken and rice served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice is moist and fluid, colored a vibrant golden-orange from the smoked paprika and broth. Thick 4cm chunks of seared chicken thighs are nestled into the rice, showing a crisp, dark golden-brown exterior. Small dices of softened red bell pepper and translucent onions are evenly distributed throughout the grains. The dish is finished with a scatter of bright green chopped parsley. A single yellow lemon wedge sits on the side of the plate. The background features a rustic wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and natural side-lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional terracotta cazuela
Accompany with crusty bread and aioli
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine like Albariño

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, and half the paprika.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 5 minutes until golden. Remove from pan.
Add onion and red pepper to the same pan. Sauté until softened.
Stir in garlic and remaining paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 18 minutes. Do not stir.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Use short-grain rice to ensure the correct starchy consistency.
Avoid stirring the rice once the broth is added to allow a slight crust to form.
Ensure the broth is hot before adding it to the pan to maintain cooking temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Brazilian Beef and Bean Stew with Crispy Potatoes and Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant, hearty composition. A portion of fluffy, light brown rice is neatly mounded on one side. Adjacent, a rich, dark brown beef and bean stew is spooned, featuring tender, generously sized chunks of braised beef, whole black beans, and colorful pieces of softened red and green bell peppers and diced tomatoes. The stew has a glossy, thick consistency. On the other side, golden-brown, crispy roasted potato cubes are artfully arranged, providing a textural contrast. Fresh, vibrant green chopped cilantro is sprinkled over the stew as a garnish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall plating is balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin beside the plate, and natural, even lighting. Traditional Brazilian flatware accompanies the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of farofa (toasted cassava flour) on the side for sprinkling over the stew.
Offer a lime wedge to squeeze over the dish for brightness.

ingredients.name: Red Chili (e.g., Bird's Eye or Fresno)

instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Season beef cubes with salt and pepper. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add chopped onion and diced bell peppers. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, sliced chili, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and beef broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add bay leaves. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5-2 hours, or until beef is very tender.

While beef simmers, cook brown rice according to package instructions. Combine 200 g brown rice with 400 ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 35-40 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Toss cubed potatoes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until golden brown and crispy.
After beef is tender, stir in drained and rinsed black beans into the stew. Simmer for another 10 minutes to heat through. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

To serve, spoon a portion of brown rice onto each plate. Ladle the beef and bean stew alongside the rice. Arrange roasted crispy potatoes next to the stew. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of wide, golden pappardelle ribbons is nested in a clean white porcelain pasta bowl. The pasta is coated in a thick, vibrant red San Marzano tomato sauce. A whole, bone-in braised chicken thigh rests centrally on the pasta, showing a rich, caramelized exterior. Small, tender cubes of carrot and celery, along with dark, wrinkled Kalamata olives, are distributed throughout the sauce. Freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a vivid green garnish. The dish is set on a dark wood table with a folded linen napkin and a silver fork. Soft, natural light emphasizes the glossy texture of the sauce and the rustic appeal of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a medium-bodied Chianti wine
Offer freshly grated Pecorino Romano at the table
instructions: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden.
Flip chicken and brown the other side.
Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the pan.
Sauté vegetables for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in wine. Deglaze the pan bottom.
Add tomatoes and olives. Stir well.
Return chicken to the pan. Cover.
Simmer 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Boil salted water. Cook pappardelle until al dente.
Drain pasta. Toss with sauce.
Place pasta in bowls. Top with one whole chicken thigh.
notes: Ensure the sauce is thick enough to coat the wide pasta ribbons
Use high-quality San Marzano tomatoes for authentic flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Chicken with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Braised Chicken is centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two succulent, bone-in chicken thighs, deeply browned from searing and braising, rest amidst a rich, amber-hued sauce. The sauce is thick with tender, caramelized onion slices, showcasing a beautiful depth of color from the spices. Flecks of vibrant green chopped cilantro are generously sprinkled over the chicken and sauce, contrasting beautifully. Golden, toasted slivered almonds add crunch. The plate maintains moderate negative space, presenting a refined yet approachable look. Beside the plate, a small white bowl holds fluffy couscous. A simple, light wooden table provides the backdrop, with natural, even lighting. A folded white cotton napkin rests near the plate. Standard flatware is positioned for a casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with couscous or fluffy basmati rice.
Offer a side of plain yogurt or a fresh cucumber-tomato salad.
Garnish with additional fresh cilantro or parsley.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook onions, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and soft, about 20-25 minutes.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and smoked paprika to the onions. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Stir in chopped tomatoes, chicken broth, honey, and cinnamon stick. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Nestle chicken into the sauce.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove cinnamon stick. Stir in fresh lemon juice.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: Ensure onions are truly caramelized for deep flavor. This step is crucial.
Adjust spice levels to personal preference.
The chicken can be made ahead and reheated; flavors often improve overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Pickled Bell Pepper and Roasted Potato Salad
recipes.visual_description: Roasted potato cubes, seared corn kernels, and colorful pickled bell pepper strips are gently mixed. Shredded chicken and crumbled feta are scattered over the top. Sourdough croutons are interspersed for texture. Earthy tones from potatoes and bread, vibrant reds, yellows, and greens from bell peppers and corn. White from feta and chicken. Crispy croutons, tender roasted potatoes, slightly firm pickled vegetables, soft chicken, crumbly cheese. Garnished with fresh parsley or dill sprigs. Served on handcrafted ceramic plates in earth tones on a light bamboo table. An undyed linen napkin rests beside the plate. The background is clean and minimalist, with soft natural lighting illuminating the dish and a subtle plant visible.

ingredients.name: red onion
ingredients.quantity: 1 small, half thinly sliced, half finely diced

ingredients.name: apple cider vinegar
ingredients.quantity: 150 ml (120 ml for pickling, 30 ml for dressing)

instructions: To pickle bell peppers: In a heatproof jar, combine sliced bell peppers and half of the thinly sliced red onion. In a small saucepan, combine 120 ml apple cider vinegar, 120 ml water, granulated sugar, 1 teaspoon salt, and sliced garlic. Bring to a boil. Pour hot brine over vegetables. Let cool completely. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
To roast potatoes: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss diced potatoes with 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.

To prepare corn: If using fresh corn, sear kernels in a hot pan with a drizzle of olive oil for 3-5 minutes until lightly browned. If using frozen, cook according to package directions and drain well.
To make sourdough croutons: Reduce oven to 180°C. Toss bread cubes with 2 tablespoons olive oil. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden and crispy.
Ensure chicken is cooked and shredded into small pieces.
To prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together 60 ml olive oil, 30 ml apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, and 1 tablespoon of the cooled pickling brine. Season with salt and pepper.

To assemble salad: In a large bowl, combine roasted potatoes, seared corn, drained pickled bell peppers, drained pickled red onion, and the finely diced raw red onion. Add shredded chicken and crumbled feta cheese. Add croutons just before serving.
To dress and serve: Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Gently toss to combine. Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley or dill.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Cheesy Chicken Enchiladas
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two golden-brown, baked chicken enchiladas, nestled in a rustic ceramic baking dish. The tortillas are generously filled with shredded chicken and a rich, spicy red sauce, then covered with a bubbly, melted layer of Monterey Jack and cheddar cheese. The cheese shows areas of slight caramelization, indicating its perfect bake. A vibrant green sprinkle of freshly chopped cilantro rests atop the cheese. Alongside the enchiladas, a dollop of cool sour cream provides a creamy contrast. Thin slices of ripe avocado are casually arranged near the enchiladas. The baking dish is placed on a well-worn wooden dining table, suggesting a comfortable home setting. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone and a fork are positioned nearby. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and rich colors of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of sour cream or crema.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.
Serve with sliced avocado or guacamole on the side.
Accompany with Mexican rice and refried beans.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.

Place chicken breasts in a pot. Cover with water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Shred chicken using two forks. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add chopped onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.

Stir in diced tomatoes, chipotle peppers with adobo sauce, chopped jalapeño, chicken broth, chili powder, cumin, and oregano. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until smooth. Pour about 125 ml of sauce into the bottom of a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Dip each corn tortilla briefly into the sauce. Place some shredded chicken down the center of each tortilla. Roll tightly. Place seam-side down in the prepared baking dish.
Pour the remaining sauce evenly over the rolled enchiladas. Sprinkle generously with shredded Monterey Jack and cheddar cheeses.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the sauce is bubbly and the cheese is melted and lightly golden brown. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: For extra spice, leave some seeds in the jalapeño or add an extra chipotle pepper.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Roulade with White Bean Puree and Apple-Onion Stuffing
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken Roulade is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table surface. Two golden-brown chicken roulades, either served whole or sliced into thick, substantial medallions, are centrally arranged on a generous swirl of creamy, off-white cannellini bean puree. The chicken exhibits a rich, seared crust, revealing glimpses of the savory apple and onion stuffing. Fresh green thyme leaves are delicately scattered over the chicken and puree for a vibrant contrast. The plate features moderate negative space, enhancing a professional, approachable composition. A cotton napkin and standard silver flatware rest beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, with a softly blurred casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Finely dice half the onion and the apple. Pulse bread into coarse crumbs.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté diced onion and apple for 5 minutes until softened.
Add breadcrumbs and leaves from 1 sprig of thyme. Cook for 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Place each chicken breast between two sheets of cling film. Pound evenly to 6mm thickness.
Spoon a quarter of the stuffing onto one end of each chicken breast. Roll tightly, tucking in sides. Secure with toothpicks.
Season roulades with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and butter in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear roulades for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove toothpicks.
While chicken bakes, finely chop remaining half onion and garlic. Heat 10ml olive oil in a saucepan.
Sauté chopped onion and garlic for 3 minutes. Add drained cannellini beans and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Cook for 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Blend mixture until smooth using an immersion blender or food processor. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon white bean puree onto plates. Slice each chicken roulade into thick medallions or serve whole. Arrange chicken on puree. Garnish with fresh thyme leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Sausage and Mushroom Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Creamy Tuscan Sausage and Mushroom Rigatoni is presented in a clean, shallow white porcelain pasta bowl. The al dente rigatoni are coated in a rich, velvety, off-white sauce. Visible throughout are browned, irregular chunks of savory Italian sausage and beautifully seared slices of cremini mushrooms. Vibrant green wilted baby spinach leaves provide a fresh color contrast. The dish is garnished with bright green, freshly chopped parsley and a delicate dusting of grated Parmesan cheese. The plating is clean, professional, with moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish. A subtly blurred background suggests a casual bistro setting, highlighting the food as the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Boil water for pasta. Add salt. Cook rigatoni al dente per package. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Heat olive oil in large skillet, medium-high heat. Add Italian sausage, break apart. Cook until browned, about 8-10 minutes. Remove sausage; set aside.
Add diced onion to skillet. Cook until softened, 5 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until browned, 7-9 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth. Simmer. Scrape browned bits.
Stir in heavy cream and cooked sausage. Gently simmer.
Add cooked rigatoni and baby spinach. Toss to combine. Cook until spinach wilts.
Stir in grated Parmesan and reserved pasta water. Mix until sauce thickens.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley and extra Parmesan.
notes: Adjust sauce consistency with more pasta water or broth if needed.
For a spicier dish, use hot Italian sausage.

recipes.recipe_name: Brined Chicken with Smashed Potatoes and Lacto-Fermented Cabbage
recipes.visual_description: A single brined chicken breast, golden-seared, rests on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. Beside it, several crispy smashed potatoes display their irregular, rustic edges and golden-brown crust, with soft white interiors visible. A vibrant pile of lacto-fermented cabbage slaw, showcasing shredded green cabbage, julienned orange carrots, and hints of red radish, provides a fresh, tangy contrast. A generous drizzle of bright green carrot top pesto artfully adorns the chicken and potatoes, adding a pop of color and natural texture. The plate features ample negative space, allowing each component to stand out with its natural beauty and texture. The dish is presented on a light, textured reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is loosely folded beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The background is clean and minimalist, with subtle hints of green foliage from a nearby plant, enhancing the eco-conscious theme. Show a single individual portion.

ingredients.name: Olive oil (for cooking chicken and potatoes)
Small potatoes (e.g., new potatoes, Yukon Golds)

instructions: Lacto-Fermented Cabbage (Prepare 3-5 days in advance):
Shred cabbage finely. Julienne carrots and radishes.
Combine cabbage, carrots, radishes, salt, garlic, ginger, spring onion, and gochugaru in a large bowl.
Massage mixture vigorously for 5-10 minutes until liquid releases.
Pack tightly into a clean glass jar. Press down to remove air bubbles. Ensure vegetables are submerged under their own brine. Use a fermentation weight if needed.
Seal jar loosely (or use an airlock). Ferment at room temperature (18-22°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess. Burp daily if not using airlock.
Once fermented, store in refrigerator.
Brine Chicken (At least 1 hour, up to 4 hours):
Combine 1 litre water, 30g salt, 15g sugar, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a container. Stir to dissolve.
Add chicken breasts. Ensure fully submerged.
Refrigerate for 1-4 hours. Do not over-brine.
Prepare Smashed Potatoes:
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes. Boil whole potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes. Arrange on a baking sheet.
Using a fork or potato masher, gently smash each potato until flattened but still holding together.
Drizzle with 45ml olive oil. Season with 5g salt and 2g black pepper.
Roast for 25-35 minutes, or until deeply golden and crispy. Flip halfway.
Make Carrot Top Pesto:
Wash carrot tops thoroughly. Remove thick stems.
In a food processor, combine carrot tops, toasted pumpkin seeds, 1 small garlic clove, 30ml olive oil, lemon juice, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper.
Process until a coarse pesto forms. Add more olive oil if too thick.
Cook Chicken:
Remove chicken from brine. Pat very dry with paper towels. Discard brine.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to preheated 200°C oven. Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.
Plate:
Place crispy smashed potatoes on one side of the plate.
Position a whole chicken breast next to potatoes.
Spoon a generous portion of lacto-fermented cabbage slaw on the plate.
Drizzle chicken and potatoes with carrot top pesto.
notes: This recipe embraces zero-waste principles by utilizing carrot tops for pesto and emphasizing fermentation for enhanced flavor and gut health. The lacto-fermented cabbage requires advance preparation for optimal flavor development.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Onion, Apple, and Walnut Salad with Balsamic Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a balanced composition. A bed of vibrant mixed greens forms the base. Warm, deeply caramelized thin onion slices are artfully scattered across the greens, their rich brown hues contrasting with the fresh elements. Thinly sliced firm apple pieces, either red or green, are arranged with a slight overlap, adding a crisp texture and bright color. Toasted walnut halves are sprinkled generously over the entire dish, providing a rustic touch and crunch. A glossy balsamic vinaigrette is drizzled over the salad, coating the ingredients and adding a subtle sheen. The arrangement is organic and natural, allowing all components to be clearly visible. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, with a clean white cotton napkin placed beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the fresh ingredients, creating an inviting and professional restaurant-style presentation.
instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and soft. Set aside to cool.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Spread walnuts on a baking sheet. Toast for 7-10 minutes until fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Let cool.
In a small bowl, whisk together balsamic vinegar, remaining 15 ml olive oil, Dijon mustard, and maple syrup. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
In a large salad bowl, combine mixed greens, cooled caramelized onions, and thinly sliced apples.
Add toasted walnuts. Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine all components evenly.
Serve immediately on individual plates.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato Basil Risotto and Roasted Bell Pepper
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, creamy tomato basil risotto forms a natural, free-flowing base on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is a rich orange-red, studded with bright green flecks of fresh basil. Resting atop is a whole, golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh, showcasing a savory, crisp crust. Beside the chicken, artfully arranged strips of tender, slightly charred roasted red and yellow bell peppers add contrasting color and texture. Fresh, whole basil leaves are scattered generously over the dish as a final garnish, enhancing the aromatic appeal. The scene is set on a simple light wooden table surface in a modern bistro style, with standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the single individual portion, highlighting the dish's fresh ingredients and appealing colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of light red Italian wine or sparkling water.
Offer crusty Italian bread for soaking up any leftover risotto.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut bell peppers into thick strips. Dice onion finely. Mince garlic.
Toss bell pepper strips with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly charred.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan and keep warm.
In the same pan, add 15g butter. Sauté diced onion for 3-4 minutes until translucent. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir for 1-2 minutes until the edges of the rice grains are translucent.
Pour in white wine (if using). Stir until the wine is fully absorbed.
Stir in the diced tomatoes.

Gradually add warm chicken broth, one ladle at a time. Stir frequently. Wait until most liquid is absorbed before adding the next ladle. Continue for 18-20 minutes until the rice is al dente and creamy.
Stir in the remaining 15g butter, half of the fresh basil (torn or chopped), and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper to taste. The risotto should have a fluid consistency.
Spoon a generous portion of tomato basil risotto onto each plate. Place a seared chicken thigh on top of the risotto.
Arrange roasted bell pepper strips beside the chicken. Garnish with the remaining fresh basil leaves.
notes: For best flavor, use good quality chicken broth.
Adjust risotto consistency by adding more broth if needed to maintain a fluid texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A rustic and inviting skillet dish featuring golden-brown chicken pieces nestled among tender, browned mushrooms in a rich, creamy, off-white sauce. The dish is generously speckled with vibrant green fresh parsley, creating a warm and comforting appearance. It's presented in a cast-iron skillet, ready to be served.

instructions.instruction: Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Cut into 1-inch pieces. Season the chicken with 1/2 teaspoon of salt and 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the seasoned chicken and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through. Remove the chicken from the skillet and set aside.

Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the same skillet. Add the diced onion and cook for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they release their liquid and start to brown. Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Sprinkle the flour over the onion and mushroom mixture, stir well and cook for 1 minute. Slowly pour in the chicken broth, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Bring the mixture to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.

Reduce heat to low. Stir in the sour cream until fully incorporated. Return the cooked chicken to the skillet. Stir to coat the chicken and mushrooms in the creamy sauce. Heat gently for 2-3 minutes until everything is warmed through. Do not boil after adding sour cream to prevent curdling.
Taste and adjust seasoning with the remaining salt and pepper if needed. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately, perhaps over rice or noodles.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef & Tomato Braise
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Spicy Beef & Tomato Braise is presented in a deep, rustic white ceramic bowl, showcasing the rich, slow-cooked Mexican flavors. Several large, tender beef chuck cubes, seared to a deep brown, are nestled in a thick, glossy, reddish-brown sauce. The sauce, made from rehydrated Ancho and Guajillo chiles and crushed tomatoes, coats the beef beautifully. A vibrant sprinkle of freshly chopped green cilantro covers the top, providing a fresh contrast. A bright lime wedge is placed on the bowl's rim. The dish sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a neatly folded white cotton napkin. Soft, natural lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors. The background is a subtly blurred, warm restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping up the braise.
Offer alongside a bowl of Mexican rice.
Provide extra lime wedges for squeezing over the dish.
instructions: Season beef chuck cubes with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Rehydrate dried Ancho and Guajillo chiles in hot water for 20 minutes. Stem and seed them. Blend rehydrated chiles with 100 ml of beef broth until smooth.
Add crushed tomatoes, chile blend, remaining beef broth, cumin, oregano, and smoked paprika to the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Stir in Mexican hot sauce. Ensure beef is mostly submerged.
Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
notes: Adjust the amount of Mexican hot sauce to control the spice level according to preference.
For deeper flavor, brown the beef well in step 2.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Piccata with Lemon Caper Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Piccata is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, occupies the center. The chicken has a tender, moist appearance. It is generously coated with a glistening, pale yellow lemon-caper sauce. Small, vibrant green capers are visibly distributed within the sauce. Bright green, freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled over the chicken and sauce. A thin, bright yellow lemon slice rests beside the chicken. The plate is placed on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro setting. Traditional flatware is arranged beside the plate. The composition is clean, organized, and professional, with appropriate negative space around the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served traditionally with linguine pasta, roasted asparagus, or crusty artisanal bread.
instructions: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of parchment paper. Pound to 1 cm thickness using a meat mallet.
Season chicken generously with salt and black pepper.
Dredge each chicken piece lightly in flour. Shake off excess flour.
Heat olive oil and 30g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Place on a plate and keep warm.
Add remaining 30g butter to the skillet. Melt.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce wine by half.
Add chicken stock and drained capers to the skillet. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Return chicken to the skillet. Spoon sauce over each piece. Cook for 1 minute to heat through.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a lemon slice before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken is pounded to an even thickness for uniform cooking.
For a thicker sauce, reduce the chicken stock slightly more.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Bourguignon
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a single portion in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl. Four large, 5cm chunks of beef are centered, coated in a glossy, deep mahogany wine reduction. The meat remains whole and tender, never sliced. Tucked around the beef are whole glazed pearl onions, vibrant orange carrot rounds, and golden-brown sautéed mushroom halves. Small crispy bacon lardons are scattered across the surface. A garnish of finely chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a fresh green contrast. The bowl sits on a dark rustic wooden table. Beside it is a small plate with two thick pieces of crusty baguette and a folded white cotton napkin. The lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the rich textures of the braised meat.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette to soak up the wine sauce
Pair with a glass of the same red wine used in the cooking
Traditional accompaniments include buttery mashed potatoes or boiled small potatoes

ingredients.name: Dry red wine (Pinot Noir or Burgundy)

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper.
Fry bacon lardons in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat until crisp. Remove lardons and set aside.
Increase heat to high. Sear beef chunks in the bacon fat until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add carrots and pearl onions to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until lightly browned.
Stir in tomato paste and garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables. Stir for 2 minutes to cook out the raw flour taste.
Return beef and bacon to the pot. Pour in wine and beef stock until meat is mostly submerged.
Add the bouquet garni. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook on low heat for 2.5 hours.
Sauté mushrooms in butter in a separate pan until golden. Stir into the stew 15 minutes before serving.
Remove the bouquet garni. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
notes: Choose a wine with good acidity to balance the richness of the beef
Ensure the beef is patted completely dry before searing to achieve a proper crust
The stew often tastes better the next day after the flavors have fully melded

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Dark Beer Stew
recipes.visual_description: The Hearty Beef and Dark Beer Stew is presented in a deep, pristine white ceramic bowl, placed centrally on a natural light wood table. The stew features generously cut 3-4 cm chunks of dark, seared beef, braised until exceptionally tender, nestled among vibrant 1.5-2 cm diced red and green bell peppers, soft translucent onion pieces, and plump, dark kidney beans. Golden corn kernels add pops of color and texture. The rich, glossy sauce is a deep reddish-brown, clinging to the ingredients. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped cilantro garnishes the top, providing a fresh contrast. The composition is clean and rustic, with ample negative space around the bowl. A simple white linen napkin and a rustic metal spoon rest beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and rich colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm tortillas
Serve with cornbread
Offer a side of fresh lime wedges
Offer a variety of hot sauces for individual preference

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 3-4 cm chunks
Red bell pepper, diced into 1.5-2 cm pieces
Green bell pepper, diced into 1.5-2 cm pieces
Canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced bell peppers. Cook for 3-5 minutes until slightly tender.
Stir in chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, dark beer, and beef broth. Stir to combine.
Bring the stew to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5-2 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Stir in drained kidney beans and corn kernels. Cook for another 10-15 minutes, uncovered, allowing the stew to thicken slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle generous portions of the stew into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.
notes: For best results, allow the stew to simmer slowly for at least 2 hours to achieve maximum tenderness and flavor.
Adjust chili powder and jalapeño to your desired level of spice.

recipes.recipe_name: Ginger Soy Shrimp with Bamboo Shoots
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Ginger Soy Shrimp with Bamboo Shoots is elegantly plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Succulent, whole pink shrimp are glistening with a rich, glossy brown ginger-soy sauce, interspersed with crisp-tender, thinly sliced bamboo shoots. The dish is arranged naturally, nestled beside a perfectly formed mound of fluffy white rice. A vibrant sprinkle of thinly chopped green scallions provides a fresh contrast on top. The background is a modern bistro setting with a simple light wooden table surface. A separate small white porcelain rice bowl filled with white rice sits adjacent to the main plate. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests neatly on a minimalist ceramic chopstick rest beside the plate. A folded white cotton napkin is placed nearby. The scene is illuminated by natural, even light, creating a clean, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with steamed white rice.
Offer a side of chili oil for those who prefer more heat.
Enjoy family-style, sharing dishes with other Chinese preparations.
instructions: Pat shrimp dry. In a bowl, toss shrimp with 5g cornstarch, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper.
In a separate bowl, whisk together soy sauce, remaining 10g cornstarch, sesame oil, and water or chicken stock. Set aside.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat.
Add seasoned shrimp. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until pink but not fully cooked. Remove shrimp from wok and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to the wok. Add julienned ginger and minced garlic. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add drained, thinly sliced bamboo shoots to the wok. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return the partially cooked shrimp to the wok. Pour in the prepared sauce mixture.
Stir constantly until the sauce thickens and evenly coats the shrimp and bamboo shoots. Cook for 1-2 minutes more.
Remove from heat. Serve immediately.
Garnish with chopped scallions.
notes: Ensure shrimp are not overcooked; they become tough and rubbery.
Adjust soy sauce quantity to taste based on desired salinity.
Fresh bamboo shoots can be used if available, requiring blanching first.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cabbage & Whole Wheat Pasta Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, fresh pasta salad is artfully arranged on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a creamy beige tone. Whole wheat fusilli pasta forms the base, interspersed with vivid diced red bell pepper, bright julienned carrots, crisp diced cucumber, and the distinctive texture of fermented cabbage. Thinly sliced green onions provide vertical accents, while plump chickpeas add a soft, earthy element. A light miso dressing subtly coats all ingredients, creating a gentle sheen. A sparse sprinkle of fresh green parsley and a few sesame seeds garnish the top. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually folded nearby. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, with a clean, minimalistic background hinting at organic elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled in individual portions
Pair with a simple, refreshing beverage like infused water
Present on natural, unadorned dining surfaces
instructions: Cook whole wheat fusilli according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Rinse with cold water. Drain again thoroughly. Let cool completely.
While pasta cools, prepare vegetables. Julienne carrots. Dice cucumber into small cubes. Dice red bell pepper into small cubes. Slice green onions thinly.
Drain sauerkraut well. Gently squeeze out excess liquid.
Rinse canned chickpeas under cold water. Drain thoroughly.
Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together white miso paste, rice vinegar, toasted sesame oil, water, grated fresh ginger, and minced garlic until smooth.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cooled pasta, julienned carrots, diced cucumber, diced red bell pepper, sliced green onions, drained sauerkraut, and rinsed chickpeas.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to ensure all components are evenly coated.
Refrigerate salad for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld. Serve chilled.
Garnish individual portions with fresh chopped parsley and a sprinkle of sesame seeds before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Apple-Onion Compote and Fresh Basil
recipes.visual_description: A single, whole pan-seared chicken breast, with a crisp, golden-brown crust and a visibly moist interior, is the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Adjacent, a rustic yet refined mound of warm apple-onion compote is artfully spooned. This compote showcases tender, small diced apples and caramelized, finely diced onions, presenting a harmonious blend of amber and golden hues. Fresh, vibrantly green basil leaves, either torn or chiffonade, are scattered judiciously over both the chicken and compote, providing a contrasting color and aromatic lift. The arrangement is clean and professional, with appropriate negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by classic silver flatware and a neatly folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, set against a softly blurred, casual bistro background.

ingredients.name: Firm apples (e.g., Honeycrisp, Fuji), cored and diced

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer pan with chicken to the preheated oven. Cook 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Let rest 5 minutes on a cutting board.
While chicken cooks, add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add diced apple and minced garlic to the pan. Cook 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Deglaze the pan with apple cider vinegar, scraping up any browned bits. Add chicken stock.
Bring to a simmer. Cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until apples are tender and liquid reduces to a compote consistency.
Season the apple-onion compote with salt and pepper to taste.
Plate each chicken breast. Spoon apple-onion compote alongside. Garnish generously with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Ribs with Red Wine Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised beef short ribs rests centrally on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The substantial, dark brown beef chunk, un-sliced, glistens from a rich, dark red wine reduction sauce generously spooned over and around it. The meat is fork-tender, with visible, succulent fibers. A small, neat mound of creamy, pale yellow polenta or smooth, white mashed potatoes is positioned beside the short rib, offering a vibrant contrast. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley adds a pop of freshness. The plate sits on a simple, dark wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro. A crisp, folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy polenta or smooth mashed potatoes.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the rich sauce.
instructions: Season short ribs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat.
Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove ribs from pot.
Add diced carrots, celery, and onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer and cook until reduced by half.
Return short ribs to the pot. Add beef broth, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaves. Liquid should almost cover the ribs.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot and transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F).
Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until meat is fork-tender.
Carefully remove short ribs from the pot. Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan, discarding solids.
Skim any excess fat from the strained liquid. Reduce the liquid over medium-high heat until it thickens into a rich sauce consistency. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve short ribs with the reduced sauce, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Stir-fried Shrimp with Bamboo Shoots
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Stir-fried Shrimp with Bamboo Shoots is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed. Plump, pink shrimp, cooked whole with tails on, glisten with a translucent, light brown sauce. They are interspersed with creamy white, crescent-shaped slices of bamboo shoots. Thin, golden julienned ginger and vibrant green 3cm lengths of green onion are visible throughout, adding color and freshness. The sauce evenly coats all ingredients, creating a cohesive, appealing sheen. A few fresh green onion slivers garnish the dish. The plate sits on a simple, light wooden table surface. Chopsticks are neatly placed to the left. A small white rice bowl with fluffy steamed white rice is positioned slightly behind the main dish. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish within a subtle modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Offer a side of chili oil for those who prefer more heat.
Eat with chopsticks.
instructions: Marinate shrimp: Combine shrimp with 5g cornstarch, 5ml Shaoxing wine, and a pinch of white pepper. Mix well. Set aside 10 minutes.
Prepare sauce: Whisk 10g cornstarch with 60ml water or chicken broth, 30ml soy sauce, 10ml Shaoxing wine, and 5g sugar. Set aside.
Heat wok or large skillet over high heat. Add 15ml vegetable oil.
Add shrimp. Stir-fry 1-2 minutes until pink and nearly cooked through. Remove shrimp from wok.
Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to wok. Add julienned ginger and minced garlic. Stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add sliced bamboo shoots. Stir-fry 2 minutes.
Return shrimp to wok. Pour in prepared sauce.
Stir constantly until sauce thickens and coats shrimp and bamboo.
Add green onion pieces. Stir-fry 30 seconds.
Drizzle with sesame oil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Turkey Roulade with Mushroom Duxelles and Prosciutto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of sliced turkey roulade is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two to three thick medallions of the roulade, cut into 2 cm thick slices, reveal concentric layers of golden-brown seared turkey, dark green mushroom duxelles, and pink prosciutto. They are arranged slightly overlapping in the center. A rich, glossy pan sauce, amber-brown, is spooned over and around the turkey. A small sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the dish, adding a vibrant green contrast. The turkey is moist with a beautiful sear. The plate rests on a rustic wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting textures and colors. The background suggests a contemporary bistro.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with roasted root vegetables or a creamy potato gratin.
instructions: Finely chop mushrooms, shallots, and garlic.
Melt 30g butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add shallots and garlic. Sauté 3 minutes.
Add chopped mushrooms. Cook until all liquid evaporates, about 10-12 minutes.
Stir in chopped fresh thyme and parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside. This is the duxelles.
Butterfly turkey breast. Place between two sheets of cling film. Pound evenly to 1 cm thickness.
Season turkey breast lightly with salt and pepper.
Lay prosciutto slices over turkey, slightly overlapping. Spread mushroom duxelles evenly over prosciutto.
Roll turkey tightly from one long side. Secure with kitchen twine at 3-4 cm intervals.
Preheat oven to 190°C.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear roulade on all sides until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes total.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove roulade from pan. Tent with foil. Let rest 10 minutes.
For sauce: Drain excess fat from pan. Add white wine. Scrape up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Whisk in chicken stock. Bring to simmer.
In a small bowl, mix 15g flour with 2 tablespoons cold water to form a slurry. Whisk into simmering sauce.
Cook sauce 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened. Whisk in remaining 30g butter until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove twine from roulade. Slice into 2 cm thick medallions.
Serve turkey medallions with pan sauce spooned over.
notes: Ensure the turkey is pounded to an even thickness for uniform cooking.
Allow the roulade to rest before slicing to keep it juicy.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni al Sugo di Salsiccia e Pomodorini
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rigatoni al Sugo di Salsiccia e Pomodorini is served on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The rigatoni, cooked al dente, is generously coated in a rich, rustic tomato sugo. Irregular, browned chunks of pork sausage are visibly interspersed throughout the pasta. Vibrant red cherry tomatoes, some whole and blistered, others halved, add bursts of color and texture. Fresh green basil leaves, torn, and finely chopped parsley are scattered over the top, providing a fresh aromatic contrast. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The dish rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's vibrant colors and textures, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano Reggiano cheese.
Offer crusty Italian bread for 'scarpetta' (mopping up sauce).
Pair with a glass of robust red wine.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil for pasta.
Remove casings from pork sausage. Crumble sausage into irregular chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add crumbled pork sausage. Brown thoroughly, breaking up chunks.
Drain excess fat from skillet. Add finely diced red onion and thinly sliced garlic to skillet. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add halved cherry tomatoes to skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until tomatoes blister and soften.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze skillet, scraping up any browned bits.
Add crushed tomatoes. Bring sauce to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni in boiling water according to package directions until al dente.
Drain rigatoni, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Add drained rigatoni to the skillet with the sauce. Add torn basil and chopped parsley. Toss to coat pasta evenly. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed for consistency.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.
Serve with grated Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Ajillo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo al Ajillo served on a clean white porcelain plate in a modern Spanish bistro setting. The dish features two whole chicken pieces—a thigh and a drumstick—with crispy, deep golden-brown skin. The chicken is surrounded by twenty whole, soft, golden-confit garlic cloves. A rich, translucent emulsion of olive oil and sherry glaze coats the meat. Bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. The arrangement is organic and centered with moderate negative space. A side of thick-cut, toasted rustic baguette sits on the edge of the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the glistening textures of the oil and the sear on the chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread to soak up the garlic oil.
Accompany with a glass of chilled dry Fino sherry.
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for a rustic look.
instructions: Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add whole garlic cloves to the oil.
Fry garlic until golden brown on all sides.
Remove garlic with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Increase heat to medium-high.
Place chicken pieces in the pan, skin-side down.
Sear chicken until deep golden brown on all sides, about 10 minutes.
Drain half of the rendered fat from the pan.
Add bay leaf and return fried garlic to the pan.
Pour in the dry sherry.
Scrape the bottom of the pan to release browned bits.
Lower heat to medium-low and cover with a lid.
Simmer for 15 minutes or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove lid and increase heat for 2 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Stir in chopped parsley and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the garlic does not burn; it should be golden and sweet, not black and bitter.
Use high-quality extra virgin olive oil for the best flavor profile.
Always verify the thickest part of the chicken reaches 75°C for safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Steak and Garlic Herb Sandwich
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty pan-seared steak sandwich rests on a simple, well-worn ceramic plate, centered on a rustic wooden kitchen table. The crusty, golden-brown bread, split horizontally, reveals thick, succulent chunks of medium-rare beef steak. The beef, seared to a deep mahogany, shows a tender pink interior. A generous layer of creamy, pale yellow garlic herb mayonnaise is spread on both bread halves, with flecks of vibrant green parsley and chives visible. The sandwich components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating an inviting, unpretentious appearance. A simple cloth napkin and a metal fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. Warm, natural lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the comforting, homely appeal of the dish. The background is minimal, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of potato chips or a dill pickle spear.
instructions: Finely mince garlic. Chop parsley and chives.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, minced garlic, chopped parsley, and chopped chives. Mix well. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Pat beef steak dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large cast-iron skillet or heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place steak in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or longer for desired doneness. Adjust heat if pan smokes excessively.
Remove steak from pan. Let rest on a cutting board for at least 5 minutes. This allows juices to redistribute.
While steak rests, slice the bread loaf lengthwise. Lightly toast bread halves in the same skillet or a toaster until golden and slightly crispy.
Slice the rested steak into thick chunks, against the grain. Do not slice thinly or fan out.
Spread a generous amount of garlic herb mayonnaise on both toasted bread halves.
Arrange the thick beef chunks evenly on the bottom bread half.
Place the top bread half over the beef. Cut the sandwich into individual portions. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, use a quality cut of steak like sirloin or ribeye.
Adjust steak cooking time based on thickness and desired doneness. Use a meat thermometer for accuracy (57°C for medium-rare).

recipes.recipe_name: Romaine and Roasted Chicken Garden Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant garden salad is presented in a wide, shallow ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. Crisp, torn Romaine lettuce forms the base, interspersed with bright red cherry tomato halves, cool green cucumber cubes, and vibrant yellow bell pepper diced into small pieces. Thinly sliced red onion adds a pop of purple. Small, irregular chunks of roasted chicken, lightly golden-brown from the oven, are nestled among the fresh vegetables, showing their tender, cooked texture. The entire salad is lightly coated in a simple vinaigrette, adding a subtle sheen without pooling. A plain white cloth napkin is casually placed beside the bowl. The scene is lit with warm, natural kitchen light, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family meal. The presentation is unpretentious and homely, emphasizing fresh ingredients and comfort.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Rub with 15 ml olive oil, 5 g salt, 2 g pepper, and dried herbs.
Place chicken on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
In a large salad bowl, combine chopped romaine lettuce, halved cherry tomatoes, diced cucumber, diced bell pepper, and thinly sliced red onion.
Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together 60 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey (if using), 2 g salt, and 1 g pepper.
Add cubed chicken to the salad bowl.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sirloin Steak with Herb Butter and Crispy Frites
recipes.visual_description: A perfectly pan-seared sirloin steak, cooked to a medium-rare pink interior with a rich, dark brown crust, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The steak is presented as a whole, thick-cut piece, not sliced. Adjacent to the steak is a generous mound of golden, crispy frites, cut into slender batons, their surfaces glistening from a second fry. A small, melting dollop of vibrant green herb butter, flecked with finely chopped parsley, sits atop the steak. The plate maintains ample negative space, showcasing the professional, balanced arrangement. The scene is set on a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin placed to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the steak's texture and the frites' crispness. The background suggests a modern bistro, subtle and out of focus, maintaining focus on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
Serve with crusty baguette
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into 1cm x 1cm batons (frites).
Rinse potatoes thoroughly in cold water until water runs clear. Pat very dry with paper towels.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy pot or deep fryer to 140°C.
Fry potatoes in batches for 6-8 minutes until tender but not browned. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on a wire rack.
Increase oil temperature to 180°C.
Pat sirloin steaks very dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until smoking.
Carefully place steaks in pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 30ml olive oil, 50g butter, smashed garlic, and fresh thyme to pan.
Tilt pan. Spoon melted butter mixture over steaks for 1-2 minutes.
Remove steaks from pan. Transfer to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
While steak rests, carefully return par-fried potatoes to hot oil (180°C).
Fry for 2-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Remove. Drain well. Season immediately with salt.
In a small bowl, combine remaining 50g softened butter with chopped fresh parsley.
Place one seared sirloin steak on each plate. Add a generous portion of crispy frites beside it. Top steak with a dollop of herb butter. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Yogurt Cake with Candied Tomato and Sweet Onion
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of a golden-hued, moist Mediterranean yogurt cake rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The cake's crumb is tender, revealing subtle swirls of deeply caramelized red onion and translucent, ruby-red candied cherry tomatoes. The onion elements appear as delicate, darker streaks, offering a visual hint of their sweet, jammy texture, while the tomatoes are distinct, jewel-like bursts of color. A thin, delicate drizzle of white yogurt glaze lightly coats the top of the cake slice, adding a touch of sheen. The cake is presented as a clean cut wedge, highlighting its inviting texture. The plate is positioned on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even light illuminates the scene from the side, creating soft shadows and highlighting the cake's appealing texture and embedded elements. In the background, slightly out of focus, the remainder of the round cake sits on a low cake stand, hinting at its complete form. The overall presentation is professional, balanced, and inviting.
instructions: Melt butter in small pan over low heat.
Add thinly sliced red onion. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, 20-25 minutes. Onions should be very soft and deeply golden.
Stir in brown sugar and pinch of salt. Cook 5 more minutes until jammy. Set aside to cool.
Halve cherry tomatoes. In a small saucepan, combine halved tomatoes, 30g granulated sugar, and 15ml water.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook gently 10-12 minutes until tomatoes are tender and liquid is syrupy. Remove from heat. Set aside to cool.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20cm round cake tin.
In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, and 3g salt.
In a large bowl, whisk together 150g granulated sugar, eggs, oil, 200g yogurt, vanilla extract, and lemon zest until smooth.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour half of batter into prepared tin. Spoon dollops of cooled sweet onion mixture and candied tomatoes over batter. Gently swirl with a knife.
Pour remaining batter over. Repeat with more dollops of onion and tomato, swirling lightly.
Bake 30-35 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into center comes out clean.
Let cake cool in tin for 10 minutes. Invert onto wire rack. Cool completely.
For glaze, whisk powdered sugar, 30g yogurt, and 5ml lemon juice until smooth.
Drizzle glaze over cooled cake.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Sausage and Tomato Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A creamy, vibrant Italian Sausage and Tomato Risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto flows naturally across the plate, showcasing its rich, fluid consistency, not stiff or mounded. Arborio rice, cooked to al dente perfection, is infused with the savory depth of browned, crumbled Italian sausage and the bright acidity of crushed tomatoes. Small, even diced onion pieces and minced garlic are visible, contributing to the dish's texture and color. A generous scattering of freshly grated Parmesan cheese melts into the warm rice, adding a golden hue and umami. Fresh, whole basil leaves are artfully placed on top, providing a verdant contrast and aromatic finish. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, allowing the dish to be the clear focal point. The plate rests on a simple wooden surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and a classic fork, creating an inviting, casual dining atmosphere with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty artisan bread for soaking up the creamy risotto.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Remove sausage from casings. Crumble sausage into small pieces.
Dice the yellow onion into small, even pieces. Mince garlic cloves.
Warm chicken broth in a separate saucepan. Keep it hot at a simmer.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add crumbled sausage to the pan. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon and set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pan.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the rice until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed by the rice.
Add crushed tomatoes to the rice. Stir well to combine.
Begin adding hot broth, one ladleful (about 125 ml) at a time. Stir constantly, allowing each addition of broth to be almost completely absorbed before adding the next.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is al dente (tender with a slight bite in the center). The risotto should be creamy and fluid, not dry.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes until butter and cheese are fully incorporated, creating a creamy consistency (mantecatura).
Stir in the cooked sausage. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Let risotto rest for 2 minutes before serving.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Vegetable & Brown Rice Bowl
