recipes.visual_description: This dish is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with a natural, earthy glaze. A generous mound of fluffy, light brown rice forms the base, its individual grains distinct. On one side, a piece of pan-seared chicken thigh, its skin a deep golden-brown with visible savory crust, rests as a whole, succulent piece. Alongside the chicken, a vibrant medley of quick-pickled vegetables – crisp, thin batons of bright orange carrots, translucent white radish rounds, and refreshing green cucumber slices – are artfully arranged, adding pops of color and texture. A sprinkle of fresh, verdant coriander leaves and a scattering of toasted sesame seeds provide a final, delicate garnish. The composition is clean and minimalist, allowing the natural colors and textures of each ingredient to shine. The bowl sits on a light, reclaimed wood table surface, accompanied by a simple, undyed linen napkin and a small ceramic spoon, all bathed in soft, natural light, creating an inviting and wholesome aesthetic.
instructions: Cook brown rice. Combine 200g brown rice with 400ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 35-40 minutes until water absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Prepare quick-pickled vegetables. Wash carrots, radish, cucumber. Peel carrots. Slice all vegetables into thin batons or rounds. Pack tightly into a clean jar.
Make pickling brine. In a small saucepan, combine 250ml water, 125ml rice vinegar, 30g sugar, and 5g salt. Bring to a boil. Stir until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat.
Pour hot brine over vegetables in the jar. Ensure vegetables are fully submerged. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or longer for more flavor.
Prepare chicken. Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Sear chicken. Heat 30ml olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs. Sear 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove from pan. Let rest 5 minutes. Slice into thick chunks or leave whole.
Assemble bowls. Divide cooked brown rice among 4 serving bowls. Arrange chicken chunks or whole thighs on top of rice.
Drain quick-pickled vegetables. Arrange a generous portion alongside chicken and rice.
Garnish. Sprinkle with fresh coriander or parsley and toasted sesame seeds, if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Turkey and Pea Quesadillas
recipes.special_requests: Mexican cuisine, Oil, mayonnaises, sugar, sauce free
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown, crispy half-moon quesadilla rests centrally on a simple, rustic ceramic plate. The corn tortilla is perfectly toasted, exhibiting a warm, inviting hue with subtle darker spots from dry-cooking. Slight bulges hint at the generous, savory filling within. Along the cut edge, the melted Monterey Jack cheese oozes gently, revealing a glimpse of the interior: browned, tender ground turkey intermingled with vibrant green peas, finely diced translucent onion, and specks of dark red hot sauce. The textures are clear: crisp tortilla, soft interior. The plate sits on a well-used wooden kitchen table, a casually placed cloth napkin nearby. Warm, inviting light illuminates the dish, emphasizing its homely comfort. A lime wedge is placed beside the quesadilla for a touch of freshness.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with lime wedges for a squeeze of fresh citrus.
Traditionally enjoyed by hand, or cut into wedges.
instructions: Heat a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Add finely diced onion. Cook, stirring, for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add a splash of water or broth if sticking occurs.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground turkey to the pan. Break it up with a spoon. Cook until browned, about 8-10 minutes. Drain any excess liquid if turkey releases too much.
Stir in thawed green peas, hot sauce, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 3-5 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Remove from heat.
Heat a separate dry non-stick pan or comal over medium heat. Place one tortilla on the hot surface. Warm for 30 seconds per side until pliable.
Sprinkle a quarter of the cheese over half of the warmed tortilla. Add a generous portion of the turkey and pea mixture on top of the cheese. Add another quarter of the cheese over the filling.
Fold the other half of the tortilla over the filling to form a half-moon. Gently press down.
Cook the folded quesadilla in the dry pan for 2-3 minutes per side, until the tortilla is golden-brown and crispy, and the cheese is melted and gooey. Repeat with remaining tortillas and filling.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to preferred spice level.
Ensure turkey is fully cooked to 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Sostenibile con Pomodoro Fermentato e Melanzane Arrosto
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of Pollo Sostenibile with Fermented Tomato and Roasted Eggplant is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The plate is ample, allowing for generous negative space. Pan-seared chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, are nestled among a vibrant, rustic sauce of red fermented and fresh tomatoes. The sauce has a rich, slightly chunky texture, showcasing the natural variations in tomato color. Interspersed are roasted eggplant cubes, about 2 cm, with their deep purple skins and tender, slightly caramelized interiors providing earthy contrast. A small, neat mound of al dente whole wheat orzo pasta is served alongside the chicken and sauce, absorbing some of its richness. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered sparingly over the dish, providing a pop of color and freshness. The composition is natural and unforced, emphasizing the inherent beauty and texture of each ingredient. The table surface is light, reclaimed wood, providing a warm, organic backdrop. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded neatly to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty whole-grain bread to sop up the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette.
instructions: Ensure 200g of pre-fermented tomatoes are ready for the sauce.
Carefully remove skin and bones from chicken thighs. Reserve skin for rendering and bones for stock. Cut chicken meat into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add chicken skin. Render until crispy and golden. Remove skin; reserve rendered fat in pan.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add chicken chunks to the pan with rendered fat. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan; set aside.
Add 15 ml olive oil to the same pan if needed. Add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Pour in white wine (if using). Scrape up any browned bits from the pan. Simmer for 1 minute.
Add fresh diced tomatoes and chopped fermented tomatoes. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Sauce should thicken slightly.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Dice eggplant into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized.
Cook whole wheat orzo pasta according to package instructions until al dente. Drain well.
Stir roasted eggplant into the chicken and tomato sauce. Add cooked orzo to the sauce. Stir gently to combine.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: For fermented tomatoes, use a simple salt brine fermentation (e.g., 2% salt by weight of tomatoes) for 5-7 days at room temperature. Ensure tomatoes are fully submerged.
To make chicken stock: cover reserved chicken bones and any vegetable scraps (onion peels, garlic skins, tomato trimmings, eggplant ends) with water. Simmer for 1-2 hours. Strain and use.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Herb Chicken with Burst Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white ceramic plate, showcasing a single generously portioned, golden-brown bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh. The chicken skin is visibly crispy, with a rich, caramelized sear. Surrounding the chicken are vibrant, burst cherry tomatoes, some still whole, interspersed with tender, thinly sliced caramelized onions and fragrant smashed garlic cloves. A rustic pan sauce, rich with roasted tomato juices and herbs, lightly pools around the chicken. Fresh, bright green basil leaves, roughly torn, are scattered over the dish, providing a contrasting color and aromatic garnish. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a rustic wooden table, complemented by a simple linen napkin and classic flatware, with a small side of crusty Italian bread.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread for dipping in the sauce.
Accompanied by a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Pair with a side of creamy polenta or al dente pasta.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down.
Sear chicken for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from skillet; set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced red onion and smashed garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Add cherry tomatoes, rosemary, and thyme sprigs to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes begin to burst.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the tomato mixture. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through.
Remove skillet from oven. Discard rosemary and thyme sprigs. Stir in torn fresh basil leaves.
Serve immediately, spooning the pan sauce and burst tomatoes over the chicken.
notes: For best flavor, use high-quality olive oil and fresh herbs.
The skin-on, bone-in chicken thighs provide more flavor and moisture; boneless, skinless can be used but cooking time will vary.

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan Pork Stir-fry with Green Beans and Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sichuan Pork Stir-fry is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features generous chunks of savory, stir-fried pork, coated in a rich, glossy reddish-brown sauce. Vibrant green beans, cut into 3 cm pieces, are interspersed with bright red diced tomato cubes, creating a striking color contrast. The pork is cut into uniform strips, showcasing its tender texture. The dish has a balanced composition, with moderate negative space on the plate. A sprinkle of fresh sliced green spring onions adds a final touch of color and freshness. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin, a pair of chopsticks, and a small white rice bowl are neatly placed beside the dish, honoring its Chinese cultural origin. Natural, even lighting highlights the food's authentic colors and textures.
instructions: Cut pork loin into 1 cm thick, 4 cm long strips. Marinate pork with 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp cornstarch for 15 minutes.
Trim green beans. Cut into 3 cm pieces. Dice tomatoes into 2 cm cubes. Mince ginger and garlic. Slice dried chilies into 1 cm pieces. Slice spring onions for garnish.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok over high heat. Add green beans. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender. Remove from wok. Set aside.
Add 2 tbsp vegetable oil to the wok. Add marinated pork. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until pork is browned and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove pork from wok. Set aside.
Add minced ginger, garlic, and dried chilies to the wok. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add doubanjiang. Stir-fry for 1 minute until oil turns red.
Add diced tomatoes. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until slightly softened.
In a small bowl, combine beef stock, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, 1 tsp cornstarch, and 1 tsp sugar. Mix well.
Pour sauce mixture into the wok. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Return cooked pork and green beans to the wok. Toss everything to coat evenly with the sauce. Cook for 1 minute.
Transfer to a serving dish. Garnish with sliced spring onions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pasta with Crispy Bacon and Tomato-Basil Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of pasta is casually twirled and placed in the center of a rustic, off-white ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The pasta strands are coated in a vibrant, rustic red tomato sauce. Small, irregular chunks of crispy, golden-brown smoked bacon are distributed throughout the pasta and nestled on top. Fresh green basil leaves, roughly torn, are scattered over the dish. A light dusting of grated white Pecorino Romano cheese covers some of the pasta. The sauce appears rich and clings to the pasta. The bowl sits directly on a well-worn, light-colored wooden kitchen table. A simple, folded off-white linen napkin is placed casually beside the bowl. A silver fork rests on the table. Lighting is warm, suggesting natural light, creating soft shadows. The background is slightly out of focus, showing hints of a homely kitchen environment. The portion is substantial for one person, filling the bowl comfortably.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Pecorino Romano cheese at the table.
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Cook pasta until al dente.
While pasta cooks, heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add smoked bacon, cut into small lardons. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Leave about 15 ml bacon fat in the skillet. Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Add crushed tomatoes to the skillet. Stir. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens.
Drain cooked pasta, reserving 60 ml pasta water. Add pasta directly to the tomato sauce.
Add crispy bacon and half of the fresh basil to the pasta and sauce.
Toss everything together. Add a splash of reserved pasta water as needed to create a glossy sauce.
Stir in half of the grated Pecorino Romano. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and Pecorino Romano.

recipes.recipe_name: Herbed Cottage Cheese Stuffed Chicken Breast
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown baked chicken breast sits centrally on an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic dinner plate. The chicken, presented as a plump, whole piece, is gently cut at one end to reveal its creamy, flecked green and white cottage cheese and spinach filling. A small, natural mound of vibrant green steamed broccoli florets rests beside the chicken, offering a fresh color contrast. The plating is casual, with ample negative space. The scene is a cozy, lived-in family kitchen. The plate sits on a well-used light wooden dining table. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually draped nearby. A standard silver fork and knife are placed simply next to the plate. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the comforting dish, set against a subtly blurred background of a homely kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad
Serve with steamed or roasted vegetables
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Butterfly each chicken breast. Alternatively, place between two sheets of cling film and pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness.
In a bowl, combine cottage cheese, spinach, minced garlic, parsley, chives, onion powder, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Spoon an equal amount of the cottage cheese mixture onto one half of each butterflied chicken breast. Fold the other half over to enclose the filling. Secure with toothpicks if needed.
Lightly brush the outside of the chicken with olive oil. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Place stuffed chicken breasts in a baking dish.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Chicken should be golden brown and cooked through.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: This recipe is designed to be low calorie and high protein.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Herb and Cottage Cheese Stuffed Chicken Breast
recipes.visual_description: The golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast, left whole, rests as the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Its exterior shows a delicate crust, hinting at a tender interior. A small, neat incision reveals the creamy, off-white cottage cheese filling, generously flecked with vibrant green, roughly chopped spinach and fresh herbs, offering a delightful contrast in color and texture. A light, glossy pan sauce is artfully drizzled around the base of the chicken. Accompanying the dish are a few bright green, tender-crisp asparagus spears, strategically placed for color balance and visual appeal. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space, set on a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin and standard flatware, under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Butterfly each chicken breast. Place between two sheets of cling film. Pound gently to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic and spinach. Sauté until spinach wilts, about 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat. Squeeze out excess liquid from spinach.
In a bowl, combine cottage cheese, grated Parmesan, chopped chives, chopped parsley, wilted spinach, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Spoon an even amount of the cottage cheese mixture onto one half of each butterflied chicken breast. Fold the other half over the filling. Secure edges with toothpicks.
Heat remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear stuffed chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer the pan to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the chicken reaches 75°C. Remove toothpicks.
Remove chicken from pan. Tent with foil. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Return pan to stovetop over medium heat. Add chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes to reduce slightly, creating a light pan sauce.
Serve chicken with pan sauce.
notes: Pounding the chicken to an even thickness ensures uniform cooking.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Baked Chicken with Roasted Tomatoes and Feta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Baked Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh is the centerpiece. It rests amidst a vibrant medley of roasted cherry tomatoes, which are slightly burst and glistening, alongside tender, caramelized red onion wedges and whole, dark Kalamata olives. Crumbled white feta cheese is scattered over the dish, melting slightly from the residual heat. Fresh green basil leaves are artfully torn and sprinkled for a pop of color and freshness. The chicken is whole, not sliced. The dish has a natural, organic arrangement with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting from above, creating subtle shadows. A folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Cut red onion into thick wedges. Smash garlic cloves.
In a large roasting dish, combine tomatoes, red onion, garlic, 30ml olive oil, oregano, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat.
Arrange chicken thighs, skin-side up, among the vegetables in the dish.
Drizzle remaining 30ml olive oil over chicken.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Remove dish from oven. Add pitted Kalamata olives and crumbled feta cheese around chicken.
Return to oven. Continue roasting for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from oven. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the dish.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of seared beef sirloin with a deep brown crust. These are mixed with thick, glossy wedges of purple red onion and bright red Roma tomatoes. Golden, thick-cut potato batons are scattered through the beef mixture, all coated in a dark, shimmering sauce. A neat, molded dome of fluffy white rice sits on the side of the plate. Fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the top. The scene is set on a light wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin and a small side bowl of spicy green aji sauce. The lighting is natural and even.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Aji Verde (green chili sauce)
Accompany with Inca Kola or a glass of red wine
Traditionally eaten with both rice and potatoes in the same meal

ingredients.name: Red onions, cut into thick wedges
Roma tomatoes, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef in batches until browned and medium-rare.
Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok.
Stir-fry onion wedges for 2 minutes until slightly charred but crisp.
Add garlic and aji amarillo paste. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the wok.
Pour in soy sauce and red wine vinegar. Toss quickly.
Add tomato wedges. Stir for 30 seconds to warm through.
Fold in the cooked potato fries and half the cilantro.
Remove from heat immediately.
Serve with white rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding beef to achieve a smoky flavor.
Do not overcook the tomatoes; they should be warm but hold their shape.
The potatoes should be added at the very last second to maintain some crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Milanese with Lemon Butter Linguine
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown chicken Milanese cutlet, crisply pan-fried and pounded thin, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is cut as a whole piece. Adjacent to it, a neatly twirled mound of al dente linguine glistens with a light lemon-butter sauce. The chicken's surface shows the textured crunch of the breading, while the pasta strands are distinct. Both the chicken and pasta are liberally sprinkled with vibrant green, freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley, providing a fresh contrast. A bright yellow lemon wedge is positioned beside the chicken. The overall color palette is warm golden, pale yellow, and fresh green against the white plate. The arrangement is balanced and professional, with appropriate negative space. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, with standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an inviting, approachable restaurant-style image.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra lemon wedges for individual preference.
Offer grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Pound chicken breasts to a uniform 0.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Prepare a breading station. Place flour in a shallow dish. Whisk eggs in a second shallow dish. Combine Panko breadcrumbs and grated Parmesan in a third shallow dish.
Dredge each pounded chicken cutlet in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg wash, ensuring full coverage. Finally, coat thoroughly with the breadcrumb-Parmesan mixture, pressing gently to adhere.
Cook linguine according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml of pasta water. Drain pasta.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry breaded chicken cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side, or until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Transfer cooked chicken to a wire rack to drain excess oil.
While chicken cooks, prepare lemon butter sauce. In a separate large skillet or pot, melt butter over medium heat. Add juice from half of the lemon. Stir to combine.
Add drained linguine to the lemon butter sauce. Add 60 ml of reserved pasta water. Toss pasta to coat. If pasta appears dry, add more reserved pasta water, 15 ml at a time, until a light sauce forms.
Plate individual portions. Place a chicken cutlet on one side of a white porcelain plate. Neatly twirl a portion of lemon butter linguine alongside the chicken.
Garnish the chicken and pasta generously with fresh chopped parsley. Place a lemon wedge beside the chicken for serving.
notes: Pounding the chicken to an even thickness ensures uniform cooking and tenderness.
Do not overcrowd the pan when frying chicken to maintain oil temperature and ensure crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Parmesan Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single, generous individual portion. The rigatoni pasta is coated in a rich, creamy, pale yellow Parmesan sauce. Scattered throughout are golden-brown, seared chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm in size, exhibiting a slight crisp exterior. Finely diced onion and minced garlic are visible within the sauce, contributing to its texture. The dish is garnished with a scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley, adding a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Traditional silver flatware is arranged to the side. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish as the focal point while maintaining a clean, unobtrusive background.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
Cut chicken breasts into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear chicken until golden brown and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C. This takes about 6-8 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add finely diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Add cooked rigatoni and seared chicken chunks to the skillet. Toss to coat the pasta and chicken with the sauce.
If the sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, one tablespoon at a time, until desired consistency is reached. Stir well.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Home-Style Bacon and Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: Pasta is twirled onto a modest, everyday cream-colored ceramic plate, forming a natural, slightly mounded portion. The rich red tomato sauce generously coats the al dente pasta strands. Visible throughout are golden-brown, crispy diced bacon pieces. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are scattered casually over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. A small amount of sauce naturally pools at the base of the pasta. The dish is presented on a well-used, light wooden dining table. A simple metal fork rests beside the plate. In the background, a small, rustic ceramic bowl holds grated Pecorino Romano cheese, ready for serving. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, lived-in atmosphere.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil for pasta.
Dice bacon into small cubes. Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced bacon.
Cook bacon until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Leave rendered fat in the skillet.
Finely dice the onion. Add onion to the skillet with bacon fat. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Mince garlic cloves. Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour crushed tomatoes into the skillet. Stir well. Bring to a gentle simmer. Season with salt and black pepper.
Simmer the sauce for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
While sauce simmers, add pasta to the boiling water. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving about 120 ml of pasta water.
Add cooked pasta to the skillet with the tomato sauce. Toss to coat. If needed, add a splash of reserved pasta water to loosen the sauce.
Stir in the crispy bacon and fresh basil leaves. Toss gently to combine.
Serve immediately. Offer grated Pecorino Romano cheese on the side if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cheesy Chicken and Potato Bake sits on a matte cream ceramic plate. The dish consists of oven-roasted, golden-brown potato cubes and seared chicken chunks arranged in a natural, overlapping heap. Melted sharp cheddar cheese drapes over the components, showing bubbly textures and toasted edges. Vibrant green chopped chives are sprinkled evenly over the cheese. The arrangement is asymmetrical and casual, filling the center of the plate while leaving clean margins. The plate rests on a dark, textured wooden table next to a stainless steel fork and a neutral linen napkin. Warm, directional kitchen lighting enhances the crispy potato skins and the glossy, melted cheese. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of sour cream
Pair with a fresh green salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel and cut potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Toss potatoes with 15ml oil, half the salt, and half the paprika.
Spread potatoes on a baking sheet.
Roast for 20 minutes.
Cut chicken into 3cm chunks.
Season chicken with remaining oil, salt, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and pepper.
Add chicken to the baking sheet with potatoes.
Roast for 15 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Sprinkle shredded cheddar over the chicken and potatoes.
Bake 3 minutes until cheese melts and bubbles.
Garnish with finely chopped chives.
notes: Cut potatoes into uniform cubes to ensure even roasting
Use sharp cheddar for the best flavor profile
Ensure chicken chunks are not touching to allow browning

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Forno con Patate e Pomodorini
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo al Forno con Patate e Pomodorini is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Tender, boneless chicken thighs, seared to a golden hue, are centrally placed. Thick-cut roasted potato wedges, with slightly crisped edges and soft interiors, are arranged around the chicken. Halved cherry tomatoes, vibrant red and slightly burst from roasting, are scattered generously, releasing their sweet juices. Melted fresh mozzarella drapes over the chicken and potatoes, creating creamy white accents. Fresh green basil leaves are torn and scattered for a fragrant, contrasting garnish. The dish exhibits a natural, organic flow with moderate negative space, highlighting the rich colors of golden brown, deep red, and white. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Wash and cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges. Place on a large baking sheet.
Toss potatoes with 15ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and chopped rosemary. Spread in a single layer.
Roast potatoes for 20 minutes.
While potatoes roast, season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove from heat.
Add seared chicken to the baking sheet with the roasted potatoes.
Halve cherry tomatoes and scatter them around the chicken and potatoes. Mince garlic and distribute over the dish.
Pour chicken broth over the ingredients on the baking sheet.
Return baking sheet to oven and bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove baking sheet from oven. Tear fresh mozzarella and scatter over the chicken and potatoes.
Return to oven for 5 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Garnish with torn fresh basil before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Crab, Mushroom, and Basil Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a classic white porcelain pasta bowl, showcasing a single, generous portion of tagliatelle. The pasta is loosely twirled, allowing its flat ribbons to cradle a rich, creamy sauce. Visible throughout the pasta are tender chunks of white crab meat, thinly sliced sautéed cremini mushrooms, and vibrant green pieces of fresh basil. The sauce has a warm, inviting reddish-orange hue from the tomato and hot sauce, contrasting beautifully with the bright green basil and pale crab. A light grating of Parmesan cheese dusts the top, adding a subtle white finish. The texture is luscious and coherent. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table. Beside it, a set of traditional Italian flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are neatly placed. A small, rustic piece of ciabatta bread rests near the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the food's inviting textures. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread, such as ciabatta, to soak up the delicious sauce.
Pair with a crisp, dry white wine like Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook tagliatelle according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, prepare sauce. Thinly slice mushrooms. Mince shallots and garlic.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add shallots. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes. Add garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in tomato paste and hot sauce. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze skillet, scraping up any browned bits. Cook until wine is mostly reduced.
Stir in heavy cream and vegetable stock. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Gently fold in crab meat. Cook for 1-2 minutes to heat through. Avoid overcooking crab.
Add cooked tagliatelle to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. Add fresh mozzarella, torn into small pieces. Add half of the fresh basil, torn.
Toss pasta until mozzarella is melted and sauce coats noodles. Add reserved pasta water as needed to reach desired consistency.
Stir in half of the grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining fresh basil and a sprinkle of Parmesan.
notes: Adjust the amount of hot sauce to suit your preferred spice level.
Using fresh, high-quality crab meat will significantly enhance the dish's flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Coffee-Marinated Portobello Steaks with Mint Chimichurri
recipes.visual_description: A single, dark brown, seared portobello mushroom steak, whole and substantial, centers a round white porcelain plate. The mushroom displays a rich, caramelized exterior from the searing process. A generous, vibrant green mint chimichurri, with visible chopped herbs, is spooned artfully over the mushroom, some spilling onto the plate. The chimichurri adds a fresh, textured contrast. Beside the mushroom, a neat portion of golden-brown roasted baby potato halves (cut into wedges) or creamy polenta provides a comforting accompaniment. A few fresh mint leaves or a small parsley sprig garnish the chimichurri. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a cotton napkin, and natural, even lighting, creating a clean, inviting restaurant-style presentation.
instructions: Prepare marinade: Combine cooled brewed coffee, soy sauce, minced garlic, smoked paprika, and 30 ml olive oil in a shallow dish. Whisk well.
Marinate mushrooms: Clean portobello mushrooms. Remove stems. Place mushrooms gill-side down in marinade. Ensure they are coated. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, up to 2 hours, flipping halfway.

Make chimichurri: While mushrooms marinate, prepare chimichurri. In a bowl, combine finely chopped fresh mint, finely chopped fresh parsley, remaining 30 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, and red chili flakes. Season with salt and black pepper. Stir well.
Cook mushrooms: Heat a large cast-iron skillet or grill pan over medium-high heat. Add a splash of olive oil if needed.
Sear mushrooms: Place marinated portobello mushrooms gill-side down in hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes until caramelized.
Flip and finish: Flip mushrooms. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until tender.
Serve: Transfer cooked portobello steaks to plates. Spoon a generous amount of mint chimichurri over each mushroom. Serve immediately with desired side like roasted baby potatoes or creamy polenta.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Artichoke-Cottage Cheese Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Artichoke-Cottage Cheese Pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A neat mound of creamy, golden-hued pasta, generously studded with tender, pale green artichoke quarters, occupies the center. The pasta exhibits a rich, al dente texture. Beside the pasta, golden-brown seared chicken breast, sliced into thick diagonal pieces, is artfully arranged. The chicken shows a perfectly cooked, moist interior. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley and bright yellow lemon zest garnishes the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. A light drizzle of olive oil glistens over the components. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a soft, blurred background maintaining focus on the food.

ingredients.name: Canned or jarred artichoke hearts, drained and quartered

instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions. Reserve 125ml pasta water before draining. Set aside.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Let rest 5 minutes, then slice into thick diagonal pieces.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter to the same pan. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in quartered artichoke hearts. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in cottage cheese until melted and creamy.
Add cooked pasta to the pan. Toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency is reached.
Stir in fresh parsley, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste. If using, stir in grated Parmesan cheese.
Divide pasta among four plates. Arrange sliced chicken beside the pasta. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Pork with Mustard and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of tender, beer-braised pork sits centrally on a round, white porcelain plate. The pork chunk is deep brown with slightly crispy edges, glistening with the rich, dark amber braising sauce. The sauce, thick and unctuous, pools around the pork, revealing hints of golden caramelized onions and flecks of whole grain mustard. Beside the pork, a neat mound of fluffy white long-grain rice provides a clean contrast. Fresh, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the pork and sauce, adding a vibrant green pop. The plate has ample negative space, highlighting the dish's rustic elegance. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and standard silver flatware. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread to soak up the rich sauce
A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette can complement the richness of the dish
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Season pork chunks generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork on all sides until deep golden brown. Remove pork and set aside.
Add thinly sliced onions to the pot. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until softened and caramelized, about 10-15 minutes.
Stir in Dijon mustard and whole grain mustard. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in the dark beer. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return the seared pork to the pot. Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Ensure liquid almost covers the pork.
Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer on the stovetop. Cover the pot tightly.
Transfer the covered pot to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until the pork is exceptionally tender and easily pulled apart.

While pork braises, rinse the long-grain rice. Cook according to package instructions. Typically, combine 300g rice with 600ml water. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let rest, covered, for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in butter.

Carefully remove pork from the braising liquid. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaves. If desired, reduce the sauce on the stovetop over medium-high heat until slightly thickened. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

Serve one large pork chunk per plate. Spoon generous amounts of the rich braising sauce over the pork. Serve with a neat mound of fluffy long-grain rice on the side. Garnish with fresh, finely chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Coffee-Rubbed Lamb Loin with Mint Gremolata
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Coffee-Rubbed Lamb Loin is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The lamb, seared to a dark, caramelized crust and sliced into thick medallions, reveals a tender, pink interior. Beside the lamb, roasted root vegetables, including golden-brown parsnip batons, vibrant orange carrot wedges, and quartered small potatoes, are artfully arranged, some with lightly charred edges. A generous spoonful of bright green Mint Gremolata, featuring finely minced mint leaves and lemon zest, garnishes the lamb, adding a burst of fresh color. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table, with a neatly folded off-white cotton napkin to the side. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and peel baby carrots and parsnips. Cut parsnips into thick batons. Halve or quarter small potatoes. Toss vegetables with 2 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast vegetables for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned.
Combine ground coffee, brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, 1 tsp salt, and 0.5 tsp black pepper in a small bowl to make the coffee rub.
Pat lamb loin dry. Rub generously with the coffee mixture.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear lamb loin on all sides until a deep crust forms, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Transfer the pan to the preheated oven. Roast for 10-15 minutes for medium-rare, or until desired doneness is reached.
Remove lamb from oven. Rest on a cutting board for 5-10 minutes.
While lamb rests, prepare gremolata. Finely chop mint leaves. Mince garlic cloves. Combine mint, minced garlic, and lemon zest in a small bowl. Stir in 3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil.
Slice rested lamb loin into thick medallions.
Arrange lamb medallions and roasted vegetables on individual plates. Spoon mint gremolata over the lamb. Serve immediately.
notes: For medium-rare, lamb internal temperature should be 57-60°C. Adjust cooking time for desired doneness.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken with Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and glistening, rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is a whole piece, not sliced. Alongside, vibrant roasted bell pepper strips in red, yellow, and orange are artfully arranged, interspersed with tender red onion wedges and burst cherry tomatoes. Dark, pitted Kalamata olives and creamy white feta crumbles are scattered throughout the vegetables, adding contrasting colors and textures. A sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley brightens the top. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a light cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread or crusty artisanal bread.
Offer a side of tzatziki or hummus.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut bell peppers into 2cm strips. Slice red onion into thin wedges.
On a baking sheet, combine bell peppers, red onion, and cherry tomatoes. Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Season with salt, pepper, and oregano. Toss to coat.
Roast vegetables for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet with chicken to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
To the roasted vegetables, add pitted Kalamata olives and crumbled feta cheese. Toss gently.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the chicken and vegetables.
Plate one chicken breast. Arrange roasted vegetables alongside. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Adjust roasting time for vegetables based on desired tenderness.
Ensure chicken is fully cooked for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Saltimbocca with Rosemary Potatoes and Cherry Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: The dish is plated simply on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing professional but approachable restaurant style. A golden-brown chicken saltimbocca, topped with crispy prosciutto and vibrant green sage leaves, is the focal point. Its surface shows a beautiful sear. Beside it, a neat mound of golden rosemary-roasted baby potatoes, their skins slightly blistered and herbs visible. A small pool of glistening pan sauce lightly coats the chicken. Separately, a vibrant side of burst cherry tomato confit with creamy white mozzarella balls and fresh basil adds a pop of color. The tomatoes are soft, and the mozzarella retains its shape. The overall composition is clean, with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. A cotton napkin and standard flatware rest beside the plate on a simple wooden table, creating a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the pan sauce.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a dry white Italian wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
instructions: Prepare potatoes: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and halve potatoes. Toss with 30ml olive oil, 2 sprigs rosemary (leaves picked), salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes until tender and golden.

Prepare tomato confit: While potatoes roast, place cherry tomatoes in a small oven-safe dish. Add 40ml olive oil, 2 whole garlic cloves (smashed), and a pinch of salt. Roast in the oven with potatoes for the last 20-25 minutes, until tomatoes burst and soften.
Prepare chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Place each breast between two sheets of parchment paper. Pound gently to an even 1.5 cm thickness.
Assemble saltimbocca: Lay 2 slices of prosciutto on each chicken breast. Place 4 sage leaves evenly over prosciutto. Secure with a toothpick.

Cook chicken: Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken, prosciutto-side down, in the hot skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes until prosciutto is crisp and golden.
Flip chicken: Flip chicken. Sear for 3 minutes on the second side. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Make pan sauce: Remove chicken from skillet. Keep warm. Discard toothpicks. Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add remaining 2 crushed garlic cloves. Sauté 30 seconds.
Deglaze: Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes until reduced by half. Add chicken stock. Simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Finish sauce: Stir in butter until melted and sauce slightly thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Assemble salad: In a small bowl, combine roasted cherry tomatoes (remove garlic cloves), drained mozzarella balls, and remaining 2 sprigs rosemary (leaves picked). Drizzle with a little olive oil.

Plate: Place a portion of rosemary potatoes on each plate. Arrange chicken saltimbocca beside potatoes. Spoon pan sauce over chicken. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve with cherry tomato and mozzarella salad.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
Pounding chicken to even thickness ensures even cooking.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing chicken. Cook in batches if necessary.
traditional_techniques: Searing: Developing a crust on the chicken and prosciutto.
Deglazing: Creating a pan sauce from browned bits.
Roasting: Cooking vegetables for tender interior and crisp exterior.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Chipotle Beef & Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A hearty portion of Smoky Chipotle Beef & Chicken Pasta is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The rigatoni pasta is coated generously in a rich, reddish-brown sauce. Visible are tender, dark brown cubes of seared beef and lighter, browned pieces of chicken. The sauce has a glossy sheen, indicating its richness. Scattered over the pasta are vibrant orange shreds of melted sharp cheddar cheese, alongside golden-brown, small diced crispy salami pieces, adding textural contrast. A light sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped cilantro adds a pop of color and freshness to the top. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin. Beside the main dish, a small, elegant clear glass bowl holds a mound of thinly sliced, pale green quick pickled cucumber, offering a fresh counterpoint. A slice of golden-brown toasted crusty sourdough bread leans against the side of the pasta bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a casual yet refined bistro ambiance with a softly blurred background.
instructions: Make quick pickled cucumber. In a small bowl, combine thinly sliced cucumber, white vinegar, water, and a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add diced salami. Cook until crispy. Remove salami with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pot.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pot if needed. Add beef cubes. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove beef. Set aside.
Add chicken cubes to the pot. Sear until browned on all sides and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C / 167°F). Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, chipotle in adobo, unsweetened cocoa powder, and granulated sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef and chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for at least 30 minutes, or until beef is tender. Season with salt and pepper.
While ragu simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 120ml pasta water.
Add cooked pasta to the ragu. Stir in mayonnaise and half of the grated cheddar cheese. Add reserved pasta water as needed to create a creamy sauce.
Toast slices of crusty bread until golden.
Serve pasta in bowls. Top with remaining grated cheddar, crispy salami, and chopped cilantro. Serve quick pickled cucumber and toasted bread on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Pork Loin with Ancho Chocolate Sauce, Pineapple Potato Hash, and Crispy Ciabatta
recipes.visual_description: A single seared pork loin medallion, thick and golden-brown, is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center on a rustic white ceramic dinner plate. It rests beside a generous mound of vibrant pineapple potato hash, featuring tender, lightly browned potato cubes interspersed with glistening, caramelized pineapple chunks. A rich, dark, glossy chili chocolate sauce pools elegantly beneath the pork and is drizzled sparingly over the medallion, its deep hue contrasting with the hash. Bright green, freshly chopped cilantro leaves are scattered across the dish, adding a pop of freshness. Crispy, irregularly torn pieces of golden-brown ciabatta bread are artfully placed to the side. The plate has ample negative space. The setting is a clean wooden table surface, with a simple cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of warm corn tortillas for scooping up sauce and hash.
Offer a sprinkle of cotija cheese over the hash for added saltiness.
instructions: Pat pork loin medallions dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat 15ml oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork medallions 4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer to a baking sheet. Finish in oven at 180°C for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C. Rest 5 minutes.

In the same skillet, add remaining 15ml oil. Sauté diced onion over medium heat 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, ancho chili powder, cumin, and oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in tomato paste.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Stir in chopped dark chocolate until melted and smooth. Season with salt. Keep warm.
In a separate large pan, heat 15ml oil over medium-high heat. Add diced potatoes. Cook 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and lightly browned.
Add diced pineapple to the potatoes. Cook 3-4 minutes until pineapple is slightly caramelized. Season hash with salt and pepper.
While hash cooks, place torn ciabatta pieces on a baking sheet. Toast in oven at 180°C for 5-7 minutes, or until golden and crispy.

Place a portion of pineapple potato hash on each plate. Arrange a seared pork medallion next to the hash. Spoon a generous amount of chili chocolate sauce over the pork and around the plate. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve with crispy ciabatta pieces and lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Marmalade & Cherry Bread Pudding with Sweet Pork Lardons
recipes.visual_description: A warm, inviting image showcases a generous individual portion of golden-brown bread pudding in a rustic ceramic bowl. The pudding is slightly puffed and moist, with soft bread cubes visible, soaked in a rich, creamy custard. Hints of bright red pitted cherries and streaks of vibrant orange marmalade peek through the surface. Scattered on top are small, crisp, golden-brown sweet pork lardons, providing a contrasting texture and a subtle sheen. The bowl sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, with a simple, slightly rumpled white cloth napkin casually placed beside it. The lighting is warm and natural, emanating from an unseen kitchen window, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. The overall scene is unpretentious, reflecting a homemade, comforting dessert ready for a family meal. The focus is entirely on the natural, appetizing appearance of the food, without any elaborate plating or decorative garnishes, emphasizing its homely comfort.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly butter a 2-liter baking dish.
Cut stale bread into 2-3 cm cubes. Set aside.
Cut pork belly into small 1 cm lardons (small cubes).

Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat. Add pork lardons. Cook slowly until crispy and golden, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat. Immediately toss crispy lardons with 1 tablespoon of the granulated sugar. Set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk milk, eggs, remaining granulated sugar, vanilla extract, and sweet paprika until well combined.
Add bread cubes to the milk mixture. Gently fold in marmalade and pitted cherries. Ensure bread is well-coated.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until the pudding is set and golden brown on top. A knife inserted into the center should come out mostly clean.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve warm, topped with the crispy sweet pork lardons.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Parmesan Risotto with Pan-Seared Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Parmesan risotto is presented in a shallow, white porcelain bowl, its pale ivory color contrasting with the golden-brown crust of a pan-seared chicken breast. The risotto flows naturally, maintaining its characteristic fluid consistency, with individual al dente rice grains visible. The chicken breast, cooked whole, rests slightly to the side of the risotto, showcasing its seared exterior. A sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley and a delicate dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese garnish the dish. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface, a clean white cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors, with a minimal, casual restaurant-style background. The presentation is professional yet approachable, emphasizing the quality ingredients and refined execution.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as the risotto's texture is best when freshly made.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Heat 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.
Finely dice the onion. Mince the garlic.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, melt 15 g butter with 15 ml olive oil over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add hot chicken broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly until each ladleful is almost completely absorbed before adding the next.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente. It should be fluid, not stiff.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. This is mantecatura. Stir vigorously until creamy.
Season risotto with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.
Slice chicken breasts into thick medallions or serve whole.
Ladle risotto onto plates. Place chicken beside or on top of risotto. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and additional grated Parmesan.
notes: Use high-quality Arborio rice for best results.
Keep chicken broth hot throughout the cooking process to maintain a consistent cooking temperature for the rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef and Root Vegetable Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Beef and Root Vegetable Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a light wooden table. A neat mound of fluffy white long-grain rice forms the base. Three substantial, dark brown braised beef chunks, each approximately 4 cm, are nestled beside the rice, showcasing their tender texture. Interspersed are vibrant orange carrot rounds, 2 cm thick, and bright yellow corn kernels, adding color. A rich, glossy, dark brown gravy generously coats the beef and vegetables, pooling elegantly around the rice. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley, providing a vibrant contrast. The composition is balanced, with appropriate negative space. A folded grey cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a modern bistro.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Prepare beef. Cut beef into 4 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Dredge beef. Lightly coat beef chunks in plain flour. Shake off excess.

Sear beef. Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Sauté aromatics. Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onion to the pot. Cook, stirring, until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Build sauce. Stir in 30 g tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Pour in 60 ml Worcestershire sauce and 100 ml beef stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Add liquids and beef. Pour in remaining 650 ml beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Return seared beef to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged in liquid.
Braise. Cover pot tightly. Transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 1 hour 45 minutes.

Add carrots. While beef braises, peel and cut carrots into 2 cm thick rounds or large dice. Add carrots to the pot. Return to oven. Continue braising for another 45 minutes, or until beef is very tender and carrots are cooked through. Total braising time: 2 hours 30 minutes.
Cook corn. During the last 10 minutes of braising, stir in 200 g corn kernels. Cook until heated through.
Cook rice. While stew finishes, prepare 300 g long-grain white rice according to package directions.

Rest and serve. Remove pot from oven. Let stew rest for 10 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Serve generous portions of braised beef and vegetables over a bed of cooked rice. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Allow braised beef to rest for 10 minutes off heat before serving for optimal tenderness.
Chuck roast or beef shin are excellent cuts for braising.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Chili Soup
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rustic ceramic bowl holds a generous portion of hearty beef and chili soup. The rich, reddish-brown broth is thick with crumbled ground beef, dark red kidney beans, and diced tomatoes, creating a comforting, textured landscape. A light scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped cilantro rests on top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The soup is served on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, reflecting a homely family kitchen atmosphere. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually placed beside the bowl. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, highlighting the inviting warmth of the dish. The presentation is unpretentious and comforting, designed for a cozy, everyday meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with cornbread or crackers.
Offer shredded cheddar cheese and sour cream as optional toppings.

ingredients.name: Canned diced tomatoes with green chilies
Canned kidney beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef. Cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, chili powder, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, diced tomatoes with green chilies, and beef broth. Stir well.
Bring the soup to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20 minutes.
Stir in kidney beans. Continue to simmer for another 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.
notes: Adjust chili powder to your preferred spice level.
This soup tastes even better the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Chicken & Fermented Tomato Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a single, refined portion in a shallow, handcrafted ceramic bowl with a natural, unglazed finish, in an earthy cream tone. A creamy, free-flowing risotto forms the base, its natural deep red-orange hue from the slow-roasted tomato paste subtly visible. Nestled naturally within the risotto are three to four golden-brown, seared chicken thigh chunks, each showing a perfectly browned exterior and moist interior. Scattered over the top are irregular, crisp shards of rendered chicken skin, adding a textural contrast. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves, subtly torn, are thoughtfully placed to provide a fresh, organic accent. The overall plating is minimalistic, with ample negative space. The setting features a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed, natural beige linen napkin is subtly placed beside the bowl. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, highlighting its textures. A minimalist background with blurred green foliage suggests a connection to nature and sustainability.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately in warm bowls.
Accompany with a simple side salad of seasonal greens dressed with a homemade vinaigrette from fermented fruit scraps.
instructions: Separate chicken skin from thighs. Pat skin dry. Cut chicken thighs into large, rustic chunks.

Heat a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add chicken skin, fat side down. Render slowly until crispy and golden brown. Remove skin, drain excess fat. Set skin aside to cool; crumble into shards later.

Increase heat to medium-high. Add 15ml olive oil to the pan. Sear chicken thigh chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) during final cooking.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine, if using. Stir until completely absorbed.
Stir in slow-roasted tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Begin adding hot chicken stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for liquid to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next ladleful. Continue for 15-18 minutes.
When rice is al dente and creamy, return seared chicken chunks to the pan. Stir gently to combine. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, ensuring chicken is heated through and cooked to temperature.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and Parmesan cheese, if using. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Let risotto rest for 2 minutes before serving.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste cooking. Chicken bones and vegetable scraps can be used to make the chicken stock.
Any leftover risotto can be repurposed into arancini.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Chicken with Potatoes and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Braised Chicken with Potatoes and Tomatoes is presented in a deep, rustic white ceramic bowl. A golden-brown, braised chicken thigh rests prominently, its skin slightly crisped. Around the chicken, quartered new potatoes, tender and imbued with flavor, are nestled within a rich, thick tomato-based sauce. The sauce, a deep reddish-orange, contains visible pieces of softened tomato, onion, and bell pepper, hinting at the smoky paprika. Freshly chopped vibrant green parsley is scattered generously over the dish, providing a bright contrast. The textures are hearty and rustic. The dish is placed on a simple, light wooden table. A folded linen napkin and a dark metal spoon are positioned beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and depth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large braising pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crisp, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pot. Sauté, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, deglaze the pot with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, and bay leaf. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Return the seared chicken thighs to the pot. Add the quartered potatoes. Ensure potatoes are mostly submerged in the liquid.
Cover the pot and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender.
Remove the bay leaf from the pot. Taste the stew and adjust seasoning as needed with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches a safe internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
For richer flavor, use bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Raspberry-Balsamic Reduction and Parmesan Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared duck breast is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. A bed of creamy, golden-yellow Parmesan polenta forms the base. Thick diagonal slices of perfectly cooked duck breast, displaying a crisp, deep golden-brown skin and tender pink interior, are arranged neatly atop the polenta. A glossy, rich deep red raspberry-balsamic reduction is generously drizzled over the duck and around the plate. The dish is garnished with a few small, vibrant green fresh thyme sprigs. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space. A white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the dish in a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Score duck skin in a crosshatch pattern. Do not cut into meat. Season duck generously with salt and pepper.
Place duck skin-side down in a cold, oven-safe pan. Cook over medium-low heat. Render fat for 10-15 minutes until skin is golden and crispy.
Flip duck. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Cook 6-8 minutes for desired doneness.
Remove duck from pan. Rest on a cutting board, skin-side up, for 10 minutes. Pour off excess fat, leaving about 15ml in the pan.
For the sauce: Add minced shallot to the pan. Sauté 1 minute. Deglaze with balsamic vinegar, scraping up browned bits.
Add raspberries, chicken stock, and honey. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes, until sauce reduces and thickens slightly.
Strain sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Discard solids.
Return strained sauce to low heat. Whisk in butter until melted and incorporated. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For the polenta: Bring 800ml water and 5ml salt to a boil in a medium saucepan.
Slowly whisk in polenta. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 15-20 minutes until thick and creamy.
Remove from heat. Stir in Parmesan cheese. Adjust seasoning.
To serve: Spoon polenta onto plates. Slice duck breast into thick diagonal pieces. Arrange duck on polenta. Drizzle generously with raspberry-balsamic reduction. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Tiramisu
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Classic Tiramisu is presented in a clear, round glass ramekin, showcasing its distinct, creamy layers. The top layer of smooth, pale mascarpone cream is generously dusted with a rich, dark brown cocoa powder, creating a soft, velvety finish.
