Delicate, thin shavings of dark chocolate are scattered artfully over the cocoa, adding a touch of elegance and contrasting texture. Through the clear glass, the coffee-soaked ladyfingers are visible as darker, distinct layers against the lighter cream. The Tiramisu sits centered on a clean, white porcelain saucer, providing ample negative space. A small, polished espresso spoon rests beside the ramekin on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed adjacent. The lighting is natural and even, creating a soft, inviting glow. The background is subtly blurred, hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere without distraction. The presentation is professional, clean, and balanced, highlighting the dessert's refined simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled, often accompanied by a small, strong espresso or a digestivo like Vin Santo.
Traditionally enjoyed as a dessert after a meal, especially in social settings.
instructions: Prepare a bain-marie. Combine egg yolks and granulated sugar in a heatproof bowl. Place bowl over simmering water. Whisk continuously until mixture is pale, thick, and reaches 70°C (158°F). Remove from heat. Continue whisking until mixture cools.
Gently fold mascarpone cheese and vanilla extract into the cooled egg yolk mixture until smooth.
In a separate chilled bowl, whip heavy cream to soft peaks.
Carefully fold whipped cream into the mascarpone mixture until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour cooled espresso into a shallow dish.
Quickly dip each ladyfinger into the espresso. Do not over-soak.
Arrange a single layer of soaked ladyfingers at the bottom of four individual serving glasses or ramekins.
Spoon a layer of mascarpone cream over the ladyfingers. Smooth the top.
Add a second layer of soaked ladyfingers.
Top with a final generous layer of mascarpone cream. Smooth the surface.
Cover each serving dish. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, to allow the tiramisu to set and flavors to meld.
Before serving, dust generously with unsweetened cocoa powder. Shave dark chocolate over the top for garnish.
notes: Ensure the egg yolk mixture is whisked sufficiently over heat to pasteurize and thicken.
Do not over-soak ladyfingers; a quick dip prevents a soggy texture.
Proper chilling time is crucial for the tiramisu to set and develop its full flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Ribs with Root Vegetable Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised beef short ribs is elegantly presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two thick, dark brown braised beef short rib chunks, fork-tender and glistening with rich sauce, are positioned centrally. They rest atop a creamy, pale yellow root vegetable puree, artfully swirled on the plate. The puree provides a smooth textural contrast. A dark, glossy red wine reduction sauce is generously spooned over the beef, creating an appealing sheen. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley adds a pop of color and freshness. The plate maintains moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and a hint of a restaurant background. Lighting is natural and even.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Season short ribs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove ribs and set aside.
Add diced onions, carrots, and celery to the Dutch oven. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Bring to a simmer and cook until reduced by half.
Return short ribs to the Dutch oven. Add beef broth, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer. Cover the Dutch oven tightly.
Transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
While ribs braise, prepare the puree. Place cubed potatoes and parsnips in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt.
Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain vegetables thoroughly. Return to the hot pot.
Add butter and warm heavy cream. Mash until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and white pepper. Keep warm.
Once ribs are tender, carefully remove them from the Dutch oven. Set aside.
Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids.
Skim excess fat from the liquid.
Bring the strained liquid to a simmer. Reduce until it thickens slightly into a sauce. Adjust seasoning.
To serve, place a generous portion of root vegetable puree on each plate.
Top with one or two braised short rib pieces.
Spoon reduced braising sauce over the ribs and puree.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or a small sprig of thyme.
notes: Braising liquid can be made ahead and refrigerated. Fat will solidify for easy removal.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Lamb Mincemeat with Corn & Pineapple Salsa and Garlic Yogurt
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a generous mound of spiced lamb mincemeat, centrally placed on a clean white porcelain plate. Over the rich, brown, crumbly mincemeat, a vibrant corn and pineapple salsa is spooned, showcasing small diced golden pineapple and bright yellow corn kernels, interspersed with finely minced red onion and fresh mint. A creamy, bright white garlic yogurt is artfully swirled around the base of the mincemeat, providing a smooth contrast. The entire dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh chopped parsley and additional mint leaves, adding a pop of green. The presentation is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by warm pita bread triangles and a neatly folded cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm pita bread
Fresh herb salad

ingredients.name: Garlic cloves
ingredients.quantity: 5 (4 minced for mincemeat, 1 minced for yogurt)

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion, 4 cloves minced garlic, and diced carrot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add lamb mincemeat to the pan. Break it apart and cook until browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Drain any excess fat. Stir in cumin, coriander, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook for 10-12 minutes, allowing liquid to reduce and flavors to meld. Season with salt and pepper.
For the salsa, combine corn kernels, small diced pineapple, very finely diced red onion, and chopped mint in a bowl. Add lime juice and a pinch of salt. Mix well.
For the garlic yogurt, combine Greek yogurt, 1 clove minced garlic, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt in a separate bowl. Stir until smooth.
To serve, spoon a generous mound of spiced lamb mincemeat onto each plate.
Top the mincemeat with a portion of the corn and pineapple salsa.
Drizzle the garlic yogurt around the base of the mincemeat and salsa.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and additional mint leaves.
notes: Adjust spice levels in the mincemeat to your preference.
Ensure fresh corn and pineapple are used for best flavor and texture in the salsa.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef and Root Vegetable Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Beef and Root Vegetable Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a light wooden table. A neat mound of fluffy white long-grain rice forms the base. Three substantial, dark brown braised beef chunks, each approximately 4 cm, are nestled beside the rice, showcasing their tender texture. Interspersed are vibrant orange carrot rounds, 2 cm thick, and bright yellow corn kernels, adding color. A rich, glossy, dark brown gravy generously coats the beef and vegetables, pooling elegantly around the rice. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley, providing a vibrant contrast. The composition is balanced, with appropriate negative space. A folded grey cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a modern bistro.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Prepare beef. Cut beef into 4 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Dredge beef. Lightly coat beef chunks in plain flour. Shake off excess.

Sear beef. Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Sauté aromatics. Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onion to the pot. Cook, stirring, until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Build sauce. Stir in 30 g tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Pour in 60 ml Worcestershire sauce and 100 ml beef stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Add liquids and beef. Pour in remaining 650 ml beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Return seared beef to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged in liquid.
Braise. Cover pot tightly. Transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 1 hour 45 minutes.

Add carrots. While beef braises, peel and cut carrots into 2 cm thick rounds or large dice. Add carrots to the pot. Return to oven. Continue braising for another 45 minutes, or until beef is very tender and carrots are cooked through. Total braising time: 2 hours 30 minutes.
Cook corn. During the last 10 minutes of braising, stir in 200 g corn kernels. Cook until heated through.
Cook rice. While stew finishes, prepare 300 g long-grain white rice according to package directions.

Rest and serve. Remove pot from oven. Let stew rest for 10 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Serve generous portions of braised beef and vegetables over a bed of cooked rice. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Allow braised beef to rest for 10 minutes off heat before serving for optimal tenderness.
Chuck roast or beef shin are excellent cuts for braising.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, charred chunks of succulent chicken submerged in a glossy, vibrant orange-red tomato gravy. The sauce has a thick, velvety texture with visible flecks of ground spices. The chicken chunks show dark, caramelized edges from the high-heat roasting. Plating is in a clean, white porcelain bowl set on a dark wooden table. A single portion is shown with a light swirl of heavy cream on top and a scattering of bright green chopped cilantro. To the side sits a stack of warm, charred garlic naan bread and a small bowl of steamed long-grain basmati rice. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the rich colors and creamy consistency of the sauce while maintaining professional negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or buttered roti
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Side of mint-yogurt raita and kachumber salad
Serve in a traditional hammered copper karahi
instructions: Combine yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp chili powder.
Toss chicken chunks in marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 220°C. Place chicken on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Roast chicken 15 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté onions until golden brown.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in remaining garam masala, turmeric, and chili powder. Toast for 30 seconds.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens and oil separates.
Stir in butter and heavy cream. Season with salt.
Add roasted chicken chunks to the sauce. Simmer 2 minutes to combine flavors.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Kashmiri chili powder provides color without excessive heat.
Ensure the chicken is well-charred for authentic smoky flavor.
Let the sauce simmer until the oil separates to ensure spices are fully cooked.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Braised Chicken with Tomato and Potato
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, clean white ceramic bowl, showcasing a rich, rust-red tomato sauce. Two generously sized, golden-brown braised chicken thighs are nestled in the sauce, tender and intact, not sliced. Surrounding the chicken are creamy, quartered waxy potatoes, softened from simmering, absorbing the sauce's color. Bright green flecks of fresh chopped parsley are sprinkled over the top, providing a vibrant contrast. Thin, fiery red chili slices are visible throughout, hinting at the dish's warmth. The textures are varied: the smooth, thick sauce, the yielding chicken, and the soft potatoes. A side of thick-cut, crusty rustic bread, with a slightly irregular shape and a golden crust, rests on a simple wooden board beside the bowl. The setting is a modern bistro table with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread for dipping into the sauce.
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides, about 4-5 minutes per side. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced chilies. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and hot sauce. Stir well.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Bring the sauce to a simmer.
Add quartered potatoes to the pot. Ensure potatoes are mostly submerged in sauce.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and potatoes are tender.
Uncover and simmer for an additional 5-10 minutes to slightly thicken the sauce, if desired.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve hot with slices of rustic bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Egg Noodles
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown seared chicken thigh is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, nestled amidst a generous portion of al dente egg noodles lightly coated in a rich, rustic tomato sauce. The vibrant sauce features tender, diced red and green bell peppers, sliced white onions, and quartered mushrooms, providing a burst of color and texture. Fresh basil leaves and finely chopped parsley are scattered over the dish, with a dusting of grated Parmesan cheese. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A cotton napkin, a small ceramic bowl of freshly grated Parmesan, a rustic bread basket with crusty Italian bread, and a glass of red wine complete the authentic Italian dining scene. Natural, even lighting illuminates the savory meal, highlighting its inviting colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a dry red wine, such as Chianti or Merlot.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until deeply golden-brown on both sides. Cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add sliced onion, diced red and green bell peppers, and quartered mushrooms to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until vegetables soften and begin to caramelize.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring the sauce to a simmer.

Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
While chicken simmers, cook egg noodles according to package instructions until al dente. Drain well.
Stir half of the fresh basil and parsley into the cacciatore sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve chicken cacciatore over egg noodles. Garnish with remaining fresh basil, parsley, and a generous sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: For best flavor, ensure chicken is deeply browned before adding vegetables.
The sauce can be made ahead and reheated; flavors often improve overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Beef and Chicken Macaroni Skillet
recipes.special_requests: Without an oven. you can add ingredients from yourself
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Creamy Beef and Chicken Macaroni Skillet is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features tender elbow macaroni mixed with browned, crumbled ground beef and small, cooked cubes of chicken breast. All components are coated in a rich, creamy, orange-hued sauce, with visible strands of melted cheddar cheese clinging to the macaroni. The texture is hearty and comforting. A light sprinkle of vibrant green chopped parsley adds a fresh contrast. The setting is a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, with warm, natural lighting. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a casually placed cloth napkin. The background is minimal, focusing on the homely, comforting meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad on the side.
Offer a bowl of dill pickle slices for a classic American accompaniment.
Enjoy as a family meal, served directly from the skillet or in individual bowls.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into small, 1.5 cm cubes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef and diced chicken to the skillet. Cook, breaking up meat with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beef broth and ketchup. Stir to combine.
Add uncooked macaroni to the skillet. Stir well to submerge macaroni.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover skillet.
Cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until macaroni is tender and most liquid is absorbed. If liquid is fully absorbed before macaroni is tender, add a small amount of hot water or broth.
Remove skillet from heat.
Stir in shredded cheddar cheese and mayonnaise until melted and creamy.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Adjust seasoning to your preference.
For extra creaminess, a splash of milk or cream can be added with the cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Gourmet Salami & Cheddar Melt with Cucumber Mayo
recipes.visual_description: A single, robust gourmet sandwich is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The sandwich is cut diagonally in half, revealing distinct layers: golden-brown, crispy sourdough bread, generously melted vibrant yellow cheddar cheese, and reddish-brown, slightly warmed salami slices. The bread edges are neatly toasted. Adjacent to the sandwich, a small, neat pile of thinly sliced cucumber rounds offers a fresh, green contrast. A small, elegant white ramekin holds a dollop of creamy, pale green cucumber mayonnaise. A few fresh dill sprigs are artfully scattered on the plate. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The setting features a light-colored wooden table surface, standard silver flatware (fork and knife) positioned beside the plate, and a neatly folded light grey cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a softly blurred, warm-toned bistro background, creating an inviting and approachable restaurant aesthetic.
instructions: Grate half the cucumber finely. Squeeze out excess water from grated cucumber. Thinly slice remaining cucumber into rounds.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, grated cucumber, chopped fresh dill, and lemon juice. Season with salt and black pepper. Stir well. Set aside.
Lay out 4 slices of sourdough bread. Top each slice with a layer of cheddar cheese.
Arrange salami slices over the cheese. Add another layer of cheddar cheese on top of the salami.
Place the remaining 4 slices of sourdough bread on top, forming 4 sandwiches.
Generously butter the outside of each sandwich with softened butter.
Heat a large non-stick pan or griddle over medium heat. Add olive oil.
Place sandwiches in the hot pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until bread is golden brown and cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove sandwiches from pan. Let rest for 1 minute.
Cut each sandwich diagonally in half.
Serve immediately with a side of sliced cucumber and a dollop of cucumber mayonnaise.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Rustic Tomato Sauce and Garlic Croutons
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single, generously portioned braised chicken thigh. The chicken, with its golden-brown seared skin, rests in a rich, thick rustic tomato sauce that gleams with deep red and orange hues. The sauce, dotted with softened pieces of diced onion and flecks of fresh green herbs, coats the chicken invitingly. Scattered around and partially on top of the chicken and sauce are golden-brown, irregular 2 cm cubes of crispy garlic croutons, providing a contrasting texture. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley adds a vibrant pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is inviting and hearty, with moderate negative space on the plate, reflecting a professional yet approachable casual dining style. The chicken is presented whole, not sliced. The scene is set on a simple light wooden table with a white cotton napkin and standard silver cutlery beside the plate, under soft natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of robust red wine.
Offer extra crusty bread on the side for dipping into the sauce.
Serve in deep, rustic ceramic bowls for a comforting presentation.

ingredients.name: Crusty bread, cut into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and beef stock. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45-50 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While chicken braises, prepare croutons. Melt butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add bread cubes.
Toast bread cubes, stirring frequently, until golden brown and crispy on all sides, about 8-10 minutes. Remove from heat.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf from the braise. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve braised chicken and sauce in individual bowls. Top with a generous handful of garlic croutons and chopped fresh parsley.
notes: For richer flavor, use bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs.
Adjust seasoning at the end to balance flavors.
Croutons should be added just before serving to maintain crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Paprika Chicken with Roasted Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single, seared chicken thigh, golden-brown and tender, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. It is nestled amongst a vibrant mix of thick-cut, roasted red, yellow, and orange bell pepper strips and caramelized onion rings, some edges subtly charred. A rich, reddish-brown paprika-infused sauce subtly coats the chicken and vegetables. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of bright green chopped flat-leaf parsley and a fresh lemon wedge positioned nearby. The overall composition is natural, uncrowded, with moderate negative space. It is presented on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded charcoal grey cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and textures against a subtly blurred modern bistro background.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Cut bell peppers into thick 2 cm strips. Slice onion into thick rings. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add sliced onion and bell peppers to the same pan. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.
Stir in minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Return chicken thighs to the pan. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and chicken to absorb sauce.
Chop fresh parsley coarsely.
Serve chicken and vegetables with the sauce. Garnish with fresh parsley and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Brined Chicken with Cultured Cream Sauce and Wilted Greens
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, light cream-colored ceramic plate. A generous, natural bed of vibrant green, lightly wilted kale and spinach forms the base. Centered atop the greens is a single, whole, golden-brown seared chicken thigh, its skin crisp and taut, showcasing the perfect sear. The chicken is unsliced, retaining its natural shape. A rich, off-white cultured cream sauce is artfully spooned around the chicken, subtly pooling on the plate. Specks of finely chopped fresh green chives and parsley are visible within the sauce, adding delicate color. The overall composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space on the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from above, highlighting the textures of the crispy chicken skin, the tender greens, and the smooth, creamy sauce. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood table and an undyed linen napkin.
instructions: Combine water, sea salt, sugar, smashed garlic, bay leaf, and peppercorns in a large bowl. Stir until salt and sugar dissolve. Submerge chicken thighs in brine. Cover and refrigerate for 2-4 hours. Discard brine after use.
Remove chicken from brine. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.
Pour off excess fat from skillet, leaving 1-2 tablespoons. Place skillet over medium heat. If using, add white wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in chicken stock and heavy cream. Add cultured garlic/onion scraps. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter, chives, and parsley. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a separate pan, or the same skillet after sauce is removed, add a splash of olive oil. Add salad greens. Cook quickly for 1-2 minutes until just wilted. Season with a pinch of salt.
Place a bed of wilted greens on each plate. Arrange one chicken thigh on top of the greens. Spoon generous amount of cream sauce over and around the chicken. Serve immediately.
notes: Save chicken bones to make homemade stock for future recipes, reducing food waste.
Utilize vegetable scraps (onion peels, garlic skins) to infuse the brining liquid or for a zero-waste vegetable broth.
Consider quick-fermenting garlic or onion scraps in a small jar with a brine solution for 3-5 days to create the 'cultured scraps' for the sauce, enhancing flavor and reducing waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Beef with Fermented Vegetables and Ajika
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-braised beef sits in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The beef is presented as two to three thick, irregular chunks, rich dark brown and fork-tender. A glossy, deep red-brown sauce generously coats the beef. Alongside, a vibrant pile of mixed fermented vegetables, such as bright green pickled green beans and pale yellow sour cabbage, adds contrasting texture and color. A small, rustic dollop of reddish-orange Ajika paste rests beside the beef. Freshly chopped green cilantro leaves are scattered sparingly over the dish. The bowl is on a light-colored, reclaimed wood table. A natural, undyed linen napkin is folded loosely. The background is clean and minimalist, with soft natural light highlighting the dish's earthy tones and textures. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the substantial portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm Shoti or Lavash bread.
Offer a side of fresh Matsoni (yogurt).

ingredients.name: Mixed fermented vegetables (e.g., pickled green beans, sour cabbage)
Homemade Ajika (from bell pepper/chili trimmings, walnuts, spices)

instructions: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Season beef chunks generously with salt and pepper. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add chopped onions and carrots to the pot. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in ground coriander, cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook 30 seconds.
Deglaze with red wine (if using). Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, and bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise 2.5-3 hours. Beef should be fork-tender.
While beef braises, prepare homemade Ajika using vegetable trimmings and walnuts. Or prepare your chosen fermented vegetables for serving.
Once beef is tender, remove bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve braised beef hot in deep bowls. Top with a generous spoonful of fermented vegetables and a dollop of Ajika. Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Utilize beef bones or trimmings to make homemade beef broth, reducing waste.
Use vegetable scraps (bell pepper cores, chili stems) to create the homemade Ajika.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Sausage, Salami & Cheddar Bread Bake
recipes.visual_description: A substantial, golden-brown portion of the Savory Sausage, Salami & Cheddar Bread Bake occupies the center of a clean white porcelain plate. The bake's surface is richly caramelized, showcasing visible melted cheddar and browned, irregular chunks of sausage. The interior texture is a blend of crisp edges and a soft, custardy crumb. Beside the bake, a vibrant mound of fresh cucumber salad is neatly arranged. The cucumbers are diced into precise 1 cm cubes, glistening lightly with dressing and flecked with bright green chopped parsley. The overall color palette is warm browns and golds from the bake, complemented by the refreshing greens and whites of the cucumber. The plating is balanced, allowing for appropriate negative space around the elements. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded, light grey cotton napkin is positioned to the left. Standard, polished silver flatware (fork and knife) are placed to the right. Lighting is soft, natural, and even, highlighting the textures without harsh shadows. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a relaxed, modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Cut bread into 2-3 cm cubes. Spread cubes on a baking sheet. Toast 10 minutes until light golden. Set aside.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add sausage, breaking it into small pieces. Cook until browned and no pink remains. Drain excess fat. Transfer cooked sausage to a large mixing bowl.
Add diced salami to the same pan. Cook until crisp. Add to the sausage in the mixing bowl.
Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté 5 minutes until soft. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Add cooked onion and garlic to the sausage mixture.
In a separate large bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, heavy cream, Dijon mustard, 5ml salt, and 2ml black pepper until well combined.
Add toasted bread cubes and grated cheddar cheese to the sausage mixture in the large mixing bowl. Toss gently to combine.

Transfer the mixture to a 20x30 cm baking dish. Pour the egg custard evenly over the bread mixture. Gently press down on the bread to ensure it absorbs the liquid. Let stand 20 minutes for optimal absorption.
Bake 35-40 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and puffed, and a knife inserted into the center comes out clean. If the top browns too quickly, cover loosely with foil.

While the bake cooks, prepare the cucumber salad. Peel cucumbers and dice them into 1 cm cubes. In a small bowl, combine diced cucumber, 30ml red wine vinegar, 2ml salt, 1ml black pepper, and 15g chopped fresh parsley. Toss gently.
Let the bread bake rest 5 minutes after baking. Cut into 4 equal portions. Serve warm with a generous spoon of fresh cucumber salad on top or alongside. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Spanish Chicken and Potato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Spanish Chicken and Potato Stew is presented in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl with a warm, earthy tone. The rich, reddish-brown stew features tender, braised chicken thigh chunks (approx. 4-5 cm) and creamy, golden-yellow potato pieces (approx. 3-4 cm, irregularly cut). Softened diced tomatoes and slivers of red bell pepper are visible within the robust, slightly thickened sauce, infused with smoked paprika and saffron. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a pop of green. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded beside it, along with a fork and spoon. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's comforting textures and deep colors. A small, rustic plate holds a slice of crusty bread nearby, ready for dipping. The overall composition is inviting and authentically Spanish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette complements the richness.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4-5 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes and cut into 3-4 cm irregular chunks.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Cut bell pepper into 2 cm pieces.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onion and bell pepper to pot. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, and saffron (if using). Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to pot. Add potato chunks and chicken broth. Ensure chicken is submerged.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir half into the stew.
Serve hot, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken Macaroni Skillet
recipes.special_requests: Without an oven. you can add ingredients from yourself
recipes.visual_description: The Creamy Chicken Macaroni Skillet is presented in a simple, well-used ceramic bowl with a slightly chipped rim, sitting on a warm, polished wooden dining table. The dish features a generous, natural portion of elbow macaroni coated in a rich, creamy, golden-orange cheddar cheese sauce. Interspersed throughout the macaroni are irregular chunks of pan-seared chicken, with a light golden-brown exterior and tender, white interior. The chicken pieces are varied in size, appearing as if roughly diced at home. A few flecks of diced, softened white onion are visible, contributing to the texture. The surface of the dish has a natural, slightly glossy sheen from the creamy sauce. A light sprinkle of vibrant green, roughly chopped fresh parsley provides a pop of color and freshness against the warm tones of the pasta and chicken. The overall impression is one of comforting, hearty home cooking. The plate is adequately filled, leaving some negative space around the edges. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen setting, with soft shadows. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a standard fork rest beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served directly from the skillet to individual bowls
Often accompanied by a simple green salad or crusty bread
instructions: Cook macaroni: Boil 2 litres of salted water in a large pot. Add macaroni. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Set aside.

Prepare chicken: Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Sauté aromatics: Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Make cheese sauce base: Sprinkle flour over onions and garlic. Stir for 1 minute to cook off raw flour taste. Gradually whisk in milk and chicken broth until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens slightly.

Finish sauce: Reduce heat to low. Add shredded cheddar cheese and mayonnaise. Stir until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth and creamy. Add mustard powder, salt, and black pepper. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Combine: Add cooked macaroni and cooked chicken to the skillet with the cheese sauce. Stir gently to coat all ingredients. Simmer for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until heated through.
Serve: Ladle into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This recipe can be easily adapted with different cheeses or by adding cooked vegetables like peas or broccoli florets.
Ensure chicken is fully cooked to 75°C for safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Potato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rustic beef and potato stew is presented in a deep, earthenware bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The stew features generous chunks of tender, dark brown beef, nestled among soft, golden-yellow potato cubes, vibrant orange carrot rounds, and earthy brown quartered mushrooms. A rich, thick reddish-brown gravy coats all ingredients, with visible flecks of dried herbs. A light scattering of fresh green chopped parsley brightens the top. The stew has a comforting, slightly irregular texture, reflecting home cooking. The bowl sits on a simple ceramic plate. A linen napkin and a sturdy spoon are casually placed beside it. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread.
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add chopped onion and carrots to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and flour. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually stir in beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Add diced tomatoes and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add potato cubes and quartered mushrooms. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 30-40 minutes, or until beef and potatoes are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chili Pork and Pineapple Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Chili Pork and Pineapple Rice Bowl is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Steamed jasmine rice forms the base, topped generously with savory, saucy pork chunks. The pork, cut into 2-3 cm cubes, is seared to a light golden brown, its surface glistening with the rich, dark sauce. Interspersed among the pork are thick slices of sautéed brown mushrooms and bright, diced pineapple pieces, about 1.5 cm, adding contrasting texture and color. Thinly sliced red chili rounds are scattered over, providing vibrant red accents. A sprinkle of fresh green onion slices and a few sesame seeds complete the dish. The overall presentation is comforting and inviting, reflecting a home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately in individual ceramic bowls.
Offer chopsticks for eating.
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice. Cook according to package directions. Set aside.
Combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, cornstarch, and chicken broth in a small bowl. Whisk until smooth. Set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Add diced pork. Sear pork until browned on all sides. Remove pork from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon vegetable oil to the skillet. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until tender, about 4-5 minutes.
Return seared pork to the skillet. Add diced pineapple and sliced red chili.
Pour the prepared sauce mixture over the pork and vegetables. Bring to a simmer.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and coats the ingredients, about 3-5 minutes.
Serve hot over cooked jasmine rice. Garnish with sliced green onions and sesame seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Pork and Broccoli Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant and aromatic Spicy Pork and Broccoli Stir-fry is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Thinly sliced, seared pork pieces are nestled among bright green, tender-crisp broccoli florets, earthy sliced cremini mushrooms, and vibrant green beans. All ingredients are coated in a glossy, rich red-orange sauce, highlighting the hot sauce and tomato paste base. The dish is artfully arranged with a moderate amount of negative space, allowing each component to be distinct. A sprinkle of thinly sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds garnishes the top, adding freshness and texture. The plate is placed on a simple wooden table surface. Alongside, a small white rice bowl filled with fluffy white rice and a pair of dark chopsticks complete the setting. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its fresh ingredients and inviting textures. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with steamed white rice
Offer chopsticks for dining
instructions: Slice pork loin thinly against the grain into bite-sized pieces. Season pork with a pinch of salt, pepper, and 1 teaspoon of cornstarch. Set aside.
Cut broccoli into small florets. Slice cremini mushrooms. Thinly slice the yellow onion. Mince garlic cloves and grate fresh ginger.
Trim green beans. Cut into 3cm pieces.

In a small bowl, whisk together tomato paste, hot sauce, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame oil. In a separate small cup, mix 1 tablespoon cornstarch with 2 tablespoons water to create a slurry. Add slurry to the sauce mixture and whisk well.
Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add pork to the hot wok in a single layer. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until browned and cooked through. Remove pork from the wok and set aside.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon vegetable oil to the wok. Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and sliced onion. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add broccoli florets, sliced mushrooms, and green beans to the wok. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Return cooked pork to the wok. Pour the prepared sauce mixture over the ingredients. Stir constantly for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens and evenly coats all ingredients.
Remove from heat. Garnish with thinly sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds.
Serve immediately over steamed white rice.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to personal spice preference.
Ensure wok is very hot for proper stir-frying technique.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Tenderloin with Dark Chocolate Apple Demi-Glace and Wild Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared pork tenderloin medallions and wild rice pilaf is elegantly arranged on a clean, white round porcelain plate. The pork, cooked medium-rare, is sliced into thick, juicy chunks with a golden-brown crust. Three substantial pork pieces are grouped naturally. Beside them, a mound of multi-colored wild rice pilaf sits, fluffy and textured. A rich, glossy dark chocolate apple demi-glace is artfully drizzled over the pork and plate, its deep brown contrasting the pink pork. Bright green fresh parsley leaves are scattered for accent. Thin, crisp apple slices are placed near the pork for a pop of color. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting creates an inviting restaurant ambiance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.

Rinse wild rice blend. In a medium saucepan, combine rice, 500ml stock, bay leaf, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 40-45 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Remove bay leaf. Fluff with a fork.
Pat pork tenderloins dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear tenderloins on all sides until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C. Remove from oven. Tent with foil. Let rest 10 minutes.

While pork rests, prepare sauce. Discard excess fat from skillet, leaving about 15ml. Add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter to skillet. Add diced shallots. Sauté 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and 1 sprig thyme. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce wine by half, about 3 minutes.
Add remaining 200ml stock and balsamic vinegar. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer 5-7 minutes, until sauce slightly thickens.
Peel and dice one apple into small cubes. Add to sauce. Simmer 3 minutes until slightly tender.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in chopped dark chocolate until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Remove thyme sprig.
Slice rested pork tenderloins into thick medallions, about 2-3 cm thick.

Plate wild rice pilaf onto serving plates. Arrange pork medallions beside rice. Spoon dark chocolate apple demi-glace over pork and around plate. Garnish with fresh parsley leaves and thin apple slices from the second apple.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken & Macaroni Skillet
recipes.special_requests: Without an oven. you can add ingredients from yourself
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Creamy Chicken & Macaroni Skillet fills a simple, deep ceramic bowl. Diced, golden-brown chicken pieces are nestled among the creamy elbow macaroni, coated in a rich, velvety sauce. Melted shredded cheddar cheese creates visible streaks of warm orange and yellow, blending with the off-white macaroni and sauce. A sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley adds a vibrant color contrast. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a plain metal fork and a casually folded cloth napkin. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures of the home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Cook macaroni according to package directions. Drain. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add diced chicken. Cook 5-7 minutes until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to skillet. Cook 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and milk. Bring to a simmer.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet.
Stir in shredded cheese and mayonnaise until melted and smooth.
Add cooked macaroni to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Tomato and Red Wine
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-braised beef with tomato and red wine is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Three substantial, dark brown beef chunks, approximately 5 cm each, are nestled amidst a rich, deep red tomato sauce. The sauce, thick and glossy, clings to the beef, showcasing hints of tender diced vegetables like carrots and celery. A vibrant green sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley garnishes the top. The beef exhibits a tender, fall-apart texture. The dish is served alongside a generous swirl of golden, creamy polenta. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin, and natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy polenta or wide pasta like pappardelle or tagliatelle.
Offer grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese at the table.
Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 5 cm chunks
Polenta or pappardelle pasta, for serving

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook until wine is reduced by half.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Stir to combine.
Bring mixture to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot over creamy polenta or pappardelle pasta. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Oyster & Kimchi Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Smoked Oyster & Kimchi Pasta is centered on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate, leaving generous white space. The linguine is loosely piled, showing its natural flow and coated in a vibrant reddish-orange sauce. Small, bright red kimchi pieces are visible throughout the pasta. Whole smoked oysters, deep amber in color, are strategically placed on top and nestled within the pasta strands. A sparse scattering of finely chopped green scallion tops provides a fresh accent. The setting features a light, textured bamboo table surface. Beside the plate rests a simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige. A small, dark grey ceramic bowl holds a pair of light wood chopsticks, subtly reinforcing the Korean aesthetic. Soft, natural daylight illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and natural colors of the ingredients against a clean, minimalist background with a blurred hint of green foliage.

ingredients.name: Scallions, sliced (white and green parts separated)

instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 200ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, mince garlic. Slice kimchi into small pieces. Slice scallions, separating white and green parts.
Heat 15ml neutral oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add white parts of scallions and minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced kimchi to the pan. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Pour in chicken stock and soy sauce. Add gochugaru if using. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes.
Add drained smoked oysters to the pan. Stir gently to combine.
Add cooked pasta to the pan. Toss to coat pasta evenly with the sauce.
Gradually add reserved pasta water, 50ml at a time, to achieve desired sauce consistency. The sauce should lightly coat the pasta.
Stir in sesame oil and green parts of scallions. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Umami Chocolate Potato Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, clean slice of the Umami Chocolate Potato Cake is elegantly presented on a pristine white round porcelain dessert plate. The slice reveals distinct layers: a dark, moist chocolate cake crumb, a subtle reddish layer of sweet tomato compote, and a rich, dark chocolate ganache frosting. The cake possesses a slightly dense, tender texture. A very light dusting of unsweetened cocoa powder adorns the plate beside the slice. A few small, whole candied cherry tomatoes, vibrant red, are strategically placed on top of the slice or beside it, providing a pop of color. The slice is positioned slightly off-center on the plate, maintaining moderate negative space. The ganache is smooth and evenly applied. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded, off-white cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. A simple, elegant dessert fork is placed to the right. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting from the side creates soft shadows, adding depth without harshness.

ingredients.name: Russet potato, cooked and very finely mashed (no lumps)

instructions: Peel and boil potato until very tender. Mash thoroughly until completely smooth. Set aside to cool.

In a small saucepan, combine beef consommé, 50g granulated sugar, star anise, cinnamon stick, and ground cloves. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently until liquid reduces by half and becomes syrupy. Strain and discard spices. Let cool completely.

In a small saucepan, combine halved cherry tomatoes, 30g granulated sugar, balsamic vinegar, and a pinch of salt. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally. Cook until tomatoes break down and mixture thickens into a jam-like consistency. Cool completely.
Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 18cm round cake pan.
Melt 150g dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl over a double boiler or in microwave. Stir until smooth.
In a large bowl, cream 100g softened butter and 180g granulated sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs one at a time.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, 2g salt, and porcini mushroom powder.

Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, alternating with milk. Begin and end with dry. Mix until just combined. Fold in cooled mashed potato and melted chocolate until no streaks remain. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into prepared pan. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. Let cool in pan for 10 minutes, then invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.

For Chocolate Ganache Frosting: In a medium saucepan, heat heavy cream until simmering. Remove from heat. Add 200g chopped dark chocolate and 20g unsalted butter. Let sit for 5 minutes, then whisk until smooth and glossy. Refrigerate for 30-45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick enough to spread.
Once cake is completely cool, slice horizontally into two even layers. Place one layer on a serving plate. Brush generously with cooled beef consommé syrup.
Spread an even layer of sweet tomato compote over the first cake layer. Top with half of the chocolate ganache.
Place the second cake layer on top. Brush with remaining beef consommé syrup. Frost the top and sides of the cake with the remaining ganache.
Refrigerate cake for at least 1 hour to set ganache. Slice and serve.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Chicken with Chocolate-Pineapple Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Smoky Chicken with Chocolate-Pineapple Sauce is presented on a rustic, round ceramic plate with earthy tones. Two bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, seared to a deep golden-brown, are nestled centrally in a rich, dark reddish-brown sauce. The sauce is thick and glossy, with visible flecks of vibrant yellow pineapple chunks and tiny green pieces of minced jalapeno and cilantro. The chicken skin is crisp, contrasting with the tender meat submerged in the sauce. The plate is adequately filled, leaving some negative space around the edges. The dish sits on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a stack of warm corn tortillas wrapped in a cloth napkin. A simple, hand-thrown ceramic bowl of fluffy white rice and a small, rustic ceramic bowl of salsa verde complete the homely setting. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, casting soft shadows. A casual, lived-in atmosphere is evident.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping the sauce.
Serve alongside fluffy white rice.
Offer a side of simple salsa verde or pickled red onions.

ingredients.name: Dark chocolate (70% cacao or higher), chopped

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes.
Flip chicken. Sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and minced jalapeno. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in ground cumin, dried oregano, and cocoa powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Add chopped dark chocolate and pineapple chunks. Stir until chocolate melts and sauce thickens slightly.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce.
Bring sauce to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove cover. Increase heat slightly. Simmer for 5-10 minutes more to thicken sauce if desired.
Stir in fresh lime juice.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped cilantro.
notes: Adjust jalapeno quantity based on desired heat level. For less heat, remove more seeds and membranes.
For a richer sauce, use chicken stock instead of broth.
traditional_techniques: Browning meat before simmering to build flavor (searing)
Building a layered sauce base with aromatics and spices

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato & Rice Salad with Shredded Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The Tomato & Rice Salad is presented generously mounded on a rustic, everyday ceramic plate. Diced red tomatoes, white fluffy rice, and crisp, diced cucumber are visibly mixed, creating a vibrant, fresh appearance. Small, tender pieces of shredded cooked chicken breast are interspersed throughout the salad, not dominating the vegetables. Finely chopped fresh parsley and mint add specks of bright green, and a light lemon-olive oil dressing coats the ingredients, giving them a subtle sheen. The salad is arranged naturally, with components touching and overlapping, as if served at a family meal. The plate rests on a well-used wooden kitchen table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light, with a casually folded cloth napkin nearby, enhancing the homely, unpretentious atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread.
instructions: Ensure chicken breast is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Shred the cooked chicken breast.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooled cooked rice, diced tomatoes, diced cucumber, and finely diced red onion.
Add the shredded cooked chicken breast to the bowl.
Stir in the chopped fresh parsley and chopped fresh mint.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, fresh lemon juice, salt, and black pepper to create the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients.
Toss gently until all ingredients are well combined and coated with the dressing.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Serve immediately or chill for later.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken Macaroni Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Cheesy Chicken Macaroni Bake is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The dish features a creamy, rich blend of elbow macaroni and tender, shredded chicken, coated in a savory, reddish-orange tomato and cheese sauce. Crowning the macaroni is a golden-brown, visibly crispy layer of baked corn tortilla pieces and toasted breadcrumbs, with streaks of melted, bubbly yellow and white cheese. A scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped cilantro garnishes the top, providing a fresh counterpoint to the warm, comforting colors of the bake. The chicken is presented as tender, shredded chunks, not fanned. The plate is set on a light wooden surface, accompanied by a simple white napkin and standard flatware, under soft, natural light, creating an inviting casual dining scene.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken breasts to the pot. Sear 3-4 minutes per side until lightly browned.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook chicken 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pot. Shred chicken using two forks. Set aside.
Stir cooked macaroni into the sauce in the pot. Add shredded Cheddar and Mozzarella. Stir until cheese melts and sauce thickens slightly.
Fold in shredded chicken. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer macaroni mixture to a 23x33 cm baking dish if not using an oven-safe pot.
Cut tortillas into 2 cm strips or tear into pieces. Toss with breadcrumbs and a drizzle of olive oil.
Scatter tortilla-breadcrumb mixture evenly over the macaroni.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until topping is golden brown and bubbly.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Chicken Parmesan with Spaghetti
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Classic Chicken Parmesan is presented on a cream-colored, slightly imperfect ceramic plate. A golden-brown, pan-fried chicken breast, pounded thin and left whole, is generously topped with bubbling, melted mozzarella cheese and a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce. The crispy breading on the chicken is clearly visible. Beside the chicken, a neat, natural swirl of al dente spaghetti, lightly coated in the same savory tomato sauce, rests. A few torn fresh basil leaves are scattered over the dish for a pop of green. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate. In the background, a rustic bread basket with slices of crusty Italian bread, a small bowl of grated Parmesan, and a bottle of olive oil create a homely, lived-in atmosphere. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and colors of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Fresh mozzarella cheese, sliced or shredded

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Pound chicken breasts to even thickness (about 1.5 cm). Season with salt and pepper.
Set up breading station: one plate with flour, one shallow bowl with beaten eggs, one plate with breadcrumbs mixed with 25g Parmesan cheese.
Dredge each chicken breast in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Pan-fry chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Do not cook through.
Transfer chicken to a baking sheet if skillet is not oven-safe.
For the sauce: In the same skillet (or a saucepan), add remaining 30ml olive oil. Sauté diced onion over medium heat until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
While sauce simmers, cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Spoon a generous amount of tomato sauce over each chicken breast. Top with sliced or shredded mozzarella cheese.
Bake in preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and cheese is melted and bubbly.
Serve chicken immediately alongside the cooked spaghetti. Spoon extra sauce over the pasta. Garnish with fresh basil or remaining Parmesan cheese, if desired.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Pounding the chicken ensures even cooking and tenderness.
Adjust sauce thickness by simmering longer for a thicker consistency or adding a splash of water for a thinner one.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Sausage and Tomato Macaroni Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A generous, comforting portion of Hearty Sausage and Tomato Macaroni fills a deep, everyday ceramic bowl. The crumbled, browned sausage pieces are interspersed with tender, plump macaroni pasta and bright red diced tomatoes. Diced onion pieces are visible throughout. A rich, thick tomato-based sauce coats all ingredients, showcasing a rustic, home-cooked texture. The dish has warm, inviting colors of red, brown, and creamy white. A light sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese melts slightly on top, and a scattering of fresh green chopped parsley adds a pop of vibrant color. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple cloth napkin nearby. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, evoking a relaxed family meal.
instructions: Remove sausage from casings. Crumble into a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook until browned, breaking it apart with a spoon. Drain excess fat.
Add olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté onion for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, water, and dried oregano. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Add macaroni pasta. Stir well. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer for 10-12 minutes, or until macaroni is tender, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. Add more water if needed.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Ensure internal temperature of sausage reaches 75°C (167°F).
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with grated Parmesan cheese and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Roasted Tomatoes and Red Wine Jus
recipes.visual_description: Two thick-cut, pan-seared beef tenderloin medallions, cooked to a perfect medium-rare, are positioned slightly offset on a clean white round plate. Each medallion boasts a dark, savory crust. Alongside, a cluster of vibrant roasted cherry tomatoes, some gently burst, adds a pop of color and sweetness. Earthy sautéed mixed mushrooms, including cremini and shiitake, are nestled nearby, showcasing their varied textures. A rich, glossy red wine jus is elegantly spooned around the beef, creating a deep, reflective pool. The dish is garnished with a fresh sprig of thyme, providing a touch of green. The overall presentation is refined yet approachable, with thoughtful negative space. It rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white linen napkin and standard European flatware, under soft, natural light.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast tomatoes for 15-20 minutes, until softened and slightly burst. Set aside.
Cut beef tenderloin into 4 equal thick-cut medallions. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, achieving a deep brown crust. Adjust time for desired doneness.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven for 5-7 minutes to finish cooking, if needed. Use a meat thermometer to check internal temperature if desired.
Remove beef from skillet. Place on a cutting board, tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes.
While beef rests, slice mushrooms. Mince shallots and garlic.
Drain excess fat from skillet, leaving 1 tablespoon. Add 20 grams butter to skillet. Reduce heat to medium.
Add sliced mushrooms to skillet. Sauté until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced shallots and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour red wine into skillet. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Add beef broth and 2 sprigs of thyme. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook until sauce thickens slightly, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove thyme sprigs. Whisk in remaining 40 grams cold butter until melted and glossy. Season jus with salt and pepper to taste.
To serve, place 1 beef medallion on each plate. Arrange roasted tomatoes and sautéed mushrooms alongside. Spoon red wine jus generously over and around the beef. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto al Pomodoro e Origano
recipes.visual_description: The Risotto al Pomodoro e Origano is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing its luscious, creamy texture. The risotto displays a vibrant, inviting red-orange hue from cooked tomatoes, with visible, distinct grains of Arborio rice. Finely diced, cooked onion and garlic are integrated throughout. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh, bright green oregano leaves, providing fragrant contrast. A few halved, ripe red cherry tomatoes add a burst of fresh color and acidity. Finely grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the surface. A delicate swirl of golden extra virgin olive oil glistens on top. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by silver flatware and a folded grey cotton napkin, under natural, soft light, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 80 g (freshly grated, plus extra for garnish)

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add finely diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Toast the rice for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent and center is opaque.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Add crushed tomatoes and dried oregano. Stir well to combine.
Begin adding hot vegetable stock, one ladleful (about 120 ml) at a time. Stir constantly, allowing each addition to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next.
Continue adding stock and stirring for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is creamy and al dente. The risotto should be fluid, not stiff.
Remove from heat. Stir in cold butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously (mantecatura) for 1-2 minutes until risotto is creamy and emulsified.
Stir in chopped fresh oregano. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately in warm bowls. Garnish with halved cherry tomatoes, extra fresh oregano leaves, and a sprinkle of Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure vegetable stock is hot before adding to maintain risotto temperature.
Stirring consistently is key for a creamy risotto texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Russian Beef and Carrot Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of hearty Russian Beef and Carrot Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The stew features tender, dark brown beef chunks (approximately 3-4 cm) nestled among vibrant orange carrot slices (2 cm thick) and soft, pale yellow potato cubes (3 cm). The rich, thick, reddish-brown gravy coats all ingredients, with a slight sheen. A small dollop of creamy white smetana (sour cream) rests on top, slightly melting into the stew. Freshly chopped bright green dill is scattered generously over the smetana and stew, adding a pop of color. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, with a simple, slightly rumpled linen napkin beside it. A traditional Russian wooden spoon rests in the bowl. Natural, soft, warm kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the homely, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of smetana (sour cream) on top.
Garnish with fresh chopped dill or parsley.
Serve with dark rye bread (Borodinsky bread) for dipping.
Serve with pickled vegetables (e.g., pickled cucumbers or cabbage) on the side.
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Toss beef with flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Return beef to the pot. Pour in beef broth. Add bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5 hours.
Add carrots and potatoes to the pot. Stir well.
Cover and continue to simmer for another 45-60 minutes, or until beef and vegetables are very tender.
Remove bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot.
notes: Browning the beef thoroughly adds deep flavor to the stew.
Adjust the consistency of the stew by simmering longer for a thicker sauce, or adding a little more broth if too thick.

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet Chicken with Creamy Corn and Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown seared chicken breast half is the centerpiece, nestled within a creamy, vibrant sauce. The sauce is generously laden with bright red halved cherry tomatoes, plump golden corn kernels, and tender, earthy sliced cremini mushrooms. All ingredients are naturally arranged on a simple, round, cream-colored ceramic plate, with the rich sauce pooling invitingly around the chicken. A scattering of fresh green chopped parsley adds a final touch of color and freshness. The plate rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, subtly showcasing its natural grain. Beside the plate, a casually folded plain white cloth napkin and a simple silver fork and knife are placed. The scene is bathed in warm, inviting light, typical of a cozy family kitchen, highlighting the comforting, homely appeal of the dish. The portion is modest and satisfying, reflecting a typical home-cooked meal.
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add butter to the skillet. Sauté diced onion for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Stir in halved cherry tomatoes and corn kernels. Cook for 3-4 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, reducing liquid slightly.
Stir in heavy cream. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Simmer for 2-3 minutes to heat through.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives, if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Vietnamese Caramelized Pork with Green Beans (Thịt Kho Đậu Que)
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of Vietnamese Caramelized Pork with Green Beans (Thịt Kho Đậu Que) is presented in a modest, deep ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden kitchen table. The tender, 3-4 cm cubed pork pieces, deeply browned and coated in a glossy, dark amber caramel sauce, are nestled alongside vibrant green beans, cooked tender-crisp. A small, separate white ceramic bowl holds a mound of fluffy white jasmine rice, ready for accompaniment. Fresh, bright green coriander leaves are scattered over the pork and beans, adding a pop of color and freshness. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests casually beside the bowls.
