Mince garlic cloves. Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add canned diced tomatoes to the pan. Bring to a simmer. Add roasted bell peppers and onion. Stir well. Simmer for 5 minutes. Season the sauce with salt and black pepper.

Pat cod fillets dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and black pepper. Heat a separate large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add a small amount of olive oil. Once hot, place cod fillets skin-side down (if applicable). Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden. Flip carefully. Sear for another 3-4 minutes. Cook until internal temperature reaches 63°C and fish is opaque and flakes easily.

Add drained pasta to the sauté pan with the sauce. Add reserved pasta cooking water or vegetable broth. Toss to coat pasta evenly. Tear fresh basil leaves. Add most basil and chopped parsley to the pasta. Toss gently.
Portion pasta into individual bowls. Top each serving with a seared cod fillet. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and a drizzle of olive oil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Onion, Chickpea and Spinach Salad with Lemon-Herb Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate, showcasing a generous individual portion on a well-used wooden dining table. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene. A bed of fresh, vibrant baby spinach leaves forms the base. Scattered throughout are deeply golden-brown, thinly sliced caramelized onions, providing soft texture and rich color. Creamy, whole chickpeas and bright red halved cherry tomatoes are interspersed, adding contrasting shapes and hues. Small, evenly diced pieces of cooked chicken are mixed in, visible but not dominating the abundant vegetables. The salad is lightly coated in a glistening lemon-herb vinaigrette, enhancing natural colors. A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley garnishes the top. A casually placed cloth napkin and simple flatware complete the homely setting.
instructions: Thinly slice onions. Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium-low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 30-40 minutes until deeply golden brown and caramelized. Set aside to cool.
Dice cooked chicken breast into small, even pieces. Ensure internal temperature reached 75°C if cooking from raw.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 45ml olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, honey, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
In a large salad bowl, combine cooled caramelized onions, diced chicken, drained chickpeas, halved cherry tomatoes, and baby spinach.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Sprinkle with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Veal with Paprika Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Braised Veal with Paprika Vegetables is presented on a clean white porcelain wide-rimmed plate. The tender, rich brown veal chunks are centered, generously coated in a vibrant reddish-orange paprika-infused sauce. Surrounding the veal are artfully arranged, slightly caramelized roasted cauliflower florets and colorful bell pepper chunks (red, yellow, orange), showcasing their distinct shapes and textures. A few fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space on the plate, allowing each component to be distinct yet harmonious. The overall presentation is clean and inviting. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a standard set of polished flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a side of simple boiled potatoes or egg noodles.

ingredients.name: Cauliflower
ingredients.quantity: 1 medium head (approx. 600 g), cut into medium florets

ingredients.name: Bell peppers
ingredients.quantity: 2 (red, yellow, or orange), cut into 2 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: 1/4 cup, roughly chopped, plus extra leaves for garnish

instructions: Pat veal cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper. Dredge lightly in flour.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear veal in batches until browned on all sides. Remove veal from pot.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic and paprika. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Return veal to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise 1.5-2 hours, or until veal is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Toss cauliflower florets and bell pepper chunks with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables 20-25 minutes, or until tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.
Stir chopped basil into the braised veal stew. Adjust seasoning.
Serve braised veal and sauce over roasted vegetables. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure veal is browned well for deep flavor.
Do not burn the paprika; it cooks quickly.
Adjust braising time based on veal tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Turkey & Corn Skillet
recipes.special_requests: low calorie, low carbs, high protein
recipes.visual_description: A modest, comforting single portion of Turkey & Corn Skillet is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain and minor imperfections. The dish features a hearty mix of browned, crumbly ground turkey, vibrant yellow corn kernels, and colorful diced vegetables including bright red and yellow bell peppers and green zucchini. All components are naturally mixed and piled, showing their tender-crisp textures. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green cilantro sits atop the dish, providing a fresh contrast. A standard silver fork and knife are placed casually beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy lighting, evoking a relaxed, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing on the comforting meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the skillet or individual plates
Pair with a simple green salad
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add ground turkey. Break it apart. Cook until browned, about 7-8 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, diced red bell pepper, and diced yellow bell pepper. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add diced zucchini and corn kernels to the skillet. Cook for another 3-4 minutes.
Stir in chili powder, cumin, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and cook for 5-7 minutes, until vegetables are tender-crisp and liquid is mostly absorbed.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Remove from heat. Serve immediately, garnished with fresh cilantro.
notes: Adjust chili powder and cumin to preferred spice level

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken with Crispy Smashed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, substantial portion of Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, cooked whole, boasts a rich, crispy golden-brown skin, highlighting its robust texture. Surrounding the chicken are several irregularly shaped, crispy smashed potatoes, their exteriors golden and textured, revealing fluffy white interiors. Artfully placed beside and partially over the chicken are tender, deep amber caramelized onion slices. Fresh green sprigs of rosemary and thyme are nestled alongside the chicken, with bright green chopped parsley scattered over the dish. A vibrant yellow lemon wedge rests on the plate's edge. The dish is set on a simple light wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, illuminated by natural, even lighting from above, creating a modern bistro ambiance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Place boiled potatoes on a baking sheet. Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Gently smash each potato with a fork or potato masher until flattened but still holding together.
Roast smashed potatoes for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy.

While potatoes roast, thinly slice onions. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 25-30 minutes until deep golden brown and caramelized. Set aside.
Pat chicken thighs very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Add rosemary sprigs, thyme sprigs, and peeled garlic cloves to the skillet.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest 5 minutes.

Discard herbs and garlic from skillet. Deglaze skillet with chicken broth over medium heat, scraping up browned bits. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced. Squeeze in juice from half a lemon.
To serve: Place a chicken thigh on each plate. Arrange crispy smashed potatoes beside it. Spoon caramelized onions over or beside the chicken. Garnish with fresh parsley and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Smoked Paprika Skillet with Beef and Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a pristine, matte white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a light wooden table in a modern bistro setting. A single portion of the Rustic Smoked Paprika Skillet features generous pan-seared beef and chicken chunks, displaying a golden-brown crust. They are artfully arranged with rustic wedges of golden-brown, crispy Yukon Gold potatoes and vibrant, tender-crisp thick strips of red and yellow bell peppers. The ensemble is lightly coated in a rich, reddish-brown paprika-infused sauce. A generous sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley adds a fresh contrast. The plating is clean, professional, and organized, with appropriate negative space. A white cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the food, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere. All elements are arranged organically, avoiding geometric shapes.
instructions: Pat beef and chicken chunks dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 30 ml of olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add beef chunks to the hot skillet in a single layer. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until well-browned. Remove beef and set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml of olive oil to the skillet. Add chicken chunks. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken and set aside with beef.
Add potato wedges to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until edges are golden and slightly tender.
Add diced onion and bell pepper strips to the skillet with potatoes. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring, until vegetables soften slightly.
Stir in minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Return seared beef and chicken to the skillet. Stir to combine with the potatoes and vegetables.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer for 5-7 minutes, or until beef is cooked to desired doneness and flavors meld.
Remove from heat. Let rest for 2 minutes before serving.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti al Pomodoro e Basilico Arrosto
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, rustic-elegant dish presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The spaghetti is twirled into a neat, moderate mound, glistening with olive oil and the light, emulsified sauce from the roasted tomatoes. Scattered throughout are the jewel-toned, burst cherry tomatoes, some still plump, others slightly collapsed. Thinly sliced, golden-brown roasted garlic cloves are interspersed. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are generously tossed in, with a few whole leaves placed on top as a garnish. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano rests on the pasta. The colors are warm and inviting: deep reds, bright greens, golden pasta. The plate is set on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin, fork, and spoon. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Offer extra Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Pair with a light red wine or sparkling water.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Place in a large roasting dish.
Add sliced garlic, 60ml olive oil, red pepper flakes (if using), salt, and pepper to tomatoes. Toss to coat.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tomatoes burst and soften.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Add spaghetti. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Before draining, reserve 250ml pasta water.
Drain spaghetti. Transfer to the roasting dish with tomatoes.
Add remaining 20ml olive oil and most of the basil leaves (reserving some for garnish).
Toss vigorously, adding reserved pasta water gradually to create a light sauce.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve immediately.
notes: Using good quality extra virgin olive oil is crucial for flavor.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Mushrooms and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two golden-brown, pan-seared bone-in chicken thighs placed centrally on a white porcelain plate. The chicken is surrounded by a rustic sauce of quartered brown mushrooms and softened cherry tomato halves. Beside the chicken, four roasted baby potato halves show crisp, browned edges. Three vibrant green blanched asparagus spears are laid parallel to the potatoes. A light dusting of finely grated parmesan cheese covers the vegetables. The plate has significant white space, emphasizing a clean bistro presentation. The setting is a dark wood table with a folded white cotton napkin and a stainless steel fork and knife. Natural side lighting highlights the textures of the crispy chicken skin and the glossy sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of light-bodied red wine like Chianti
Provide crusty bread to mop up the tomato and mushroom juices
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss halved potatoes with 15ml olive oil and salt.
Roast potatoes on a tray for 25 minutes until golden.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until crispy.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes. Remove chicken from pan.
Sauté diced onion and smashed garlic in the same pan for 3 minutes.
Add quartered mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes until browned.
Stir in halved tomatoes and chicken stock.
Return chicken to the pan and simmer for 10 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Boil asparagus in salted water for 2 minutes then drain.
Plate one whole chicken thigh per person and spoon sauce over the meat.
Arrange potatoes and asparagus on the side and top with grated parmesan.
notes: Use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken hits 75°C
Do not crowd the pan when searing chicken to ensure a crispy skin

recipes.recipe_name: Apple & Sweet Wine Crumble with Sabayon
recipes.visual_description: A single, warm Apple & Sweet Wine Crumble is presented in a rustic, round, light brown ceramic ramekin. The golden-brown crumble topping, with its uneven, coarse texture, covers the surface, showing hints of the tender, slightly collapsed baked apple chunks underneath at the edges. A light, airy dollop of pale yellow sweet wine sabayon rests gently on one side of the crumble. The ramekin sits on a simple, well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain. Beside the ramekin is a small, plain white ceramic plate, ready for serving, and a vintage silver spoon. The scene is bathed in warm, soft kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. The portion is generous and comforting, inviting immediate enjoyment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served warm, often with cream or custard. Here, a sweet wine sabayon accompanies it.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (fan 160°C).
Peel, core, and dice apples into 2cm cubes. Place in a saucepan.
Add 50g caster sugar, lemon juice, lemon zest, sweet wine, and cinnamon (if using) to apples.
Cook over medium heat for 8-10 minutes. Apples should soften slightly but retain shape. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine 150g flour and 50g brown sugar.
Add 100g cold cubed butter. Rub butter into flour mixture with fingertips until coarse crumbs form.
Divide cooked apple mixture among 4 individual oven-safe ramekins or a 20cm baking dish.
Sprinkle crumble topping evenly over apples.
Bake for 25-30 minutes. Crumble topping should be golden brown and apples bubbling.
Prepare Sweet Wine Sabayon: In a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water, combine 2 egg whites, 20g caster sugar, and 2 tablespoons of the sweet wine.
Whisk continuously until mixture is pale, thick, and foamy (about 5-7 minutes).
Serve warm crumble with a spoonful of sweet wine sabayon. Offer milk or cream alongside, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is a warm, pale yellow hue, studded with tender, golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2cm) and sautéed earthy brown mushroom slices. Finely diced onion pieces are visible throughout the creamy rice. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the top, alongside delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese. The dish has a natural, organic arrangement, showcasing its rich texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with classic silver Italian flatware (fork and spoon) placed beside it, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same pot.
Sauté finely diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, ensuring all grains are coated.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add one ladleful (about 250ml) of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly and wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is creamy and al dente, stir in cooked chicken.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra shaved Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Lamb and Mushroom Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: The Lamb and Mushroom Ragu with Pappardelle is presented on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a rich, inviting composition. The wide, flat ribbons of al dente pappardelle pasta are generously coated in a deep, glossy, reddish-brown ragu. Tender, irregular chunks of slow-cooked lamb, approximately 3-4 cm, are visible throughout the sauce, their natural shape retained. Interspersed among the lamb are earthy brown sliced mushrooms, diced red onion, and subtle flecks of green herbs. A light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese provides a delicate contrast and texture. The dish is topped with a scattering of freshly chopped vibrant green parsley, adding a pop of color. The overall presentation is natural and abundant, with the pasta and ragu creating an organic flow on the plate, leaving moderate negative space around the edges. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface, with a cotton napkin folded beside the plate and traditional flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese at the table.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of robust red wine.
instructions: Season lamb chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear lamb chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove lamb and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 3-4 minutes until mushrooms release moisture.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up browned bits from the pot bottom. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Return lamb to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 2-2.5 hours, or until lamb is very tender.
Remove rosemary sprigs, thyme sprig, and bay leaf. Shred lamb chunks using two forks directly in the pot, mixing with the sauce.
Cook pappardelle according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta to the ragu. Add grated Parmigiano Reggiano and a splash of reserved pasta water. Toss well to combine.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: The ragu can be made ahead and refrigerated for up to 3 days, or frozen for longer. Flavors deepen overnight.
Ensure lamb is browned well for rich flavor development.
Do not overcook the pasta; it should be al dente.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a single, generous individual portion on an everyday round ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Whole roasted chicken thighs, their skin golden-brown and crispy, are nestled among tender, fluffy 3 cm potato chunks. Some potato edges are slightly caramelized. Thick wedges of soft, sweet roasted onion and smashed garlic cloves are interspersed throughout. A few fresh rosemary sprigs and scattered leaves provide a vibrant green contrast. Natural pan juices lightly pool around the ingredients, adding a glossy sheen. The arrangement is organic and casual, as if plated directly from the roasting pan in a home kitchen. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, enhancing the inviting, lived-in atmosphere. A simple metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate, with a casually folded cloth napkin nearby.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into 3 cm chunks. Cut onion into thick wedges. Smash garlic cloves.
In a large roasting pan, combine potatoes, onion, and smashed garlic. Add 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 teaspoon salt, 0.5 teaspoon black pepper, and leaves from 1 sprig fresh rosemary. Toss to coat.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Rub with 1 tablespoon olive oil, 0.5 teaspoon salt, and 0.25 teaspoon black pepper.
Arrange chicken thighs on top of the vegetables in the roasting pan. Pour chicken broth into the pan. Add the remaining rosemary sprig.
Roast for 40-50 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, and potatoes are tender. Ensure internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Do not overcrowd the roasting pan to ensure even cooking and crispiness.
Adjust seasoning to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Smoked Pork Stuffed Cabbage Rolls with Sweet Bean Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of two neatly rolled, vibrant green cabbage rolls rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The tender cabbage leaves encase a rich, savory filling of ground beef, diced smoked pork, and bright green peas. A glossy, dark amber glaze, reduced from the braising liquid, is generously drizzled over and around the rolls, catching the light. The interior of a cut roll reveals the textured, savory filling. A small, artfully placed quenelle of creamy white mayonnaise sits delicately on the side of the plate, offering a visual contrast. Fresh, finely chopped parsley is sprinkled over the rolls, adding a pop of verdant green. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors. The background suggests a modern bistro, subtle and unobtrusive, focusing entirely on the refined presentation of the dish.
instructions: Carefully remove 8-10 large outer leaves from the cabbage head. Blanch leaves in boiling salted water for 3-5 minutes until pliable. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain and pat dry. Trim thick veins from leaves.
Dice smoked pork belly into small cubes. Dice onion finely. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced smoked pork belly. Cook until crispy. Remove pork with a slotted spoon. Leave rendered fat in the pan.
Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground beef to the pan. Break it up with a spoon. Cook until browned. Drain excess fat.
In a large bowl, combine cooked ground beef, crispy smoked pork, cooked rice, and green peas. Stir in 15g of Chinese sweet bean paste. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
Lay out a blanched cabbage leaf. Place a portion of the filling near the stem end. Fold in the sides. Roll tightly from the stem end to form a neat parcel. Repeat for all rolls.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Arrange cabbage rolls snugly in a baking dish. In a separate bowl, whisk together chicken stock, verjus, and remaining 15g of Chinese sweet bean paste. Pour mixture over the rolls.
Cover the baking dish tightly with foil or a lid. Bake for 45-50 minutes, or until cabbage is tender and filling is heated through. Internal temperature of beef should reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove rolls from the dish. Transfer braising liquid to a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Reduce until slightly thickened to a glaze consistency.
Finely chop fresh parsley.
Plate 2-3 cabbage rolls per serving. Drizzle with the reduced glaze. Place a small quenelle or drizzle of mayonnaise beside the rolls. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken Cashew Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Chicken Cashew Curry is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim, reflecting a homely kitchen. The curry fills about two-thirds of the bowl, showcasing its rich, warm golden-orange hue, characteristic of turmeric and tomato. The chicken chunks, cut into robust 3-4 cm pieces, are nestled within the thick, velvety gravy, their surfaces glossy from simmering. The sauce is creamy from the cashew paste, with subtle flecks of red from chili and hints of dark green from ground spices. A generous sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped coriander leaves provides a vibrant contrast on top. The dish has a natural, comforting appearance, with the chicken and sauce naturally settling. The bowl sits on a well-worn, light-colored wooden dining table. Alongside the bowl, a small mound of perfectly cooked basmati rice or a warm, fluffy naan bread is casually placed, ready for scooping. A simple, sturdy metal spoon rests beside the bowl. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting, casting soft shadows and highlighting the comforting textures of the food. The background is minimal, perhaps a blurred glimpse of a kitchen counter or a simple cloth napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with basmati rice or warm naan bread.
Offer a side of simple cucumber raita (yogurt dip) or pickled onions.
Eat using hands with bread, or a spoon with rice.

ingredients.name: Raw cashews
ingredients.quantity: 50g, soaked in hot water for 15 minutes

instructions: Soak cashews in hot water for 15 minutes. Drain and blend to a smooth paste with 50ml water. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add whole spices if using. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced onions. Cook until softened and golden brown, 8-10 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and slit green chilies. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, and red chili powder. Stir well for 30 seconds.
Pour in tomato puree. Cook, stirring frequently, until oil separates, 5-7 minutes.
Add chicken chunks and salt. Mix well to coat chicken. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken changes color.
Add 150ml water or chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover pot and cook 15 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Stir in cashew paste and garam masala. Cook another 3-5 minutes, uncovered, stirring gently, until curry thickens. Adjust consistency with more water if needed.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped coriander. Serve hot.
notes: Adjust green chili and red chili powder for desired heat level.
Soaking cashews ensures a smoother paste.
Cook chicken until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Calabrese con Patate e Peperoncino
recipes.visual_description: A rustic and inviting Southern Italian dish. The central focus is two golden-brown, braised chicken pieces, one thigh and one drumstick, nestled amidst chunky, fork-tender potato wedges. A rich, deep red tomato sauce, infused with Calabrian chili, coats the chicken and potatoes. The sauce shows specks of softened onion and garlic. Bright green, roughly torn fresh basil leaves are scattered generously over the top, providing a vibrant contrast. The dish is presented on a simple, round white porcelain plate. The chicken and potatoes are arranged organically, allowing the sauce to pool naturally around them. The background features a warm, natural wood table surface. A white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. Traditional silver flatware, a fork and knife, are placed to the side. Lighting is soft, natural, and even, highlighting the textures and vibrant colors of the food. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. The setting evokes a cozy, authentic Italian trattoria.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Serve with a glass of robust red wine.

ingredients.name: Calabrian chili paste (or dried red pepper flakes)

instructions: Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken in batches until golden on all sides. Do not overcrowd. Remove chicken.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 30ml olive oil. Add chopped onions. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add sliced garlic and Calabrian chili paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return browned chicken pieces to the pot. Add potato chunks. Stir gently to combine.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and potatoes are fork-tender.
Uncover. If sauce is too thin, increase heat and simmer uncovered for 5-10 minutes to reduce.
Stir in fresh basil just before serving. Taste and adjust seasoning.
notes: For best flavor, use bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces.
Adjust chili quantity to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Vegetable & Tempeh Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving of the Fermented Vegetable & Tempeh Rice Bowl is presented in a handcrafted, smooth, light cream-colored ceramic bowl, showcasing a minimalist and natural aesthetic. The base is a generous mound of perfectly cooked white rice, its grains distinct and fluffy. Arranged artfully atop the rice are vibrant elements: crisp, thinly shredded quick pickled cabbage, carrots, and radishes in shades of pale green, orange, and fuchsia, providing a tangy contrast. Alongside, neatly fanned slices of fresh green avocado and thin rounds of cucumber add cool, refreshing tones. Golden-brown, pan-seared tempeh chunks are placed deliberately, offering a substantial, textured protein. The dish is subtly garnished with finely sliced green spring onion and a light sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds, enhancing color and texture without clutter. The composition emphasizes clean lines and natural forms, with ample negative space. The bowl rests on a light-colored, natural wood or stone surface, accompanied by a simple, undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the organic textures and fresh colors of the ingredients against a clean, uncluttered background, possibly with a hint of natural greenery.

ingredients.name: White cabbage (outer leaves and trimmings reserved)

instructions: Prepare quick pickled vegetables: Thinly shred cabbage, carrots, and radishes. In a bowl, combine shredded vegetables with 2 g salt and 5 g sugar. Massage for 2 minutes until slightly softened. Add 30 ml rice vinegar and 50 ml water. Press down to submerge. Set aside.

Prepare vegetable stock water: In a small saucepan, combine reserved cabbage outer leaves, carrot ends, and peels with 500 ml water. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15 minutes. Strain, reserving the flavorful water. Discard solids.

Cook rice: Rinse rice thoroughly. Combine rice with the prepared vegetable stock water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 12-15 minutes, until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Prepare tempeh: Slice tempeh into 1 cm thick rectangular pieces. In a shallow dish, whisk together 60 ml soy sauce, 15 ml rice vinegar, 15 ml sesame oil, grated ginger, and minced garlic. Add tempeh slices. Marinate for 10 minutes, flipping once.
Cook tempeh: Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add marinated tempeh. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and slightly crispy. Remove from pan.
Prepare fresh vegetables: Thinly slice cucumber into rounds. Halve avocado and slice thinly.

Assemble bowls: Divide cooked rice among four individual serving bowls. Arrange quick pickled vegetables, cucumber slices, avocado slices, and cooked tempeh neatly over the rice. Garnish with sliced spring onion and toasted sesame seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Potatoes and Pearl Onions
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a rustic yet refined single portion of braised beef, potatoes, and pearl onions on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. Succulent, fork-tender beef chuck, cut into substantial 5cm chunks, is deeply browned from searing and then slow-braised to a rich mahogany. Interspersed are golden-brown potato wedges, approximately 4cm, their edges slightly softened from braising, and whole, caramelized pearl onions. A glossy, deep reddish-brown red wine reduction sauce generously coats the ingredients, pooling slightly at the base. The composition is a central mound, allowing moderate negative space on the plate. A sprinkle of vibrant fresh parsley, finely chopped, adds a contrasting green accent. The presentation is natural and inviting, set on a simple wooden table with a white linen napkin and standard flatware, under even natural light, evoking a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Trim beef chuck of excess fat. Cut beef into 5cm chunks.
Pat beef dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Dredge beef chunks lightly in flour. Shake off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Add pearl onions and carrots, cut into 4cm chunks, to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Mince garlic. Add garlic and tomato paste to the pot. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Braise for 2 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Peel potatoes. Cut potatoes into 4cm wedges. Add to the pot. Cook for another 30-40 minutes, uncovered, until potatoes are tender and sauce has thickened.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Stir in butter. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Apple & Pear Composition
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of a sustainable dessert is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate, providing ample negative space. A smooth, pale yellow pool of fermented apple puree forms the base. Artfully arranged on top are warm, golden-brown caramelized apple and pear wedges, showing subtle char marks and a soft sheen. A generous, off-white dollop of thick, creamy cashew vanilla cream sits beside the fruit, its smooth texture contrasting with the fruit. A few delicate, crinkled apple skin crisps, in shades of light brown and red, are placed upright, adding a crisp textural element and a zero-waste touch. The overall presentation is clean, simple, and elegant, highlighting the natural beauty and textures of the ingredients. The setting features a light, textured bamboo table surface, an undyed natural linen napkin, and soft, diffused natural lighting. A minimalist background with subtle green plant elements is visible.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Apple Puree: Core and roughly chop 300g tart apples. Combine apples, 150ml filtered water, 15ml lemon juice, and 2g salt in a blender. Blend until smooth. Transfer to a clean glass jar. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 2-3 days, or until tangy. Stir daily. Chill before serving.

Prepare Cashew Vanilla Cream: Soak 100g raw cashews in hot water for 30 minutes, then drain. Combine soaked cashews, 120ml filtered water, 30ml maple syrup, 5ml vanilla, and a pinch of salt in a high-speed blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. Chill for at least 1 hour to thicken.

Prepare Apple Skin Crisps: Preheat oven to 120°C (250°F). Spread apple skins in a single layer on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake for 30-45 minutes, until completely dry and crisp. Cool completely. Store in an airtight container.

Caramelize Apple & Pear: In a large skillet, melt 5g butter or coconut oil over medium heat. Add 200g apple wedges and 200g pear wedges. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened. Drizzle with 15ml maple syrup and cinnamon (if using). Continue cooking, stirring occasionally, for 3-5 minutes until caramelized and tender-crisp.

Assemble Dish: Spoon a portion of the chilled fermented apple puree onto the base of each serving plate. Arrange caramelized apple and pear wedges artfully on top. Dollop cashew vanilla cream beside the fruit. Garnish with a few apple skin crisps. Serve immediately.
notes: For true zero-waste, apple cores and remaining peels can be used to make apple scrap vinegar or fruit stock.
Adjust sweetness of puree and cream to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Decadent Chocolate Fudge Layer Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant slice of dark chocolate fudge cake sits on a clean white porcelain plate, positioned slightly off-center. The cake features two distinct, moist, deep brown layers, generously filled and topped with a glossy, rich dark chocolate ganache. The cut surface reveals a tender, dense crumb. Beside the slice, a scattering of vibrant red raspberries and deep blue blueberries provides a fresh, colorful contrast. A light dusting of cocoa powder delicately covers part of the plate and cake top. In the soft-focused background, the remaining whole, perfectly frosted cake rests on a simple cake stand, hinting at its full indulgence. The setting is a modern bistro, with a natural wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the cake's textures and colors against a minimalist, warm-toned background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour two 15 cm round cake pans. Line bottoms with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, cocoa powder, baking soda, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate medium bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, melted butter, and vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Carefully stir in the hot water or coffee until batter is smooth and thin.
Divide batter evenly between prepared cake pans.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cakes in pans on a wire rack for 10 minutes. Invert cakes onto rack to cool completely.
To make ganache: Place chopped dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl.
Heat heavy cream in a small saucepan until simmering. Do not boil.
Pour hot cream over chopped chocolate. Let sit for 5 minutes.
Whisk gently from the center outwards until ganache is smooth and glossy.
Let ganache cool at room temperature for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens to a spreadable consistency.
Once cakes are completely cool, level tops with a serrated knife if needed.
Place one cake layer on a serving plate or cake stand. Spread about one-third of the ganache evenly over the top.
Place the second cake layer on top. Pour remaining ganache over the cake. Spread evenly over top and sides.
Chill cake for at least 30 minutes to set ganache.
Slice and serve with fresh berries. Dust with cocoa powder before serving.
notes: Ensure cakes are completely cool before frosting to prevent ganache from melting.
Use high-quality dark chocolate for the best ganache flavor and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Tomato Mushroom Risotto is presented in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl, set on a well-used wooden dining table. The risotto is a warm, inviting off-white with visible specks of red from diced tomatoes and earthy brown slices of sautéed mushrooms. The rice grains are plump, coated in a luscious, fluid sauce. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese melts on top, adding a golden hue. Finely chopped parsley garnishes the center. The bowl is positioned slightly off-center. Traditional Italian flatware rests casually beside the bowl on a simple cloth napkin. A small chunk of Parmesan with a grater and a basket of crusty bread sit nearby, enhancing the homely, authentic Italian meal. Warm, soft light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy family dinner.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately
Offer extra freshly grated Parmesan at the table
Serve with crusty bread for mopping up sauce

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 80 g, grated, plus extra for serving

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are softened and browned.
Stir in Arborio rice. Toast for 1-2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine, if using. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add chopped tomatoes. Stir well to combine.
Add one ladle of hot vegetable stock to the rice. Stir constantly until liquid is almost fully absorbed.
Continue adding stock one ladle at a time, stirring continuously, until each addition is absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18-20 minutes. The rice should be creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese. This is 'mantecatura'.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir in fresh chopped parsley.
Serve immediately.
notes: Risotto requires constant stirring for optimal creaminess.
Serve immediately for the best texture and consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Porcini Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Chicken and Porcini Risotto is presented in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl, centrally placed on a simple wooden table surface. The risotto has a fluid, free-flowing consistency, not stiff or mounded. Its color is a warm, inviting beige-gold from the broth and Parmesan. Visible within the creamy rice are tender, golden-brown seared chicken cubes and various shades of brown from the sliced cremini and chopped porcini mushrooms. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley adorns the top, adding a pop of color. A small mound of freshly grated Parmesan cheese rests beside the parsley. The plate is clean, with moderate negative space. A neatly folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware are positioned beside the bowl. The setting suggests a modern bistro, with soft, natural lighting creating subtle shadows and highlighting the dish's texture. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty ciabatta bread to soak up the creamy sauce.
Pair with a crisp, dry white wine like Pinot Grigio or Soave.
Offer a simple, lightly dressed green salad as a refreshing counterpoint.
instructions: Rehydrate dried porcini mushrooms: Place porcini in 250 ml hot water for 20 minutes. Strain liquid through a fine sieve; reserve liquid. Chop rehydrated porcini.
Prepare ingredients: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Slice cremini mushrooms. Finely dice onion. Mince garlic.

Sear chicken: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, 7-9 minutes. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan; set aside.

Sauté aromatics: In the same pan, add remaining 15 ml olive oil and 20 g butter. Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and sliced cremini mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms soften, 5-7 minutes.
Toast rice: Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges of grains are translucent.
Deglaze: Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed.

Add broth: Add reserved porcini liquid to the pan. Stir until absorbed. Begin adding warm chicken broth, 150 ml at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for each addition to be almost fully absorbed before adding more broth. Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.

Combine and finish: Stir in chopped rehydrated porcini and seared chicken. Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 40 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1 minute until risotto is creamy and glossy (mantecare).
Season: Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper.
Serve: Ladle risotto immediately into warm bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken broth is warm before adding to the risotto; this maintains a consistent cooking temperature and promotes even absorption.
Constant stirring is key for a creamy risotto; it helps release starch from the Arborio rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Chocolate Chicken Crêpes
recipes.visual_description: Two golden-brown crêpes, neatly folded or rolled, are presented slightly overlapping on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The crêpes reveal glimpses of the rich, dark brown chicken filling, which has a subtle sheen from the melted chocolate. Tender, shredded chicken pieces are visible within the folds. The dish is generously garnished with vibrant green chopped cilantro and delicate white crumbles of queso fresco, providing a fresh contrast. A hint of the rich, savory sauce from the filling subtly pools around the crêpes. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, with a neatly folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual bistro setting, allowing the dish to be the clear focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Mexican red rice or refried beans.
Offer a simple fresh pico de gallo or a dollop of Mexican crema on the side.
Accompany with a light, crisp green salad.

ingredients.name: Dark chocolate (70% cocoa or higher, unsweetened)

instructions: Prepare crêpe batter: In a large bowl, whisk flour, eggs, milk, and a pinch of salt until smooth. Melt 15g butter, stir into batter. Let batter rest 30 minutes.

Cook crêpes: Heat a 20 cm non-stick pan over medium heat. Lightly grease with butter. Pour approximately 60 ml of batter, swirling to coat the pan bottom thinly. Cook 1-2 minutes until edges are golden. Flip. Cook 30 seconds more. Transfer to a plate. Repeat with remaining batter, stacking crêpes.

Prepare chicken filling: Dice chicken thighs into 2 cm cubes. In a large skillet, melt 15g butter over medium heat. Add diced onion, sauté 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken to skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes, browning all sides. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chopped chipotle, chicken broth, cumin, coriander, and oregano. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat, cover, and cook 15-20 minutes until chicken is tender and cooked through.
Remove chicken from skillet. Shred chicken using two forks. Return shredded chicken to skillet with sauce.
Grate dark chocolate directly into the chicken mixture. Stir until chocolate melts and sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Assemble crêpes: Lay each crêpe flat. Spoon a generous amount of chicken filling onto the center. Fold or roll the crêpe neatly.
Serve immediately: Arrange two filled crêpes per plate. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and crumbled queso fresco.
notes: Using dark, unsweetened chocolate is crucial for a savory profile; avoid milk or sweet chocolate.
The chipotle in adobo provides a smoky heat; adjust quantity to your spice preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Estofado de Ternera con Pimientos y Champiñones
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of rich, deeply colored Estofado de Ternera is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Succulent, tender beef chunks, approximately 4-5 cm, are nestled amongst vibrant strips of roasted red bell pepper and quartered brown mushrooms, all coated in a glossy, dark reddish-brown sauce. The sauce, thickened naturally, pools invitingly around the ingredients. A scattering of fresh, finely chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a pop of bright green contrast. The dish is set on a simple wooden table. Beside the plate, a small, rustic piece of crusty Spanish bread is placed, along with a cotton napkin and a wine glass filled with red wine. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the textures and rich colors, with a subtly blurred bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with crusty bread (pan de pueblo) for dipping into the sauce
Accompanied by a simple green salad
Paired with a glass of robust Spanish red wine
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until well browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red bell pepper strips. Cook for 3-4 minutes until bell pepper slightly softens.
Stir in smoked paprika and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, quartered mushrooms, red wine, beef broth, and bay leaf. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged in the liquid.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Poblano Rellenos de Maíz y Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted poblano pepper, split lengthwise to reveal its vibrant, abundant filling, rests centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The poblano's deep green, slightly charred skin contrasts with the warm hues of the filling. Inside, diced chicken, golden corn kernels, dark black beans, and fluffy quinoa are tightly packed, showcasing a mix of textures. A rich, red tomato-jalapeño sauce pools gently around the pepper, adding a complementary color. Fresh, bright green cilantro sprigs are artfully placed on top of the filling, and a bright lime wedge sits beside the pepper. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, hinting at a modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh ingredients and meticulous preparation. A folded cotton napkin is placed to the side, completing the professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of warm corn tortillas
Offer a small bowl of pico de gallo or salsa roja for extra freshness
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).

Roast poblano peppers: Place whole poblanos on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes. Skin should be blistered and charred. Transfer peppers to a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap. Let steam for 10 minutes. Peel skins, make a lengthwise slit, remove seeds carefully.

Cook quinoa: Rinse quinoa under cold water. Combine quinoa and chicken broth in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.

Prepare chicken: Dice chicken breast into 1 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 5 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear until cooked through and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Sauté aromatics: Add remaining 10 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add finely diced white onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.

Prepare filling: Add fresh corn kernels, black beans, cooked chicken, ground cumin, smoked paprika, and dried oregano to the skillet. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Stir in cooked quinoa. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Make sauce: In a separate small saucepan, combine crushed tomatoes and minced jalapeño (if using). Simmer gently for 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Stuff peppers: Carefully fill each roasted poblano pepper with the chicken and quinoa mixture. Place stuffed peppers in a baking dish. Pour the tomato sauce around the peppers.
Bake: Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until peppers are heated through and filling is bubbling.
Serve: Garnish with fresh cilantro and lime wedges. Serve immediately.
notes: For spicier peppers, leave some seeds in the jalapeño or add a pinch of cayenne pepper to the filling.
Ensure poblanos are fully roasted and steamed for easy peeling.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of hearty chicken and vegetable stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The stew fills the bowl, showcasing a rich, savory broth. Prominent chunks of seared chicken, approximately 3cm, are nestled amongst thick slices of tender leeks and 1cm slices of celery, cooked until soft but retaining shape. Bright green, medium-sized broccoli florets add fresh contrast, cooked just tender-crisp. Colors are natural and inviting: golden-brown chicken, pale green leeks, light green celery, and vibrant green broccoli, all bathed in an amber-hued broth. Freshly chopped green parsley garnishes the top. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, accompanied by a simple metal spoon. Warm, cozy light evokes a comforting, homestyle meal.
instructions: Cut chicken into 3cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Clean leeks. Trim ends. Slice white and light green parts into 1cm thick rounds.
Slice celery into 1cm thick pieces.
Cut broccoli into medium florets.
Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add onion, leeks, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and thyme. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir and cook 2 minutes.
Gradually pour in chicken broth, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Add bay leaf.
Return chicken to the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through.
Add broccoli florets. Cook uncovered 5-7 minutes, until broccoli is tender-crisp.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Baked Chicken and Chorizo Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown chicken thigh, its skin crispy and glistening, rests centered on a white porcelain plate. It is nestled atop a generous portion of vibrant, saffron-infused short-grain rice, generously studded with thick, ruby-red slices of Spanish chorizo and diced cooked tomatoes. Around the chicken and rice, rustic chunks of roasted potato exhibit slightly charred edges, alongside caramelized apple wedges. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of color. A vibrant yellow lemon wedge sits beside the chicken. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a small bowl of crisp mixed green salad with thin cucumber slices. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting textures and rich colors against a softly blurred bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the flavorful juices.
Offer a simple green salad as a refreshing counterpoint.

ingredients.name: Firm apple, cored and cut into wedges

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add chorizo slices to the same pan. Cook for 3-5 minutes until browned and fat is rendered. Remove chorizo. Set aside.
Drain most chorizo fat, leave about 15ml. Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and saffron (if using). Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and sugar. Cook 5 minutes, breaking down tomatoes. This creates the sofrito base.
Add rice to the pan. Stir to coat rice in sofrito. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs and chorizo to the pan, nestling them into the rice. Cover the pan tightly with a lid or foil.
Place the pan in the preheated oven. Bake for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, toss potato chunks and apple wedges with remaining 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a separate baking tray.

After 25 minutes, remove lid from rice pan. Add potato and apple mixture around the chicken and rice in the pan. Continue baking uncovered for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender, chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature, and potatoes/apples are golden and tender.
While baking finishes, prepare the side salad: combine salad greens and cucumber slices. If desired, whisk Greek yogurt with a squeeze of lemon juice for a light dressing.
Remove pan from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and the fresh green salad on the side.
notes: For best results, use a short-grain rice like Calasparra or Arborio, though any short-grain rice will work.
Adjust the amount of smoked paprika to your preferred level of smokiness and spice.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Mole Poblano
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Pollo en Mole Poblano is presented on a clean, round, white porcelain dinner plate. A large, dark-skinned chicken thigh, deeply caramelized from searing, rests prominently on a pool of rich, glossy mole sauce. The mole, a deep, complex reddish-brown, exhibits a smooth, thick consistency, clinging to the chicken. A scattering of bright green, finely chopped fresh cilantro leaves provides a vibrant color contrast against the dark sauce, along with a sprinkle of pale, toasted sesame seeds for texture. The chicken piece is whole, showcasing its succulent, tender appearance. The plate sits on a simple, warm-toned wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A crisp, folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. A small, white ceramic bowl of fluffy white rice and a stack of warm, soft corn tortillas are positioned nearby, along with a traditional Mexican talavera-style water glass. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the sauce's sheen and the chicken's inviting texture, creating an authentic and approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping the mole sauce.
Accompany with a side of traditional Mexican rice.
Offer a small bowl of pickled red onions or jalapeños for a tangy counterpoint.
Serve with a refreshing Agua Fresca or Horchata.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt.
Sear chicken skin-side down in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Cook until skin is golden and crispy. Flip and sear other side briefly. Remove chicken, set aside.

Carefully remove stems and seeds from dried chiles. Toast chiles in the dry pot for 30 seconds per side until fragrant. Do not burn. Place chiles in a bowl. Cover with hot water. Let rehydrate for 20 minutes.
In the same pot, add a little oil. Sauté chopped tomatoes, onion, and garlic until softened and lightly browned.

Drain rehydrated chiles. Add chiles, sautéed vegetables, almonds, raisins, half of the sesame seeds, tortilla piece, cinnamon stick, cloves, peppercorns, and cumin seeds to a blender. Add 200 ml chicken broth.
Blend until very smooth. Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl. Press solids to extract liquid. Discard solids.

Heat 15 ml lard or oil in the pot over medium heat. Add strained mole paste. Cook, stirring constantly, for 10-15 minutes. The paste will thicken and darken. This step is crucial for flavor development.
Gradually whisk in remaining chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Add chopped dark chocolate and sugar. Stir until chocolate is fully melted and incorporated. Season with salt to taste.

Return seared chicken thighs to the mole sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Serve chicken with mole sauce. Garnish with fresh cilantro and remaining toasted sesame seeds.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The mole paste requires patient cooking to develop its deep flavor and color.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of hearty beef stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The stew fills the bowl, showcasing tender, browned beef chunks, soft, chunky potatoes, and vibrant orange carrot pieces nestled in a rich, dark brown, slightly glossy gravy. The ingredients are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a comforting, unpretentious look. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a functional garnish and a pop of color. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table with visible grain. Beside the bowl, a simple, off-white ceramic plate holds a slice of crusty bread. A plain, folded linen napkin in a neutral tone and a sturdy, everyday metal fork are casually placed. Warm, cozy lighting from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the steam gently rising from the stew. The background hints at a lived-in kitchen, slightly blurred, maintaining focus on the food. Beef chuck is cut into 3-4 cm cubes, carrots into 2 cm chunks, and potatoes into 3 cm chunks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Serve with a simple green salad.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 3-4 cm cubes
Carrots, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks
Potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir for 1 minute to cook off raw flour taste.
Pour in red wine (if using) and beef broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add dried thyme and bay leaves.
Add potatoes. Ensure liquid covers most ingredients. Add more broth if needed.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot.
Cook on low heat for 2-2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaves before serving. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Ladle hot stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best flavor, brown the beef well in batches.
Stew can be made ahead and reheats well. Flavors often improve the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato & Chicken Ensalada with Crispy Tortilla
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Potato & Chicken Ensalada is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. The salad, a vibrant mix of 1.5 cm diced golden potatoes, shredded white chicken, finely diced red onion, and coarsely chopped green cilantro, is mounded organically in the center. Crumbled white queso fresco is scattered throughout, adding pockets of bright contrast. Crispy, golden-brown corn tortilla strips are casually piled on top, creating height and texture. A light coating of lime-cilantro dressing glistens on the ingredients. The plate rests on a well-worn, light-colored wooden kitchen table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. Beside the plate, a small, unglazed terra cotta bowl holds extra lime wedges. A simple, folded cotton napkin in a muted tone is placed nearby. The scene is lit with warm, soft light, suggesting a cozy kitchen ambiance. The portion is generous yet balanced, showcasing the potato and chicken equally. No meat is fanned. The ceramic plate and terra cotta bowl evoke a homestyle Mexican setting. The presence of lime wedges and tortilla strips reinforces the cultural theme.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra lime wedges on the side.
Offer a bowl of salsa verde or pico de gallo as an accompaniment.
Pair with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender. Drain. Let cool slightly. Dice into 1.5 cm cubes.
Poach chicken breast in lightly salted water until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Shred chicken into bite-sized pieces.
Slice corn tortillas into 0.5 cm wide strips. Heat vegetable oil in a large pan to 175°C. Fry tortilla strips in batches until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels. Season with a pinch of salt.
Finely dice red onion. Mince jalapeño, removing seeds if desired. Coarsely chop cilantro.
In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, olive oil, ground cumin, chili powder, salt, and black pepper for the dressing.
In a large mixing bowl, combine diced potatoes, shredded chicken, diced red onion, minced jalapeño, and chopped cilantro.
Pour dressing over the potato mixture. Gently toss to coat all ingredients.
Crumble queso fresco into the salad. Gently fold in.
Serve immediately on a bed of shredded romaine lettuce, if desired. Top each portion with crispy tortilla strips.
traditional_techniques: Frying tortillas to make totopos (tortilla chips/strips).

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & White Bean Stew with Crispy Skins
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of a refined, plant-forward stew is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl in a natural off-white or light grey hue. The stew, a rustic yet elegant blend of creamy white beans and vibrant, broken-down fermented tomatoes, occupies the center, leaving ample white space around the rim. The color palette is earthy and warm, with deep red tomato notes and creamy white beans. A few fresh basil leaves, roughly torn, are placed thoughtfully on top, adding a pop of green and natural texture. A small, delicate spoonful of dark, glistening basil seed 'caviar' is precisely placed on the side of the stew. Two or three crisp, curled tomato skins are delicately placed on top or leaning against the side, showcasing a zero-waste element. The overall composition is clean, minimalistic, and celebrates the natural beauty of the ingredients. The dish rests on a light-colored, natural wood or stone surface, with an undyed linen napkin subtly visible to one side. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting textures and colors without harsh shadows.
instructions: If using dried beans, soak overnight. Drain. Cook beans in fresh water until tender. Set aside. (Skip if using canned beans).
If fermenting fresh tomatoes, peel and reserve skins. Ferment tomatoes as desired (e.g., in a salt brine for 5-7 days).
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add thinly sliced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add fermented tomatoes and their brine. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, breaking down tomatoes.
Stir in cooked white beans and vegetable broth. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat. Simmer for 20 minutes to meld flavors.
Season the stew with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. Adjust acidity if needed.
For crispy tomato skins: Preheat oven to 150°C. Lay reserved tomato skins flat on a baking sheet. Drizzle with a tiny bit of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Bake for 15-20 minutes until crisp.
For basil seed 'caviar': In a small bowl, combine basil seeds and water. Stir well. Let sit for 10 minutes until seeds swell and form a gel-like coating.
Serve the stew hot. Garnish each portion with roughly torn fresh basil, a spoonful of basil seed 'caviar', and crispy tomato skins.
notes: The vegetable broth can be made by simmering vegetable scraps (onion peels, carrot tops, celery ends, mushroom stems) in water for at least 30 minutes, then straining.

To ferment tomatoes: Quarter ripe tomatoes. Place in a clean jar with 2% salt brine (20g salt per liter of non-chlorinated water) to cover. Seal loosely and ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days, burping daily, until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Lemon Garlic Chicken and Rice
recipes.special_requests: healthy food, less calories, less fat, no oregano, no thyme, no zucchini, no broth cuisine
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of One-Pan Lemon Garlic Chicken and Rice is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A generous portion of fluffy, golden-yellow rice, infused with paprika and lemon, forms the base. Two whole, seared boneless chicken thighs, golden-brown and juicy, are nestled naturally atop the rice. Visible among the rice are vibrant diced red and yellow bell peppers, along with wilted dark green spinach leaves, providing bursts of color and texture. The arrangement is casual and home-style, with components touching and slightly overlapping, as if served directly from the cooking pan. A standard metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate on a simple, casually folded cloth napkin. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy lighting, suggesting a relaxed family dining area with a lived-in atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing on the dish as the centerpiece of a comforting home-cooked meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with half the salt, pepper, and paprika.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and diced bell peppers. Cook 3 minutes more.
Stir in uncooked rice, remaining paprika, dried parsley, salt, and pepper. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in water and lemon juice. Bring mixture to a simmer. Stir well.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the rice mixture.
Cover skillet tightly with a lid or foil. Transfer to preheated oven.
Bake 25-30 minutes, or until rice is tender and water is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove skillet from oven. Stir in fresh spinach and lemon zest. Cover and let rest 5 minutes until spinach wilts.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice Stew with Orzo
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Spanish Chicken and Rice Stew with Orzo is presented in a deep, rustic, terracotta-toned ceramic bowl. The stew features succulent, irregular chunks of tender chicken, visibly cooked to perfection. Golden-hued rice and small, creamy orzo pasta are intertwined, absorbing the rich, reddish-brown broth. Diced potato cubes, softened cremini mushroom pieces, and off-white cannellini beans are interspersed throughout, adding texture and color. A vibrant scattering of fresh, finely chopped flat-leaf parsley garnishes the top, providing a fresh contrast. The bowl rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, placed on a simple wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and traditional flatware are positioned beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting, creating an inviting, casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread for dipping.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar on the side.

ingredients.name: Canned cannellini beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and quartered mushrooms. Cook 3-4 minutes until fragrant and mushrooms soften.
Stir in smoked paprika, ground cumin, saffron threads, and a pinch of cayenne if desired. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Add diced potatoes and bring to a simmer. Return seared chicken thighs to the pot.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, or until chicken is nearly cooked through.
Stir in rice and orzo pasta. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for 15-20 minutes. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. Cook until rice and orzo are tender and liquid has thickened.
Stir in rinsed cannellini beans. Cook 2-3 minutes more to heat through.
Remove chicken from pot. Check internal temperature. Chicken must reach 75°C (167°F). Cut chicken into 2-3 cm chunks.
Return chicken chunks to the stew. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished generously with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The stew should be thick but still have a saucy consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Fermented Chili Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beer-Braised Chicken with Fermented Chili Pasta is presented on a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic plate. The plate sits on a reclaimed light wood surface. Tender, shredded chicken pieces are nestled among al dente rigatoni, all coated in a rich, reddish-brown braising sauce. The sauce features subtle specks of diced braised vegetables. A sprinkle of freshly grated white parmesan cheese adds contrast. Crispy, golden-brown chicken skin shards are scattered over the dish for texture. Finely chopped green parsley adds a fresh pop of color. The setting includes a simple, natural beige undyed linen napkin and minimalist flatware. Soft natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and earthy color palette. The background is clean and unobtrusive, with a subtle hint of green plant life.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until deeply golden and crispy. Remove chicken. Set aside. Reserve crispy skin for garnish.
Dice onion, carrot, and celery into small cubes. Add to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Mince garlic. Add to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Add chicken stock and parmesan rind. Stir in fermented chili paste.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from the pot. Shred the chicken meat from the bones using two forks. Discard bones.
Return pot to stovetop. Remove parmesan rind. Simmer braising liquid over medium heat until slightly reduced and thickened, about 5-10 minutes.
Cook rigatoni according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain, reserving 125 ml of pasta water.
Add cooked pasta and shredded chicken to the sauce. Add reserved pasta water as needed to achieve desired consistency. Toss to combine.
Grate parmesan cheese. Finely chop fresh parsley.
Serve pasta with chicken. Garnish with grated parmesan, crispy chicken skin, and fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice.
