The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Savory Crepes
recipes.visual_description: The finished dish presents a single, generously filled crepe, golden-brown and gently rolled, resting on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The crepe's delicate texture is evident, with a hint of its creamy chicken and mushroom filling peeking from the ends. Chicken is diced into small cubes, and mushrooms are thinly sliced, all coated in a rich, savory cream sauce. A light dusting of finely chopped fresh parsley and a delicate sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese adorn the top, adding vibrant green and pale yellow accents. The plate maintains moderate negative space, enhancing the visual appeal. Set on a simple wooden table surface, a contemporary fork and knife are placed beside the plate on a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere with a blurred bistro background.
instructions: Prepare crepe batter: Whisk flour, eggs, milk, 50ml heavy cream, 50g plain yogurt, vanilla extract, and 2g salt until smooth. Let batter rest 15 minutes.
Cook crepes: Heat a lightly buttered non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour a thin layer of batter, swirling to coat the bottom. Cook 1-2 minutes per side until golden.
Repeat for remaining batter. Stack cooked crepes on a plate.

Prepare chicken: Dice chicken breast into small cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook chicken until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken and set aside.

Sauté vegetables: Thinly slice mushrooms. Dice onion and mince garlic. In the same pan, add more olive oil if needed. Sauté onion until softened. Add garlic and mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned.

Make sauce: Pour 100ml heavy cream, 100g plain yogurt, and chicken broth into the pan with vegetables. Stir in chopped thyme. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 3-5 minutes, until sauce slightly thickens.
Combine filling: Add cooked chicken cubes back into the sauce with mushrooms. Stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Fill crepes: Lay a crepe flat. Spoon a portion of the chicken and mushroom filling onto the center. Roll or fold the crepe securely.
Serve: Place filled crepes on serving plates. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and optional grated Parmesan cheese. Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Braised Beef Ragu with Pappardelle is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed. The wide, flat pappardelle noodles are thoroughly coated in a rich, dark red-brown ragu, forming an appealing mound. Tender, large chunks of braised beef are visibly nestled within the sauce and pasta, showcasing their fork-shredded texture. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped Italian parsley adds a vibrant color contrast, along with a generous dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese, providing a touch of white and a slightly coarser texture. The plating is organized yet retains a natural, flowing quality, with moderate negative space on the plate. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface, illuminated by natural, even light, capturing the warmth and richness of the dish. Traditional flatware is placed beside the plate, and a crisp cotton napkin completes the modern bistro setting. The entire plate is visible, highlighting the professional, approachable presentation. The beef is presented as large chunks, while the vegetables in the soffritto are finely diced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Pecorino Romano cheese at the table.
instructions: Season beef chunks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Work in batches to avoid overcrowding. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add finely diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook until wine has mostly evaporated, about 5 minutes.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, bay leaf, and thyme.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot tightly.
Transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F) or continue simmering on stovetop over very low heat. Cook for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef from the pot. Shred the beef into smaller pieces using two forks. Discard bay leaf and thyme sprigs.
Return shredded beef to the sauce. Stir well. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Cook pappardelle in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add drained pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly.
Serve immediately. Garnish each plate with grated Pecorino Romano cheese and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Vanilla Bean Sponge Cake with Raspberry Diplomat Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant slice of Vanilla Bean Sponge Cake stands tall on a clean white porcelain plate. The sponge layers are light golden-brown, airy and moist. Between the sponge, distinct layers of pale pink Raspberry Diplomat Cream are visible, smooth and rich. A vibrant, slightly textured ruby-red raspberry compote layer is nestled within the cream. The slice is cleanly cut, showcasing the refined layers. A delicate dusting of white icing sugar covers the top of the cake. Beside the slice, a small cluster of plump, fresh red raspberries are artfully placed, accompanied by a tiny, vibrant green sprig of fresh mint. The plate is presented on a simple wooden table, under soft, even natural light, with ample negative space. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and inviting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a hot cup of coffee or a delicate tea.
instructions: Preheat oven to 170°C. Grease and flour a 15cm round cake tin.
Whisk eggs and 100g caster sugar until pale and thick.
Sift 100g plain flour and baking powder into egg mixture. Fold gently.
Warm 50ml milk and 50g melted butter with 2ml vanilla bean paste. Add to batter. Fold until just combined.
Pour batter into tin. Bake 25-30 minutes, until golden and springy. A skewer inserted should come out clean.
Cool cake in tin for 10 minutes. Invert onto wire rack. Cool completely.
Heat 200ml milk in saucepan until simmering.
Whisk 2 egg yolks, 50g caster sugar, and cornflour in a bowl until smooth.
Pour hot milk slowly into egg mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until very thick.
Remove from heat. Stir in 25g butter until melted.
Pour pastry cream into a clean bowl. Cover surface with cling film. Chill completely.
Combine 100g raspberries, 20g caster sugar, and lemon juice in small saucepan.
Cook over medium heat 5-7 minutes, until berries break down and mixture thickens slightly.
Cool completely.
Once pastry cream is chilled, remove cling film. Whisk until smooth.
Whip cold heavy cream to soft peaks.
Gently fold whipped cream into pastry cream until combined. This is the diplomat cream.
Slice cooled sponge cake horizontally into two even layers.
Place one sponge layer on serving plate.
Spread half the diplomat cream evenly over the sponge.
Spread all raspberry compote over the cream.
Top with second sponge layer.
Spread remaining diplomat cream on top. Smooth the top surface.
Chill cake for at least 1 hour to set.
Slice cake into 4 portions. Plate one slice on a white porcelain plate.
Dust lightly with icing sugar. Arrange a few fresh raspberries beside the slice. Add a small mint sprig.
notes: Ensure pastry cream is completely chilled before folding in whipped cream for best results.
Chilling the assembled cake is crucial for clean slicing and stability.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Lemon Herb Chicken and Rice Skillet
recipes.special_requests: healthy food, less calories, less fat cuisine
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Mediterranean Lemon Herb Chicken and Rice is presented on an off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled among fluffy, earthy brown rice. Vibrant diced red and yellow bell peppers, soft zucchini half-moons, and burst cherry tomatoes are visible throughout. Fresh green chopped parsley is scattered over the top, adding a pop of color. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a comforting, home-style mound without overcrowding the plate. The entire plate is visible, showcasing ample negative space. The dish sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A standard fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate, with a simple cloth napkin nearby. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a lived-in family kitchen setting, maintaining focus on the homely, expertly prepared meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain Greek yogurt for a creamy tang
Offer warm whole-grain pita bread for scooping
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, red bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper to the skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften.
Add minced garlic, dried oregano, and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in brown rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly to lightly toast the rice.
Pour in chicken broth. Add halved cherry tomatoes. Bring mixture to a boil.
Return seared chicken chunks to the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is nearly tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

Stir in zucchini half-moons and lemon zest. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for another 10-15 minutes, or until rice is fully cooked, zucchini is tender, and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Add lemon juice.
Remove skillet from heat. Let it rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Stir in fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For extra flavor, use homemade chicken broth.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple Walnut Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous, homely portion of Apple Walnut Salad is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. Thinly sliced crisp red and green apples are casually mixed with fresh mixed greens and delicate slivers of red onion. Roughly chopped, toasted walnuts are scattered abundantly over the top, adding a warm, golden-brown contrast. The ingredients are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating an inviting, unpretentious mound. A light apple cider vinaigrette coats the vibrant greens and glistening apple slices, with some dressing visible at the base of the salad. The scene is bathed in warm, soft kitchen light, enhancing the natural colors and textures. A casually folded linen napkin and simple flatware are placed beside the plate, completing the comfortable, everyday dining setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Spread walnuts on a baking sheet. Toast for 5-7 minutes until lightly golden and fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Let cool.
Wash and thoroughly dry the mixed greens. Place in a large salad bowl.
Core the apples. Thinly slice the apples into crescent shapes. Add to the salad bowl.
Peel the red onion. Thinly slice or finely dice the red onion. Add to the salad bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, maple syrup, salt, and black pepper until well combined.
Add the cooled, roughly chopped walnuts to the salad bowl.
Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss until all ingredients are evenly coated.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef, Mustard, and Apple Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of hearty Beef, Mustard, and Apple Soup is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. Rich, amber-brown broth fills the bowl, studded with tender, browned beef chunks, soft diced carrots, celery, and onion, and plump short-grain rice. The diced Granny Smith apple pieces are subtly integrated, adding a light, contrasting color. The soup's surface is lightly dotted with a sprinkle of vibrant, finely chopped fresh parsley, providing a fresh green accent. The textures are inviting: yielding beef, creamy rice, and soft vegetables. The bowl is centered on a simple, light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin positioned to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the soup's warmth and depth, creating an inviting, professional yet approachable visual.

ingredients.name: Granny Smith apple
ingredients.quantity: 1 medium, peeled, cored, diced into 1cm cubes

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add beef cubes in batches. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Dijon mustard. Cook for 1 minute.
Return beef to the pot. Pour in beef broth. Add bay leaf and thyme sprigs.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5 hours, or until beef is tender.
Stir in rinsed short-grain rice and diced apple. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is cooked and soup has thickened slightly.
Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Bread and Cheese Bake
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown Savory Bread and Cheese Bake is presented on a simple white ceramic plate, occupying a generous, homely portion. The top crust is visibly crisp and deeply golden, with patches of caramelized cheese peeking through. Below, soft, custardy bread cubes are interspersed with melted, gooey Gruyère and diced, savory ham. Small flecks of fresh green thyme leaves are visible throughout the bake. The dish is cut into a thick, rustic square, showcasing its hearty interior. The plate rests on a well-used wooden kitchen table, alongside a casually folded plain cloth napkin and a simple fork. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene from an unseen kitchen window, casting soft shadows.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a simple side salad of mixed greens and a light vinaigrette.
Offer a dollop of Dijon mustard on the side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease a 23x33 cm baking dish.
In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more until fragrant. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper. Stir in chopped thyme.
Add bread cubes, grated cheese, diced ham, and cooked onion-garlic mixture to the egg mixture. Toss gently to combine. Ensure all bread is coated.
Pour mixture into the prepared baking dish. Press down gently to ensure even distribution.
Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until golden brown and puffed. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Using slightly stale bread is key for best texture; it absorbs the custard better without becoming soggy.
This dish can be assembled the night before and refrigerated. Let it come to room temperature for 30 minutes before baking, or add 10-15 minutes to baking time if baking directly from cold.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Milanese with Spicy Garlic Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A golden, crispy chicken Milanese medallion rests on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a perfectly twirled nest of spaghetti, glistening with a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce. The sauce is flecked with small pieces of minced garlic and thinly sliced red chili, showing depth. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered artfully over both the pasta and the chicken, adding a pop of color. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the pasta. The chicken is a uniform oval shape, its crumb coating visibly crunchy. The overall plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, with silver cutlery and a white cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread
Offer fresh grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table
Pair with a simple green salad
instructions: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of cling film. Pound with a mallet to 1 cm thickness.
Set up breading station: Place flour in first shallow dish. Whisk eggs in second shallow dish. Place breadcrumbs in third shallow dish. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Dredge each chicken piece in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, letting excess drip off. Coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat 50ml olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry chicken Milanese for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Transfer to a wire rack.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add spaghetti. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, mince garlic. Thinly slice red chili. Heat remaining 50ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic and sliced chili. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Add drained spaghetti to the sauce. Add reserved pasta water. Toss well to coat. Cook for 1-2 minutes, allowing pasta to absorb sauce.

Divide spaghetti among four plates, forming a neat swirl. Place one chicken Milanese alongside the pasta on each plate. Grate fresh Parmesan cheese over pasta. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic-Mustard Roasted Chicken with Chili-Garlic Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Garlic-Mustard Roasted Chicken and Chili-Garlic Rice is presented on an off-white, slightly imperfect ceramic dinner plate. A golden-brown, whole roasted chicken thigh, cooked until the skin is slightly crispy and the meat is tender, rests prominently on one side of the plate. Adjacent to it is a fluffy mound of white long-grain rice, speckled with vibrant red finely chopped chili and small flecks of minced garlic. The rice is light and separate. The overall presentation is natural and unforced, with components touching as if served directly from a home kitchen. The setting is a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, illuminated by soft, inviting kitchen light. A simple metal fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. A loosely folded, light-colored cloth napkin completes the homely scene. The background is minimal, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere, with perhaps a blurred hint of a simple serving bowl.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
In a mixing bowl, combine mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, 3 minced garlic cloves, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper.
Coat chicken thighs thoroughly with the mayonnaise mixture.
Place chicken on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While chicken roasts, prepare rice. Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add remaining 3 minced garlic cloves and the finely chopped red chili. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed rice to the saucepan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast lightly.
Pour in 500ml chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Remove rice from heat. Let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Rest roasted chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve roasted chicken whole with chili-garlic rice.
notes: Adjust the amount of red chili to your preferred level of heat.
Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs yield the most flavor and a crispier skin.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Orange Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared duck breast is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The duck breast, cut into thick, succulent pieces, showcases a rich, crispy golden-brown skin and tender, rosy interior. A glossy, vibrant amber-orange reduction sauce is artfully spooned over and around the duck. Alongside, bright orange carrot batons, lightly glazed, are neatly arranged. A small, fresh green thyme sprig garnishes the plate, adding a touch of natural elegance. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a silver fork and knife, and a white cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a refined bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a side of potato gratin or pommes dauphinoise
Accompanied by haricots verts (green beans) or a simple green salad with vinaigrette
instructions: Pat duck breasts dry. Score the skin in a crosshatch pattern, without cutting into the meat. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Place duck breasts skin-side down in a cold, oven-safe skillet. Cook over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes until skin is crispy and golden brown. Pour off rendered fat as it accumulates.
Flip duck breasts. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook for 5-7 minutes for medium-rare, or until desired doneness (internal temperature 60-65°C).
Remove duck from skillet. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil, for 10 minutes.
While duck rests, drain all but 15 ml rendered fat from skillet. Add minced shallots. Sauté over medium heat for 2 minutes until softened.
Deglaze skillet with red wine vinegar. Scrape up browned bits. Add orange juice and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.

Reduce sauce by half, about 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat. Whisk in cold butter cubes, one at a time, until sauce is glossy and emulsified. Stir in orange zest and honey/maple syrup if using. Season with salt and pepper.
For carrots: Cut carrots into 5 cm batons. Steam or boil until tender-crisp. Sauté briefly in a separate pan with a knob of butter and a pinch of salt until lightly glazed.
Slice each duck breast diagonally into 2-3 thick pieces. Do not fan.
Plate sliced duck breast. Spoon orange reduction generously over and around the duck. Arrange glazed carrot batons beside the duck. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Chicken and Roasted Vegetable Rice
recipes.special_requests: healthy food, less calories, less fat cuisine
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lemon Herb Chicken and Roasted Vegetable Rice is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple light wooden table. The base is a well-formed mound of fluffy, light brown rice. Thick, succulent medallions of pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a golden-brown hue, are artfully placed atop the rice. Around the chicken and rice, vibrant roasted bell pepper strips in red and yellow, along with bright yellow whole corn kernels, are arranged organically, showcasing their slightly charred edges and tender textures. A sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley adds a pop of color and freshness. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits beside the chicken. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting includes a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware beside the plate, all illuminated by natural, even lighting that enhances the food's colors and textures without harsh shadows. The background suggests a modern bistro, clean and unobtrusive.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Rinse brown rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package directions using 500 ml vegetable broth. Simmer until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender, about 40 minutes. Keep warm.
Cut red and yellow bell peppers into 2 cm wide strips. In a large bowl, toss bell pepper strips and corn kernels with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables on a baking sheet. Roast in preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, or until tender-crisp and slightly charred. Stir halfway through.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season chicken with salt, pepper, and dried oregano. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.

Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add minced garlic and the juice of half a lemon to the skillet. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring garlic, until fragrant.

Add remaining 250 ml vegetable broth to the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook chicken for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Rest for 5 minutes.
Slice chicken breasts into thick medallions. Do not fan out slices.
To serve, spoon cooked brown rice onto individual plates. Arrange sliced chicken medallions on top of the rice. Place roasted bell pepper strips and corn kernels around the chicken.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Apple Goulash with Rice
recipes.visual_description: A generous, rustic portion of rich, dark brown beef goulash is spooned onto a bed of fluffy white rice. The beef is cut into 3-4 cm irregular chunks, showcasing its tenderness from slow braising. Interspersed are soft, slightly collapsed 2 cm apple pieces and tender diced onion, all coated in the thick, glossy, savory sauce. The goulash has a deep reddish-brown hue from paprika and tomato, with a slight sheen. The rice is mounded naturally beside the goulash, appearing soft and distinct. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley contrasts with the deep colors. The dish sits on a well-used wooden dining table, served on a cream-colored ceramic plate. A plain linen napkin and simple fork and knife rest beside it. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, hinting at a cozy, lived-in kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled gherkins or a simple green salad dressed with vinegar and oil.
A slice of crusty rye bread for soaking up the sauce.

ingredients.name: Firm cooking apples (e.g., Granny Smith or Braeburn)

instructions: Cut beef into 3-4 cm chunks. Pat dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, tomato paste, paprika, and caraway seeds. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in beef stock until smooth. Bring to a simmer.
Return beef to the pot. Stir in Dijon mustard.
Peel, core, and cut apples into 2 cm chunks. Add to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
While goulash simmers, cook rice. Rinse rice under cold water.
Combine rice with 600ml water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not lift lid.
Remove rice from heat. Let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Taste goulash. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve goulash hot over fluffed rice. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This goulash benefits from slow cooking, making the beef exceptionally tender. The apples add a subtle sweetness and tartness that balances the richness of the beef and mustard.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Pasta Shells with Sausage and Ricotta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Baked Pasta Shells with Sausage and Ricotta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Three to four golden-baked giant pasta shells, generously stuffed, are nestled in vibrant, rich red tomato sauce. Creamy white ricotta-sausage filling peeks from openings. Bubbly, melted mozzarella covers the tops, studded with crispy, small diced salami pieces. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered as a garnish. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and inviting colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Offer extra freshly grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Cook pasta shells in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add 2 cloves minced garlic; cook 1 minute more.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer sauce for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Set aside.
In a separate pan, cook Italian sausage over medium-high heat, breaking it apart with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
In a large bowl, combine cooked sausage, ricotta cheese, remaining 2 cloves minced garlic, and 30 g Parmesan cheese. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper.
Carefully stuff each cooked pasta shell with the sausage-ricotta mixture.
Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce on the bottom of the prepared baking dish. Arrange stuffed shells in a single layer over the sauce.
Pour remaining tomato sauce over the shells. Sprinkle with shredded mozzarella and diced salami. Top with remaining 20 g Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and shells are heated through.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Mushroom Ragu with Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous home-style portion of Hearty Beef and Mushroom Ragu with Tagliatelle is presented in a simple, rustic ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The golden-yellow tagliatelle pasta forms a loose nest, topped abundantly with the deep reddish-brown ragu. Prominent, fork-tender beef chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, are visible alongside soft, earthy sliced mushrooms and a rich, clinging tomato sauce. A sprinkle of vibrant green fresh parsley adds a pop of color. The bowl rests on a well-worn, warm wooden kitchen table, evoking a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. Soft, inviting natural light illuminates the dish. A plain linen napkin is casually placed beside the bowl, with a simple fork resting on the table, completing the unpretentious, comforting scene.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 3-4 cm chunks. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef chunks in batches until deep golden on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove browned beef from pot and set aside.

Add diced onion to the same pot. Cook, scraping up any browned bits, until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for another 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and lightly browned.
Pour in red wine (if using). Scrape up any remaining browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine reduces by half.
Return browned beef to the pot. Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, bay leaf, and dried thyme. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and simmer for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. Remove bay leaf before serving.
While ragu simmers, cook tagliatelle according to package instructions in a separate pot of salted boiling water until al dente. Drain well.
Serve: Spoon hearty portions of ragu generously over individual servings of tagliatelle. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve immediately with grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Black Tea & Chamomile Reduction
recipes.visual_description: Pan-seared duck breast, skin rendered to a crisp, golden-brown, is presented as two thick, succulent chunks, showing a rosy medium-rare interior. The meat is arranged off-center on a round, matte white porcelain plate. A glossy, deep amber reduction sauce, infused with black tea and subtle chamomile notes, pools elegantly beside and slightly over the duck. Alongside, a small cluster of roasted baby potatoes, their skins slightly browned, and a few bright green blanched asparagus spears provide color and texture contrast. A single fresh thyme sprig garnishes the sauce. The plate is set on a light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded grey linen napkin and simple, modern silver cutlery. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and inviting textures. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a cozy bistro.
instructions: Score duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Do not cut into meat. Season duck breasts generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a cold, oven-safe pan over medium heat. Place duck breasts skin-side down in the cold pan.
Render fat slowly for 8-10 minutes until skin is crispy and golden brown. Pour off excess fat periodically.
Flip duck breasts. Add thyme sprigs to the pan. Cook meat-side down for 3-5 minutes for medium-rare, or longer to desired doneness.
Transfer duck breasts to a cutting board. Rest for 5-10 minutes.
For the sauce: Pour off most duck fat from the pan, leaving about 1 tablespoon. Add diced shallots to the pan. Sauté until softened, 2-3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with red wine. Scrape up browned bits. Reduce wine by half.
Add chicken or duck stock, black tea bags (or loose leaf in sachet), and dried chamomile flowers (in sachet). Bring to a simmer.
Reduce sauce by half until slightly thickened. Remove tea bags/chamomile. Stir in honey.
Whisk in cold butter, one piece at a time, until sauce is glossy and emulsified. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice rested duck breasts into thick chunks. Arrange on plates. Spoon sauce over and around duck. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Chili-Cheese Sauce and Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of beer-braised chicken is centrally plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The fork-tender chicken thigh, with its rich, savory brown exterior, is nestled beside vibrant green roasted broccoli florets, which show slight charring at their edges. A generous, luscious pool of golden-orange chili-cheese sauce is spooned over and around the chicken, its creamy texture visible. Scattered fresh basil leaves provide a pop of contrasting green and freshness. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a subtle cotton napkin placed beside the plate, and a natural, even overhead light. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, maintaining focus on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm cornbread or steamed rice.

ingredients.name: Red chili (e.g., Anaheim or mild red bell pepper)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss broccoli florets with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and chili to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in beef stock. Return chicken to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover the pot and transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender.
While chicken braises, prepare cheese sauce. Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in shredded cheddar cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove chicken from oven. Carefully transfer chicken to serving plates. Discard excess braising liquid if desired, or reduce it slightly on the stovetop for a thinner sauce.
Spoon chili-cheese sauce generously over the chicken. Arrange roasted broccoli florets alongside.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust chili powder and fresh chili quantity based on desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a single, hearty portion of golden-brown roasted chicken thighs and potato wedges on a simple, rustic ceramic plate. Two bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, their skin crisped and deeply caramelized, are nestled amongst irregularly cut potato wedges, roasted to a tender interior and crisp exterior. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley and a few roasted garlic cloves enhance the visual appeal. The natural colors of the ingredients dominate: rich browns and golden hues from the roasted chicken and potatoes, contrasted with the bright green herbs. The plate is positioned on a worn wooden dining table, alongside a casually folded plain linen napkin and basic flatware. Warm, inviting light suggests a cozy family kitchen setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in pan juices.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or red potatoes)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges.
In a large roasting pan, combine potato wedges, smashed garlic cloves, rosemary, and thyme.
Drizzle with olive oil. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange chicken thighs, skin-side up, among the potatoes in the pan.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden brown and crispy.
Check chicken internal temperature with a thermometer. It must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Cooking time may vary based on oven and chicken size. Always check internal temperature.
For extra crispiness, broil for the last 2-3 minutes, watching carefully.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Lemon Herb Chicken with Potatoes and Cauliflower
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and crispy-skinned, rests centrally on a rustic off-white ceramic plate. Surrounding the chicken are generously portioned, tender-crisp potato wedges, their skins lightly browned and interiors fluffy. Scattered among the potatoes are soft, caramelized cauliflower florets, showing hints of char at their edges. Two bright yellow lemon wedges, slightly roasted, are placed alongside the chicken, adding a touch of freshness. A few vibrant green rosemary sprigs are nestled amongst the vegetables, providing an aromatic garnish. The plating is natural and casual, with components touching and slightly overlapping, reflecting a homely, comforting meal. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light, with a simple fork and knife casually placed beside the plate. The scene conveys a lived-in family kitchen atmosphere, highlighting the dish as the comforting centerpiece.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (392°F).
Wash potato. Cut potato into 2 cm wedges.
Wash cauliflower. Cut cauliflower into small florets.
Peel garlic cloves. Smash garlic cloves lightly.
Pat chicken thigh dry with paper towel.
Rub chicken thigh with a small amount of olive oil. Season generously with salt and pepper.
In a medium bowl, combine potato wedges, cauliflower florets, remaining olive oil, rosemary sprigs, and smashed garlic. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Arrange chicken thigh on a baking sheet. Distribute seasoned vegetables around the chicken.
Cut lemon half into two wedges. Place lemon wedges on the baking sheet with chicken and vegetables.
Roast for 30-35 minutes. Chicken skin should be golden brown and crispy. Vegetables should be tender and lightly caramelized.
Check internal temperature of chicken. Insert meat thermometer into thickest part of thigh, avoiding bone. Temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Saffron Rice with Bell Peppers and Corn
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Chicken and Saffron Rice with Bell Peppers and Corn is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A vibrant, slightly mounded bed of golden-orange saffron-infused rice forms the base. Tender, seared chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, are nestled atop and around the rice, showcasing their golden-brown crust. Diced red, yellow, and green bell peppers, cut into 1.5-2 cm pieces, are scattered throughout the rice, providing bursts of color and texture. Bright yellow corn kernels are interspersed, adding sweetness. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley. The overall presentation is clean and organized, with moderate negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, and traditional flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and vibrant colors. The background is minimal, creating a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Accompany with crusty bread for soaking up any remaining juices.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Dice all bell peppers into 1.5-2 cm pieces. Finely dice the onion. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add diced bell peppers and minced garlic. Cook for 5-7 minutes until peppers are slightly tender.
Stir in rice, smoked paprika, and ground cumin. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Add saffron threads. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the skillet. Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in frozen corn kernels. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 5-7 minutes. Rice should be tender and liquid absorbed. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Adjust salt and pepper to your taste.
For best results, use a good quality saffron for vibrant color and aroma.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown chicken cutlet, perfectly pan-fried, rests on a clean white porcelain plate. It is generously topped with vibrant red tomato sauce, melted, bubbly mozzarella cheese, and a sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan. Fresh green basil leaves are artfully scattered over the top, providing a pop of color. Beside the chicken, a modest portion of al dente spaghetti tossed in a simple tomato sauce is neatly arranged. The chicken maintains its whole, unsliced form, showcasing its crispy texture. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and knife, and a folded cotton napkin, reflecting a casual Italian bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, emphasizing its inviting appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a side of pasta (e.g., spaghetti al pomodoro) or a simple green salad.
Offer crusty Italian bread for soaking up the sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Pound chicken breasts to 1.5 cm thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Set up a breading station: Place flour in one shallow dish. Whisk eggs in another. Combine breadcrumbs and 25g grated Parmesan in a third dish.
Dredge each chicken piece in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumb mixture. Press gently to adhere.
Heat 100ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry chicken cutlets 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Drain on paper towels.

For the sauce: In a small saucepan, heat 2 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Sauté minced garlic 1 minute until fragrant. Add crushed tomatoes and a pinch of salt. Simmer 10 minutes. Stir in half the fresh basil.
Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce on the bottom of an oven-safe dish. Place fried chicken cutlets over sauce. Top each cutlet with more sauce, then mozzarella slices and remaining Parmesan.
Bake 15-20 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and chicken is heated through.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Saffron Chicken and Rice with Roasted Tomatoes and Olives
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Golden saffron-infused Basmati rice forms a loose, inviting bed, its individual grains distinct and slightly glistening. Two pieces of pan-seared chicken thigh, with deeply browned, slightly crisp skin, are nestled atop the rice. The chicken is presented as whole pieces, not sliced. Vibrant red roasted cherry tomatoes, slightly blistered, are scattered amongst the rice, alongside dark, glossy Kalamata olives. A generous sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley adds a fresh contrast. A lemon wedge rests on the side of the plate. The composition is balanced and approachable, with moderate negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard flatware beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh green salad tossed with lemon vinaigrette
Offer a side of crusty bread to soak up juices
A dollop of plain Greek yogurt can complement the flavors
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pot.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion. Sauté 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to the pot. Stir 1 minute to toast lightly.
Crumble saffron threads into warm chicken stock. Pour stock into the pot with rice. Stir gently. Bring to a simmer.
Nestle seared chicken thighs into the rice mixture. Scatter whole cherry tomatoes and pitted Kalamata olives around the chicken.
Cover pot tightly with a lid or foil. Transfer to the preheated oven. Bake 25-30 minutes, or until rice is tender and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove pot from oven. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the dish. Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beet, Fennel, and Chickpea Stew
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rustic ceramic bowl holds a generous portion of the hearty stew. The stew is thick, with visible chunks of deep purple-red beets, pale green-white fennel, and golden-brown chickpeas. The vegetables are cut into rustic 2cm cubes, showing their natural shapes and textures. A slight sheen from the rich, tomato-based broth coats the ingredients. A vibrant scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley sits on top, providing a pop of color. The bowl rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, off-white ceramic plate is next to it, with a metal spoon resting casually beside the bowl. A folded, textured linen napkin in a neutral tone is nearby. Warm, inviting natural light comes from a window, creating soft shadows. The background is slightly blurred, hinting at a comfortable, lived-in kitchen environment.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced beets and fennel. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, dried thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes. Beets should be tender.
Stir in drained chickpeas. Cook for another 5 minutes to heat through.
Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Cottage Cheese Dumplings
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown garlic cottage cheese dumplings is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The small, irregular gnocchi-like dumplings are loosely arranged in the plate's center, coated in a glistening garlic butter sauce. Thinly sliced, lightly golden garlic pieces are visible among the dumplings, along with vibrant flecks of finely chopped fresh parsley. A light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese adds a subtle white contrast. The dish has a balanced composition with moderate negative space, highlighting the soft yet slightly crisp texture of the pan-seared dumplings. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silverware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, set against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Place cottage cheese in a fine-mesh sieve. Let drain for 15 minutes to remove excess moisture.
In a large bowl, combine drained cottage cheese, egg, flour, minced garlic, 30g grated Parmesan, salt, and black pepper. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Lightly flour a clean work surface. Scoop small portions of the dough and gently roll into irregular gnocchi-like shapes, about 2-3 cm long. Repeat until all dough is used.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Carefully add dumplings to the boiling water in batches. Cook for 2-3 minutes after they float to the surface, ensuring they are cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat.
Add thinly sliced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden. Do not brown.
Add cooked dumplings to the skillet. Toss gently to coat in the garlic butter. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing dumplings to lightly brown.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in chopped fresh parsley and lemon zest. Squeeze in a little lemon juice.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Homely Cottage Cheese Walnut Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously cut slice of Homely Cottage Cheese Walnut Cake rests on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The cake slice features a golden-brown baked top and a moist, dense, creamy off-white interior dotted with visible chopped walnut pieces. The whole, round cake, slightly rustic with uneven edges, is visible in the background on a wooden cutting board, lightly dusted with powdered sugar. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually placed cloth napkin and a simple fork beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere characteristic of a family kitchen. The presentation is natural and unpretentious, focusing on comfort and homemade appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm or at room temperature
Accompanied by fresh berries or a dollop of plain Greek yogurt
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20 cm round cake pan with butter.
In a food processor, blend cottage cheese until smooth. Scrape down sides as needed.
In a large bowl, whisk together smoothed cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, eggs, sugar, vanilla extract, and lemon zest until well combined.
In a separate bowl, combine whole wheat flour, baking powder, and salt.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in chopped walnuts.
Pour batter into prepared cake pan. Smooth top.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean and the top is golden brown.
Cool cake in pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack. Cool completely before slicing.
notes: Ensure cottage cheese is blended very smooth for best cake texture.
Do not overmix the batter once flour is added to keep the cake tender.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Roasted Beet and Fennel
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared duck breast is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. The duck breast, cut into thick, succulent medallions, is arranged neatly beside vibrant roasted beet wedges and tender-crisp fennel pieces. The duck skin exhibits a rich, golden-brown crispness, contrasting with its rosy interior. Beets display their deep ruby-red hue with slightly caramelized edges, while the fennel offers a delicate pale green and white. A glossy, light orange pan sauce is drizzled artfully over the duck and vegetables. A fresh sprig of thyme garnishes the dish, adding a touch of green. Standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin rest beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting. The entire plate is visible, with appropriate negative space.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel beets. Cut into 2 cm wedges. Trim fennel bulbs, halve lengthwise, then cut into 2 cm wedges.
Toss beets and fennel with 30 ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and smashed garlic on a baking sheet. Arrange in a single layer.
Roast for 25-30 minutes. Vegetables should be tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.
Score duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern, without cutting into meat. Season skin and flesh with salt and pepper.
Place duck breasts skin-side down in a cold, oven-safe skillet. Cook over medium-low heat for 8-10 minutes. Render fat. Skin should be crispy and golden.
Flip duck breasts. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 6-8 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove duck from oven. Rest on a cutting board, skin-side up, for 10 minutes.
Drain most duck fat from skillet, leaving 1-2 tablespoons. Add orange juice to skillet. Scrape up browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes. Stir in butter and orange zest until melted. Season sauce.
Slice each duck breast into 1.5 cm thick medallions. Do not fan.
Arrange roasted beets, fennel, and duck medallions on plates. Drizzle with pan sauce. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.
notes: Ensure duck internal temperature reaches 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Cottage Cheese & Garlic Dumplings
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Savory Cottage Cheese & Garlic Dumplings is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple, light wooden table surface. The dumplings are plump, soft, and slightly irregular in shape, with a light off-white color, indicating their tender texture. They are arranged in a natural, slightly overlapping mound, showcasing their handcrafted form. A generous portion of golden-brown, deeply caramelized diced onions is spooned over the dumplings, providing a contrasting color and crispy texture. Freshly chopped vibrant green dill is scattered liberally over the top, adding a pop of color and herbaceous aroma. Beside the main plate, a small, rustic ceramic bowl holds a dollop of thick, white sour cream, ready for dipping. The setting is a modern bistro style with natural, even lighting from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the food's textures. A simple cotton napkin, folded neatly, is placed beside the plate. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere, ensuring the dish remains the clear focal point. The presentation emphasizes rustic charm and homemade appeal while maintaining a clean, professional aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a generous dollop of cold sour cream
Garnish with fresh chopped dill
Serve with caramelized onions
instructions: In a large bowl, combine cottage cheese, egg, grated hard cheese, minced garlic, 3g salt, and 1g black pepper. Mix well to form the filling.

On a clean surface, create a well with 300g flour. Add 2g salt. Pour 150ml warm water into the well. Bring flour into the water gradually. Knead dough until smooth and elastic, about 7-10 minutes. Cover and let rest 15 minutes.
Divide dough into two portions. Roll one portion thinly, about 2mm thick. Use a 7cm round cutter to cut circles.
Place a spoonful of filling onto the center of each dough circle. Fold dough over filling to form a half-moon. Pinch edges firmly to seal. Repeat with remaining dough and filling.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Gently drop dumplings into boiling water, do not overcrowd. Cook 3-5 minutes after they float to the surface. Remove with a slotted spoon.

While dumplings cook, melt butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and golden brown, about 10-15 minutes. Season with remaining salt and pepper.
Transfer cooked dumplings to a serving plate. Top with caramelized onions. Garnish generously with fresh chopped dill. Serve immediately with a side of cold sour cream.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef Ragu with Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A generous, mounded portion of tagliatelle pasta, deeply coated in rich, reddish-brown beef ragu, is presented centrally on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The tender, shredded beef pieces are visibly intertwined with the golden-yellow pasta strands and the thick, savory tomato-based sauce. A few vibrant green fresh basil leaves are artfully scattered over the top, providing a pop of color and aromatic freshness. A light, delicate dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese crowns the dish, adding a subtle texture and sharpness. The overall presentation is rustic yet refined, showcasing the hearty textures of the ragu and the al dente pasta. The beef is shredded, integrated into the sauce. Onion, carrots, and celery are finely diced (mirepoix) within the sauce. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin to the left and standard silver flatware (fork and knife) to the right. Natural, even lighting highlights the inviting textures and rich colors of the dish, creating a warm, casual bistro atmosphere in the softly blurred background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the rich ragu sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef cubes in batches until well browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes, scraping up any browned bits.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Bring to a simmer. Reduce wine by half, about 5 minutes.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, and Worcestershire sauce. Stir well to combine.
Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot.
Cook for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is very tender and easily shreds with a fork. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Remove beef from the pot. Shred beef using two forks. Return shredded beef to the sauce.
Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper as needed.
Cook tagliatelle according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta directly to the ragu sauce in the pot. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Vegetarian Bibimbap Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Vegetarian Bibimbap Bowl presented in a wide, shallow, white ceramic bowl, showcasing distinct sections of beautifully prepared vegetables over a bed of fluffy white short-grain rice. The center features a generous dollop of bright red gochujang sauce. Around the sauce, julienned carrots gleam orange, deep green spinach is artfully piled, pale green courgette strips add contrast, earthy brown shiitake mushrooms provide depth, and white bean sprouts offer a fresh texture. Each vegetable is cooked to a tender-crisp perfection, retaining its natural color and shape. The entire dish is lightly sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds, adding a subtle golden crunch. The plating is clean and organized, with moderate negative space, allowing each colorful component to stand out. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table with chopsticks resting beside it, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of kimchi.
Offer additional gochujang sauce for personal preference.
Mix all ingredients together thoroughly before eating.
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Cook rice in 450ml water according to package directions or in a rice cooker. Let stand 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Prepare vegetables: Julienne carrots and courgette into thin strips. Slice shiitake mushrooms thinly. Mince garlic cloves.
Blanch spinach: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add spinach; cook 30 seconds. Drain immediately. Rinse with cold water. Squeeze out excess water. Roughly chop.
Season spinach: In a bowl, combine spinach with 1 minced garlic clove, 10ml soy sauce, 5ml sesame oil, and 5g toasted sesame seeds. Mix well. Set aside.
Blanch bean sprouts: In the same boiling water, add bean sprouts; cook 1 minute. Drain immediately. Rinse with cold water. Squeeze out excess water.
Season bean sprouts: In a bowl, combine bean sprouts with 1 minced garlic clove, 10ml soy sauce, 5ml sesame oil, and 10g yellow mustard. Mix well. Set aside.
Sauté carrots: Heat 10ml vegetable oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add julienned carrots. Sauté 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Sauté mushrooms: Heat 10ml vegetable oil in the same pan. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Season with 10ml soy sauce and 5ml sesame oil. Set aside.
Sauté courgette: Heat 10ml vegetable oil in the same pan. Add julienned courgette. Sauté 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. Season with 10ml soy sauce and 5ml sesame oil. Set aside.
Prepare Bibimbap sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together gochujang, 1 minced garlic clove, 15ml sesame oil, rice vinegar, sugar, and 15ml water until smooth.

Assemble bowls: Divide cooked rice among 4 large serving bowls. Arrange prepared vegetables (carrots, mushrooms, courgette, spinach, bean sprouts) in distinct sections on top of the rice. Place a dollop of gochujang sauce in the center of each bowl. Garnish with remaining toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Feel free to add other vegetables like bell peppers, cucumbers, or fermented fernbrake (gosari) for more variety.
For a richer flavor, you can lightly toast the sesame seeds before sprinkling.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef Cheek with Fermented Carrots and Lentil Purée
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-cooked beef cheek, presented as two generous, dark brown chunks, rests on a smooth, pale orange mound of red lentil purée on a handcrafted cream ceramic plate. The beef is visibly tender, with a rich, glossy surface from the braising liquid. Beside the beef, a small, artful cluster of vibrant orange pickled carrot batons adds a contrasting pop of color and crisp texture. A deep crimson, concentrated tomato-garlic reduction is elegantly drizzled alongside the beef, pooling slightly on the plate. Fresh green oregano leaves are scattered sparingly for a fresh accent. The plate has ample white space, emphasizing a clean, minimalistic aesthetic. It sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, with an undyed linen napkin subtly placed. Soft, natural lighting highlights the dish's earthy tones and simple beauty.
instructions: For pickled carrots: Wash and peel carrots. Slice into thin batons (approx. 5cm long, 0.5cm thick). Combine apple cider vinegar, 100ml water, sugar, 5g sea salt, and peppercorns in a small saucepan. Heat until sugar dissolves. Let brine cool completely. Pack carrot batons into a clean jar. Pour cooled brine over carrots. Seal and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight for best flavor.

For slow-cooked beef cheeks: Pat beef cheeks dry. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef cheeks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot and set aside.

Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pot. Add 4 minced garlic cloves and half of the oregano sprigs. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce wine by half.

Return beef cheeks to the pot. Add bay leaves and enough vegetable stock to almost cover the beef. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Turn beef every hour. Remove beef and bay leaves. Keep beef warm.

For tomato-garlic reduction: Roughly chop tomatoes. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. In a separate saucepan, combine chopped tomatoes, minced garlic, and remaining oregano sprigs. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes break down and liquid reduces to a thick sauce (approx. 20-25 minutes). Remove oregano sprigs. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

For red lentil purée: Rinse red lentils. Combine lentils with 500ml fresh water (or vegetable stock) in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer, uncovered, for 15-20 minutes, or until lentils are very tender and most liquid is absorbed. Stir occasionally. Remove from heat. Mash or blend lentils until smooth. Add a splash of hot water or stock if purée is too thick. Season with sea salt and black pepper.

To serve: Ladle a mound of red lentil purée onto each plate. Place 2 chunks of slow-cooked beef cheek on the purée. Arrange a small cluster of pickled carrot batons beside the beef. Drizzle the concentrated tomato-garlic reduction generously over and around the beef. Garnish with fresh oregano leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes sustainable practices through the use of beef cheek, a less common cut, and eco-conscious preparation methods like pickling and maximizing ingredient use.
The pickled carrots can be prepared up to a week in advance for deeper flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Spinach and Cottage Cheese Gnudi with Brown Butter Sage Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents soft, pillowy spinach and cheese gnudi, lightly coated in a glistening golden-brown butter sauce with crisp sage leaves. The gnudi are small, irregular oval shapes, showcasing their delicate handmade nature. Scattered amongst them are vibrant halved cherry tomatoes, adding bursts of red and a hint of acidity. A sprinkle of finely grated Parmesan cheese provides a snowy white contrast, while fresh basil leaves add a pop of bright green. The arrangement is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space on a clean white porcelain plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table and a neatly folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
instructions: Blanch spinach for 30 seconds. Drain immediately. Cool under cold water. Squeeze spinach very dry. Chop finely.
In a large bowl, combine well-drained cottage cheese, egg, grated Parmesan, finely chopped spinach, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Gradually add flour to the mixture. Mix gently until a soft, cohesive dough forms. Do not overmix.
Lightly flour a clean surface. Roll small portions of dough into ropes, about 2 cm in diameter. Cut ropes into 2 cm pieces. Gently shape each piece into a small oval or cylinder.
Place shaped gnudi on a floured baking tray. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to firm up.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle simmer. Carefully drop gnudi into the simmering water. Cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding.
Cook gnudi until they float to the surface, then continue cooking for 2-3 more minutes. Remove cooked gnudi with a slotted spoon.

While gnudi cook, melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add sage leaves. Cook until butter turns golden brown and sage leaves become crisp. Add halved cherry tomatoes (if using) and cook for 1 minute.
Add cooked gnudi directly into the brown butter sage sauce. Gently toss to coat all gnudi.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and extra grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure cottage cheese is very well-drained to prevent a watery dough.
Do not overwork the gnudi dough; gentle mixing keeps them tender.
traditional_techniques: Gentle dough handling for delicate dumplings

recipes.recipe_name: Bacon-Wrapped Garlic Butter Chicken Thighs with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a well-used, rustic wooden dining table, set with an everyday, cream-colored ceramic plate. A single, golden-brown bacon-wrapped chicken thigh sits centrally, its crispy bacon glistening. Alongside are several thick-cut, roasted potato wedges, tender and lightly browned. A cluster of vibrant green beans, slightly blistered from roasting, completes the plate. The elements are naturally arranged, touching but not overcrowded, reflecting a home-cooked meal. Colors are warm and inviting: golden chicken, earthy potatoes, and bright green beans. Textures are a mix of crispy bacon, tender chicken, soft potatoes, and firm-tender beans. Lighting is warm and cozy, suggestive of a relaxed family kitchen atmosphere. A simple, casually placed cloth napkin and perhaps a fork rest nearby. The portion is modest and approachable, ideal for a comforting individual serving.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (180°C fan/Gas Mark 6).
In a small bowl, combine softened butter with minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Rub chicken all over with half of the garlic butter.
Wrap each chicken thigh with two slices of bacon, securing with toothpicks if needed.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into thick wedges. In a large bowl, toss potato wedges with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Arrange chicken thighs and potato wedges in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Remove tray from oven. Add trimmed green beans to the tray, tossing gently with pan drippings. Spread remaining garlic butter over the beans.

Return tray to oven. Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and bacon is crispy. Potatoes should be tender and golden, green beans tender-crisp.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato Pasta with Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pasta rests on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The pasta, a medium shape, is generously coated in a rich, rustic fermented tomato sauce, vibrant red with visible basil and fresh tomato flecks. The sauce is fluid, coating each strand. Tender-crisp roasted broccoli florets and thin, charred rounds of broccoli stem are nestled among the pasta, showcasing deep green and browned edges. Fresh basil leaves and delicate, crispy roasted broccoli leaves add contrasting texture and color. A glistening drizzle of garlic-infused olive oil lightly coats the dish. The plate has ample negative space, highlighting natural ingredient beauty. The setting is a light reclaimed wood table, with an undyed linen napkin and a single fork. Soft, natural lighting illuminates a clean, minimal background.
instructions: Part 1: Fermented Tomato Sauce (Start 3-5 days in advance)
Roughly chop 700g tomatoes. Place in a clean jar.
Add 2 cloves minced garlic and 10g salt.
Mash tomatoes lightly to release juices.
Top with non-chlorinated water if needed to cover tomatoes, leaving 2cm headspace.
Place a fermentation weight or small bag of water to keep solids submerged.
Cover with an airlock lid or burp daily.
Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved.
Once fermented, blend the mixture into a sauce. Taste and adjust salt. Store in the fridge.
Part 2: Roasted Broccoli
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Separate broccoli florets. Peel broccoli stem and slice into 1cm thick rounds.
Wash broccoli leaves thoroughly.
Toss florets and stem slices with 2 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray.
Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Toss broccoli leaves with a drizzle of olive oil and salt. Spread on a separate small baking tray.
Roast leaves for 5-8 minutes, until crispy. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Part 3: Pasta and Assembly
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, gently warm the fermented tomato sauce in a large pan over medium-low heat. Do not boil vigorously.
Roughly chop remaining 100g fresh tomatoes.
Finely mince 2 cloves garlic.
In a separate small pan, heat 100ml olive oil with minced garlic over low heat for 5 minutes to infuse. Do not brown garlic.
Drain pasta, reserving 100ml pasta water.
Add cooked pasta to the pan with warm fermented tomato sauce.
Add chopped fresh tomatoes and half of the fresh basil, torn.
Toss well, adding reserved pasta water as needed to create a saucy consistency.
Serve pasta immediately. Top each portion with roasted broccoli florets and stem slices.
Drizzle with garlic-infused olive oil. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and crispy broccoli leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pineapple Sea Buckthorn Caramel Cake
recipes.special_requests: Make me a cake with pineapple, sea buckthorn and fish sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant slice of Pineapple Sea Buckthorn Caramel Cake is presented on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The cake features two distinct, golden-brown cake layers, subtly studded with small, baked pineapple cubes. Between the layers, a vibrant, glossy orange sea buckthorn curd provides a striking color contrast. The top of the cake slice is artfully drizzled with a rich, amber-hued fish sauce caramel, which glistens under natural, even light. A few fresh sea buckthorn berries, bright orange and spherical, are delicately placed alongside the slice as a garnish. The entire plate is visible, showcasing moderate negative space around the cake. In the background, a whole round cake on a simple, light-colored cake stand, and a neatly folded white cotton napkin are visible on a natural wooden table surface, creating a clean, modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake pan.
Combine flour, 180g granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Add 120g softened butter, 2 eggs, and milk to dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in finely diced pineapple. Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. Cool completely on a wire rack.
For Sea Buckthorn Curd: Whisk sea buckthorn puree, 80g granulated sugar, and egg yolks in a heatproof bowl set over a pot of simmering water. Do not let the bowl touch the water.
Stir constantly until the mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon (approximately 8-10 minutes). Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in 50g cubed butter until completely melted and smooth. Chill the curd completely in the refrigerator.
For Fish Sauce Caramel: In a medium saucepan, melt 100g granulated sugar over medium heat until it turns a golden amber color. Do not stir, just swirl the pan gently.
Carefully pour in the warm heavy cream (it will bubble vigorously). Stir well until smooth.
