Beside the bowl, a neatly folded white cotton napkin and a piece of crusty rustic bread (pan de pueblo) are arranged. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, highlighting the textures and warm colors of the stew against a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
A simple green salad on the side.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (waxy, e.g., Desiree or Yukon Gold)

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add chopped onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic, paprika, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer for 2 minutes until reduced slightly.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, and bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5 hours, or until beef is nearly tender.
Add potato cubes to the pot. Stir gently to combine.
Cover and continue to simmer for another 30-40 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and the sauce has thickened.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. Remove bay leaves before serving.
notes: Browning the beef properly adds depth of flavor.
Adjust the consistency of the stew by simmering longer for a thicker sauce, or adding a splash more broth if too thick.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken and Tomato Skillet with Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of al dente pasta forms the base, topped with a rich, rustic deep-red tomato sauce. Thick, irregularly cut chunks of golden-brown seared chicken are nestled within the sauce. Vibrant green fresh basil leaves are scattered over the top, along with a dusting of pale grated Parmesan cheese. The dish is presented on a sturdy, slightly imperfect ceramic plate, sitting on a well-used wooden dining table in a warm, cozy home kitchen. A simple cloth napkin is casually placed beside the plate. The lighting is natural and inviting, creating a relaxed family dining atmosphere. The overall presentation is homely and comforting, with components touching and overlapping naturally, showcasing the hearty texture of the sauce and tender chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad.
instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides, about 4-5 minutes per side. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through.
While chicken simmers, cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain thoroughly.
Remove chicken from sauce. Cut or shred chicken into thick, irregular chunks.
Stir fresh basil into the tomato sauce.
Serve sauce and chicken over cooked pasta. Garnish generously with grated Parmesan.
notes: Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
For a deeper flavor, use bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and remove skin before cutting.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and glistening, rests centrally on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. Around the chicken, a rustic scattering of roasted potato chunks and vibrant green broccoli florets creates a natural, unarranged look. The potato chunks are golden-edged with some browned spots, while the broccoli maintains a bright green hue with slightly charred tips. Smashed garlic cloves and a few thin, caramelized lemon slices are interspersed among the vegetables. Components touch and overlap naturally, conveying a comforting, home-cooked feel. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple cloth napkin is casually folded beside the plate. Standard metal flatware is present. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The background shows a relaxed family dining area with minimal, natural clutter, suggesting a lived-in atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and pat dry chicken thighs. Season chicken generously with salt, pepper, and half of the dried herbs.
Wash potatoes. Cut larger potatoes into 2-3 cm chunks or wedges. Leave small potatoes whole.
Peel garlic cloves. Smash lightly.
In a large bowl, combine potatoes, broccoli florets, smashed garlic, olive oil, remaining dried herbs, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange chicken thighs on a large baking tray. Scatter seasoned potatoes and broccoli around the chicken. Ensure vegetables are in a single layer for even roasting.
Slice half of the lemon into thin rounds. Place lemon slices over and around chicken and vegetables. Squeeze juice from the other half of the lemon over everything.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip chicken and stir vegetables. Continue roasting for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender and lightly browned.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Cooking time may vary based on oven and chicken piece size. Use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken is cooked through.
For extra flavor, marinate chicken for at least 30 minutes or overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Coconut Pineapple Pumpkin Soup
recipes.special_requests: Make me a very tasty and interesting soup with boiled pineapple and pumpkin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant Thai Coconut Pineapple Pumpkin Soup is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The soup, a smooth, creamy orange hue, has a balanced consistency – not too thick, not too thin. Floating on top are a few small, golden-brown roasted pineapple cubes, adding a caramelized sweetness and textural contrast. A delicate swirl of rich coconut cream adorns the surface, and fresh, bright green cilantro leaves are scattered artfully for a pop of color and herbaceous aroma. The bowl is centered on a simple, light wooden table surface. Beside it rests a traditional polished metal Thai soup spoon, and a small, pristine white bowl of fluffy jasmine rice. A folded natural cotton napkin completes the casual yet refined bistro setting. Natural, soft, even lighting highlights the soup's warm tones and inviting textures, creating an authentic and appealing visual.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a small dish of 'Prik Nam Pla' (fish sauce with sliced chilies and lime juice) for those who prefer extra heat and tang.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.quantity: 1 stalk, bruised and cut into 3 pieces

instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add red curry paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to bloom the flavors.
Add diced pumpkin and most of the diced pineapple (reserve about 50g for garnish). Stir to coat with the curry paste.
Pour in vegetable broth and coconut milk. Add bruised lemongrass pieces. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until pumpkin is very tender.
Remove lemongrass pieces from the pot. Use an immersion blender to blend the soup until smooth. Alternatively, carefully transfer to a blender and blend in batches.
Return soup to the pot. Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and brown sugar. Season with salt to taste. Adjust flavors as needed (more fish sauce for savory, lime for sour, sugar for sweet).
While soup simmers, quickly roast the reserved pineapple pieces in a dry pan or small oven until lightly caramelized for garnish.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with roasted pineapple cubes and fresh cilantro leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: For a richer flavor, you can roast the pumpkin pieces before adding them to the soup.
traditional_techniques: Balancing the four fundamental Thai flavors: sweet, sour, salty, and spicy.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Cod with Cherry Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centrally composed. A perfectly seared cod fillet, its skin golden-brown and slightly crisp, sits as the focal point. The cod is a whole, thick piece, flaky and white inside. Beside it, a vibrant mound of cherry tomato confit glistens. The confit features burst, soft red cherry tomato halves, interspersed with dark, glossy Kalamata olive halves and small, briny capers. Thin slices of golden-brown roasted garlic are visible throughout the confit, all coated in a rich, amber olive oil. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered artfully over the confit and cod, providing a fresh contrast. The overall color palette is warm reds, deep greens, and crisp white, with inviting textures. Moderate negative space surrounds the dish. The setting is a modern bistro table with a simple wooden surface, a white cotton napkin folded beside the plate, and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the freshness of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread to absorb the rich confit oils.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with lemon and olive oil.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Combine halved cherry tomatoes, sliced garlic, 60ml olive oil, salt, and pepper in a baking dish.
Roast for 30-40 minutes. Tomatoes should be soft and slightly burst.
Remove from oven. Stir in pitted olives, capers, and remaining 40ml olive oil. Add white wine if using. Keep warm.
Pat cod fillets dry with paper towels. Season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place cod fillets skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip cod fillets. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until fish is opaque and flakes easily.
To serve, place a cod fillet on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of cherry tomato confit next to or over the cod.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Mole Poblano with Corn-Lime Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rich Chicken Mole Poblano is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, set on a simple wooden table. The chicken thigh, cooked whole and tender, is generously coated in a deep, glossy dark brown mole sauce. The sauce exhibits subtle specks of toasted sesame seeds. Adjacent to the chicken, a neat scoop of fluffy, white corn-lime rice is placed, showcasing vibrant yellow corn kernels and flecks of fresh green cilantro. A small, vibrant side salad of crisp mixed greens and thinly sliced red onion provides a fresh contrast. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds over the mole and a lime wedge placed beside the chicken. The overall composition is balanced and professional, with appropriate negative space, illuminated by natural, even lighting that highlights the textures and colors of the ingredients. A cotton napkin and traditional flatware complete the modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Extra lime wedges
A side of pickled red onions
instructions: Toast dried chilies in a dry pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Do not burn. Remove stems and seeds. Rehydrate chilies in hot water for 20 minutes. Drain.
In a large pot, heat 15 ml vegetable oil. Brown chicken thighs on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside. Season with salt and pepper.
In the same pot, add tomatoes, tomatillos, onion, garlic, almonds, sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, and torn tortilla. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly browned.

Add rehydrated chilies to the pot. Cook for 2 minutes. Transfer all ingredients to a blender. Add 250 ml chicken broth and blend until very smooth. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl, pressing solids to extract liquid.

Clean the pot. Heat remaining 15 ml vegetable oil. Pour the strained mole sauce into the pot. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly to prevent sticking. Cook for 15 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken and flavors to meld. Add chopped dark chocolate, stir until melted and incorporated.

Return browned chicken to the mole sauce. Add remaining chicken broth. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender. Stir occasionally.

While mole cooks, prepare rice. Rinse rice thoroughly. In a saucepan, combine rice, 500 ml water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Stir in corn kernels, cover, and let steam for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork. Stir in half of the chopped cilantro and half of the lime juice.
Prepare salad: Combine mixed greens and thinly sliced red onion in a bowl. Dress with olive oil, remaining lime juice, salt, and pepper.

To serve, place a portion of corn-lime rice on a white porcelain plate. Arrange a chicken thigh next to the rice. Spoon generous amount of mole sauce over the chicken. Garnish with a sprinkle of sesame seeds and fresh cilantro. Serve with a side of crisp green salad and lime wedges.
notes: The depth of flavor in mole comes from the careful toasting and rehydration of chilies and other ingredients. Do not rush this process.
Authentic mole can take hours; this recipe offers a more approachable version while retaining traditional flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Spanish chicken and rice served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice is moist and fluid, colored a vibrant golden-orange from the smoked paprika and broth. Thick 4cm chunks of seared chicken thighs are nestled into the rice, showing a crisp, dark golden-brown exterior. Small dices of softened red bell pepper and translucent onions are evenly distributed throughout the grains. The dish is finished with a scatter of bright green chopped parsley. A single yellow lemon wedge sits on the side of the plate. The background features a rustic wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and natural side-lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional terracotta cazuela
Accompany with crusty bread and aioli
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine like Albariño

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, and half the paprika.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 5 minutes until golden. Remove from pan.
Add onion and red pepper to the same pan. Sauté until softened.
Stir in garlic and remaining paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 18 minutes. Do not stir.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Use short-grain rice to ensure the correct starchy consistency.
Avoid stirring the rice once the broth is added to allow a slight crust to form.
Ensure the broth is hot before adding it to the pan to maintain cooking temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Chicken, Pumpkin, and Pineapple Soup
recipes.special_requests: Make me a very tasty and interesting soup with boiled pineapple and pumpkin
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of vibrant, creamy Thai Chicken, Pumpkin, and Pineapple Soup is presented in a deep, clean white ceramic bowl. The soup is a rich, inviting orange-yellow hue. Tender, 2cm diced chicken pieces are nestled amongst soft 2.5cm pumpkin cubes and bright 2cm pineapple chunks, creating a textural and color contrast. The surface is garnished with a generous scattering of fresh, bright green coriander leaves and a few thin, vivid red chili slices. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a white cotton napkin and a sleek ceramic soup spoon. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and comforting steam. The background suggests a modern bistro, subtly blurred to keep focus on the elegant, culturally authentic presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of steamed jasmine rice.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Peel and dice butternut pumpkin into 2.5 cm cubes. Peel and core pineapple, then cut into 2 cm chunks.
Finely mince ginger and garlic. Bruise lemongrass stalk with the back of a knife.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add red curry paste. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in minced ginger and garlic. Cook for another 30 seconds.
Add chicken cubes to the pot. Cook until lightly browned on all sides, about 3-4 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Pour in coconut milk and chicken broth. Add diced pumpkin, bruised lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves.
Bring the soup to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until pumpkin is tender.
Stir in pineapple chunks. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing pineapple to heat through and soften slightly.
Remove lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves. Season the soup with fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed.
Ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and thin slices of red chilies.
traditional_techniques: Balancing sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Vietnamese Sour Fish and Pineapple Soup (Canh Chua Ca)
recipes.special_requests: Make me a very tasty and interesting soup with boiled pineapple
recipes.visual_description: The soup is presented in a clean, white ceramic bowl, showcasing a vibrant medley of colors and textures. Large, golden-yellow pineapple wedges are prominently featured, their cooked edges slightly softened. Tender, white fish chunks are nestled among them. Bright red tomato wedges and green okra rounds add pops of color. The clear, amber-hued broth shimmers, indicating a well-balanced sour and sweet flavor. A generous, fresh garnish of thinly sliced green onion, cilantro, sawtooth coriander, and rice paddy herb floats on top, adding a fresh, aromatic contrast. A scattering of crispy fried garlic bits and a drizzle of golden garlic oil complete the presentation. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin and a pair of traditional chopsticks beside it.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Offer a side of nuoc cham (fish sauce with chili) for dipping or extra seasoning

ingredients.name: White fish fillets (e.g., basa, catfish, cod)
Fresh pineapple
ingredients.quantity: 300g, peeled, cored, cut into 1.5cm thick wedges

ingredients.name: Fresh herbs for garnish (sawtooth coriander, rice paddy herb, cilantro, green onion)

instructions: Prepare fish: Season fish chunks lightly with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Prepare tamarind: Dissolve tamarind pulp in 100ml hot water. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract liquid. Discard solids.
Sauté aromatics: Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add shallot and 3 cloves thinly sliced garlic. Sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute. Do not brown.
Add liquid and pineapple: Pour in water or fish stock. Bring to a boil. Add pineapple wedges. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Season soup base: Stir in strained tamarind liquid, sugar, and fish sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. The soup should be a balance of sour, sweet, and savory.

Cook vegetables and fish: Add okra and tomatoes to the soup. Simmer for 3 minutes. Gently add fish chunks. Cook until fish is just opaque and cooked through, about 3-5 minutes depending on thickness. Fish should reach 75°C (167°F). Do not overcook.
Add bean sprouts: Stir in bean sprouts just before serving. Cook for 1 minute until slightly wilted.

Prepare fried garlic oil: While soup simmers, heat 15ml vegetable oil in a small pan. Add 2 cloves minced garlic. Fry until golden brown and crispy. Remove garlic with a slotted spoon. Set aside oil and crispy garlic.
Serve: Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish generously with fresh herbs, sliced chilies (if using), a drizzle of fried garlic oil, and crispy fried garlic bits.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Chicken and Carrot Tagine
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Moroccan Chicken and Carrot Tagine is presented in a traditional, rustic ceramic tagine base, showcasing the rich, savory stew. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh sits centrally, surrounded by vibrant orange, thick-cut carrot rounds and pieces of diced tomato. The chicken is tender, falling off the bone. The thick sauce, infused with warm spices, coats all ingredients. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped cilantro and parsley adds a pop of color and freshness. A thinly sliced piece of preserved lemon rind rests beside the chicken. The dish is set on a simple light wooden table. A patterned Moroccan-style napkin is folded beside the tagine. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors. The background is soft and uncluttered.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty Moroccan bread (khobz) for scooping the sauce.
Offer a side of plain couscous to accompany the tagine.
Provide a small bowl of harissa for those desiring extra heat.
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in ground cumin, ground coriander, ground turmeric, sweet paprika, ground cinnamon, and saffron threads. Cook spices for 1 minute until aromatic.
Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and thick-cut carrot rounds to the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in the liquid. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in chopped fresh cilantro, fresh parsley, and thinly sliced preserved lemon rind. Cook for 2 minutes more.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Spicy Chicken Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Korean Spicy Chicken Rice Bowl is presented in a deep, matte black ceramic bowl, centered on a light wooden table. Fluffy, pearly white short-grain rice forms the base. Generous, irregularly cut 3 cm chunks of pan-seared chicken thighs, cooked to a rich reddish-brown from the gochujang marinade, are arranged naturally atop the rice. Translucent, slightly caramelized thin onion wedges are interspersed. A glossy, deep red-orange sauce lightly coats the chicken and seeps into the rice. The dish is vibrantly garnished with thinly sliced bright green scallion rings and pale golden toasted sesame seeds. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. Beside the bowl, dark wooden chopsticks rest on a simple ceramic chopstick rest. A folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors. The background is a soft, blurred restaurant setting, focusing on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with small side dishes (banchan) such as kimchi or pickled radish.
Offer additional gochujang or sriracha on the side for those who prefer extra heat.
Traditionally eaten with chopsticks and a spoon for the rice and sauce.
instructions: Rinse 400g short-grain rice until water runs clear. Cook with 500ml water in a rice cooker or pot.
In a bowl, combine 60ml soy sauce, 80g gochujang, 30g sugar, 15ml sesame oil, 4 minced garlic cloves, and 15g grated ginger. Mix well.
Add 700g chicken chunks to the marinade. Toss to coat. Marinate for at least 20 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.

Heat 30ml cooking oil in a large non-stick pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken. Cook for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until chicken is browned and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add sliced onion wedges to the pan with the chicken. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until onions soften slightly and become translucent.
Divide cooked rice among 4 individual serving bowls. Spoon generous portions of the spicy chicken and onion mixture over the rice.
Garnish each bowl with thinly sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust gochujang quantity for desired spice level.
Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C for safety.
traditional_techniques: Marinating with gochujang for flavor depth

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beer-Braised Chicken with Rice is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, with its skin crisped, is positioned slightly off-center. Generous scoops of fluffy, white long-grain rice are mounded beside the chicken. A rich, amber-brown sauce, studded with diced red bell pepper, golden corn kernels, and earthy sliced mushrooms, generously coats the chicken and pools around the rice. The vibrant green of freshly chopped basil leaves is scattered over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The textures are varied: tender chicken, soft rice, and slightly firm vegetables. The overall presentation is warm, inviting, and truly homely, under cozy kitchen lighting, with a simple cloth napkin folded casually nearby.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt, black pepper, and dried thyme.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crisp, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onion, diced red bell pepper, and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and start to brown, about 7 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes and Dijon mustard. Stir well.
Pour in 330ml beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nesting them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

While chicken braises, cook rice: Combine 250g long-grain rice with 500ml chicken stock and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
After 30 minutes, stir in 150g corn kernels and most of the chopped fresh basil into the braising liquid. Simmer uncovered for 5 more minutes.
Squeeze juice from 1/2 lemon over the chicken and sauce.
Serve chicken and sauce over fluffy rice. Garnish with remaining fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Pineapple Chicken Soup
recipes.special_requests: Make me a very tasty and interesting soup with boiled pineapple
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Thai Pineapple Chicken Soup is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The clear, light golden broth reveals tender 2.5 cm chicken cubes, bright yellow 2 cm pineapple chunks, halved red cherry tomatoes, and pale straw mushrooms. Green kaffir lime leaves and sliced galangal are visible. The soup is garnished generously with vibrant green cilantro leaves and thinly sliced green onions floating on top, adding a fresh contrast. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table with a natural grain. A white cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. A traditional ceramic Thai soup spoon rests in the bowl. A small, round white bowl of fluffy steamed jasmine rice is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and balanced colors in a clean, inviting restaurant-style setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a side of prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies) for extra heat.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2.5 cm cubes. Peel and cut pineapple into 2 cm chunks. Halve cherry tomatoes. Slice straw mushrooms.
Thinly slice galangal. Bruise lemongrass stalks with the back of a knife. Tear kaffir lime leaves.
Slice shallots and garlic. Thinly slice bird's eye chilies.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add sliced shallots, garlic, and chilies. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken cubes to the pot. Brown chicken lightly for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Add galangal, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and pineapple chunks. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer for 10-12 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through to 75°C internal temperature.
Add cherry tomatoes and straw mushrooms. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and thinly sliced green onions.
notes: Taste and adjust seasoning; the balance of sour, sweet, salty, and spicy is key to authentic Thai flavor.
Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
traditional_techniques: Balancing the four fundamental Thai flavors (sour, sweet, salty, spicy)
Bruising aromatics (lemongrass, galangal) to release flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Bolognese with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of rich, deep red-brown Bolognese ragu generously coats wide, golden pappardelle pasta, naturally twirled on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Visible are tender chunks of browned ground beef, small vibrant orange carrot cubes, and green celery flecks interspersed within the luscious sauce. Freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano lightly dusts the top, with a few bright green basil leaves artfully placed for a vibrant contrast. The sauce clings perfectly to the al dente pasta, appearing moist and inviting. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded, off-white cotton napkin is placed to the left. A traditional silver fork and spoon are to the right. Natural, even lighting creates a warm, inviting atmosphere, hinting at a modern Italian bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese at the table.
Pair with a robust red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes. This is your soffritto.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add ground beef. Break up the meat with a spoon. Brown beef thoroughly, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine mostly evaporates, about 5 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, whole milk, dried oregano, and bay leaf. Season with salt and black pepper.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for at least 2 hours, stirring occasionally. Simmer longer for richer flavor, up to 3 hours.
Remove bay leaf before serving.
Cook pappardelle pasta according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta directly to the Bolognese sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Carrot & Fermented Coconut Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Carrot & Fermented Coconut Salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. Long, vibrant orange carrot ribbons are loosely intertwined with thin, translucent red onion rings, both lightly glossy from pickling. Fresh, dark green spinach leaves form a bed, interspersed with crisp, bright green cucumber rounds and delicate pink radish slices. The creamy, off-white fermented coconut dressing is lightly drizzled and coats the ingredients, showcasing their natural textures. A scattering of golden-brown toasted coconut flakes adds a contrasting texture and warm color. The arrangement is natural and unforced, allowing each ingredient’s shape and color to be visible. The plate is centered on a light bamboo table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually placed to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the freshness of the ingredients. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery visible, emphasizing the eco-conscious and ingredient-focused presentation.

ingredients.name: Unsweetened fermented coconut yogurt or kefir

instructions: Prepare the pickling brine: Combine vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in a small saucepan. Heat until sugar and salt dissolve. Let cool completely.
Prepare vegetables for pickling: Peel carrots. Use a vegetable peeler to create long, thin carrot ribbons. Thinly slice red onion into rings. Place carrot ribbons and red onion into a clean jar.
Pour cooled brine over carrots and red onion. Ensure vegetables are submerged. Seal the jar. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or up to 1 week.
Prepare remaining vegetables: Thinly slice cucumber into rounds. Thinly slice radishes into rounds.
Make the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together fermented coconut yogurt or kefir, lime juice, sesame oil, grated ginger, and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Assemble the salad: In a large bowl, combine fresh spinach, sliced cucumber, and sliced radishes. Add pickled carrot ribbons and red onion, draining excess brine.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to coat all vegetables.
Divide salad among four plates. Garnish each serving with toasted coconut flakes.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Spiced Chicken with Smoky Chili Couscous
recipes.visual_description: The Moroccan Spiced Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A mound of golden, fluffy couscous forms the base. Succulent, tender chicken chunks, browned from searing, are arranged atop the couscous. A rich, reddish-brown, aromatic sauce generously coats the chicken and pools slightly around the couscous. Scattered artfully over the dish are vibrant green sprigs of fresh cilantro and a few charred red onion wedges and red bell pepper strips, adding color and texture. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits on the side of the plate. The composition is balanced, leaving moderate negative space to highlight the dish. The scene is set on a simple light wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and traditional flatware positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere typical of a modern bistro.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm khobz (Moroccan bread) for dipping into the sauce.
Offer a small side of harissa for those who prefer extra heat.
Accompany with a simple fresh salad of cucumber and tomato.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced red onion (reserving a few wedges for garnish) and red bell pepper (reserving a few strips for garnish). Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and minced chipotle chile. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in ground cumin, ground coriander, smoked paprika, turmeric, and ground ginger. Cook 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and tender. Internal temperature of chicken should reach 75°C.

While chicken simmers, prepare couscous. Place couscous in a heatproof bowl. Bring 250 ml water or chicken stock to a boil. Pour hot liquid over couscous. Cover bowl tightly with a lid or plastic wrap. Let stand 5 minutes until liquid is absorbed. Fluff couscous with a fork.
For garnish, lightly char or roast reserved red onion wedges and red bell pepper strips. Use a dry pan or small oven broiler.
Stir half of the chopped fresh cilantro into the chicken stew.

To serve, spoon a generous portion of fluffy couscous onto each plate. Arrange chicken chunks and a ladle of rich sauce over the couscous. Garnish with charred onion wedges, bell pepper strips, remaining fresh cilantro, and a lemon wedge.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The chipotle chile adds a smoky depth; adjust quantity based on desired heat level.

recipes.recipe_name: Cucumber & Savory Beef Salad
recipes.special_requests: make beef mince the main protein. not shepherds pie. surprise me with something a bit different.
recipes.visual_description: A homely, generous portion of warm Cucumber & Savory Beef Salad is presented on an everyday ceramic plate, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A bed of vibrant green baby spinach leaves forms the base. Warm, browned beef mince, cooked with minced garlic and thinly sliced red onion, is spooned over the spinach. Scattered amongst the beef are bright red diced tomatoes and crisp green diced cucumber, adding fresh contrast. The salad is drizzled with a zesty lime-coriander dressing, pooling slightly on the plate. Visible are flecks of chopped fresh coriander and optional red chili. The presentation is natural and unpretentious, as if served at a family meal. A simple fork rests beside the plate. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting appeal.
instructions: Prepare vegetables: Dice the cucumber into 1 cm cubes. Dice the tomatoes into 1 cm cubes. Thinly slice the red onion. Mince the garlic cloves. Roughly chop the fresh coriander. Finely chop the red chili, if using.

Cook beef: Heat 30 ml of olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the beef mincemeat. Break apart the mince with a spoon and cook until fully browned and no pink remains. Drain any excess fat from the pan.

Add aromatics: Stir the minced garlic and thinly sliced red onion into the cooked beef. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the onion softens and becomes fragrant. Season the beef mixture generously with salt and black pepper.

Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together the juice from both limes, the remaining 30 ml of olive oil, the chopped coriander, and the chopped chili (if using). Season the dressing with salt and black pepper to taste.

Assemble salad: Divide the fresh baby spinach leaves among four individual plates or arrange them on a large serving platter. Top the spinach with the diced cucumber and diced tomatoes. Spoon the warm beef mixture evenly over the vegetables.
Dress and serve: Drizzle the prepared lime-coriander dressing generously over each salad portion. Serve immediately while the beef is still warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Mexican Crab Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Spicy Mexican Crab Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The stew is a rich, inviting red-orange, showcasing substantial white crab chunks, vibrant green diced bell pepper, and thin slices of jalapeno. The stew has a comforting, fluid consistency, not overly thick. Fresh, chopped cilantro leaves are scattered casually over the top. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. Beside the bowl, a small stack of warm corn tortillas is nestled in a simple cloth napkin. A small ceramic dish holds several bright green lime wedges. A sturdy, everyday ceramic spoon rests on the table next to the bowl. The scene is bathed in warm, soft light, characteristic of a homely family kitchen, with a hint of natural clutter in the background, suggesting a lived-in atmosphere. The overall presentation is natural and unpretentious, focusing on the hearty appeal of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping the stew.
Offer extra lime wedges for a fresh citrus squeeze.
Accompany with a side of Mexican rice or refried beans.
instructions: Clean crab sections. Cut into manageable pieces if large.
Dice onion, red bell pepper. Mince garlic. Thinly slice jalapeno chiles, remove seeds for less heat.
Dice tomatoes or use crushed canned tomatoes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, bell pepper, and sliced jalapeno. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, beer, and broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes to meld flavors.
Add crab pieces to the pot. Ensure crab is submerged in the liquid.
Cover and continue to simmer for 8-10 minutes, or until crab is cooked through and opaque.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Finely chop fresh cilantro for garnish. Cut lime into wedges.
Serve the stew hot, garnished with fresh cilantro and lime wedges on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Red Wine Stew
recipes.visual_description: A generous, hearty portion of rich Beef and Red Wine Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The beef chunks are dark brown, substantial, and look fork-tender. Vibrant orange carrot chunks and creamy yellow potato chunks are softened but hold their shape. The stew's sauce is a glossy, dark red-brown, thick and rich, coating all ingredients. Components are naturally arranged, with some beef and vegetables peeking out from the sauce. A sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley rests on top, adding a pop of color. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen setting. A simple, plain white ceramic side plate holds a thick slice of crusty bread. A casually placed linen cloth napkin and a dark-colored fork and spoon complete the scene. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the dish, creating a lived-in, inviting atmosphere. The background is subtly blurred to keep focus on the food while hinting at a comfortable kitchen environment. The beef is presented as whole braised chunks, not sliced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices for dipping
Accompany with a simple green salad with vinaigrette
instructions: Cut beef into 4-5 cm chunks. Pat beef dry. Season beef with salt and pepper. Dredge beef lightly in flour.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onions to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze the pot with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes to reduce slightly.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 1.5-2 hours, or until beef is tender. Stir occasionally.
Meanwhile, peel and chop carrots into 2-3 cm chunks. Peel and chop potatoes into 3-4 cm chunks.
After 1.5-2 hours, add carrots and potatoes to the pot.
Continue simmering, covered, for another 30-45 minutes, or until vegetables are tender and sauce has thickened.
Check beef for tenderness. It should be fork-tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best flavor, prepare the stew a day in advance; flavors deepen overnight.
Adjust sauce consistency by simmering longer for a thicker sauce, or adding more broth if too thick.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy chicken and mushroom pasta rests in a round, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown, 2 cm seared chicken cubes are nestled amongst the al dente pasta strands, which are thoroughly coated in a rich, pale cream sauce. Sliced, earthy brown mushrooms are interspersed throughout, adding depth. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley provides a pop of color on top. The dish is presented casually, as if just served from the stove, with the pasta naturally piled. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a plain cloth napkin, emphasizing the homely, unpretentious comfort of the meal.
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Pat chicken breast cut into 2 cm cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Add cooked chicken back to the pan with the sauce. Add drained pasta. Toss to coat everything evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Italian Sausage and Tomato Soup with Fresh Cucumber
recipes.special_requests: make a dish using only these 4 ingredients and spices
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Italian Sausage and Tomato Soup is presented in a deep, clean white ceramic bowl, resting on a simple light wooden table surface. The soup is a warm, inviting reddish-orange hue, showcasing a rich tomato base. Irregular, rustic chunks of browned Italian sausage are visible throughout the broth, providing hearty texture. Small, vibrant green diced cucumber cubes are scattered on top, adding a fresh, crisp contrast to the warm soup. A few fresh, whole basil leaves are artfully placed on the surface as a garnish, contributing a pop of green. The bowl is positioned slightly off-center, with ample negative space. A folded white cotton napkin lies to the side, completing the modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, creating an appealing and approachable presentation.
instructions: Remove sausage from casings. Crumble sausage into a large pot or Dutch oven. Cook over medium-high heat until browned. Break up large pieces with a spoon. Drain excess fat. Remove sausage from pot; set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add olive oil and butter to the pot. Add diced yellow onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return cooked sausage to the pot. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
While soup simmers, peel and dice cucumber into small cubes.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Top each serving with fresh diced cucumber and fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Tomato and Green Beans
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. On one side, tender braised chicken chunks, rich reddish-brown from the sauce, are nestled among vibrant red quartered tomatoes and bright green crisp-tender green beans. The chicken pieces are whole, not sliced. The sauce is glossy and coats the ingredients. Adjacent to the chicken, a neat mound of fluffy, white steamed rice is perfectly portioned. The dish is garnished with freshly chopped bright green scallions scattered over the chicken and vegetables. The overall presentation is balanced, clean, and inviting. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table. Chopsticks are placed neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the food, highlighting its textures and colors, with a soft focus background showing a subtle, casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve family-style with other shared dishes
Offer a small bowl of clear broth soup on the side
instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly. Cook rice in a rice cooker or pot according to package directions. Set aside.
Cut chicken thighs into 4-5 cm chunks. Quarter tomatoes. Trim ends off green beans. Mince garlic and ginger. Slice scallions for garnish.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the hot oil. Sear until lightly browned on all sides. Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.
Add minced garlic and ginger to the wok. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add quartered tomatoes to the wok. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Return chicken to the wok. Add Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, and chicken broth.
Bring to a simmer. Cover the wok. Reduce heat to medium-low. Braise for 15 minutes.
Add green beans to the wok. Stir gently. Continue to braise, uncovered, for another 5-7 minutes, until chicken is cooked through to 75°C (167°F) and green beans are tender-crisp.
In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with 2 tablespoons of water to create a slurry. Pour slurry into the simmering sauce. Stir constantly until sauce thickens to desired consistency.
Serve braised chicken and vegetables alongside steamed white rice. Garnish generously with fresh scallions.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Cucumber and Chorizo Salad with Roasted Tomatoes
recipes.special_requests: make a dish using only these 4 ingredients and spices
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, showcasing a vibrant mix of colors and textures. Diced bright green cucumber cubes form the base, interspersed with softened, rich red roasted cherry tomato halves and quarters. Small, crispy cubes of dark red chorizo are scattered throughout, adding a savory depth and textural contrast. Fresh, finely chopped flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled generously over the top, providing a verdant garnish. A glossy sherry vinaigrette lightly coats all components, enhancing their natural sheen. The arrangement is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a light wooden table surface, suggesting a casual bistro setting. A simple white cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's freshness and visual appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the flavorful dressing.
Enjoy as a light tapa or a refreshing side dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast tomatoes for 15-20 minutes, until slightly softened and caramelized. Remove and let cool.
Dice the chorizo sausage into 1 cm cubes. Heat a large pan over medium heat. Add chorizo cubes. Cook until crispy and fat is rendered, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Melt butter in a small saucepan. Whisk in minced garlic, sherry vinegar, remaining 45 ml olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Set aside.
Dice cucumbers into 1 cm cubes. In a large bowl, combine diced cucumber, roasted tomatoes, and cooked chorizo cubes.
Pour the dressing over the salad mixture. Add chopped fresh parsley. Gently toss to combine all ingredients.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Cheesy Southwestern Chicken, Rice, and Pasta Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of One-Pan Cheesy Southwestern Chicken, Rice, and Pasta Skillet is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, are nestled among tender long-grain white rice and small pasta shapes. Diced red and green bell peppers, about 1 cm, and diced yellow onion add vibrant color. The dish is coated and bound by glistening, melted golden-orange cheddar cheese. Fresh, bright green chopped cilantro provides a refreshing top garnish. The presentation is cohesive and balanced, with appropriate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors, creating an inviting, casual restaurant-style atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a well-proportioned individual serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm flour tortillas or corn chips for scooping.
Offer a side of salsa or sour cream for individual customization.

ingredients.name: Small pasta (e.g., ditalini or elbow macaroni)

instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the skillet. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add diced onion and bell peppers to the same skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, chili powder, and cumin. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chicken broth and undrained diced tomatoes. Bring mixture to a simmer.

Add rice and pasta to the skillet. Stir well. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until rice and pasta are tender and most liquid is absorbed. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Stir in 150g of the shredded cheddar cheese until melted and well combined.
Return cooked chicken chunks to the skillet. Stir gently to combine.

Sprinkle remaining 50g shredded cheddar cheese over the top of the skillet. If not oven-safe, transfer to a baking dish. Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 5-7 minutes, or until cheese is bubbly and melted.
Remove from oven. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.
notes: Adjust chili powder and cumin to your preferred spice level.
For extra richness, a tablespoon of butter can be added with the cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Spinach and Thai Spiced Beef Salad
recipes.special_requests: make beef mince the main protein. not shepherds pie. surprise me with something a bit different.
recipes.visual_description: The Spinach and Thai Spiced Beef Salad is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing its vibrant colors and textures. A generous bed of fresh, dark green spinach forms the base. Scattered atop are bright orange julienned carrots, translucent half-moon cucumber slices, and ruby red diced tomatoes, interspersed with delicate rings of thinly sliced red onion. Central to the composition is a mound of richly browned beef mince, its crumbly texture providing a savory anchor. A creamy, pale tan peanut-lime dressing is artfully drizzled over the entire salad, creating subtle trails and pooling gently at the bottom. The dish is garnished with a generous scattering of bright green chopped coriander, adding freshness and aromatic contrast. The arrangement is balanced, allowing each component's color and form to be appreciated, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, set in a modern bistro style.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed jasmine rice.
Offer extra lime wedges for individual seasoning.
Traditionally eaten with a fork and spoon, using the spoon to scoop and the fork to push food onto the spoon.
instructions: Heat coconut oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add 2 cloves minced garlic, grated ginger, and 1/2 chopped chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add beef mincemeat to the pan. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned and fully cooked through. Drain any excess fat.
Stir in 1 tablespoon lime juice and soy sauce. Mix well. Set aside to cool slightly.
In a small bowl, whisk together peanut butter, coconut cream, 45ml lime juice, honey/maple syrup, soy sauce, 1 clove minced garlic, and 1/2 chopped chili (if using).
Gradually add warm water, whisking until the dressing is smooth and pourable. Adjust consistency as needed.
In a large mixing bowl, combine spinach, julienned carrots, thinly sliced cucumber, diced tomatoes, and thinly sliced red onion.
Add the slightly cooled beef mince to the vegetables.
Pour half of the dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to combine, ensuring all ingredients are lightly coated.
Divide the salad among 4 serving plates. Drizzle remaining dressing over each portion. Garnish generously with fresh chopped coriander. Serve immediately.
traditional_techniques: Balancing of sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Pork Loin with Apple-Peach Chutney
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted pork loin is artfully arranged on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pork is cut into two to three thick, tender medallions, displaying a golden-brown crust and a light pink, juicy interior. Beside the pork, a vibrant, chunky spoonful of apple-peach chutney showcases diced fruits in shades of red, yellow, and orange, interspersed with translucent pieces of red onion. A glossy, light amber pan sauce is drizzled elegantly over the pork and around the plate, catching the light. A small, fresh sprig of thyme and a thin, bright yellow lemon slice are positioned as delicate garnishes. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin placed to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere, keeping the focus entirely on the meticulously plated food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat pork loin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork loin on all sides until golden brown, about 3 minutes per side.

Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast pork for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 70°C. Remove from oven, transfer pork to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil and let rest for 10 minutes. Temperature will rise to 75°C.
While pork rests, prepare chutney. Dice apples and peaches into 1 cm cubes. Finely chop red onion, garlic, and ginger.
In a saucepan, heat 10 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add red onion, cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Add garlic and ginger, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Stir in diced apples and peaches. Add apple cider vinegar and brown sugar. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until fruits are tender and liquid has thickened, about 15-20 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

For the pan sauce, return skillet used for pork to stovetop over medium heat. Discard excess fat, leaving browned bits. Pour in chicken stock and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.

Bring stock to a simmer and reduce by half, about 5-7 minutes. Squeeze in juice from half a lemon. Add 2 sprigs of fresh thyme. Stir in butter until melted and sauce is slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Strain sauce if desired for a smoother consistency.
Slice rested pork loin into thick 2 cm medallions. Do not fan slices.

Plate 2-3 pork medallions per serving. Place a generous spoonful of apple-peach chutney beside the pork. Drizzle pan sauce over the pork and around the plate. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig and a thin lemon slice.

recipes.recipe_name: Caribbean Chicken and Black Bean Rice
recipes.visual_description: A generous single portion of Caribbean Chicken and Black Bean Rice is presented on an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic plate. The dish is centrally placed on a rustic, well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen light. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm in size, are nestled among fluffy white long-grain rice and dark, glossy black beans. Diced red bell pepper and onion pieces add pops of color. A scattering of vibrant green chopped fresh cilantro provides a fresh garnish. The components are naturally mixed, showing a comforting, hearty texture. A simple metal fork rests beside the plate. The background features a blurred, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of ripe plantains or sliced avocado.
This dish is often served family-style in a large pot or platter.
Enjoy with a simple green salad.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt, pepper, cumin, oregano, and paprika.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown chicken chunks in batches for 3-4 minutes per side. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened, scraping up any browned bits.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to the pot. Stir well to coat the grains. Cook for 2 minutes.
Return browned chicken chunks to the pot. Add rinsed black beans and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove pot from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice and chicken mixture with a fork. Stir in fresh chopped cilantro.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Baked Chicken with Mozzarella and Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of rustic baked chicken is presented on a round, matte ceramic plate with a slightly uneven, natural texture. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh, cooked whole, sits prominently. Melted, bubbly fresh mozzarella cheese drapes over the chicken and some of the roasted vegetables. Around the chicken, roasted potato wedges with soft interiors and slightly browned edges are nestled alongside burst, juicy cherry tomatoes and tender, caramelized red onion wedges. The potatoes are cut into rustic 2-3 cm wedges. The overall color palette is warm, with deep golden browns, vibrant reds from tomatoes, and creamy white from the cheese, accented by fresh green parsley. The plating is natural and unforced, as if served directly from the baking dish onto a family dinner table. The scene is lit with warm, inviting light, suggesting a cozy kitchen atmosphere. A simple, dark linen napkin and a silver fork are visible beside the plate, hinting at a comfortable home meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread to soak up the pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.

ingredients.name: Medium potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or Red Bliss)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Prepare a large baking dish.
Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges. Halve cherry tomatoes. Slice red onion into thick wedges. Mince garlic.
In the baking dish, combine potato wedges, cherry tomatoes, red onion wedges, and minced garlic.
Drizzle vegetables with 30ml olive oil. Season with 3g salt and 1g black pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Rub chicken with remaining 30ml olive oil. Season chicken generously with remaining 2g salt, 1g black pepper, dried oregano, and dried basil.
Arrange seasoned chicken thighs skin-side up over the vegetables in the baking dish.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender.
While chicken bakes, slice fresh mozzarella into 0.5 cm thick rounds.
Remove baking dish from oven. Arrange mozzarella slices over chicken and vegetables.
Return to oven. Bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and chicken skin is golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Chicken with Spiced Rice and Caramelized Banana
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Moroccan chicken is presented on a round, matte white porcelain plate. Two succulent, braised chicken thighs, rich golden-brown with tender, fall-off-the-bone texture, are nestled on a generous bed of fluffy, white basmati rice. A vibrant, thick sauce, deep orange-red from tomatoes and spices, is spooned generously over the chicken and rice, showcasing visible flecks of diced carrots and herbs. Beside the chicken, three golden-brown caramelized banana slices are arranged neatly, offering a contrasting sweet note. Freshly chopped bright green cilantro and parsley are sprinkled over the dish for a pop of color and freshness. The plate is placed on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A folded off-white linen napkin sits to the side. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish from above, highlighting the textures. The background is subtly blurred, featuring warm, inviting restaurant tones.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm khobz (Moroccan flatbread) for dipping in the sauce.
Offer a small side of green olives or preserved lemons.
Traditionally accompanied by a glass of Moroccan mint tea.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Brown chicken thighs on all sides until golden. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion and diced carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, ground cumin, ground coriander, ground turmeric, ground ginger, cinnamon stick, and sweet paprika. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot. Add canned diced tomatoes, chicken stock, and the juice and zest of one orange. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken cooks, rinse basmati rice. Cook rice according to package directions.
Slice bananas into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Melt butter in a separate pan over medium heat. Add banana slices and cook for 2-3 minutes per side until caramelized and golden.
Stir chopped fresh cilantro and parsley into the chicken tagine. Adjust seasoning.
Serve chicken and sauce over spiced rice. Garnish with caramelized banana slices.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Tomato & Strawberry Cream Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of penne pasta is presented in a clean, round white porcelain pasta bowl. The pasta is coated in a smooth, light orange-red cream sauce, showcasing its glossy texture. Scattered throughout the dish are softened, slightly collapsed halves of roasted cherry tomatoes and smaller, tender pieces of roasted strawberry. Fine, golden-brown strands of caramelized onion are subtly integrated within the pasta. The dish is topped with a generous sprinkle of freshly grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese, with a few vibrant green, whole basil leaves artfully placed for a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is natural and flowing, not rigid, with appropriate negative space in the bowl. The bowl rests on a simple, warm-toned wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating subtle shadows and a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Quarter strawberries.
Spread halved tomatoes and quartered strawberries on a baking tray. Drizzle with 30 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.
While roasting, thinly slice the yellow onion. Mince garlic cloves.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onion. Cook slowly for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden and caramelized.
Add minced garlic to the pan with caramelized onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add penne pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Transfer roasted tomatoes and strawberries to a blender. Add warm milk. Blend until smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Drain cooked pasta, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Add the blended tomato-strawberry sauce to the pan with caramelized onions and garlic. Stir to combine. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Add grated Parmesan cheese. Stir well to coat pasta. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency is reached.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sausages with Roasted Tomatoes and Cucumber Salad
recipes.special_requests: make a dish using only these 4 ingredients and spices
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared sausages, roasted cherry tomatoes, and fresh cucumber salad arranged on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown pan-seared sausages, cooked to perfection, are placed slightly off-center. Beside them, a vibrant cluster of roasted cherry tomato halves, slightly collapsed and caramelized, offers a rich red and orange hue. Opposite the tomatoes, a neat mound of crisp, bright green cucumber half-moons or thick diced pieces glistens from a light dressing. A delicate drizzle of golden-brown butter sauce cascades over the sausages and roasted tomatoes. Fresh green parsley leaves are sparingly scattered for a final touch of color. The setting is a simple wooden table with a white linen napkin and polished silver flatware, under natural, even lighting, featuring a blurred modern bistro background.

ingredients.name: Red wine vinegar or lemon juice

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast tomatoes for 15-20 minutes. They should be slightly softened and caramelized.
Wash cucumber. Cut into half-moons or thick diced pieces. Place in a bowl.
Season cucumber with a pinch of salt and 15ml red wine vinegar or lemon juice. Toss gently.
Melt 50g butter in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add sausages to the pan. Sear until golden brown on all sides.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook sausages until internal temperature reaches 75°C (approx. 15-20 minutes, depending on thickness).
Remove sausages from pan. Keep warm.
Add remaining 50g butter to the same pan. Cook until melted and lightly browned, scraping up any pan drippings.
Plate the dish. Arrange two sausages per plate. Spoon roasted tomatoes alongside.
Place a neat mound of fresh cucumber salad next to the tomatoes.
Drizzle the brown butter sauce over the sausages and roasted tomatoes.
Garnish with fresh parsley or basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Sweet Potato and Kale Salad with Grilled Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, hearty salad presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The base is a generous mix of deep green, finely chopped massaged kale providing a soft, crinkled texture. Scattered throughout are golden-orange roasted sweet potato cubes, each with slightly caramelized edges, offering a tender bite. Interspersed are tender, diced grilled chicken pieces, displaying a light char. Thin slivers of vibrant red onion add a sharp contrast. Toasted pecan halves and ruby-red dried cranberries are distributed, providing crunchy and chewy textures. A glossy, light vinaigrette lightly coats all ingredients. The presentation is natural and abundant, showcasing the diverse colors and textures. The bowl is centered on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin beside it, under soft, even natural lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss diced sweet potato with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized. Let cool.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Grill over medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes per side, until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest, then dice into 1.5 cm cubes.
While sweet potato roasts and chicken grills, prepare kale. Wash and remove tough stems. Chop kale into bite-sized pieces. Place in a large bowl.
Drizzle kale with 5 ml olive oil and a pinch of salt. Massage kale with hands for 2-3 minutes until softened.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 40 ml olive oil, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, maple syrup, salt, and pepper for the dressing.
In a large salad bowl, combine cooled roasted sweet potato, diced chicken, massaged kale, thinly sliced red onion, toasted pecans, and dried cranberries.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine all components evenly.
Serve immediately.
notes: Massaging the kale is crucial for tenderness and flavor absorption.
Ensure sweet potatoes are cooled before mixing to prevent wilting other ingredients.
Toasting pecans enhances their nutty flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and White Bean Salad with Caramelized Red Onion
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A vibrant bed of crisp mixed greens forms the base. Artfully mounded atop the greens is the warm mixture of sliced, browned cremini mushrooms, tender caramelized red onion strips, and creamy white cannellini beans. The components are distinct yet harmoniously integrated. Shaved Parmesan cheese is lightly scattered over the top, adding a delicate texture and pale yellow hue. A few fresh thyme sprigs provide a touch of green garnish. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silverware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the earthy browns, creamy whites, and vibrant greens. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere, maintaining focus on the well-proportioned and visually appealing individual serving.
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced red onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside.

While onions cook, heat 1 tbsp olive oil in another large pan over medium-high heat. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook, without stirring much, until browned and tender, about 7-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Add minced garlic and chopped thyme to the mushrooms. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Remove from heat.
Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, and honey or maple syrup. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large mixing bowl, combine rinsed cannellini beans, cooked mushrooms, and caramelized red onions. Pour dressing over. Toss gently to combine.
Arrange mixed greens on individual serving plates. Top with the warm bean and mushroom mixture.
Garnish with shaved Parmesan cheese if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy chicken and mushroom pasta rests in a round, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown, 2 cm seared chicken cubes are nestled amongst the al dente pasta strands, which are thoroughly coated in a rich, pale cream sauce. Sliced, earthy brown mushrooms are interspersed throughout, adding depth. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley provides a pop of color on top. The dish is presented casually, as if just served from the stove, with the pasta naturally piled. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a plain cloth napkin, emphasizing the homely, unpretentious comfort of the meal.
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Pat chicken breast cut into 2 cm cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Add cooked chicken back to the pan with the sauce. Add drained pasta. Toss to coat everything evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Coriander Beef Larb Salad
recipes.special_requests: make beef mince the main protein. not shepherds pie. surprise me with something a bit different.
recipes.visual_description: The Coriander Beef Larb Salad is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim, reflecting a homely feel. A generous bed of vibrant green spinach leaves forms the base. Piled centrally atop the spinach is the warm, crumbly beef mince, cooked to a rich brown, interspersed with small, bright red chili slices and finely diced red onion, showcasing its savory and spicy character. The mince is loosely arranged, allowing its texture to be visible. To the side of the mince, thinly sliced, crisp cucumber rounds and bright orange, thinly sliced carrot pieces are casually arranged, adding fresh color and a crunchy contrast. A scattering of roughly chopped fresh green coriander leaves is mixed into the mince and garnishes the top, along with a light dusting of the pale brown, coarse toasted ground rice powder.
